entries.title: Isaiah 1:2 "Listen, O heavens, and hear, O earth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:2 "Listen, O heavens, and hear, O earth" These two IMPERATIVES are from different roots, but mean basically the same.

  1. listen, BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 1:10,15,19; 6:8,9 (twice),10, etc.
  2. hear, BDB 24, KB 27, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 1:2,10; 8:9; 28:23; 32:9; etc.

This was a striking way to jolt His people into acknowledging their rebellion. YHWH was initiating a court case against His own people! This opening is similar to Micah 1:2, Isaiah's contemporary Judean prophet.

This sets the stage for chapter 2, which is also a court scene. God is taking his people to trial. This is a common literary technique in the Prophets (i.e. Mic. 6:6-8; Jer. 2:1ff; Rom. 8:31ff). This is a common procedure in the OT of providing two witnesses (i.e. heaven and earth) to confirm a covenant or a testimony (cf. Deut. 4:26; 30:19; 31:28; 32:1; Ps. 50:4).

"Heaven" (BDB 1029) here refers to the atmosphere above the earth which was part of original creation (cf. Genesis 1). In this context it does not refer to "God's abode" (i.e. The Third Heaven).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

▣ "For the Lord speaks" This is the covenant name for Israel's Deity. YHWH can speak but the idols of the nations cannot!

A similar form appears in v. 20. The Jewish Study Bible, p. 784, mentions that this inclusio literary form often sets the limits of a literary unit (i.e. Isa. 1:2-20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "Sons I have reared and brought up" Here again God is described in anthropomorphic, familiar terms as a loving parent of Hosea 11:1-4 (also note Exod. 4:22; Deut. 32:6; Jer. 3:4; 31:9). The best human analogies to comprehend the character and actions of YHWH are

  1. parent
  2. marriage partner (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD)
  3. kinsman redeemer (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KINSMAN REDEEMER)

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "revolt" This VERB (BDB 833, KB 981, Qal PERFECT) implies active, violent, open-eyed, settled, personal rebellion (cf. Isa. 1:28; 43:27; 46:8; 53:12; 59:13; 66:24; see Robert B. Girdlestone, Synonyms of the Old Testament, p. 81). This rebellion came from the family of God (i.e. the covenant people).

▣ "Me" Sin is primarily a violation against God (cf. Gen. 39:9; 2 Sam. 12:13; Ps. 41:4; 51:4). Norman H. Snaith, The Distinctive Ideas of the Old Testament, says "(the prophets) thought of it (sin) as rebellion rather than transgression" (p. 65). Sin is a perversion of the divine image and likeness of God in humankind (cf. Gen. 1:26,27). God wants the world to know Him! He chose a person (Abram), a family (Jacob), and a nation (Israel) to reveal Himself to all humanity, but Israel failed to reflect the holiness and compassion of YHWH. They rebelled against Him with "opened eyes." The essence of sin is "me," more for me at any cost (i.e. the Fall of Genesis 3)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

entries.title: Isaiah 1:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:3 This verse may have been a well known, cultural proverb. Even dumb animals do not bite the hand that feeds them, but Judah does!

▣ "Israel does not know" The VERB "know" (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT) does not imply only facts about a subject, but personal knowledge of someone (cf. Gen. 4:1; Jer. 1:5). Israel did not know their own creator, savior, and protector because they would not listen (cf. Isa. 5:12,13; 6:9-13; 30:9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ "My people" This is covenant language (cf. Hosea 1-3,11). It must be remembered that in the OT, election is God's primary initiating choice of Abraham and Israel. There is commensurate responsibility after God's initial choice known as covenant. This involves responsibility on both sides.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE

▣ "do not understand" This VERB (BDB 106, KB 122, Hithpalel PERFECT) in this stem means "to be inattentive," negated. The problem was not lack of knowledge, but their unwillingness to obey (cf. Isa. 6:9,10; Deut. 4:6; 32:29). They were content with a facade of religiosity (the cultus of Israel), but without the necessary lifelong faith, repentance, and personal trust! Their true nature is described in Isa. 5:18-23, esp. Isa. 1:21 (cf. Isa. 29:13; Micah 4:12). They were covenant people in title, but not covenant people in heart (cf. Rom. 2:28-29; 9:6)!

entries.title: Isaiah 1:4 "Alas"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:4 "Alas" The INTERJECTION (BDB 222) introduces declarations of judgment (i.e. a funeral dirge, which is another common prophetic model, cf. Isa. 10:5; 17:12; 28:1; 29:15; 31:1; 45:9,10; Jer. 22:18; 34:5; Amos 5:18; 6:1).

▣ "sinful nation" The common term "sinful" (BDB 306, KB 305, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) means "to miss the mark" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT)

The term "nation" is goy (BDB 156). This term is often used for the Gentiles, but it can refer to Israel (cf. Exod. 19:5-6). Israel was meant to be a holy nation (cf. Exod. 19:5-6), yet she turned out to be a sinful nation. What a reversal of expectations!

▣ "People weighed down with iniquity" This term "to be bent" or "heavy" (BDB 458) is imagery to describe sin as a burden on mankind's back (cf. Matt. 11:28). All of the Hebrew words for sin are related to crookedness or being bent. It is contrasted to the Hebrew term for righteousness used of God as a "measuring reed" or "ruler." His character is the standard.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "Offspring of evil-doers,
  Sons who act corruptly" This seems to relate to Exod. 20:5 where the evil lifestyles of the parent are communicated to the children.

Notice the parallelism.

  1. sinful nation, Isa. 1:4
  2. weighed down with iniquity, Isa. 1:4
  3. offspring of evildoers, Isa. 1:4
  4. sons who act corruptly, Isa. 1:4

Also notice the parallel clauses that follow.

  1. they have abandoned (BDB 736, KB 806, Qal PERFECT) the Lord
  2. they have despised (BDB 610, KB 658, Piel PERFECT) the Holy One of Israel
  3. they have turned away (BDB 266, KB 267, Niphal PERFECT) from Him

All speak of the actions of an informed, but rebellious, covenant people (notice the number of different word pictures for sin). By their actions and choices they are rejecting YHWH! These three PERFECT stems denote a settled attitude!

These people were to be the blessed "seed" (BDB 282) of Abraham (cf. Gen. 12:7; 13:15,16; 16:10; 22:17,18; 24:7; 26:3,4,24; 28:13,14; 32:12), but they had become the "seed" of evildoers! What a tragedy of wasted revelation and opportunity (cf. Luke 12:48)!

▣ "the Holy One of Israel" This is a favorite title for Deity in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 1:4; 5:19; 10:17,20; 12:6; 17:7; 29:19,23; 30:11,12,15; 31:1; 37:23; also in the second part of Isaiah, 40:25; 41:14,16,20; 43:3,14, 15; 45:11; 47:4; 48:17; 49:7; 54:5; 55:5; 60:9,14; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE). Because He is "holy," His people should be holy (cf. Lev. 11:44-45; 19:2; 20:7; Matt. 5:48; 1 Pet. 1:16).

This title, in a sense, expresses the impossible tension of a sinful, fallen people conforming to a holy standard. The Mosaic Covenant was impossible to keep (cf. Acts 15; Galatians 3; Hebrews). The old covenant was a way to show the impossibility of humans to conform to God's standard, yet He was with them, for them, preparing them for His answer to their fallen condition. He does not lower His standard, but provides it through His Messiah. The new covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36) is a covenant of faith and repentance, not human performance, though it issues in Christlikeness (cf. James 2:14-26). God wants a people who reflect His character to the nations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "They have turned away from Him" This literally is "turned away" (BDB 266, KB 267, Niphal PERFECT) and "backward" (BDB 30, cf. Isa. 44:25). We would say, "they have willfully turned their back on Him" (cf. Isa. 1:2).

entries.title: Isaiah 1:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:5 Here God's people are personified a physically sick individual. This is a good example of physical sickness as imagery for sin (cf. Isa. 53:4-6; Ps. 103:3; Hosea 5:13). Physical healing is not part of the promise of atonement, but a full and complete forgiveness is! In Jewish thought sin and sickness are related (cf. John 9:2; James 5:5).

▣ "Where" NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NIV, RSV, ASV, REB, JPSOA, LXX, and Peshitta correctly translate this as "why" (BDB 752 II), which focuses on the reason for such continuing rebellion.

▣ "As you continue in your rebellion" This VERB (BDB 414, KB 418, Hiphil IMPERFECT) denotes a repeated, continuing attitude of rebellion against God's clearly revealed will.

▣ "whole head. . .whole heart" This parallelism denotes the whole person (thoughts, motives, and actions). The second phrase is also found in Jer. 8:18 and Lam. 1:22, which shows it was a common idiom.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

entries.title: Isaiah 1:6 "nothing sound in it"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:6 "nothing sound in it" This NOUN (BDB 1071) denotes "completeness," "innocence," or "integrity." In this context it functions as imagery for

  1. a life without integrity (cf. Gen. 20:5,6; Ps. 78:72; 101:2)
  2. an unhealthy person (cf. Ps. 38:3)

    The remainder of Isa. 1:6 describes ancient medical procedures.

    1. pressed out
    2. bandaged
    3. softened with oil (oil as medication, cf. Luke 10:34; James 5:14)

A person (or nation) whose wound was not properly cleaned and bandaged could not hope to recover (cf. Hosea 6:1).

entries.title: Isaiah 1:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:7 This reflects an invasion and exile, probably either:

  1. the Assyrian attack in 701 B.C.
  2. the invasion of Israel in 732 B.C.
  3. possibly the Neo-Babylonian invasion of Judah in 586 B.C.

Remember, Isaiah the book, is a compilation of his messages. The exact historical setting of each prophetic message is not stated. Often his poems can refer to different invasions. They may even have been structured for purposeful ambiguity. It reflects the curses of Deuteronomy 28.

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, REB, Peshitta  "strangers"
NRSV  "aliens"
TEV, NJB, LXX  "foreigners"
NET  "foreign invaders"

This PARTICIPLE (BDB 266, KB 267, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, twice) denotes someone from a different family, tribe, nation (cf. Isa. 25:2,5; 29:5; 61:5), usually an enemy of the covenant people. YHWH judges His people by the use of pagan enemies (cf. Isa. 10:5).

The JB, NEB, REB, and the footnote in the JPSOA have "it is as desolate as Sodom after its overthrow." This is because

  1. the FEMININE "overthrow" is always used of Sodom (i.e. Isa. 13:19; Jer. 49:18; 50:40; Amos 4:11
  2. Sodom appears in Isa. 1:9 and experiences a similar divine destruction by fire

There is no Hebrew textual evidence for this emendation.

entries.title: Isaiah 1:8 "The daughter of Zion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:8 "The daughter of Zion" The parent-child motif is begun in Isa. 1:2. Here it is continued into imagery that will recur often in prophetic literature.

  1. daughter of Zion, Isa. 1:8; 10:32; 16:1; 37:22; 52:2; 62:11; Jer. 4:31; 6:23; Lam. 1:6; 2:1,4,8; 2:18; Mic. 4:8,10,13; Zeph. 3:14; Zech. 2:10; 9:9 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION)
  2. daughter of Jerusalem, Isa. 37:22
  3. daughter of Judah, Lam. 2:2,5,13,15; Micah 4:8
  4. daughter of Tyre, Ps. 45:12
  5. daughter of Babylon, Ps. 137:8; Isa. 47:1 (virgin daughter); Jer. 50:42; 51:33; Zech. 2:7
  6. daughter of my people, Isa. 22:4; Jer. 4:11; 6:26; 8:11,19,21,22; 9:1,7; Lam. 2:11; 3:48; 4:6,10
  7. virgin daughter, Isa. 23:12; 37:22; Jer. 14:17; 46:11; Lam. 1:15; 2:13
  8. daughter of Egypt, Jer. 46:24
  9. daughter of Edom, Lam. 4:21,22
  10. daughter of Tarshish, Isa. 23:10
  11. daughter of the Chaldeans, Isa. 47:1,5
  12. faithless daughter, Jer. 31:22

Obviously it was a tender idiom referring to the inhabitants of a nation, region, or city.

▣ "Like a watchman's hut in a cucumber field" This refers to the very fragile, flimsy structure (cf. Isa. 24:20) that is erected during harvest time as a shelter for guards to protect the crop from robbers. Without God His people have no protection or hope (cf. Isa. 1:9).

entries.title: Isaiah 1:9 "the Lord of Hosts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:9 "the Lord of Hosts" See SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

▣ "Had left us a few survivors" This refers to the terrible judgment of the Assyrian and/or the Neo-Babylonian exiles of God's people from the Promised Land.

It denotes the concept of "a faithful remnant" of believers (cf. Isa. 10:20-22; 11:11,16; 37:4,31,32; 46:3), which Paul refers to and expands to include Gentiles in Rom. 9:19-29! Not everyone will be redeemed!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses)

▣ "Sodom. . .Gomorrah" This is a historical allusion to God's judgment recorded in Genesis 18-19. These Canaanite cities became an ANE proverb for both evil and God's judgment of evil.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOMOSEXUALITY

entries.title: Isaiah 1:10 "Hear. . .Give ear"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:10 "Hear. . .Give ear" The two IMPERATIVES of Isa. 1:2 are repeated.

▣ "You rulers of Sodom. . .You people of Gomorrah" Judah is like Sodom and Gomorrah, both her leaders and people are morally corrupt. This phrase was a shocking slur on the covenant people, as was the use of the term goy of Isa. 1:4.

NASB, JPSOA  "instruction"
NKJV, LXX, Peshitta  "law"
NRSV, TEV, REB  "teaching"

This is the term Torah (BDB 435, KB 1710-1712). Notice the possible connotations. In this context it could refer to

  1. Scripture (particularly the writings of Moses, Genesis ‒ Deuteronomy)
  2. the preaching of the prophets
  3. the teachings of the priests

They knew God's revealed will, but chose not to follow it.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

entries.title: Isaiah 1:10-15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 1:10-15 Israel's defense against God's charges of Isa. 1:2-6 is her religiosity!

entries.title: Isaiah 1:11 "What are your multiplied sacrifices to me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:11 "What are your multiplied sacrifices to me" It must be remembered, this is not an attack on sacrifice as such, but the attitudes in which people bring their sacrifices and to whom they bring them (cf. Isa. 29:13; Jer. 6:20; 7:21-22; Hosea 6:6; Amos 5:21-27; Mic. 6:6-8). Ritual can be meaningful if accompanied by a right attitude toward God (cf. Ps. 50). See Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 207-208, 274-275.

The sacrificial system given by God in Leviticus was His way to allow sinful people to approach and maintain fellowship with a Holy God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SACRIFICIAL SYSTEMS OF THE ANE

▣ "I have had enough" This VERB (BDB 959, KB 1302, Qal PERFECT) means bloated or sated.

▣ "burnt offerings" This refers to totally burnt sacrifices which symbolized total dedication to God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERINGS

▣ "The fat of fed cattle" This refers to sacrifices when only part of the animal (fat of lower viscera) was offered on the altar and the rest was given to the priest or to the person bringing the sacrifice to eat as a communal meal with God and family, friends, and neighbors. The meat of large animals could not be preserved and had to be eaten quickly.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING

SPECIAL TOPIC: SACRIFICIAL SYSTEMS OF THE ANE

▣ "I take no pleasure in" This VERB without negation (BDB 342, KB 339, Qal PERFECT) denoted YHWH's acceptance of a sacrifice. The usual idiom was "a soothing aroma" (cf. Gen. 8:21; Exod. 29:18,25). However, YHWH rejected these people's worship (cf. Isa. 1:10-15), as He rejected Cain's in Genesis 4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SOOTHING AROMA

entries.title: Isaiah 1:12 "to appear before Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:12 "to appear before Me" This refers to one's personal attendance at the tabernacle/temple (i.e. Exod. 23:17). They were not coming for true worship, but only in liturgical ritual religiousity!

This phrase is possibly a scribal alteration from "to see my face," which UBS Text Project, p. 1, gives a "C" rating (considerable doubt). It mentions that the scribes made this same type of alteration in Exod. 23:15; 34:20,23,24; Deut. 16:16; 31:11; 1 Sam. 1:22; Ps. 42:3; 84:8. No one can see YHWH's face and live

SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?

entries.title: Isaiah 1:13 "worthless offerings"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:13 "worthless offerings" This term (BDB 996) means "empty," "vain," "nothing."

SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY, VAIN, FALSE, NOTHINGNESS

▣ "Incense is an abomination to Me" The term "incense" (BDB 882, KB 1095) means "that which goes up." Therefore, it could refer to

  1. the smoke of sacrifices
  2. the smell of incense (usually spices placed on top of the sacrifice)
  3. smoke from the incense altar before the inner veil of the tabernacle/temple (see SPECIAL TOPIC: INCENSE ALTAR)

These are strong words! It reminds me of Jeremiah's "temple sermon" of Jeremiah 7. Ritual and liturgy had replaced repentance and faith. They were blind and deaf (cf. Isa. 6:9-10). They had a form of godliness, but denied true faith (cf. 2 Tim. 3:5). The tragedy is that they thought they were right with God! They thought they were His people! They were wrong, as are so many religious, normal, active religionists in every age.

The term "abomination" ("BDB 1072, KB 1702-1704) is used primarliy in Deuteronomy, Proverbs, and Ezekiel. It describes God's reaction to many things.

  1. homosexuality, Lev. 18:22
  2. other sexual sins, Lev. 18:26,27,29,30
  3. idolatry, Deut. 7:25,26; 12:31; 14:3; 17:4; 27:15; 32:16; 2 Kgs. 16:3; 23:13; Jer. 32:35
  4. blemished animal sacrifices, Deut. 17:1
  5. occult practices, Deut. 18:9,12
  6. confusion of gender, Deut. 22:5
  7. sacred prostitution, Deut. 23:18; 1 Kgs. 14:24
  8. remarriage after divorce, Deut. 24:4
  9. commercial cheating, Deut. 25:15-16; Prov. 11:1; 20:10,23
  10. the crooked man, Prov. 3:32; 6:16-19; 8:7; 11:20; 12:22; 15:26; Jer. 7:10
  11. sacrifice of the wicked, Prov. 15:8,9; 21:27
  12. the proud, Prov. 16:5
  13. arrogant leaders, Prov. 16:12
  14. bribed judges, Prov. 17:15
  15. ritualistic offering of incense without lifestyle faith, Isa. 1:13

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

▣ "New moon and Sabbath, the calling of assemblies" Remember the Hebrews used the lunar calendar. Every Sabbath was significant, as was every new moon (cf. Num. 28:11-15; 2 Kgs. 4:23; Isa. 66:23). They had a religious orientation as well as the three yearly feasts appointed in the Mosaic law (cf. Exod. 23:14-17; 34:18-26; Leviticus 23; Deut. 16:1-17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, II., A., D.

entries.title: Isaiah 1:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:14 The Hebrew syntax here is broken because of the great emotion expressed by Isaiah on behalf of God. The first three VERBS are all PERFECTS (completed).

▣ "I hate" This is literally "My soul hates." This is the term nephesh, which is used of

  1. animals ‒ Gen. 1:20
  2. human beings ‒ Gen. 2:7

It simply denotes a life form connected to this planet. In this context, it is simply denoting YHWH as personal.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

entries.title: Isaiah 1:15 "you spread out your hands in prayer"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:15 "you spread out your hands in prayer" Notice that "in prayer" is in italics, which means it is not in the Hebrew text. Prayer in Israel was expressed visually by

  1. standing ‒ 1 Sam. 1:26; 1 Kgs. 8:22; Jer. 18:20
  2. uplifted and spreading out of the hands ‒ Exod. 9:29,33; 1 Kgs. 8:22,38,54; 2 Chr. 6:12
  3. uplifted eyes ‒ John 11:41; 17:1

God refuses to hear (cf. Isa. 8:17; 54:8; 59:2; Deut. 31:17; Jer. 11:11; Ezek.8:18) the prayer of sinful Judeans in their time of need because they came to Him in prayer like they came to Him in sacrifice. Whereas, many sacrifices do not appeal to YHWH, neither does much prayer without heart-felt faith, repentance, and covenant obedience.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "Your hands are covered with blood" This refers to violent death or premeditated murder of the innocent.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MURDER

entries.title: Isaiah 1:16-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:16-17 The prophet expresses the heart of YHWH in a series of commands.

  1. wash yourselves, BDB 934, KB 1220, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. make yourselves clean, BDB 269, KB 269, Hithpael IMPERATIVE
  3. remove the evil, BDB 693, KB 747, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  4. cease to do evil, BDB 292, KB 292, Qal IMPERATIVE
  5. learn to do good, BDB 540, KB 531, Qal IMPERATIVE
  6. seek justice, BDB 205, KB 233, Qal IMPERATIVE
  7. reprove the ruthless, BDB 80, KB 97, Piel IMPERATIVE (possibly "rebuke the oppressor")
  8. defend the orphan, BDB 1047, KB 1622, Qal IMPERATIVE
  9. plead for the widow, BDB 936, KB 1224, Qal IMPERATIVE

Notice that YHWH's will is expressed in terms of a person's righteous acts of compassion (cf. Matt. 25:31-46). One cannot be rightly related to God and hateful and neglectful toward his covenant brother/sister (cf. 1 John 4:20).

Often there is confusion about biblical faith. Is it based on the character of God (i.e. grace, mercy) or on the actions of believers? And the answer is "yes"! A good example of the covenant reciprocity (always initiated by God) is comparing Ezek. 18:31 with Ezek. 36:26-27 (also note Eph. 2:8-9,10 and Phil. 2:12c-13)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

1:17
NASB  "reprove the ruthless"
NKJV  "reprove the oppressor"
NRSV  "rescue the oppressed"
TEV  "help those who are oppressed"
NJB  "discipline the violent"
LXX  "deliver him that is suffering wrong"
Peshitta  "do good to the oppressed"
JPSOA  "aid the wronged"

The MT has "set right the oppressors" (found only here), but the VERB means "called blessed" or "set right" (BDB 80, KB 97, Piel IMPERATIVE), which does not fit this context. It is probably best to change the vowel points of the MT from "the oppressors" to "those who are oppressed" (i.e. Qal PARTICIPLE, BDB 330, NET Bible, see note p. 1184).

▣ "orphan. . .widow" This pair is a symbol of all oppressed and socially disempowered people (cf. Exod. 22:21-22; Deut. 24:17,19,20,21; Job 24:3; Ps. 68:5; Jer. 7:6; 22:3; Lam. 5:3; Ezek. 22:7; Zech. 7:10; Mal. 3:5). They are used together many times in Deuteronomy as the object of YHWH's personal care and attention (i.e. Deut. 10:18; Ps. 10:14,18; 68:5; Jer. 49:11).

It was especially the office of king in the ANE that was responsible for social justice and fairness! See Documents For Old Testament Times, p. 124.

entries.title: Isaiah 1:18-20 "Come now, and let us reason together"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:18-20 "Come now, and let us reason together" The prophet has used the literary imagery of a "court scene" (i.e. YHWH divorcing His people; see SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL FAITH IS CORPORATE) to communicate the message of personal responsibility and its consequences! This courtroom analogy continues.

YHWH is ready to forgive if His people will repent and obey! If they refuse, the consequences of covenant disobedience will come (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28).

There are two VERBS expressing God's invitation for Judah to dialog with the Divine Judge.

  1. come now (lit. "walk," "go"), BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)
  2. let us reason together, BDB 406, KB 410, Niphal COHORTATIVE, cf. Job 23:7

Notice the result if (first "if" clause, Isa. 1:19) they respond appropriately (i.e. consent and obey, Isa. 1:19).

  1. sins forgiven (from scarlet to white as snow)
  2. sins forgiven (from red to white wool)
  3. eat the best of the land

Notice the result (2nd "if" clause, Isa. 1:20) if they refuse (BDB 549, KB 540, Piel IMPERFECT) and rebel (BDB 598, KB 632, Qal PERFECT with waw). They will be devoured (BDB 37, KB 46, Qal PASSIVE IMPERFECT).

It is interesting that the Sovereign God calls on His covenant people to respond appropriately. This is the mystery of predestination and free will. Both are true. They form the basic orientation of the covenant relationship initiated by God, but requiring a response on the part of His people (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP). The fellowship of Genesis 1-2 is restored in a redeemed, covenant relationship. The effects of the Fall can be reversed (even within time).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "Though your sins are as scarlet" Remember that dyed material in the ancient world could not be changed (i.e. they had no bleach). God's forgiveness (and forgetfulness) is miraculous but possible (cf. Ps. 103:11-14; Isa. 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; Mic. 7:19)! When God forgives, He forgets (cf. Ps. 103:12; Isa. 38:17; 43:25; 44:23; Micah 7:19)! Wow!

The color red as imagery for sin may come from the previous phrase "hands are full of bloodshed," mentioned in Isa. 1:15. Red as a symbol for sin is not known outside of the OT in the ANE.

entries.title: Isaiah 1:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:19 There is a wordplay between Isa. 1:19, "obedience will open the door for abundance" (lit. "eat the best of the land"; the VERB [BDB 37, KB 46, Qal IMPERFECT], which has always been God's will) and the same VERB in Isa. 1:20 translated "devoured" (i.e. they will be eaten; Qal PASSIVE IMPERFECT or Pual IMPERFECT), if they do not repent and obey (cf. Deut. 30:15,19). There are covenant blessings and responsibilities and they are connected (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-29)!

▣ "If you consent and obey" Remember the covenants in the OT are both conditional and unconditional. They are unconditional as far as God's promises to redeem fallen mankind, but they are conditional on individual human response (cf. Luke 6:46; John 1:12; 3:16; Rom. 10:9-13; James 2:14-26), both initially and throughout life.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Isaiah 1:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:20 There is an interesting textual option.

  1. The MT and LXX have, "You will be devoured by the sword."
  2. However, a revocalization is, "Locust-beans, you will eat," which fits well as an antithesis to v. 19.

The UBS "Interim Text Project" gives option #1 a "B" rating (some doubt).

▣ "Truly, the mouth of the Lord has spoken" God's Word will come to pass (cf. Isa. 24:3; 25:8; 40:8; 55:10-11; Matt. 5:18; 24:35; Luke 16:17)!

Believers' hope rests on

  1. the unchanging character of God
  2. the merciful character of God
  3. the trustworthiness of His promises
  4. the accuracy of His revelation

Notice how YHWH speaking introduces and closes chapter 1:2-20.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

entries.title: Isaiah 1:21 "faithful"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:21 "faithful" This is the basic meaning of this root in the Hebrew Bible.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT

▣ "a harlot" This could be imagery for

  1. a spiritual adultery, going after other gods
  2. a reference to the Canaanite fertility cults

The "virgin daughter of Zion" has become corrupted!

▣ "justice" See SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE

▣ "righteousness" See SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

entries.title: Isaiah 1:21-23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:21-23 This section deals with Jerusalem of Isaiah's day, the special place where YHWH caused His name to dwell (i.e. the temple or earlier, the tabernacle, cf. Deut. 12:5,11,14). It has become unfaithful and does not fulfill covenant stipulations (cf. Isa. 1:23). This section is characterized by Hebrew lament meter or beats, which is another common prophetic literary device (i.e. funeral dirge, cf. v. 4).

Notice her covenant violations.

  1. murderers (cf. Exod. 20:13, premeditated, intentional taking of life, BDB 953, KB 1283, cf. Jer. 7:9; Hosea 4:2; see SPECIAL TOPIC: MURDER)
  2. rulers as rebels
  3. rulers as companions of thieves
  4. lovers of bribes (cf. Isa. 5:23; Exod. 23:6,8; Deut. 16:19; 1 Sam. 8:3; Ps. 26:10; Amos 5:12; Micah 3:11; 7:3)
  5. chasers of rewards
  6. not defenders of orphans (see texts in #7)
  7. not supplicants for widows (cf. Exod. 22:21-24; Deut. 10:18-19; 24:17-21; Jer. 5:28; 7:6; 22:3; Ezek. 22:7; Zech. 7:10)

These are violations of the Mosaic covenant summarized in Deuteronomy. Note that Judah is condemned for covenant violations, not idolatry in this context (unless the word "harlot" in Isa. 1:21 implies Canaanite fertility worship).

entries.title: Isaiah 1:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:22 These are two images for Jerusalem/Judah's moral corruptness. She (PRONOUN in v. 22 is FEMININE SINGULAR) was initially pure, but now she has become corrupted by her own motives, choices, and actions!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO "CITIES" IN ISAIAH

NASB  "drink"
NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA, LXX, Peshitta  "wine"
REB  "fine liquor"

This (BDB 685, KB 738) is not the normal term for wine (see SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOLISM). This SINGULAR FEMININE occurs only here. Because of the related cognate root in Akkadian, it may refer to beer (NET), beer that has been diluted (i.e. ruined) by water (NASB, JPSOA). In Arabic the root means "wine" or "imported wine."

entries.title: Isaiah 1:23 "Everyone loves a bribe"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:23 "Everyone loves a bribe" Justice was not based on YHWH's law or pity for the poor and helpless. All levels of Judah's leadership could be bribed (cf. Jer. 5:28; 6:13; Amos 5:12; Micah 3:11; 7:3). Money and power were their true gods!

▣
NASB, NKJV, LXX, Peshitta  "rewards"
NRSV, TEV, REB, JPSOA  "gifts"
NJB  "presents"

This term (BDB 1024) occurs only here in the OT. BDB says it means "rewards" or "bribe" (parallel to bribe [BDB 1005] in the previous line). The basic root may be related to

  1. shalom (BDB 1024), "peace," "health," "wholeness,"
  2. "recompense" (BDB 1024, cf. Isa. 59:18; NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 143)

In Jerusalem the only peace was for wicked, wealthy, powerful groups in society.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

entries.title: Isaiah 1:24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:24 Notice the two Divine names in Isa. 1:24!

  1. the Lord, God of hosts (adon, YHWH, cf. Ps. 110:1; NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp.1297-1298)
  2. the Mighty One of Israel (or "the Mighty One of Jacob," cf. Gen. 49:24; Ps. 132:2,5; Isa. 49:26; 60:16)

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (adon and kurios)

entries.title: Isaiah 1:24-26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:24-26 YHWH speaks of His future plans of restoring His people (cf. v.26) after judgment on the wicked leadership.

  1. "I will be relieved of My adversaries," Isa. 1:24, BDB 636, KB 688, Niphal IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense
  2. "I will avenge Myself on My foes," Isa. 1:24, BDB 667, KB 721, Niphal COHORTATIVE
  3. "I will also turn My hand against you," Isa. 1:25. BDB 996, KB 1427, Hiphil COHORTATIVE (see SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND)
  4. "I will melt away your dross as with lye," Isa. 1:25, BDB 864, KB 1057, Qal IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense
  5. "I will remove all your alloy," Isa. 1:25, BDB 693, KB 747, Hiphil COHORTATIVE
  6. "I will restore your judges," Isa. 1:26, BDB 996, KB 1427 Hiphil COHORTATIVE
  7. "I will restore your counselors," Isa. 1:26 (same as #6, one VERB, two OBJECTS; these must relate to the Exodus period)

Note that the purpose of judgment is restoration (cf. Isa. 1:27)!

entries.title: Isaiah 1:25 "will smelt away"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 1:25 "will smelt away" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

entries.title: Isaiah 1:25-26 "you. . .your"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:25-26 "you. . .your" These two verses use FEMININE SINGULARS to denote that YHWH is addressing the unfaithful capital city of Judah, Jerusalem, with all her economic, military, and religious power structures.

As Isa. 1:19 and 20 used the same VERB in contrasting ways, so too, Isa. 1:25 and 26 with

  1. I will turn My hand against you, BDB 996, KB 1427, Hiphil COHORTATIVE (see SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND)
  2. I will restore, BDB 996, KB 1427, Hiphil COHORTATIVE

The same term is used in Isa. 1:27, "the returnees" (BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) to describe those touched by God's justice and righteousness.

entries.title: Isaiah 1:26 "A faithful city"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:26 "A faithful city" Is this an obvious reversal of the sarcasm of Isa. 1:21? Jerusalem is no longer "a harlot," but a restored, faithful woman (i.e. "city" is FEMININE). She has finally become true to her title, faithful to God, faithful to His covenant, and faithful to each other!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO "CITIES" OF ISAIAH

entries.title: Isaiah 1:27-28
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:27-28 Note the parallelism.

  1. Isa. 1:27, the people of the restored city (Isa. 1:26 lines 3 and 4) will be characterized by "justice" and "righteousness"
  2. Isa. 1:28, the one who refuses to repent (turn back) will be "crushed" and "come to an end" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT])

Therefore, there is antithetical parallelism within Isa. 1:27 and 28.

There is some question about Isa. 1:27. Does it describe what God is doing and will do or does it describe faithful covenant people? The answer is "yes." God wants a righteous people to reflect His character to the lost nations. These qualities are objective (God) and subjective (believers).

Just an added thought about the ultimate condition of the unrepentant person. Do you notice that destruction is the final state of the wicked? This is like the contrast of John 3:16; either eternal life or perish (also note Rom. 6:23). I am becoming more and more convinced of "limited immortality." I hope you will view the YouTube videos:

  1. Steve Gregg ‒ "Hell, Three Christian Views"
  2. Edward Fudge ‒ "The Fire That Consumes"

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY, III.

entries.title: Isaiah 1:29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:29 This verse describes Judah's idolatry. It could refer to

  1. Ba'al, Asherah worship (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE) at local shrines (i.e. Asherah was symbolized by a live tree or carved stake, cf. Deut. 12:2; Isa. 57:5; Jer. 3:9; Hosea 4:13)
  2. worship at sacred trees (local gods, cf. Isa. 65:3; 66:17)
    SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES
  3. worship in sacred gardens often associated with a secret place for idolatry. In ANE literature temples and special gardens were often connected.

It must be added that it is possible that the paragraph (Isa. 1:27-31) refers to the exploitation and materialism of the wealthy classes of Judean society. The references in Isa. 1:29 are to choice property (i.e. violation of YHWH's special love toward the poor, ostracized, powerless) and not idolatry (i.e. violation of YHWH's uniqueness).

Read the chapter and decide for yourself! Whichever it is, it fails to reflect YHWH's character to the nations!

entries.title: Isaiah 1:30 "fades"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 1:30 "fades" This VERB (BDB 615, KB 663, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) is used as imagery for the fleetingness of human existence (cf. Isa. 34:4; 64:6; Ps. 90:5-6).

entries.title: Isaiah 1:31
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
1:31 Fire is often associated with judgment or cleansing (i.e. Isa. 6:13; Jer. 4:4; Amos 5:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

NASB  "the strong man"
NKJV, NRSV, NJB  "the strong"
LXX, Peshitta  "their strength"
REB  "the strongest tree"
JB  "the men of high estate"

This ADJECTIVE (BDB 340) is found only here and Amos 2:9, both in context that relates to trees (cf. Isa. 1:29,30). Possibly the REB is best. It refers to idolatry involving wood, trees, or a garden.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES

▣ "tinder" This term (BDB 654), in its VERBAL form, usually means "shaken out" (cf. Isa. 33:9,15), but the NOUN, used only twice in the OT, refers to the string/rope (tow) from flax (cf. Jdg. 16:9).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. How long did Isaiah serve as the chief prophet for Judah?
  2. Why is God spoken of in such anthropomorphic terms?
  3. Is God displeased with sacrifice?
  4. Define a person's responsibility in salvation, OT and NT.

entries.title: Isaiah 2:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:1 It is uncertain why Isaiah's messages are described as

  1. a vision, Isa. 1:1; 29:7 (BDB 302, cf. Micah 3:6)
  2. he saw, Isa. 1:1; 2:1; 13:1; 26:11; 33:17; 48:6; 57:8 (cf. Micah 1:1)

This is the mystery of revelation. It comes in different ways to different biblical authors (visions, dreams, theophanies, words, etc.). Moderns do not know how much freedom the individual writers (authors, editors, compilers) had to structure and present God's message. They obviously used their own language skills and vocabularies. Even without a full and complete understanding of the way revelation works, the concept is crucial! These are God's messages given through a historically conditioned person, to a particular time and group, yet they are relevant for all people in all times! The key for a proper interpretation is that the intent of an original inspired author must be the criteria for interpretation (one meaning but many significances/applications).

A good book that has helped me deal with the cultural particularity of Scripture is Gordon Fee, Gospel and Spirit. Another good book that helps identify and deal with different biblical genres is Fee and Stuart, How To Read the Bible for All Its Worth, ISBN 0-310-24604-0

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

▣ "the son of Amoz" See note at Isa. 1:1.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Isaiah 2 begins with another introductory phrase, like Isa. 1:1. It is possible that editors or compilers put Isaiah's sermons/visions/messages together based on
    1. chronology (under which king)
    2. topic
    3. catch words
    4. unknown literary scheme
    5. a written copy of several Isaiah messages
      See note in The Jewish Study Bible, p. 787.

  2. This chapter is typical of the prophet's messages.
    1. hope for all nations through YHWH's covenant people (Isa. 2:2-4)
    2. judgment for covenant violations and wickedness (Isa. 2:5-22; note Lev. 26 and Deut. 28)

  3. YHWH wants a righteous, holy, covenant people to reflect His character to the nations so that they can respond to Him in faith and righteousness (cf. Isa. 45:22; 49:6; 60:3; 66:18,23).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

  4. Remember in these poetic literary units (visions), do not push the details or single lexical studies, but the overall pattern of parallelism, word plays, and contrasts! The whole poem is meant to convey one major truth! Be careful of picking and choosing themes, words, or truths you are comfortable with or that fit you're á priori systematic theology. Let Isaiah speak!
    SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY

  5. Because of the unifying theme of Jerusalem (judged and blessed), Isaiah 2-4 forms a literary unit.

  6. A book that has helped me understand the language of prophecy and apocalyptic is D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic, IVP, ISBN 0-83-8-2653-X.

BRIEF OUTLINE

  1. The Parabolic Song, Isa. 2:1-6

  2. The Ironical Interpretation, Isa. 2:7

  3. The resultant Judgment of YHWH, Isa. 2:8-30
    1. Series of woes, Isa. 2:8-23
    2. Judgment, Isa. 2:24-30
      1. natural, Isa. 2:25
      2. invader, Isa. 2:26-30

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 2:2 "In the last days"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:2 "In the last days" This phrase refers to the future horizon of the particular biblical writer (see G. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible, chapter 14, "The Language of Eschatology," pp. 243-271). It denoted a time of fulfillment of God's purposes.

  1. the Messianic kingdom, Gen. 49:1-27 (esp. 49:10); Num. 24:14-25 (esp. 24:17); Isa. 2:2; Jer. 48:47; 49:39; Ezek. 38:8,16
  2. Israel's rebellion, Deut. 31:29
  3. Israel's return to YHWH in repentance and faith, Deut. 4:30; Hosea 3:5; Jer. 23:19-22 (esp. 23:20)
  4. an end-time attack on the covenant people, Ezek. 38:16; Dan. 2:28; 10:14 (possibly Psalm 2)
  5. exile, Amos 4:2

Only context can clarify which period. Be careful of your systematic theology!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE LAST DAYS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE MESSIANIC ERA

▣ "The mountain of the house of the Lord" This refers to the temple located on Mt. Moriah in Jerusalem. It was the place of centralized worship of YHWH (the place He caused His name to dwell, cf. Deut. 12:5,11,14,18,21,26; 14:25; 15:20; 16:2,6,11,15; 17:8,10; 18:6; 26:2; 31:11).

The NIV Study Bible (pp. 962-3) comments how common in Isaiah is the theme of the mountain of the Lord where all the nations come in the last days (cf. Isa. 11:9; 27:13; 56:7; 57:13; 65:25; 66:20).

In a sense this elevation of Mt. Zion (i.e. Jerusalem, the site of the temple of YHWH) is depicted in Canaanite myth (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 1314-1321). For the Canaanites the gods dwelt on Mt. Zaphon in the far north (cf. Isa. 14:13), but Ps. 48:2 changes the imagery to Mt. Zion. YHWH is above all Canaanite deities!

This same concept of a temple or a city being raised is also found in Mesopotamian literature (cf. The Weidner Chronicle, Assyrian inscriptions, Marduk Prophecy). So the concept is not unique to Isaiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, JERUSALEM, ZION

▣ Notice the metaphorical language used to describe the chief place of YHWH's revelation to Abraham's descendants.

  1. "the chief of the mountains," i.e. the place of true revelation
  2. "raised above the hills," a symbol of preeminence and exclusiveness
  3. "all the nations will stream to it," this has always been YHWH's goal, cf. Gen. 3:15; 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6; Ps. 22:27; 66:1-4; 86:8-10; Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:6-8; 60:1-3; 66:23; Jer. 3:17; Micah 4:1-4; Mal. 1:11; John 3:16; 4:42; Acts 10:34-35; 1 Tim. 2:4; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:2; 4:14! This is the natural result of monotheism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE THE END-TIME EVENTS SO CONTROVERSIAL?

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "all the nations will stream to it" This VERB (BDB 625, KB 676, Qal PERFECT with waw) denotes an ever-flowing stream of water, like an artesian well. Here, it is imagery for the unending flow of the nations to YHWH (i.e. Isa. 56:6-8).

entries.title: Isaiah 2:2-4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:2-4 This brief paragraph summarizes the OT perspective on the place and purpose of the covenant people (similar to Micah 4:1-5). They were to be a light to the nations (cf. Isa. 51:4,5; Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:47; Acts 1:8)!

The Jewish Study Bible calls vv. 2-4 "one of the most famous texts in the Bible," p. 787.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 2:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:3 The JPSOA translates "will stream to it" as "will gaze on it with joy." Originally the priests and Levites were to be the teachers of the Law (cf. Deut. 31:9; 33:10). People who wanted to know YHWH and His will would come to the temple (i.e. both Israelites and Gentiles, cf. 1 Kgs. 8:43,60; Isa. 57:6; Mark 11:17).

Notice the request of the nations.

  1. "come,"BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. "let us go up to the mountain of the Lord," BDB 748, KB 828, Qal IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense
  3. "That He may teach us concerning His ways," BDB 434, KB 436, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  4. "that we may walk in His paths," BDB 229, KB 246, Qal COHORTATIVE (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)
  5. "that the law (teachings) will go forth from Zion," BDB 422, KB 425, Qal IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense (see SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION)

▣ "Lord. . .God" The first title/name is YHWH, the covenant name for Israel's Deity, first used in Gen. 2:4.

The second title/name is Eloah, which is the SINGULAR form of Elohim, or possibly for El, the God of creation from Gen. 1:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, A., C., D.

▣ "His paths" This term (BDB 73) is used several times in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 2:3; 3:12; 26:7,8; 30:11; 33:8; 40:18; 41:3) and prominently in Proverbs (cf. Isa. 1:19; 2:8,13,15,19,20; 3:6; 4:14,18; 5:6; 8:20; 9:15; 10:17; 12:28; 15:10,19,24; 17:23; 22:25). It is imagery to denote a lifestyle faith that obeys and walks in God's teachings (cf. Exod. 16:4; Isa. 30:20; 42:24; Jer. 9:12; 26:4; 32:23; 44:10,23; Zech 7:12).

This imagery for lifestyle, faithful living became the first title of the NT church, "The Way" (cf. John 14:6; Acts 9:2; 19:9,23; 22:4; 24:14,22; 18:25-26).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "Zion" Jerusalem (like Rome) was built on seven hills. Zion (BDB 851, KB 1022, meaning uncertain, but KB's suggestions from an Arabic root are

  1. citadel
  2. barren place
  3. or bare hill)

was the hill on which the original Canaanite city of Jebus or Salem was built (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:1; 2 Chr. 5:2). As Jerusalem grew it became a way of referring to the whole city and temple (cf. Isa. 2:3, lines 6 and 7; Jer. 50:28: 51:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

entries.title: Isaiah 2:4 "He will judge. . .render decisions"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:4 "He will judge. . .render decisions" These two VERBS (BDB 1047, KB 1622, Qal PERFECT with waw and BDB 406, KB 410, Hiphil PERFECT with waw) describe the reasonings and decisions of a wise ruler. YHWH and His Messiah are the ultimate wise rulers (cf. Isa. 11:1-5; Mic. 5:4)!

▣ The Lord's presence and teachings will cause the nations to abandon their attacks on His people (cf. Psalm 2; Ezekiel 38-39). They will pursue peace (cf. Isa. 9:6-7; 11:6-9; 57:19; Hosea 2:18; Zech. 9:10).

▣ "swords into plowshares" This is an idiom for peace. The opposite occurs in Joel 3:10, where it is an idiom for war.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE AND WAR

entries.title: Isaiah 2:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:5 Notice the parallel between Isa. 2:3 (the nations) and Isa. 2:5 (the Israelites). Lifestyle faith is the evidence of a personal, trusting relationship with God. Humans must know the truth, walk in the truth, and share it with others! The nations were to learn this from Israel, but they did not!

The "light of the Lord" is imagery for true revelation (cf. Isa. 60:1-2,19-20). The worship of the lights of the night sky is false revelation. This verse may be a rejection of Babylonian astral worship (cf. Isa. 2:6). YHWH and His Messiah are the true light for the nations (cf. Isa. 9:2; 42:6; 49:6; 51:4; 53:11).

entries.title: Isaiah 2:6-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:6-9 These verses describe why YHWH abandoned (BDB 643, KB 695, Qal PERFECT) His own covenant people.

  1. They are filled with influence from the east, Isa. 2:6.
  2. They are soothsayers (BDB 778 II), like the Philistines, Isa. 2:6.
  3. They strike bargains with the children of foreigners, Isa. 2:6.
  4. They are wealthy and militarily strong (and trust in these things), Isa. 2:7 (notice the three-fold repetition of "filled," BDB 569, KB 583, Niphal IMPERFECT with waw in Isa. 2:7 and 8).
  5. They are idolatrous, Isa. 2:8 (cf. Isa. 17:8; 37:19; 40:19; 44:17).
  6. They treat the common people with disdain, Isa. 2:9 (cf. Isa. 2:11,17; it is possible that this verse is parallel to Isa. 2:8 and refers to idolatry, cf. NKJV).

What can the nations learn from people like this?!

Concerning #6 above (Isa. 2:9), the NASB and NKJV translate it as another in a series of descriptions of how the covenant people are acting, but NRSV and TEV translate it as a summary and the last line is a plea for YHWH, not to forgive them (Peshitta) or a statement by YHWH that He will not forgive them (LXX).

2:6
NASB, NRSV  "from the east"
NKJV  "eastern ways"
TEV, JPSOA  "from the East"
Peshitta  "olden days"
REB  "traders"

The UBS Hebrew OT Text Project gives "from the east" or "from olden times" (both possible meanings of this NOUN, BDB 869, KB 1069) a "B" rating (some doubt). The NEB and REB add one consonant and make it "traders." It seems to refer to religious influences (pagan idol worship) from the east (i.e. Syria, Assyria, Babylon, see RSV) which corrupted Israel's faith.

▣ "soothsayers" If this was meant to be a strict parallelism with the line above, it is possible that a NOUN parallel to "soothsayer" (BDB 778 II), such as "diviners" (cf. Lev. 19:26; Deut. 18:9-12; see SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION), has inadvertently dropped out of the MT. The MT is not the earliest Hebrew text. It does have textual problems! However, remember that these kinds of problems do not affect major doctrines.

NASB  "they strike bargains with the children of foreigners"
NKJV  "they are pleased with the children of foreigners"
NRSV  "they clasp hands with foreigners"
TEV  "they follow foreign customs"
NJB  "is overrun with foreigners"
LXX  "many strange children were born to them"
Peshitta  "they reared many alien children"
REB  "the children of foreigners are everywhere"
JPSOA  "they abound in customs of the aliens"

The term "children" is not in the MT. The VERB "they strike hands" (i.e. make bargains, BDB 706 I, KB 765, Hiphil IMPERFECT) is ambiguous. It can refer to

  1. a commercial transaction
  2. a political alliance
  3. a friendship
  4. an affirmation of the customs of foreigners

Obviously in context the unique faith of Israel is being compromised!

entries.title: Isaiah 2:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 2:7 This description of Judean leadership is in direct contradiction to Deut. 17:16-17. Humans who have resources tend to trust in them (cf. Isa. 31:1), but Isa. 2:22 (cf. Isa. 31:3) shows the failure of trusting in physical or human resources (i.e. wealth and military equipment).

entries.title: Isaiah 2:9 "man. . .man"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:9 "man. . .man" Isaiah 2:9 is a two-line, synonymous parallelism (cf. 2 Kgs. 7:10). The two most common terms for mankind are parallel.

  1. adam, BDB 9, KB 14, cf. Gen. 1:26; 6:1,5,6,7; 9:5,6
  2. ish, BDB 35, KB 43, Gen. 2:23; Num. 23:19

See Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the Old Testament for "Adam," pp. 45-48 and for "ish," pp. 48-50.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, JPSOA  "do not forgive them"
NJB, NIV  "do not raise them again"
LXX  "do not pardon them"
REB  (omits as gloss, cf. Dead Sea Scroll and JB footnote)

The VERB (BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) means "to lift" or "to carry." Here it has the sense of "carry away" (i.e. remove their sin). This may be an exclamation from Isaiah, himself.

This VERB (in Hebrew and Greek) is such an important and wonderful action.

  1. God will forgive sin ‒ Isa. 33:24
  2. Christ takes away sin ‒ John 1:29; 1 John 3:5
  3. carried/bore ‒ Isa. 53:4; Matt. 8:17; 1 Pet. 2:24

In this context, it is negated. The prophet asks that YHWH does not act on behalf of these flagrant covenant violators.

The footnote of JPSOA suggests an emendation to "and their idols with them," from vv. 17-21 (p.788).

entries.title: Isaiah 2:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:10-11 These two verses describe YHWH's advice to these covenant violators (Isa. 2:10a).

  1. enter the rock, BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE (i.e. this relates to Isa. 2:19-21, and possibly refers to caves or manmade tunnels, cf. Rev. 6:15-17)
  2. hide in the dust, BDB 380, KB 377, Niphal IMPERATIVE

They are to hide from (Isa. 2:10b)

  1. the terror of the Lord, cf. Isa. 2:19,21
  2. the splendor of His majesty (cf. Isa. 2:11c, 19,21; 2 Thess. 1:9)

The result will be (Isa. 2:11, note parallel in Isa. 2:17)

  1. the proud look of men will be abased, BDB 1050, KB 1631, Qal PERFECT (opposite of Isa. 2:9)
  2. the loftiness of man will be humbled, BDB 1005, KB 1458, Qal PERFECT with waw (opposite of Isa. 2:9, cf. Isa. 13:11; 23:9; 2 Cor. 10:5)
  3. the Lord alone will be exalted in that day, BDB 960, KB 1305, Niphal PERFECT with waw (note parallel in Isa. 2:17 and the phrase about the "terror" and "splendor" of YHWH in Isa. 2:19c and 21b)

Some commentators think that Isa. 2:10 is encouraging the righteous to hide from YHWH's coming judgment on the wicked (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 377), but in context (i.e. Isa. 2:19-21) it refers to the covenant violators.

entries.title: Isaiah 2:11 "in that day"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:11 "in that day" This refers to the last days of Isa. 2:2a. It becomes a dominate theme in Amos. The theme in Isaiah is resumed in Isa. 2:12 (cf. Isa. 2:20; 3:17; 5:30; 28:5-6; Amos 2:16; 8:9; Hosea 2:18). See SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

Conscious creation (humans and angels) will one day stand before its Creator and give account of the stewardship of the gift of life (i.e. Matt. 25:31-46; Rev. 20:11-15). YHWH is a moral, ethical God; creation is a moral, ethical creation. Humans do not break God's laws so much as break themselves on God's laws. The laws are for our protection in a fallen world, but humans see them as restrictions and loss of personal freedoms. One day every conscious creation, human and angel, will give an account before God (cf. Phil. 2:9-11)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

entries.title: Isaiah 2:12 "For the Lord of hosts will have a day of reckoning"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:12 "For the Lord of hosts will have a day of reckoning" This does not follow the Hebrew text. The MT has "For the day of the Lord of hosts" (cf. NKJV). The NASB translation is trying to link this back to Isa. 1:18.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DAY OF THE LORD

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

▣ Notice the two types of parallelism in v. 12. Lines 2 and 3 are in a synonymous parallelism, while line 4 is in an antithetical parallelism to them.

One day the pride of wicked leaders and the wealthy will be brought low (cf. v. 11).

entries.title: Isaiah 2:12-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:12-13 Notice the recurrent use of terms denoting arrogant, prideful humans and nations.

  1. "everyone who is proud" (BDB 144, KB 168), Isa. 2:12.
  2. "and lofty" (BDB 926, KB 1202, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE (note the same form in Isa. 2:13, 14), Isa. 2:12
  3. "everyone who is lifted up" (BDB 669, KB 724, Niphal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE (note the same form in Isa. 2:13,14), Isa. 2:12
  4. "all the cedars of Lebanon that are lofty and lifted up," Isa. 2:13 (imagery for proud humans and nations)

entries.title: Isaiah 2:12-16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:12-16 Note the repeated use of "against" (BDB 752, KB 825).

  1. against everyone who is proud and lofty, Isa. 2:12
  2. against all that is lifted up, Isa. 2:12
  3. against all the cedars of Lebanon that are lofty and lifted up, Isa. 2:13
  4. against all the oaks of Bashan (who are also lofty and lifted up), Isa. 2:13
  5. against all the lofty mountains, Isa. 2:14
  6. against all the hills that are lifted up, Isa. 2:14
  7. against every high tower, Isa. 2:15
  8. against every fortified wall, Isa. 2:15
  9. against all the ships of Tarshish, Isa. 2:16
  10. against all beautiful craft, Isa. 2:16 (this word "craft" [BDB 967] appears only here and its meaning is uncertain; it may parallel "ships of Tarshish" in Isa. 2:16a)

The Lord opposes the proud (cf. Isa. 2:11 and 17).

entries.title: Isaiah 2:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:13 Because of the allusion to idolatry with trees (Isa. 1:29) and gardens (Isa. 1:29-30) and that YHWH will burn them, one wonders if this mention of lofty trees reflects

  1. the pride and arrogance of nations
  2. the worship of idols connected with trees/wood

Because of the larger context (i.e. "against" series) the first option seems best. The problem of human pride is summarized in Isa. 2:17 (which may be the theme of the entire book).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES

entries.title: Isaiah 2:16 "all the ships of Tarshish"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:16 "all the ships of Tarshish" See note at Isa. 23:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TARSHISH

NASB, NRSV  "against all the beautifl craft"
NKJV  "upon all the beautiful sloops"
NJB  "for everything held precious"
TEV, LXX  "beautiful ships"
NET  "impressive ships"
JPSOA  "all galant banks"
REB  "stately vessels"
Peshitta  "against all pleasant sights"
Rotherham  "upon all desirable banners"

This word (BDB 967, KB 1327) occurs only here in the OT. The question is, "Is it parallel to the line about large ocean-going merchant ships or about human imagination?" Most lexicons chose "ships."

  1. MT ‒ שׂכיות (BDB meaning very dubious)
  2. "lookout point" or "banners/standards" ‒ שׂכיה (Gesenius Thesaurus)

entries.title: Isaiah 2:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 2:17 This is parallel in thought to Isa. 2:11, which is the opposite of what evil leaders and wealthy socialites had done to the poor and humble in Isa. 2:9. Many see this verse as a summary theme of the entire book (Jewish Study Bible, p. 788)!

entries.title: Isaiah 2:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:18 Idolatry will cease completely (cf. Isa. 21:9) because the worship of them is "emptiness" (cf. Isa. 30:22; 31:7; 40:18-20; 44:9-20; 46:5-7)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Isaiah 2:19 "When He arises to make the earth tremble"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:19 "When He arises to make the earth tremble" The first VERBAL "arise" (BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) can denote

  1. appear on the scene, Exod. 1:8; Deut. 34:10; Jdg. 5:7; 2 Kgs. 23:25
  2. arise for action (from His throne), Num. 10:35; 2 Chr. 6:41; Job 31:14; Ps. 76:9; 132:8

The second VERBAL "tremble" (BDB 791, KB 888, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) describes physical creation as its Creator approaches (cf. Isa. 13:13; 24:1,19,20; Ps. 18:7; 68:7-8; Hag. 2:6; also note Rom. 8:19). YHWH can come for blessing or judgment. In this context it is for judgment!

entries.title: Isaiah 2:20-21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:20-21 To clarify the first line of Isa. 2:10, humans will try to hide from God

  1. in caves in the rocks (cf. Isa. 2:21)
  2. in manmade tunnels

They will try to get rid of their precious idols

  1. cast away to moles (NASB, Peshitta; the meaning of the word is uncertain)
    1. LXX has "vanities"
    2. REB has "dung-beetles"
    3. JPSOA has "flying foxes" (a type of bat, therefore, parallel to the next line of poetry)
      It is related to the VERB "to dig" (BDB 343), therefore, to animals that dig or live in the ground
    4. NET has "rodents"
  2. cast away to bats

These two verses have a series of INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS.

  1. to the moles (lit. "to dig"), BDB 343, KB 340, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT
  2. to worship (lit, "bow down"), BDB 1005, KB 295, Hishtaphel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT
  3. to go into, BDB 97, KB 112, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT
  4. arises, BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, same form as Isa. 2:19 (line 5)
  5. tremble (lit. "to frighten," BDB 791, KB 888, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, same as Isa. 2:19 (line 5)

In the IVP Bible Background Commentary "a Sumerian Hymn of Enheduanna to the goddess Inanna from the third millennium depicts gods fluttering away like bats to their caves from the goddess's terrible presence" (p. 588). This means that it must remain a possibility that it is the idols themselves that were carried down by insects (beetles) or digging animals seeking refuge from the coming of YHWH because they could not move themselves.

entries.title: Isaiah 2:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
2:22 The VERBAL PHRASE "stop regarding" (Qal IMPERATIVE and a Niphal PARTICIPLE) is emphatic! Some humans trust in themselves (cf. Ps. 146:3; Jer. 17:5) and not YHWH. Faithful followers should not give a thought to them! They look prosperous and happy, but their day will come when they stand before God in judgment, both in time and at the end of time.

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 3:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:1 Chapter three continues the prophet's surprising prediction of YHWH's judgment on Jerusalem and Judah.

▣ "Lord God of hosts" This title ("Adon" plus "YHWH of Hosts") for Israel's Deity is used several times early in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 1:24; 3:1; 10:16,33; 19:4). See full note at Isa. 1:24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (Adon and Kurios)

▣ "is going to remove" This VERB (BDB 693, KB 747, Hiphil PARTICIPLE) in the Hiphil stem means "remove" or "take away."

  1. YHWH to remove Israel's sickness, Exod. 23:25; Deut. 7:15
  2. Israel to remove the accursed things (i.e. Achan's sin), Josh 7:13
  3. Israel to put away foreign gods, Jdg. 10:16
  4. Saul removes mediums and spiritists, 1 Sam. 28:3
  5. individuals did not put away God's laws, 2 Sam. 22:23; Ps. 18:23

But notice here it is God who removes all of Judah's support, strength, and idolatrous leadership.

  1. supply (lit. "staff," BDB 1044) of bread, Isa. 3:1
  2. supply (lit. "staff") of water, Isa. 3:1
  3. mighty men, Isa. 3:2
  4. warriors, Isa. 3:2
  5. judge, Isa. 3:2
  6. prophet, Isa. 3:2, cf. Isa. 9:14-15; 28:7; 29:10
  7. diviner, Isa. 3:2
  8. elder, Isa. 3:2, cf. Isa. 9:14-16
  9. captain of fifty, Isa. 3:3
  10. honorable man, Isa. 3:3
  11. counselor, Isa. 3:3
  12. expert artisan, Isa. 3:3, cf. Isa. 40:20 (idol maker)
  13. skillful enchanter, Isa. 3:3

Remember this judgment was YHWH, the loving parent, disciplining His children so that they might be strong, stable, happy, and a light to the nations. His personal attention to Judah was a sign of His love and concern. He loved them enough not to leave them in their sin!

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGE, JUDGMENT, and JUSTICE (שפט) IN ISAIAH

NASB  "Both supply and support"
NKJV  "the stock and store"
NRSV  "support and staff"
TEV  "everything and everyone that the people
  depend on"
NJB  "of resources and provisions"
LXX  "the mighty man and the mighty woman"
Peshitta  "stay and staff"
REB, JPSOA  "every prop and stay"

The MT has MASCULINE and FEMININE forms which BDB 1044 defines as "support and staff" (cf. 2 Sam. 22:19). In Leviticus 26:26 it is "the staff of bread."
