READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 3:2 "diviner"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:2 "diviner" See SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

3:3
NASB  "skillful enchanter"
NKJV, NRSV, REB, JPSOA  "expert enchanter"
TEV  "everyone who uses magic to
  control events"
NJB  "soothsayer"
LXX  "intelligent hearer"
Peshitta  "expert enchanter"
NET  "skilled in magical arts"

The NOUN (BDB 538, KB 527) means "whispering" or "charming" (NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 794). It originally referred to snake charming (cf. Ps. 58:5; Eccl. 10:11; Jer. 8:17). It came to denote soft speaking (cf. Isa. 26:16; 2 Sam. 12:19; Ps. 41:7).

The same term is used in Isa. 3:20 for idolatrous amulets worn by Judean women. It refers to magical practices and charms, forbidden to Israel and Judah.

The JPSOA footnote suggests an emendation to "expert craftsman" (see NET Bible footnote, p. 1188, #6).

entries.title: Isaiah 3:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:4 Judah's elder leadership will be removed (by YHWH Himself) even to the highest levels. Ineffective and senseless young people will lead (cf. Eccl. 10:16).

NASB  "children"
NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA  "babes"
NJB  "lads"
LXX, Peshitta  "mockers"
NET  "malicious young men"

The difference is between the MT עלולים (BDB 760, "wantonness," cf. Deut. 22:14,17; Ps. 141:4, NET Bible) and an emendation to עוללים (BDB 760, "children," cf. Ps. 8:3), which seem to fit the context.

entries.title: Isaiah 3:5-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:5-6 The oppression and abuse are described.

  1. oppressed by one another
  2. oppressed by neighbors
  3. generational tensions
  4. societal tensions
  5. family tensions

entries.title: Isaiah 3:7-12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:7-12 The person the family chooses to lead will not accept the position because of the current crisis (Judah is wounded [1:6], only God can heal [30:26]) and the family's (i.e. Judah) rebellion against YHWH.

  1. their speech is against YHWH, Isa. 3:8
  2. their actions are against YHWH, Isa. 3:8
  3. they rebel against His glorious presence, Isa. 3:8
  4. their partiality shows on their faces, Isa. 3:9
  5. their sin is displayed like Sodom's, Isa. 3:9
  6. they have brought evil on themselves, Isa. 3:9
  7. they reap what they sow, Isa. 3:10-11
    1. the righteous
    2. the wicked
  8. they are oppressed by youthful leaders (cf. Isa. 3:4), Isa. 3:12
  9. they are ruled over by women, Isa. 3:12
  10. their leaders lead them astray, Isa. 3:12
  11. their paths (i.e. plans and goals) are confused, Isa. 3:12

These consequences of rebellion are a reflection of Deut. 28:15-68.

JPSOA puts Isa. 3:10 and 11 in a parenthesis.

3:8
NASB, NRSV  "His glorious presence"
NKJV  "the eyes of His glory"
TEV  "God himself"
NJB  "his glorious gaze"
LXX  "their glory"
Peshitta  "the majesty of his glory"
REB  "his glory"
JPSOA  "His majestic glance"
NET  "his royal authority"

The MT is followed closely by NKJV. The "eyes" represented God's personal presence.

The term "glory" (kabod, BDB 458) is common, but has a wide semantic flield.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE USED TO DESCRIBE GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod)

entries.title: Isaiah 3:9 "The expression of their faces bears witness against them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:9 "The expression of their faces bears witness against them" The Aramaic Targums have "their partiality in judgment (legal abuses and bribery) accuse them" (cf. Deut. 1:17; 16:19). This may be a play on the eyes of the Lord mentioned in Isa. 3:8 versus the look of sinful Judeans in Isa. 3:9.

▣ "They display their sin like Sodom" Again, as in Isa. 1:10, Isaiah compares the sins of Judean society to the sins of Sodom (cf. Genesis 19). These Judean leaders (and their families) were flaunting publicly their pride, wealth, and exploitation of the weak and powerless of society.

Sodom was arrogant (Ezek. 16:50) and YHWH destroyed them, so too, now Judah (Isa. 3:16) and they also will be destroyed (Isa. 3:16-26, the subject moves from prideful women to prideful Jerusalem).

▣ "brought evil on themselves" They reap what they sow (cf. Isa. 3:10-11). This is a spiritual principle. God is ethical/moral and so is His creation. Humans break themselves on God's standards. We reap what we sow. This is true for believers (but does not affect salvation) and unbelievers (cf. Job 34:11; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 12:14; 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:19; Ezek. 33:20; Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12).

entries.title: Isaiah 3:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:10-11 This is a contrasting proverb, like Psalm 1.

3:12
NASB, NKJV, NRSV  "Their oppressors are children,
  And women rule over them"
TEV  "moneylenders oppress my people and
  their creditors cheat them"
NJB  "the oppressors pillage them, and
  extortioners rule over them"
LXX  "exactors strip you, and extortioners
  rule over you"
Peshitta  "The princes shall pluck my people out,
  and women shall rule over them"
REB  "Money lenders strip my people bare,
  And usurers lord it over them"
JPSOA  "My people's rulers are babes,
  It is governed by women"

The MT has "my people, their oppressors, children and women rule over them." Obviously TEV, NJB, and REB follow the LXX (change "women," נשים, BDB 61 to "creditors"

  1. BDB 673 I, cf. Isa. 24:2, ACTIVE PARTICIPLE PLURAL of נשא, cf. Isa. 24:2
  2. BDB 674 I, ACTIVE PARTICIPLE PLURAL of נשה, cf. Exod. 22:25)

The UBS Text Project, p. 9, accepts this emendation but gives it a C rating (considerable doubt).

These phrases could be

  1. literal
    1. child king
    2. controlled by
      (1)  a strong "Queen mother"
      (2)  the child king's wives
      (3)  the women at court
  2. figurative of weak and inexperienced leadership
NASB, NRSV, JPSOA  "confuse"
NKJV  "destroy"
NJB  "efface"
LXX  "pervert"
Peshitta  "disturbed"
REB  "to ruin"

The VERB (BDB 118, KB 134, Piel PERFECT) means "engulf" or "swallow up" (cf. Exod. 15:12; Num. 16:30,32,34; 26:10; Deut. 11:6). In the Piel stem it also denotes "shallowing," but is used as imagery for destruction or something being confounded (cf. Isa. 9:16; 19:3; 28:7).

Hebrew scholars are still discussing the possibility of one, two, or three Hebrew roots/cognates using these same three letters (בלע).

entries.title: Isaiah 3:13 "Arises. . .stands"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:13 "Arises. . .stands" This visual image of YHWH arising from His throne can denote

  1. His readiness to act on behalf of His people
  2. His judicial act of pronouncing judgment. This is the context of v. 13
▣
NASB, NKJV, TEV, NJB, LXX, Peshitta, REB, NET  "people"
NRSV, JPSOA  "peoples"

The SINGULAR comes from the LXX followed by the Peshitta. The MT has the PLURAL. In this context the SINGULAR fits best because the prophet is addressing Judea (i.e. Isa. 3:14). In other contexts in Isaiah "the nations," "the peoples," is used. Context, context, context! The MT is not inerrant! Context must be the final guide!

entries.title: Isaiah 3:13-15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:13-15 YHWH enters into a dispute (i.e. court scene, cf. Isa. 1:2; Hosea 4:1; Micah 6:2) with His people's leaders (elders and princes). They have destroyed His community (i.e. "vineyard," Isa. 3:14). They have taken advantage of the poor, helpless, and powerless of society.

They used the legal system inappropriately (cf. Isa. 3:9) to their advantage, and must now stand before YHWH's judgment.

The prophets hold Israel/Judah accountable to the requirements of the Mosaic covenant, obedience had consequences and disobedience had consequences (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Isaiah 3:14 "elders and princes"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 3:14 "elders and princes" These two terms are synonymous (cf. Jdg. 8:14) and do not denote two separate leadership groups. For more information on these terms, see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 68-70.

entries.title: Isaiah 3:16-26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:16-26 YHWH condemns the wives and daughters of the wealthy, elite leadership.

  1. prideful walk ("head high" or "outstretched neck")
  2. seductive (i.e. painted eyes)
  3. flirtatious steps (i.e. quick, small steps, like a child)
  4. attractive, musical ankle jewelry

YHWH will (typical biblical reversal)

  1. afflict the scalp with scabs (only here, BDB 705, KB 764)
  2. strip away their jewelry
  3. strip away their festive clothes
  4. take away their cosmetics and perfumes
  5. kill their husbands and lovers

The Jewish Study Bible, using the JPSOA translation and footnotes, mentions that many of the items in Isa. 3:18-24 are uncertain. They may refer to specific items of beauty or idolatrous symbols. They were worn by men and women.

3:16
NASB, NJB  "tinkle the bangles"
NKJV, Peshitta  "making a jingling"
NRSV, JPSOA  "tinkling"
TEV  "bracelets on their ankles jingle"

The VERB (BDB 747, KB 824, Piel IMPERFECT) denotes the sound made by ankle bracelets as a person walks (i.e. to draw attention). The root is found only here and Prov. 7:22.

3:17
NASB, NJB, REB  "make their foreheads bare"
NKJV  "uncover their secret parts"
NRSV, Peshitta  "lay bare their secret parts"
TEV  "shave their heads and leave them bald"
LXX  "expose their form"

The MT uses a rare word (BDB 834) meaning

  1. sockets (for a door), 1 Kgs. 7:50
  2. secret parts (feminine reproductive organs), Isa. 3:17 (?)

There is an Akkadian root (KB 983) which means "forehead," which is also an option. These proud, well-dressed, wealthy exploiters will be humbled by having their veils removed in public!

The IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT) mentions that

  1. shaving half of ones' head was a public way to bring shame
  2. slaves had their heads completely shaved or a characteristic style that denoted their social standing

It also mentions that in line 1 of v. 17, the words which describe the head are uncertain and both may refer to baldness, particularly of the forehead.

entries.title: Isaiah 3:18 "in that day"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:18 "in that day" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

▣ "headbands" The IVP Biblical Background Commentary says these refer to "sun ornaments." So as the "crescent ornaments" reflect moon worship these represent sun worship.

▣ "crescent ornaments" This (BDB 962; NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 325, #5) was a symbol of moon worship.

  1. on the military camels, Jdg. 8:21
  2. on Midianite kings, Jdg. 8:26
  3. on wealthy Judean women, Isa. 3:18

Another example of their open idolatry!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP

entries.title: Isaiah 3:20 "perfume boxes"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 3:20 "perfume boxes" The term (BDB 108) translated "boxes" is literally "houses." In the Tyndale OT Commentaries, J. Alec Motyer thinks it may refer to a "high collar" (p. 58). There is so much that we moderns do not know about the details of ANE cultures that often our interpretations are educated guesses based on cognates and context. None of these details are crucial to an understanding of the larger context and theological issues. The vast majority are interesting, but not important to understanding the central truth of the strophe or paragraph. Do not focus on the minutia.

entries.title: Isaiah 3:24 "Instead of a belt, a rope"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:24 "Instead of a belt, a rope" This seems to refer to prisoners being tied together and marched into exile by Assyria.

NASB, NKJV  "And branding insteaad of beauty"
NRSV, TEV  "instead of beauty, shame"
NJB, REB  "brand marks instead of beauty"
Peshitta  "for their beauty shall be destroyed"
LXX     ---omitted---

The MT has "instead of beauty." The term "branding," from BDB 464 (burn, scorch, brand), is assumed. However, the word "shame" in NRSV and TEV is also not in the MT, but is found in the Isaiah scroll from the DSS (1QIsa.).

entries.title: Isaiah 3:26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
3:26 Jerusalem ("her," FEMININE, Isa. 3:25,26) is personified as weeping over the losses. Zion's festival clothing is restored in Isa. 61:3, also note Zech. 3:4 (only Isa. 3:22 and Zech. 3:4 share the same rare term for festival clothing).

▣ "she will sit on the ground" This was a physical symbol of mourning and grief.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES, #6

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 4:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:1 This verse seems to link with Isa. 3:6 (different VERBS, Isa. 3:6, BDB 1074 and Isa. 4:1, BDB 304, but both mean "to grasp firmly"). It surely links to the Messianic age (i.e. Isa. 4:2, "Branch", see SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE). Hebrew poetry is difficult to "lock down." It is often a play on words and similar actions.

▣ "seven women" Seven is the number for perfection in Jewish thought relating to Genesis 1. Therefore, this

  1. like Isa. 3:25-26, refers to all inhabitants of Jerusalem/Judah
  2. refers to Gentile nations coming to YHWH

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4

▣ "take hold" This VERB (BDB 304, KB 302, Hiphil PERFECT with waw) denotes someone taking a firm grip on another person or some object (i.e. Deut. 22:25; 25:11; 1 Sam. 15:27; 2 Sam. 1:11; 1 Kgs. 1:50; 2 Kgs. 2:12; 4:27; Prov. 7:13; 26:17; Zech. 8:23).

▣ "let us be called by your name" The name was a symbol of the person and his characteristics. The purpose of this action is revealed in the next phrase, "take away our reproach" (BDB 62, KB 74, Qal IMPERATIVE). Who can do this?

  1. the righteous of Isa. 3:10 can give guidance and knowledge about Israel's God
  2. the Messianic "Branch" of Isa. 4:2-6

SPECIAL TOPIC: " THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT)

▣ "take away our reproach" For the VERB (BDB 62, KB 74) see note above.

This NOUN, "reproach" or "shame" (BDB 357), may refer to

  1. a symbol of their sin and rebellion against YHWH
  2. their widowhood with no children because all the men were killed in battle, Isa. 3:25-26 (NASB Study Bible, p. 965, NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 75)

Isaiah 54:4 fits both options because "widowhood" could refer to being divorced (i.e. legal imagery) by YHWH.

The book of Revelation clearly contrasts two wives of YHWH.

  1. faithless Israel called the great harlot (cf. Rev. 17-18)
  2. the faithful redeemed church called the bride of Christ (cf. Rev. 21:1,9; 22:17)

YHWH divorces Israel (i.e. the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple by Rome in A.D. 70) and marries the Church. See my full Partial Preterist Commentary on Revelation online.

entries.title: Isaiah 4:1-4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:1-4 The JPSOA translation divides verses 1-6 into two poetic sections and one prose.

  1. Isa. 4:1b-3, poetry
  2. Isa. 4:4, poetry
  3. Isa. 4:5-6, prose

Most other versions take Isa. 4:1 with Isa. 3:16-4:1. They also do not structure these verses as poetry. The NKJV has Isa. 4:2 and NJB has Isa. 4:2-6 as one long poetic context (JB had poetic division at Isa. 4:2-3 and 4-6), but most of the others have prose. This should show us how difficult it is to know when a Hebrew text is elevated prose or poetry and also where the natural/subject breaks occur. Be careful of modern chapter and verse divisions! They are not an inspired guide!

entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
ISAIAH 4

PARAGRAPH DIVISIONS OF MODERN TRANSLATIONS

NASB NKJV NRSV TEV NJB
A Remnant Prepared The Renewal of Zion Jerusalem's Restoration Jerusalem Will Be Restored Yahweh's Seedling

(2) (2-6)
4:3-6

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 4:2 "In that day"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:2 "In that day" This refers to a future time when YHWH comes (for blessing or judgment) to His people (cf. Isa. 2:2,11,12,20; 3:7,18; 4:1,2). This is a recurrent theme in Isaiah. It is hard to be certain if this referred in Isaiah's mind to

  1. restoration from exile by Zerubabbel and Joshua in the Persian period (i.e. Ezra and Nehemiah)
  2. restoration by the Maccabees in the Seleucid period
  3. Jesus' first coming (inauguration of the New Covenant)
  4. Jesus' second coming (consummation of the New Covenant)

Notice how the Prophet swings from radical, complete judgment to radical complete forgiveness and restoration! This is typical in the prophetic literature. One could not be presented without the other! The purpose of judgment is always restoration. A helpful book for me to understand Hebrew prophecy has been D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DAY (yom)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

▣ "the Branch of the Lord" To describe this title (BDB 855, Targums interpreted it as the Messiah) let me quote from my commentary on Daniel and Zechariah where the term is also used (but just a note of caution, we must be careful about assigning a technical meaning everywhere a word or phrase is used-context, context, context is crucial). This term may have developed over time from a reference of ideal abundance to God's special Servant who will restore that abundance (i.e. a shoot, a branch).

Let me share notes from my commentary on Zechariah.

Zech. 3:8 "the Branch" This may be "sprout" (BDB 855). This is another Messianic title (cf. Isa. 6:12; Isa. 4:2; 11:1; 53:2; Jer. 23:5; 33:15). See full discussion and SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE.

This title is used of Zerubbabel in Isa. 6:12 as a symbol of the royal Davidic line. It is surprising that it is used in this context, which emphasizes the priestly aspect of the Messiah. The twin aspects of redeemer (priestly, cf. Isaiah 53) and administrative leader (kingly, cf. Isa. 9:6-7) are merged in the book of Zechariah (cf. chapter 4).

Zech. 6:12 "Branch" This word (BDB 855) means "sprout" (cf. Isa. 3:8; 6:12; Isa. 4:2; 11:1; 53:2; Jer. 23:5; 33:15). This is a title for the Messiah. In Zechariah it refers to Zerubbabel as a type of the Messiah (cf. Ibn Ezra and Rashi). The name, Zerubbabel, in Akkadian, means "shoot of Babylon." This was possibly a play on his name since he rebuilt the temple in 516 B.C., but it is really an ultimate reference to Jesus. This title and the matching VERB ("will branch out," Qal IMPERFECT) appear together in this verse.

▣ Verse 2 describes YHWH's "Branch" (NKJV, NRSV, JB)

  1. "beautiful," BDB 840, cf. Jer. 3:19 (often used of Promised Land in Dan. 8:9; 11:16,41)
  2. "glorious," BDB 458 means "abundance," "honor," and "glory"

These two terms are often used together (cf. Isa. 13:19; 28:1,4,5).

Some versions take this verse as a reference to plant growth in the period of restoration (LXX, Peshitta, TEV, NJB, REB, NET Bible). In a sense the Messiah and the age of restoration are lexically linked (first part of Isa. 4:2 is about the Messiah; the second part is about a restored, fruitful Promised Land).

▣ "the survivors of Israel" Isaiah addresses them and describes them often (cf. Isa. 10:20; 37:31,32; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES), but which group did he address? See opening comment on Isa. 4:2.

The Spirit is the true author of Scripture. In prophecy and apocalyptic passages often the human author did not fully realize the full extent of his own message. I do think this means that these passages had multiple meanings (i.e. Sensus Plenior), but that progressive revelation clarified the intended meaning. Often the concept of multiple fulfillment is what links the full intent of the Spirit's message (i.e. Isa. 7:14). However, proper hermeneutics must begin with "authorial intent" as the place to begin and evaluate an interpretation of any biblical text and any genre. Only further inspired revelation trumps original context and authorial intent.

entries.title: Isaiah 4:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:3 This verse is probably what caused the Jews of Jeremiah's day who were not exiled to view themselves as YHWH's favored people, but Ezekiel, chapters 8-10, shows this was not the case. YHWH would primarily deal with the returnees (cf. Ezra and Nehemiah).

▣ "Holy" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

▣ "everyone who is recorded for life in Jerusalem" There are two interpretive issues.

  1. Is this referring to life in Jerusalem the capital of Judah or "New Jerusalem," the symbol of the new age (cf. Revelation 21:1-22:5)? Is it historical or eschatological? See my new Partial Preterist Commentary on Revelation (2024) free online.
  2. Is this registration an aspect of the book of life?

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD

entries.title: Isaiah 4:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:4 This verse has two images for spiritual cleansing.

  1. washing
    1. wash away, BDB 934, KB 122, Qal PERFECT
    2. purged (lit. "rinsed away"), BDB 188, KB 216, Hiphil IMPERFECT (had sacrificial connotation, cf. 2 Chr. 4:6; Ezek. 40:38)
  2. fire
    1. by a spirit of judgment, cf. Isa. 28:6
    2. by a spirit of burning, cf. Isa. 1:31; 9:19

It is quite possible that "spirit" (ruah) should be understood as a violent, destructive wind of YHWH's judgment. Judah will be judged and cleansed of her willful rebellion.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BAPTISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

▣ "filth" This is a strong term (BDB 844) which is used of sin.

  1. Isaiah 28:8 of human vomit
  2. Isaiah 36:12 of human feces (cf. Deut. 23:14; Ezek. 4:12)

▣ "the daughters of Zion" This is the imagery used of Jerusalem in Isa. 3:16-26. In this context, it is parallel with "Jerusalem." See full note at Isa. 1:8.

▣ "bloodshed" This (BDB 196) is imagery for the premeditated taking of life. Here it probably refers to the exploitation of the poor and socially ostracized (i.e. "from her midst").

SPECIAL TOPIC: MURDER

entries.title: Isaiah 4:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:5 This is a historical allusion to YHWH's personal presence and care during the Exodus and Wilderness Wandering Periods. It refers to the Shekinah cloud of glory—cloud by day, fire by night—to guide and protect (i.e. Exod. 13:21,22; 40:38; Num. 9:15-23; Ps. 78:14; 99:7; 105:39). He (or His angel) would personally lead His people again and provide for all their needs in abundance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

▣ "the Lord will create" This VERB (BDB 135, KB 153, Qal PERFECT with waw) is used only of God's creating (cf. Gen. 1:1; and here).

▣ "canopy" The term (BDB 342 I) can refer to

  1. a protective covering like the Shekinah cloud (over the whole of the people, as during the Exodus and Wilderness Wanderings, cf. Ps. 105:39)
  2. a covering of YHWH's personal presence over the tabernacle, as in Exod. 40:34-38
  3. a covering tent for a wedding (cf. Ps. 19:5; Joel 2:16)

Some link this wedding imagery to the desperate women of Isa. 4:1, while other commentators link it to the tabernacle and a future restored temple in Jerusalem, which would denote the union of YHWH/Messiah and His people in marriage imagery (cf. Isa. 5:1; Hosea 1-3; Eph. 5:21-33).

entries.title: Isaiah 4:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
4:6 There are several images combined to show YHWH's protection (from heat and storm)

  1. shelter, BDB 697, cf. Isa. 1:8; Ps. 27:5; 31:20; same concept in Isa. 32:2
  2. refuge, BDB 340 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE)
    1. NOUN, Isa. 25:4
    2. VERB, Isa. 14:23; 57:13
    3. in Psalms, 14:6; 46:1; 61:4; 62:7,8; 71:7; 73:28; 91:2,9; 94:22; 142:5
  3. from other texts in Isaiah, a "defense," BDB 731, cf. Isa. 17:10; 27:5

Often these images refer to YHWH as

  1. a protective mother bird (i.e. under the shelter of its wings, see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW AS A METAPHOR FOR PROTECTION AND CARE)
  2. a high fortress or stronghold (cf. Ps. 18:1; see my exegetical notes online)

Believers can trust the protection and tender care of their covenant God! He is with us and for us, if we only repent, believe, obey, serve, worship, and persevere. The covenant has promises (benefits) and responsibilities (obligations). Both have consequences (i.e. Lev. 26; Deut. 28)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 5:1 "Let me sing"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:1 "Let me sing" This introductory VERB (BDB 1010, KB 1479, Qal COHORTATIVE) is also used in Isa. 26:1 and 42:10. The NOUN also appears in Isa. 5:1. Often songs were used to mark events (cf. Exod. 15:1; Num. 21:17; Jdg. 5:1; 1 Sam. 18:6).

Here the song is used to draw the attention of the passers-by, so that they would stop and listen. This implies it was sung in the market place.

▣ "well-beloved. . .beloved" These are two different Hebrew words. The first one (BDB 391) is usually used in poetry of a family member. The second one (BDB 187) is used often in Song of Songs for the lover. Here it refers to a special field for which the owner had special expectations. This would have resonated well with Judah's agricultural society.

▣ "vineyard" The grapevine (or vineyard) is often a symbol of national Israel (i.e., Exod. 15:17; Ps. 80:8; Jer. 2:21; 12:10) as were the olive tree and the dove. Judah was seen by the prophets as the only true "people of God." In John 15:1 Jesus says "I am the true vine," not faithless Israel. See full note online at John 15:1.

This parable about a vineyard is related to Jesus' parable of the wicked tenant farmers (Matt. 21:33-46; Mark 12:1-12; Luke 20:9-19). The fact it is repeated in all three Synoptic Gospels shows its importance.

The following parable in Matt. 22:1-22 continues the theme of Israel's rejection and Gentile inclusion (also note John 10:16). I have become a Partial Preterist. I hope you will look at my commentaries on the Olivet Discourse and the book of Revelation. I see YHWH divorcing faithless Israel and marrying the faithful believers in Jesus!

▣ "fertile hill" "Hill" is literally the word "horn" (BDB 901) used in the sense of an isolated hill positioned just right to receive the sunlight and sloped just right for the rain to drain. The perfect "hill," perfectly prepared to be planted with the "best" grapevines, for the best harvest!

The ADJECTIVE "fertile" is literally "son of oil" or "son of fat" (BDB 1032), which is Hebrew imagery for fertility and abundance (cf. Isa. 28:1,4).

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BACKGROUND STUDY

  1. It is difficult to know the historical context of this chapter. It may apply to any part of the preaching ministry of Isaiah. Moderns do not know how the prophetic books were complied. They are not chronological.

  2. Apparently this folk ballad was sung at some gathering of the nation of Judah. Whether it was in a temple or in the marketplace is uncertain.

  3. It is important to remember that privilege brings responsibility (i.e., "the Two Ways," cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30:15,19; Psalm 1; and note Luke 12:48).

  4. Allusions to the folk song are found in several places in the NT (cf. Matt. 21:33-46; Mark 12:1-2; Luke 20:9-19).

  5. It must be remembered that Judah, during most of Isaiah's prophetic ministry (i.e., the eighth century B.C.) was an extremely successful and prosperous nation. This prosperity brought spiritual weakness and a dependency upon human resources instead of on YHWH and His covenant promises and requirements.

BRIEF OUTLINE

  1. The Parabolic Song, Isa. 5:1-6
  2. The Ironical Interpretation, Isa. 5:7
  3. The Resultant Judgment of YHWH, Isa. 5:8-30
    1. series of woes, Isa. 5:8-23
    2. judgment, Isa. 5:24-30
      1. natural, Isa. 5:25
      2. invader, Isa. 5:26-30

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 5:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:2 There is a play on the VERB "do" (BDB 793, KB 889) in Isa. 5:2-5, used seven times. It is translated

  1. yield, Isa. 5:2 (twice)
  2. do, Isa. 5:4 (twice), what God will do for His vineyard
  3. yield, Isa. 5:4 (twice)
  4. do, Isa. 5:5, what God will do to His rebellious, ungrateful vineyard

▣ "He dug it all around, removed its stones" This first VERB (BDB 740, KB 810, Piel IMPERFECT with waw) is found only here in the OT. The KJV has "fenced." Although I do not believe this is an accurate translation of the Hebrew word, it does fit the context. When stones were dug out of a rocky field in Palestine, they were usually stacked into a fence. Often the vineyards were protected by a ditch (also possible meaning of first VERB, REB) with a stone hedge (LXX, Vulgate). It is surely possible that Isaiah is describing terracing techniques. The stones would be used to level parts of the field.

It is also possible that the stones were put in piles and used to keep the grape clusters off the ground (James Freeman, Manners and Customs of the Bible, pp. 360-363).

▣ "the choicest vine" This refers to the bright red grapes known as "sorek" (BDB 977 I, cf. Jer. 2:21). These grapes got their name from a valley in Palestine (cf. Jdg. 16:4). They are mentioned in Jer. 2:21 as being the most expensive and sought after variety of grapes. See UBS Fauna and Flora of the Bible, p. 190.

This grapevine species is even mentioned in a Messianic passage (cf. Gen. 49:11).

▣ "tower" This (BDB 153, "watchtower" built from stones dug out of the field) was for security purposes and was usually occupied only during the planting time and the harvest time in September (it would serve the same purpose as the word "booth" mentioned in Isa. 1:8). This same word can refer to a military tower (cf. Isa. 2:15). Context, context, context!

▣ "hewed out a wine vat" This would have been a shallow man-made depression in a rock surface which allowed the women to crush the grapes with their feet and then a channel in the rock to a deeper depression where the juice would be stored.

▣ "Then He expected it to produce good grapes" YHWH did everything possible (i.e. Rom. 9:4-5) to assure that His covenant people reflected His character to the nations, but they did not (i.e. Ezek. 36:22-32). YHWH wanted all humans made in His image and likeness (i.e. Gen. 1:26-27) to know Him.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

NASB  "worthless one"
NKJV, NRSV, NJB, REB, JPSOA, Peshitta  "wild grapes"
TEV, JB  "every grape was sour"
LXX  "thorns"

The Hebrew term (BDB 93) can refer to

  1. stinking or noxious weeds, SINGULAR, cf. Job 31:40
  2. stinking things, worthless things, PLURAL

The basic root refers to the stink of

  1. corpses, Isa. 34:3 (cf. Isa. 5:25); Joel 2:20; Amos 4:10
  2. locusts, Joel 2:20 (imagery for a dead army)

The MT in this context refers to "wild grapes," which were not sweet and plump, but small and sour, unfit to make wine.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:3 The prophet is bringing his audience into a decision-making process. This is the point of the genre of parable (see SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERPRETING PARABLES). They will judge themselves!

The VERB "judge" (BDB 1047, KB 1622) is a Qal IMPERATIVE and is similar to Matt. 21:40, which is Jesus' strongest condemnation of faithless Israel!

entries.title: Isaiah 5:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 5:4 This question is the heart of the love song. YHWH did everything for His people, but they rejected Him (cf. Matt. 21:33-45; 22:14).

entries.title: Isaiah 5:5-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:5-6 The prophet, speaking for YHWH, declares (BDB 393, KB 390, Hiphil COHORTATIVE) what He will do to His disappointing vineyard (i.e. His covenant people).

  1. remove its hedge, consequently it will be consumed by animals
  2. break down it's protective wall, consequently the vines will be trampled to the ground
  3. refuse to tend it, consequently the briars and thorns will come up (cf. Isa. 7:23,25; 9:18; 27:4)
  4. refuse to send rain, consequently it will dry up and die (cf. Deut. 28:23-24)

entries.title: Isaiah 5:6 "I will lay it waste"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:6 "I will lay it waste" The VERB (BDB 1011, KB 1483) is a Qal IMPERFECT. YHWH will make His vineyard a "waste" (BDB 144). The term is found only here. It can mean "end" or "destruction." The judgment of YHWH is total and final (cf. Isa. 5:30)! Thank God for chapters 7-12! There will be a new day (chapters 40-55) and a new heaven and earth (chapters 56-66, cf. Rev. 21-22).

▣ "I will also charge the clouds to rain no rain on it" Nature has been, and continues to be, affected by mankind's sin (cf. Gen. 3:17-19 and Rom. 8:19-26). It is used by God for blessing or judgment (i.e., Lev. 26:4; Deut. 11:14; 28:12; Amos 4:7; Zech. 14:17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

entries.title: Isaiah 5:7 "the Lord of hosts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:7 "the Lord of hosts" See SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord of Hosts

▣ "the house of Israel" This term normally seems to refer to all of Israel collectively before the political split in 922 B.C., although in this verse the term refers to Judah (line 2). At this time in the history of the people of God, their nation was split into the northern ten tribes known as Israel, Ephraim, or Samaria and the southern three tribes known as Judah, which included Judah, Benjamin, Simeon, and most of the Levites/priests.

▣ "justice. . .bloodshed. . .righteousness. . .a cry of distress" This is a play on two different sounds in Hebrew that cannot be reproduced in an English translation:

  1. םשפט Mishpat (justice, BDB 1048) vs. משׁפח Mispach (bloodshed, BDB 705)
  2. צדק Zedakah (righteousness, BDB 842) vs. צעק Zeakah (cry of distress, BDB 858)

Another biblical reversal of expectations.

5:8
NASB, NKJV, NJB, REB, Pehsitta  "Woe"
NRSV, JPSOA, LXX  "Ah"
TEV  "You are doomed"

There is some debate among commentators as to whether there are six or seven "woes" (BDB 222) listed. This is not literally the Hebrew term "woe" (BDB 17, which denotes a lament, cf. Isa. 3:9,11; 6:5; 24:16). This translation suggestion from BDB is "ah," "alas," or "ha" (cf. Isa. 1:4; 10:1,5; 17:12; 28:1). It expresses painful dissatisfaction with the current situation or consequences.

They begin the consequences of judgment on Judah because of their straying from YHWH's covenant. They are basically a listing of the sins of the Judean society.

▣ "to those who add house to house and join field to field" This refers to the greedy land owners who exploited the poor by taking their ancestral lands (i.e., the land division by Joshua, cf. Joshua 13-19) to accumulate more and more land for themselves (cf. Jer. 22:13-17; Micah 2:2). The law of Moses protected the allotted lands by enacting "the Year of Jubliee" (cf. Lev. 25:8-55; Num. 36:4). All land must return to the original tribal family owners every fiftieth year. Although there is no record in the OT of Israel ever honoring this release, it was still the expressed will of God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, II. C.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:9 The opening of Isa. 5:9 is very emphatic, with no VERB, literally "in my ears, the Lord of hosts." This is a clear claim of verbal divine revelation (cf. Isa. 22:14)! This is not Isaiah's message, nor Isaiah's emotion! YHWH is shouting through His prophet to His wayward people.

This judgment is similar to Amos 5:11 and Micah 6:15. The expectations of the rich and exploitive elements of society will not materialize. They will not enjoy their ill-gotten gain! We reap what we sow (see note at Isa. 3:10-11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

entries.title: Isaiah 5:10 "For ten acres of vineyard"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:10 "For ten acres of vineyard" "Acres" is literally "a couple" or "a pair" (BDB 855, cf. 1 Sam. 14:14), which denoted animals yoked together for agricultural purposes. One "yoke" was the amount of land an oxen could plow in one day.

▣ "will yield only one bath of wine" The term "bath" (BDB 144 II) is a liquid measurement in Hebrew and it is equal to eight to ten gallons (see SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES (Metrology). In this context it is imagery for the fruitlessness of the usurped land.

▣ "And a homer of seed will yield but an ephah of grain" Again this is striking imagery for the fruitlessness of the usurped land. We learn from Ezek. 45:11 that there were ten ephahs in one homer; therefore, this is stating that if a farmer plants one hundred pounds, he will only harvest ten.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:11 "Woe to those who rise early in the morning that they may pursue strong drink"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:11 "Woe to those who rise early in the morning that they may pursue strong drink" The next sin mentioned is one of riotous pleasure-seeking from morning to evening. It needs to be stressed that the Bible does not condemn wine, but it does condemn the abuse of wine. This same imagery of strong drink is used in Isaiah 28. Other poignant passages on this subject are found in Prov. 20:1 and 23:29-35. However, one must add the balance of Ps. 104:14-15; Eccl. 9:7.

"Strong drink" (BDB 1016) is a Hebrew term describing the addition of intoxicating grain liquors to wine.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOLISM

entries.title: Isaiah 5:12 "Their banquets are accompanied by"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:12 "Their banquets are accompanied by" This is a way of speaking of the cultural entertainment of the day. It depicts a wealthy class given to worldly pleasures.

▣ "But they do not pay attention to the deeds of the Lord,
  Nor do they consider the work of His hands" YHWH's covenant people's refusal to hear and understand His will is a recurrent theme (cf. Isa. 1:2-3,10a; 5:12,13,24; 6:9-10; 30:9). YHWH had given them spiritual ears and eyes (cf. Deut. 29:4), but their collective blindness and deafness had caused YHWH to remove the possibility of comprehension (cf. Isa. 6:9-10; 29:9-10).

The tragedy of these verses is that the Judeans of Isaiah's day were depending on their own resources and schemes instead of the provision of their Covenant God. One should compare Isa. 5:24d,e with Deut. 8:11-20.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:13 "Therefore My people go into exile for their lack of knowledge"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:13 "Therefore My people go into exile for their lack of knowledge" This is obviously a prediction of exile. There has been some speculation about whether it refers to the Assyrian exiles (722 B.C.) of the northern ten tribes or the Babylonian exiles of Judah (i.e., 605, 597, 586, 582 B.C.) of the southern three tribes (plus most Levites). The immediate context seems to lend itself to either (this is so common in Isaiah, maybe purposeful). Assyria is mentioned specifically in Isa. 7:18 and 10:5ff. I think that Isa. 13:1-14:27 also refers to Assyria who destroyed the city of Babylon and Assyria's king took the title, "King of Babylon."

The mention of an exile out of the Promised Land was shocking. Canaan was promised to Abraham's seed (i.e. Genesis 12; 15). Now the covenant with the Patriarchs was being rescinded because of Judah's disobedience to the covenant requirements (i.e. a conditional covenant). They rejoiced in and clung to the promises, but ignored the requirements (cf. Jeremiah 7).

In a theological sense this parallels Genesis 2 (God's ideal fellowship with mankind) and Genesis 3 (Adam and Eve's open-eyed rebellion). Mankind was driven out of the Garden of Eden (cf. Gen. 3:24). This was unexpected and shocking! So too, the revelation of an exile. What was thought to be a permanent promise by God was affected by human sin. In a similar way "the New Covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34 was a shocking revelation. The everlasting covenants were being superceded because of human inability to perform their part of the covenant. Therefore, a new relationship with God would need to be established based on

  1. God's performance (new heart, new mind, cf. Ezek. 36:22-36)
  2. mankind's enabling by God's Spirit to be obedient

God still wants a righteous people to reflect His character to a lost and needy world (i.e., the nations). The means of that "righteousness" have changed. Human ability proved to be inadequate (cf. Galatians 3). The OT was a means of showing mankind's inability!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

SPECIAL TOPIC: EDEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

▣ "for their lack of knowledge" This is a willful rejection of knowledge, not ignorance (cf. Isa. 1:3; Hosea 4:6,14). Judah rebelled against the revealed will of YHWH (i.e., the Mosaic Covenant). She left the clearly marked path!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

entries.title: Isaiah 5:13-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:13-17 Here is a list of what will happen to Judah's wealthy, exploitive citizens.

  1. exiled, Isa. 5:13
  2. famished, Isa. 5:13
  3. parched, Isa. 5:13
  4. swallowed by Sheol, Isa. 5:14
  5. humbled, Isa. 5:15
  6. abused, Isa. 5:15 (twice)
  7. strangers eat of the fat of the wealthy, Isa. 5:17

entries.title: Isaiah 5:14 "Sheol has enlarged its throat and opened its mouth without measure"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:14 "Sheol has enlarged its throat and opened its mouth without measure" "Sheol" is a Hebrew term (BDB 982) which refers to"the realm of the dead." Here it is personified as an animal with a ravenous appetite (cf. Prov. 1:12; 27:20; Hab. 2:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, I. B.

▣ "And Jerusalem's splendor, her multitude, her din of revelry, and the jubilant within her, descent into it" This shows a total reversal of expectations!

entries.title: Isaiah 5:15 "So the common man will be humbled, and the man of importance abased"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:15 "So the common man will be humbled, and the man of importance abased" This is referring to judgment on an entire society (cf. Isa. 2:9,12,17). There seems to be a theological contrast between the Hebrew terms for "man," "adam" (BDB 9, NASB, "common man") and "Ish" (BDB 35, NASB, "man of importance"). This same distinction can be seen in Isa. 2:9; 31:8.

▣ "The eyes of the proud will also be abased" This is a recurrent theme throughout Scripture and is repeated in a slightly different way in Isa. 5:20 and 21 through the imagery of light and darkness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIFTED UP

entries.title: Isaiah 5:16 "But the Lord of hosts will be exalted in judgment"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:16 "But the Lord of hosts will be exalted in judgment" The descendants of Abraham were chosen to reveal YHWH. They were to reveal Him in their faithfulness resulting in a stable and abundant society or they will reveal Him in their waywardness resulting in His judgment.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness" This line of poetry is in a synonymous parallel relationship to the previous line of poetry. Hebrew poetry must be interpreted in light of its paralellism!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY, III.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:17 "Then the lambs will graze as in their pasture,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:17 "Then the lambs will graze as in their pasture,

 And strangers will eat in the waste places of the wealthy" There has been much discussion among commentators about the exact relationship of this verse to the preceding context. Some say

  1. it refers to God's care for those remaining in the land
  2. it refers to God's judgment of the wealthy landowners
  3. it refers to the remaining Jewish remnant after the exile
  4. it refers to Gentiles resettled in Judah's territory after the exile of her citizens

It seems to me that the immediate context of judgment must relate it to the destruction and judgment of the wealthy and the ruin of their illegally procured land. It is public land now!

The JPSOA footnote suggests an emendation based on Ezek. 34:17-22, where a distinction is made between:

  1. lambs vs. rams/male goats
  2. lean sheep vs. fat sheep

This would continue Isaiah 5's condemnation of the rich and powerful exploiters of His faithful poor and powerless followers.

The UBS Text Project, pp. 12-13, gives three ways to interpret these lines of poetry. If this is a crucial issue for you, see that detailed textual study.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

entries.title: Isaiah 5:18 "Woe"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:18 "Woe" See note at 1:8.

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, JPSOA  "as if with cart ropes"
Peshitta  "a bridle on the neck of a heifer"
LXX  "as with a strap from a
  heifer's yoke"
REB  "a heifer's rope"

The MT has "of the cart" (BDB 722), but the word for "heifer" is spelled exactly the same but with different vowel points.

  1. העגלה ‒ the cart
  2. העגלה ‒ the heifer

The UBS Text Project, p. 13, gives "of the cart" a "B" rating (some doubt). Both fit the poetic parallelism.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:18-19 "Woe to those who drag iniquity with the cords of falsehood,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:18-19 "Woe to those who drag iniquity with the cords of falsehood,

 And sin as if with cart ropes" The Hebrew is uncertain. This seems to refer to a group of people whom I have designated as practical atheists. They admit YHWH's existence theologically, but refuse to walk in this knowledge. They choose to live as if there were no God and even taunt His existence (cf. Isa. 5:19). They hold on to their sin at any cost! They are tied/bound to their self-centered lifestyles!

entries.title: Isaiah 5:18-23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:18-23 Another strophe of "woes" on the wicked is enumerated because

  1. Isa. 5:18, they lead evil around like an animal on a leash
  2. Isa. 5:19, they demand YHWH to quickly fulfill His covenant promises (without regard for the covenant requirements)
  3. Isa. 5:20, this may be related to Isa. 5:19. When God does not act the way they wanted, they called His acts evil, dark, and bitter
  4. Isa. 5:21, they assume their own wisdom to be true and God's false (Isa. 5:19-20)
  5. Isa. 5:22, they are drunkards
  6. Isa. 5:23, they use bribery to achieve their ends

These are manipulative religious egotists!

entries.title: Isaiah 5:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:19 There are several commands in this verse.

  1. let Him make speed, BDB 554, KB 553, Piel IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  2. let Him hasten, BDB 301, KB 300, Hiphil COHORTATIVE
  3. let the purpose of the Holy One of Israel draw near, BDB 897, KB 1132, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  4. come to pass, BDB 97, KB 112, Qal COHORTATIVE
  5. that we may know it, BDB 393, KB 390, Qal COHORTATIVE

To whom does verse 19 refer?

  1. It relates to those wealthy faithless Judeans who do not pay attention to YHWH's revelation (cf. 5:12).
  2. It relates to faithful Israelites who want YHWH to act quickly on their behalf (The Jewish Study Bible, p. 794).

The context of v. 18 favors option #1.

The NASB Study Bible makes an interesting comment about #1 and #2 above.

"The Hebrew for the words 'make speed' and 'hasten' correspond to that of the first and third elements of the name 'Maher-shalal-hash-baz' (meaning 'swift is the booty, speedy is the prey,' see Isa. 8:1,3), he may have been responding to the sarcastic taunts of sinners" (p. 967).

▣ "the Holy One of Israel" "The Holy One of Israel" is a title for Deity so common in Isaiah; see note at Isa. 1:4; and SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE)

entries.title: Isaiah 5:20 "Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:20 "Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil" Many scholars say that this refers to the judges of Israel. Although that fits Isa. 5:18-23, it seems to me that this is a reference to the society as a whole, not limited to a group of judges. This is a poignant example of the tragedy of what happens when our light becomes darkness (cf. Matt. 6:22-23). The fall of Genesis 3 has affected the moral compass of the creatures made in the image and likeness (cf. Gen. 1:26-27) of the God of Justice, Righteousness, and Fairness!

This is the essence of the NT's "unpardonable sin."

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALLOF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE UNPARDONABLE SIN

entries.title: Isaiah 5:21 "Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:21 "Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes,

 And clever in their own sight" This again refers to the sin of prideful arrogance (i.e. results of Genesis 3). Probably one of the most classical passages of this is Jer. 9:23-24 (also note Prov. 3:7; 1 Cor. 3:18-20). Real wisdom is in knowing and trusting YHWH! Humans are smoke-blinded by self, sin, and their own importance (cf. Prov. 26:5,12,16; 28:11).

entries.title: Isaiah 5:22 "Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:22 "Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine" Isaiah is using sarcasm because the term "heroes" normally refers to "mighty men of war," but in this context it refers to "drinking bouts" and not military exploits.

For "woe" see note at 1:8.

▣ "mixing strong drink" There has been some question as to what this (BDB 1016) refers.

  1. mixing wine with water, Isa. 1:22, like the Greeks and Romans, but the Isaiah texts refer to bad wine, not normal drinking wine
  2. old strong wine mixed with new wine
  3. wine mixed with other distilled fruit or honey liquors, which made it more intoxicating (they did not have fermented drinks with high alcohol content, as are available today)

This is the NOUN form of the VERB "to become drunk." Drunkenness is condemned often in Scripture (cf. Isa. 5:11,22; 28:7; 56:12; Prov. 20:1; 23:29-35; Micah 2:11). It is even used as imagery for the judgment of YHWH (cf. Ps. 75:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOLISM

entries.title: Isaiah 5:23 "Who justify the wicked for a bribe"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:23 "Who justify the wicked for a bribe" This is the place in the strophe where commentators discuss the absence of a seventh woe. The interpretive question is whether there are seven woes (the perfect number) or six woes (the number of human imperfection).

Bribery was regularly condemned in Isa. 1:23; 10:1-2 (cf. Exod. 23:8; Deut. 10:17; 16:19; Prov. 17:23; Micah 3:11; 7:3).

▣ "the rights" This term (BDB 842) is a form of "righteousness." This is a crucial theological term. YHWH chose it to describe His own character (i.e. Isa. 5:16) and fallen mankind's diviation from that standard. See the important Special Topic below.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

entries.title: Isaiah 5:24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:24 Fire is imagery for judgment and cleansing (i.e., chaff and stubble burn quickly and completely thereby not useful for cooking or heating, cf. Isa. 33:11; 47:14; Joel 2:5; Matt. 4:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

▣ "So their root will become like rot and their blossom blow away as dust" This is Hebrew agricultural imagery for total destruction.

▣ "For they have rejected the law of the Lord of hosts,
   And despised the word of the Holy One of Israel" This is the reason for judgment. It was the willful, purposeful rejection of the Judean people of their covenant God (esp. Isa. 5:19). Notice the two titles for Deity.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

entries.title: Isaiah 5:25 "On this account the anger of the Lord has burned against His people"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:25 "On this account the anger of the Lord has burned against His people" Judgment will begin with the household of God. God's anger is as biblical a theme as is His love! The anger is even accentuated in the presence of great light (cf. Luke 12:48).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

▣ "And the mountains quaked" Many have assumed that this refers to the violent earthquake recorded in the days of Uzziah (cf. Amos 1:1; Zech. 14:5). However, it may well be hyperbole of a Theophany. Nature quakes at the coming of her Creator. This imagery is common in the OT (i.e., Isa. 64:3; Exod. 19:18; Jer. 4:24; Joel 2:10; Nah. 1:5).

▣ "their corpses lay like refuse in the middle of the streets" OT people were shocked by unburied bodies, rotting, exposed, or eaten by animals (i.e., Ezek. 39:4,17-20; Nahum 3:3). A proper burial affected one's joy in the afterlife. It was a curse and horror to be unburied (cf. 1 Sam. 31:8-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BURIAL PRACTICES

▣ "His hand" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

entries.title: Isaiah 5:26 "He will also lift up a standard to the distant nation"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:26 "He will also lift up a standard to the distant nation" A "standard" or battle flag (BDB 651) was a way for armies to communicate (cf. Isa. 11:12; 18:3; 30:17; 31:9; 49:22). It can be positive (restoration) or negative (invasion) depending on the context. In this context it signals the invaders to come!

This is an extremely significant passage for the following reasons:

  1. notice that YHWH is in control of history, all history, as well as nature
  2. notice that YHWH lifts up a standard to the Gentile nations. Many have seen this verse as an allusion to Deut. 28:49-57.

Within the book of Isaiah it seems to be a reference to the inclusion of the Gentiles (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 11:9,10,11; 27:13; 49:22; 56:7; 62:10; 66:19; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)!

The term "nations" in the Masoretic text is PLURAL (LXX, Peshitta), goyim. Most modern translations change it to SINGULAR, however, the PLURAL possibly refers to an invading mercenary army made up of many nations. Assyria and Babylon conscripted the soldiers of defeated armies into their ranks. The UBS Text Project, p. 13, gives the PLURAL a "B" rating (some doubt).

▣ "will whistle for it" This is imagery for YHWH calling Gentile nations into conflict with His own sinful people (cf. Isa. 7:18).

The same root (BDB 1056) also means "hiss" (BDB 1056, KB 1656, Qal PERFECT with waw) as a sign of disgust, amazement, or derision. Here, it denotes a signal for the nations to invade (cf. Isa. 7:18). This same imagery is positive in Zech. 10:8.

▣ "from the ends of the earth" This is a hyperbolic phrase. It denotes a nation out of the local sphere of regular trade and politics. It reflects the covenant curse of Deut. 28:49.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:27-30
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:27-30 This strophe describes the invincible invading army. They are not tired or weary. They do not stumble because YHWH is with them! The shock of this description is that it follows the very terms used to describe faithful Israel in Isa. 40:29-31. YHWH is against His own covenant people! He will fight on behalf of the invading pagan enemy (cf. Habakkuk 1-2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SECOND COMING, IV.

entries.title: Isaiah 5:28 "bows are bent"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:28 "bows are bent" The Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE basically means "to march" or "to tread upon." Here, it is used figuratively of how ancient archers fixed their bows for action by stepping on them to get the string to cause the wooden shaft to bow (cf. Ps. 7:12; 11:2; Isa. 21:15; Jer. 9:3; 46:9; 50:14). See Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, p. 244.

▣ "like a whirlwind" The term (BDB 693) describes a destructive storm.

  1. literally, Isa. 17:13; 21:1; Job 21:18; 37:9; Ps. 83:15
  2. imagery, Isa. 29:6; Jer. 4:12-13
    1. of YHWH's chariot, Isa. 66:15; Jer. 4:13
    2. the invaders YHWH sends, Isa. 5:28

entries.title: Isaiah 5:29 "no one to deliver it"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 5:29 "no one to deliver it" This PARTICIPLE (BDB 664, KB 717, Hiphil PARTICIPLE ) means "to snatch away" or "deliver" (cf. Isa. 42:22; 43:13; 47:14; Hosea 5:14; Micah 5:8). YHWH's actions are sure. No one or no thing can thwart His will (i.e., judgment or salvation).

entries.title: Isaiah 5:30b,c
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:30b,c The land of the light of YHWH has become the land of darkness and gloom. The pagan army revels over its divinely appointed victory! What a reversal of expectations!!!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIGHT

SPECIAL TOPIC: DARKNESS

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why did Isaiah choose this method (folk song) of presenting truth?
  2. What is the difference between active, temporal judgment and passive temporal judgment? (cf. Romans 1:24, 28)
  3. What is the central truth of this parable song? How does it apply to our day?
  4. List the sins alluded to in Isa. 5:8-23.
  5. What nation does Isa. 5:26ff refer to and why?

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 6:1 "King Uzziah's"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:1 "King Uzziah's" Uzziah (792-740 B.C.; there is no scholarly consensus on the dates of his co-reign or reign) was one of the godly kings of Judah (cf. 2 Kgs. 15:3; 2 Chr. 26:4-5). It is possible that Isaiah and Uzziah were related ("iah," an abbreviation for YHWH, may have been a royal ending to names). Uzziah offered incense (which only Levitical priests could do) and was struck by God with leprosy (cf. 2 Kgs. 15:5; 2 Chr. 26:16-23).

Uzziah is called Azariah in 2 Kings 15 and Uzziah in 2 Chr. 26. Uzziah ("my strength is YHWH") was a throne name or we learn from 2 Chr. 26:17 that the High Priest was also named Azariah, so to avoid confusion 2 Chr. uses Uzziah. It was a dark day for Isaiah and Judah when he died in 740 B.C. Judah had become stable under his reign.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED KINGDOM

▣ "I saw the Lord" It was a common belief that to see God (here, Adon, BDB 10) meant death (cf. Gen. 16:13; Exod. 33:20; 1 Kgs. 19:13; Isa. 6:5; John 1:18; 6:46; 1 Tim. 6:16). This was a very traumatic moment! Apparently, Isaiah saw God's throne and dress, but not His face (cf. John 12:41).

There are some OT texts that imply God can be seen.

  1. Moses, Exod. 33:11; Num. 12:8; Deut. 34:10
  2. Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the seventy elders, Exod. 24:10-11

The question has to do with the consequences of a sinful person in the presence of a holy God. It is a question of intimate personal fellowship. Apparently sight is not the key, but a relationship initiated by God!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?

▣ "the Lord" This is translated from the Hebrew word adonai (BDB 10). Some ancient Hebrew manuscripts have "YHWH."

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "throne" YHWH depicted as sitting on a throne is first found in the vision of the heavenly court of 1 Kgs. 22:19; Ps. 103:19; and later in Isa. 66:1. In Ezekiel 1 and 10 YHWH's throne is His portable throne chariot (i.e. going away from the temple in Jerusalem).

This is ANE anthropomorphic language (cf. Isa. 6:5; Rev. 4:2,3; 20:11, see G. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible, pp. 172-182). Remember, YHWH is an eternal spiritual being who does not have a physical body.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL

▣ "train of His robe" Kingly robes were of very long length. Isaiah saw God as the people of his day expected Him to be. He was in the heavenly Temple (cf. Heb. 9:11,24; Revelation 5-6).

Many commentators have seen this long flowing robe as a way to hide the features of God's face (as is the smoke of Isa. 6:4). It functioned as a covering, something like the Shekinah Cloud of Glory during the Wilderness Wandering Period.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. There has always been a question about why Isaiah's call to ministry occurs in chapter 6 and not chapter 1.
    1. The OT books are arranged in ways that moderns, especially westerners, do not understand. Often they are not chronological, which surprises modern western interpreters. They are thematic, but in word plays or parallelisms on a strophe level.
    2. It is surely possible that Isa. 1-5 is a general introduction to the content of the entire book. Many, if not all, of the major themes are introduced.
      1. the covenant people's sin
      2. the consequences of disobedience
      3. restoration through the special Coming One
      4. a new day of righteousness
      5. the universal reign of God in an idealistic setting (Eden restored)

  2. The Jewish Study Bible (p. 796) makes an interesting comment about the placement of chapter 6. The footnotes assert that chapter 6 is not the beginning of Isaiah's ministry, but a new assignment. In chapters 1-5 the prophet calls on Judah to repent, but after the revelation of Isa. 6:9-10, never again in all the prophecy (chapters 7-66) does he call on them to repent. Judgment is sure and unavoidable. There is hope in a new day, but it is a future hope only.

  3. As chapter 6 reveals the terrible and complete judgment of YHWH on the disobedient covenant people, Isa. 12 reveals the new day of hope and restoration. Even the missionary mandate is renewed (cf. Isa. 12:4-5). This theological tension is characteristic of the prophet's message. They enforce the Mosaic covenant's
    1. consequences for disobedience and
    2. promises for obedience

BRIEF OUTLINE

  1. Isaiah saw God as He is. Isa. 6:1-4

  2. Isaiah saw himself as he was. Isa. 6:5

  3. Isaiah saw his society for what it was. Isa. 6:5

  4. Isaiah was cleansed to serve. Isa. 6:6-7

  5. Isaiah was ready to go. Isa. 6:9-13

WORD PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 6:2 "Seraphim"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:2 "Seraphim" A type of throne angel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SERAPHIM

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS IN THE BIBLE

▣ "six wings" It is interesting what their wings are used for.

  1. to cover the eyes. God's glory is overwhelming even to throne angels.
  2. to cover the feet. Be careful of turning the details of a Theophany into literal objects or creatures. Often feet are euphemistic of the genitalia (cf. Isa. 7:20; Exod. 4:25; Jdg. 3:24; Ruth 3:4,7,8,14; 1 Sam. 24:3), but here, because of Matt. 22:30, probably not. Both #1 and #2 may be a sign of humility in the presence of holiness (cf. Exod. 3:5).
  3. imagery for doing YHWH's bidding quickly (cf. Isa. 6:6)

entries.title: Isaiah 6:3 "Holy, Holy, Holy"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:3 "Holy, Holy, Holy" Holiness is a central theme in Isaiah.

  1. דקושׁ, ADJECTIVE, BDB 872, "holy," "sacred"
    1. holiness of
      (1) God, Isa. 5:16; 6:3 (thrice)
      (2) His name, Isa. 40:25; 49:7; 57:15
      (3) His abode, Isa. 57:15
      (4) His Sabbath, Isa. 58:13
  2. קדשׁ, VERB, BDB 872, "to be set apart," "consecrated"
    1.  God's character, Isa. 5:16; 29:23
    2.  God, Isa. 8:13; 65:5
    3.  God's angels, Isa. 13:3
    4.  God's name, Isa. 29:23
    5.  festival, Isa. 30:29
    6.  consecrated humans, Isa. 66:17
  3.  קדשׁ, NOUN, BDB 871, "apartness," "sacredness"
    1.  holy seed, Isa. 6:13
    2.  holy mountain, Isa. 11:9; 27:13; 56:7; 57:13; 65:11,25; 66:20
    3.  set apart, Isa. 23:18
    4.  way of holiness, Isa. 35:8
    5.  sanctuary, Isa. 43:28; 62:9; 64:11
    6.  holy city, Isa. 48:2; 52:1
    7.  holy One, Isa. 49:7
    8.  holy arm, Isa. 52:10
    9.  Holy day, Isa. 58:13
    10.  holy people, Isa. 62:12
    11.  Holy Spirit, Isa. 63:10,11
    12.  God's throne, Isa. 63:15
    13.  holy place, Isa. 63:18 
    14.  holy cities, Isa. 64:10

The threefold repetition denotes a Hebrew SUPERLATIVE (cf. Jer. 7:4; Ezek. 21:27 ; see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW GRAMMAR).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

▣ "Lord of hosts" See SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS.

▣ "the whole earth" This is the implication of monotheism (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM. YHWH has always been the God of all humanity (cf. Gen. 1:26,27; 3:15; 12:3; Exod. 19:5,6; Num. 14:21; Ps. 2:8; 22:27-28; 59:13; 72:8,19; Isa. 45:21-22; 49:6; 52:10; Micah 5:4). Isaiah's theology is universal (i.e. Isa. 12:5; 24:14-16; 42:10-12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE END-TIME EVENTS SO CONTROVERSIAL?

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 6:4 "of him who called out"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:4 "of him who called out" This can refer to the voice of God (cf. Isa. 6:8) or, in context, the Seraphim (i.e. "Holy, Holy, Holy," of Isa. 6:3).

▣ "was filling with smoke" The VERB (BDB 569, KB 583, Niphal IMPERFECT) is also used in the theophany of Ezek. 10:4. It may reflect Num. 14:21; Ps. 72:19; and Hab. 2:14. This refers to either

  1. a symbol of God's judgment
  2. a reference to the Shekinah cloud, which symbolized but hid God's physical presence (cf. Exod. 40:34)
  3. smoke from an incense altar so that God could not be seen.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?

entries.title: Isaiah 6:5 "Woe is me, for I am ruined"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:5 "Woe is me, for I am ruined" This VERB (BDB 198 II, KB 225, Niphal PERFECT) denotes the destruction (i.e. "silencing") of someone or something.

  1.  of cities
    1.  of Moab, Isa. 15:1
    2.  of Philistia, Jer. 47:5
  2.  of people
    1.  Israel, Hosea 4:6
    2.  Jerusalem, Zeph. 1:11
    3.  Edom, Obad. 1:5
  3.  of kings
    1.  Israel, Hosea 10:7,15
    2.  Egypt, Ezek. 32:2
  4.  of humans under the metaphor of animals, Ps. 49:14,20
  5.  of Isaiah, because he saw YHWH, Isa. 6:5

The holiness of God informed Isaiah of his lack of righteousness accompanied by the biblical demanded response of judgment! Grace is key, but holiness is the goal (cf. Lev. 11:44-45; 19:2; 20:7,26; Deut. 18:13; Matt. 5:48)! One cannot remain the same person after contact with God, yet this is exactly what His covenant people did.

▣ "unclean lips" Human speech reflects the heart (cf. Matt. 15:18; Mark 7:20,23). This is reflected in Isa. 29:13 (Matt. 15:8-9) and Ezek. 33:30-32.

Isaiah is acknowledging his own sin (i.e. individual covenant responsibility, cf. Ezekiel 18 and 36) and the sin of his community (corporate responsibility). Both are true and have consequences and benefits! God's people were to reflect YHWH's character to the nations, but they had been corrupted by the nations. Perhaps the "pure in heart can see God" (cf. Matt. 5:8), but Isaiah knew he was not one of them, nor were the covenant people. This is "the" tension of "conditional covenants" and the hope for an "unconditional covenant" that will issue in a godly people (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "my eyes have seen the King" See note at Isa. 6:1.

▣ "the King" Judah's kings represented YHWH who was the true king of the Covenant people (i.e. Exod. 15:18; Num. 23:21; Jdg. 8:23; 1 Sam. 8:7; 12:12; 1 Kgs. 22:19; Jer. 46:18; 48:15; 51:57; Zeph. 3:15). Modern Judaism calls Him "the King of the Universe."

entries.title: Isaiah 6:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:6 This verse is very detailed imagery. Isaiah was having a vision of the heavenly temple, the abode of Deity. It is always hard to know what is real and what is imagery! Fallen humans see through a fog into the spiritual realm. We are not meant to develop a detailed understanding of heaven from texts like this. It is the general impression/truth that is crucial.

The amazing thing is that God has initiated revelation with fallen humanity. He reveals

  1. Himself
  2. His plans
  3. the current, as well as future, rejection of His people (cf. Isa. 6:9-13)

Judah refuses to hear and see (cf. Isa. 6:9-13), but Isaiah, who admits his sin, is cleansed and is available (cf. Isa. 6:8).

▣ "burning coal" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

▣ "the altar" This (BDB 258) seems to refer to either

  1. the incense altar before the veil
  2. altar of sacrifice in front of the Holy Place

It's touching Isaiah's mouth symbolized ritual, cultic cleansing.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE OF THE WILDERNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF INCENSE

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF SACRIFICE

entries.title: Isaiah 6:7 "touched my mouth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:7 "touched my mouth" This method of cleansing and commissioning is similar to Jer. 1:9 and Dan. 10:16. However, Ezekiel was told to eat a scroll (cf. Ezek. 2:8-10; 3:3), which is similar to Jer. 15:16 and Rev. 10:8-11. All of these are imagery for internalizing the Word of God so as to speak it truly to others.

▣ "your iniquity is taken away" The VERB (BDB 693, KB 747, Qal PERFECT with waw) means "to turn aside" or "take away." Here it is parallel to "forgiven" (lit. "covered," "atoned for," BDB 497, KB 493, Pual imperfect, cf. Isa. 22:14; 27:9; 28:18; see SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS IN THE OT). Isaiah has been changed in his vision of YHWH. The past has been effectively dealt with and the future will be different. This is declared by the Seraphim, who speak for YHWH! This is a tremendous passage on grace, much like Paul's Damascus road encounter with the risen Christ (cf. Acts 9).

The mechanism for the full and complete forgiveness and atonement is not clearly stated in this text, but from Isa. 53:5-6 the key role of the Messiah, the Suffering Servant, and the concept of "vicarious, substitutionary atonement" is revealed (i.e. Gen. 3:15; Mark 10:45; Rom. 5:12-21; 2 Cor. 5:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: A SUFFERING MESSIAH

entries.title: Isaiah 6:8 "who will go for Us"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:8 "who will go for Us" The "us" implies plurality (there are several places in the OT where this plurality is seen cf. Gen. 1:26; 9:6; Deut. 6:4-5; Ps. 110, as does the PLURAL title Elohim, Gen. 1:1; 5:1).

  1. Philo and Eben Ezra say this is later Hebrew grammatical feature called "THE PLURAL OF MAJESTY"
  2. others claim it is "the heavenly council" (i.e. Rashi, cf. 1 Kgs. 22:19-23; Job 1:6-12; 2:1-6; see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL)
  3. It could refer to a foreshadowing of the concept of a Triune God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY)

▣ "Here am I" This is a Hebrew idiom for availability (cf. Gen. 22:1,7,11; 27:1; 31:11; 46:2; Exod. 3:4; 1 Sam. 3:4,5,6,8,16; 22:12; 2 Sam. 1:7).

▣ "Send me" The VERB "send" (BDB 1018, KB 1511) is a Qal IMPERATIVE used as a prayer request. This is Isaiah's response to YHWH's question. It clearly reveals his availability.

One wonders how much this Hebrew concept of "divinely sent one" is typological of Jesus as "the sent one" in John's Gospel and believers as His "sent ones" into the world (cf. John 17:18; 20:21). God is reaching out to His rebellious creation! I recently heard a line from a new Christian song that says "God sent His Son, He sends His children still." Powerful words about God and about His people!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEND

entries.title: Isaiah 6:9-10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:9-10 As YHWH reveals His purpose for Isaiah's ministry, He also reveals to Isaiah the reaction his message will have on Judah.

  1. go, Isa. 6:9, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. tell, Isa. 6:9, BDB 55, KB 65, Qal PERFECT with waw
  3. keep listening, Isa. 6:9, Qal IMPERATIVE and Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of BDB 1033, KB 1570
  4. but do not perceive, Isa. 6:9, BDB 106, KB 122, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Isa. 1:3; 5:21; 10:13; 29:14
  5. keep looking, Isa. 6:9, Qal IMPERATIVE and Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of BDB 906, KB 1157
  6. but do not understand, Isa. 6:9, BDB 393, KB 380, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  7. render the hearts of this people insensitive (lit. "fat"), Isa. 6:10, BDB 1031, KB 1566, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  8. their ears dull, Isa. 6:10, BDB 457, KB 455, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  9. and their eyes dim, Isa. 6:10, BDB 1044, KB 1612, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

These IMPERATIVES are followed by the consequences (three IMPERFECTS of previously used VERBS, "see," "hear," and "perceive"). God knows (either by His foreknowledge (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREKNOWLEDGE) or His hardening of their already wayward hearts/minds; see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD HARDENED) that they will not respond and be saved.

  1. lest they repent, BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal PERFECT with waw negated (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT])
  2. lest they be healed, BDB 950, KB 1272, Qal PERFECT with waw negated (note Isa. 53:4-6). Healing is imagery for conversion not physical healing.

Isaiah will preach and though some may respond, the vast majority of his people/his society will not (cf. Rom. 1:24,26,28; Eph. 4:19) or cannot respond (cf. Isa. 29:9,10; Deut. 29:4; Matt. 13:13; Rom. 11:8)! Isaiah is not an evangelist here, but a prophet of covenant disobedience/consequences (cf. Matt. 13:13; Mark 4:12; Luke 8:10). His message of hope is for a future day, not his day!

entries.title: Isaiah 6:10 "their eyes are dim"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:10 "their eyes are dim" This (BDB 1044, KB 1612, Hiphil IMPERATIVE) is literally "covered with secretions" (cf. Isa. 29:9; 32:3).

It is note worthy that this very text was quoted by Jesus in His last public message (John 12:40). He clearly stated it referred not only to ancient Judah, but to the Jews of His day who refused to see, hear, and respond to His person and message.

This is a good example of why we must check the NT for a fuller meaning and implications of OT texts in relation to progressive revelation (e.g. Matt. 13:14-23; Acts 28:26-29, use of Isa. 6:9-10).

▣ "hearts" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

▣ "return" In the OT this term (BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal PERFECT with waw) means "a change of action." In the NT repentance means a "change of mind." Both concepts are involved!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 6:11 "how long"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:11 "how long" This refers to the length of time God's message will be rejected.

entries.title: Isaiah 6:12 "has removed men far away"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:12 "has removed men far away" This refers to an exile, but whether Assyria taking the northern tribes or Babylon taking the southern tribes is uncertain (possibly purposeful ambiguity).

entries.title: Isaiah 6:13 "Yet there will be a tenth portion in it"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:13 "Yet there will be a tenth portion in it" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES. Also note (1) Isaiah's son, Shear-jashub, Isa. 7:3, means "a remnant shall return" also (2) note the discussion at Isa. 10:20-22.

▣ "it will be subject to burning" Isa. 6:13, lines b and c, could be understood in two ways.

  1. literary context ‒ God's people, using imagery of a great tree, has been cut and burned, but there is life in the stump. A shoot will come forth (i.e. the Messiah or Messianic community, cf. Isa. 4:2; 11:1; 53:2; Jer. 23:5; 33:15; Zech. 3:8; 6:12). But future problems remain (i.e. burning).
  2. historically, culturally ‒ the Canaanite fertility idols (i.e. Asherah) will be completely burned (NEB). God's people will be freed from idolatry one day!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BRANCH OF THE LORD

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL'S MANDATED RESPONSE TO CANAANITE FERTILITY WORSHIP

SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES

▣ "Whose stump remains when it is felled" Isa. 6:13 has two words used only here in the OT, key words!

  1. "felled," BDB 1021 I, same root used of a gate in the temple (cf. 1 Chr. 26:16). The root's basic meaning is "to throw," "to cast," or "to fling."
  2. "stump," BDB 663, usually used of sacred stone pillars
    1. by Patriarchs and Moses (cf. Gen. 28:18,22; 31:13; 33:20; 35:14; Exod. 24:4)
    2. by Canaanite fertility worshipers (i.e. Ba'al)

▣ "The holy seed is its stump" This, like Isa. 4:2, has Messianic connotations. See note at Isa. 11:1. This phrase is left out of the LXX.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why did Uzziah's death affect Isaiah so deeply?
  2. Who did Isaiah see?
  3. Why was Isaiah's message rejected?
  4. How does Isaiah's day compare to our own?
