READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 10:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:2 Things are so upside down when the very ones YHWH seeks to protect (i.e. widows and orphans) have become the spoil and plunder!

10:3
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, JPSOA  "day of punishment"
LXX  "day of visitation"
REB  "when called to account"
Peshitta  "day of recompense"

The MT has "day of visitation." This visitation (BDB 924) by YHWH can be for blessing (i.e. Job 10:12) or punishment. Here, for judgment (cf. Jer. 8:12; 10:15; 49:8; HOs. 9:7; Mic. 7:4).

A series of questions spells out the fate of these exploiters! One day, whether temporally or eschatologically, the Creator will call His creatures, made in His image and likeness, to give an account of the stewardship of the gift of life (cf. Isa. 10:4). YHWH is a moral, ethical, compassionate Deity and He demands these characteristics in His covenant people so that "the nations" may know and come to Him!! Israel was giving a false message!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "And in the devastation which will come from afar" The judgment visitation by Israel's covenant God comes at His initiation (cf. Isa. 5:26-30). This is surely a prelude to the exile of Israel by Assyria and a foreshadowing of the exile of Judah by Neo-Babylon (v. 11).

YHWH's people clearly forgot that His promises were conditional on obedience. Rebellion has terrible consequences (i.e. Lev. 26; Deut. 28).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Isaiah 10:4 "His anger does not turn away"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:4 "His anger does not turn away" This is the Hebrew root (BDB 996, KB 1427) for repentance. YHWH's judgment of His faithless covenant people will not turn away (Qal PERFECT).

This very anger on Israel was clearly demonstrated in God's judgment on Jerusalem and the temple in A.D. 70 by the Roman army (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SECOND COMING, IV). I have come to believe that

  1. Matthew 21-25
  2. Mark 13 (Olivet Discourse)
  3. Luke 17; 21 (Olivet Discourse)
  4. 2 Thessalonians 2 ("man of lawlessness")
  5. the book of Revelation (i.e. Rev. 1:7)

refers to this A.D. 70 event. The new Jewish church is separated completely from the synagogue. See my exegetical notes on these NT passages free online.

▣ "His hand is still stretched out" This is a recurrent phrase in this literary unit (cf. Isa. 9:12,17,21). It is an anthropomorphic way of expressing God's unrelenting judgment.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE USED TO DESCRIBE DEITY

entries.title: Isaiah 10:5-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:5-19 This is a literary unit on YHWH's activity involving the nation of Assyria. It was the cruelest ANE power. It was brutal toward captive people groups. YHWH will use this godless pagan nation to accomplish His purposes (cf. Isa. 10:5b; 6b; as Hab. 1:12-17 asked God about His use of the Babylonian exile). God uses evil to do His biding! He did not make them (i.e. Satan, demons, fallen angels, evil empires), but He directs them for the larger good (cf. Job 12:23; Ps.47:7-8; 66:7; Dan. 2:21; Acts 17:26, i.e. His universal redemptive plan, see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

However, evil reaps the consequences of their acts. One day they, too, will be judged (cf. Deut. 32:34-43; Isa. 14:24-27; 30:27-33; 31:5-9). What Assyria did to others, Babylon (cf. Isa. 13:5) will do to them!

entries.title: Isaiah 10:5 "Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:5 "Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger" YHWH's tool for punishing His people's rebellion was the cruel nation of Assyria (cf. Isa. 7:17; 8:7). However, Assyria was responsible for her acts (cf. Isa. 10:24-27). The arrogance of Assyria is seen in Isa. 10:8-11,12.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:5-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:5-6 Notice the parallel words for YHWH's using Assyria as the rod of His discipline and judgment towards His covenant people (v. 6a).

  1. "My anger," v. 5a, BDB 60 I, cf. Isa. 5:25; 9:12,17,21; 10:4,25; 13:9,13
  2. "My indignation," v. 5b, BDB 276; cf. Isa. 5:5,25; 13:5; 30:27
  3. "My fury," v. 6b, BDB 720; cf. Isa. 9:18; 10:6; Jer. 7:29

Covenant love spurned turns into Divine wrath (i.e. Lev. 26; Deut. 28). To whom much is given, much is required (i.e. Romans 9).

entries.title: Isaiah 10:6 "a godless nation. . .the people of my fury"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:6 "a godless nation. . .the people of my fury" Oh, my, this refers to the nation of Israel (cf. Isa. 9:17,19)! This same phrase is used of Israel in Isa. 19:17; 32:6. What irony, the covenant people are called "godless" and said to be morally equivalent to "godless" Assyria!

▣ "To capture booty and to seize plunder" As Isa. 10:21, "a remnant will return," reflects Isaiah's first son's name (cf. Isa. 7:3), this reflects his second son's symbolic name (cf. Isa. 8:1,3).

entries.title: Isaiah 10:7 "Yet it does not so intend Nor does it plan so in its heart"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:7 "Yet it does not so intend
  Nor does it plan so in its heart" Assyria did not know that YHWH was directing its actions for His purposes. Assyria was only after more and more spoil.

The intent of YHWH for the king of Assyria is revealed in a series of Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS (Isa. 10:6) against Israel.

  1. capture booty (BDB 1021, KB 1531)
  2. seize plunder (BDB 102, KB 117)
  3. trample down (VERBAL BDB 962, KB 1321, NOUN BDB 942)

The intent of the King of Assyria is expressed in two Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS in Isa. 10:7c,d.

  1. to destroy (BDB 1029, KB 1552)
  2. to cut off (BDB 503, KB 500)

entries.title: Isaiah 10:8-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:8-11 The King of Assyria's thoughts (i.e. "boasts," TEV) are revealed in these verses.

  1. all his military commanders are kings (NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, Peshitta), Isa. 10:8 (i.e. this could refer to vassal kings)
  2. his (Tiglath-Pileser III, who reigned from 745-727 B.C., or possibly Sennacherib, who reigned 705-681 B.C..) army has defeated several other trans-Euphrates cities and nations, along with all their gods, Isa. 10:9
    1. Calno (or Calneh), city in northern Syria (cf. Amos 6:2) fell in 742 B.C. (all these dates are estimates only)
    2. Carchemish, major city of the Hittites near the headwaters of the Euphrates, joined Assyrian coalition in 738 B.C.
    3. Hamath, city on the northern boundary of Israel (cf. 2 Chr. 8:4) on the Orontes River, fell in 738 B.C.
    4. Arpad, city in northwest Syria fell in 741 B.C.
    5. Samaria (capital of Israel) fell in 722 B.C. to Sargon II
    6. Damascus (capital of Syria) fell in 732 B.C.
  3. he threatened to destroy Jerusalem and her "idols" as he had Samaria, Isa. 10:11. He had no knowledge of the distinction between "idols" (cf. Isa. 2:8) and the true worship of YHWH.

Just a word about which Assyrian invasion is depicted. The place names follow a traditional invasion route of ANE empires from Mesopotamia. Because of the desert, they had to follow the Euphrates River to its headwaters and then go south along the coastal plain. The problem with identifying which Assyrian invasion is complicated because Sennacherib, who did approach Jerusalem to besiege it, actually came from the south of the city in 701 B.C. The fall of the cities mentioned occurred under Tiglath-Pileser III (i.e. Pul). Therefore, I think the route was "idealized" as a northern invader.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA

entries.title: Isaiah 10:11 "images"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:11 "images" This is an interesting word (BDB 47). Its basic meaning is uncertain, but it is spelled similarly to Elohim, which has caused scholars to assume it refers to weak and non-existent idols (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 411). Monotheism is the uniqueness of Israel's faith. There are other spiritual beings, but only one true God (cf. Deut. 4:35,39; 6:8; 32:39; Isa. 43:9-11; 45:21-22; Jer. 2:11; 5:7,10; Rom. 3:30; 1 Cor. 8:4,6; 1 Tim. 2:5; James 2:19). The idols represent nothing, only the false hopes and fears (superstitions) of fallen humanity realizing there is more to reality than the physical, but unable to comprehend spiritual truth (i.e. revelation).

Since vv. 8-11 refer to the arrogant claims of the Assyrian kings (as do vv. 13-14), v. 11 was the invader's confidence that since his army had conquered many of the natives of Canaan and their gods (idols), why should he not be able to do the same to Israel and Judah?

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS IN THE BIBLE

entries.title: Isaiah 10:12-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:12-14 YHWH asserts His control of Assyria and her victories. He will judge the king of Assyria (Isa. 10:12) for his

  1. arrogant heart
  2. haughtiness of his eyes (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LIFTED UP)

The Assyrian king's pride is shown in a series of self praises (Isa. 10:12-14), which sound very much like Assyrian documents of the period (see The IVP Bible Background Commentary OT, p. 599)

  1. by the power of my hand
  2. by my wisdom

He robbed the nations on the west banks of the Euphrates as one robs a bird's nest!

10:13
NASB  "like a mighty man"
NKJV  "like a valiant man"
NRSV, TEV, REB  "like a bull"
NJB  "like a hero"

The ADJECTIVE'S (BDB 7) basic meaning, "strong," can refer to

  1. mighty/violent man, Job 24:22; 34:20; Jer. 46:15; Lam. 1:15
  2. stubborn minded, Isa. 46:12
  3. angels, Ps. 78:25
  4. animals
    1. bulls, Isa. 10:13 may refer to a bull because a winged bull was the symbol of Assyria (i.e. on the sides of the Ishtar gates, cf. Ps. 22:13; 68:30; Isa. 34:7)
    2. horses, Jdg. 5:22; Jer. 8:16; 47:3; 50:11

The ancient versions are very different in their understanding of this last poetic line of v. 13.

  1. LXX ‒ "and I will plunder their strength"
  2. Peshitta ‒ "and I have plundered their wealth, and subjugated the inhabited cities"
  3. the MT ‒  "I have brought down, like a bull, those who sat on thrones."
  4. JPSOA ‒ "I plundered their treasuries, and exiled their vast population."

entries.title: Isaiah 10:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:14 The Bible often uses bird imagery to describe God's protection and care (cf. Exod. 19:4; Deut. 32:11; Ruth 2:12; Isa. 31:5; Matt. 23:37; Luke 13:34; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW/SHADE), but here the imagery is reversed! God has removed His protection!

The nations of the ANE were as defenseless as bird nests on the ground.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:15-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:15-19 YHWH responds to the boasts of the King of Assyria by questioning.

  1. Is the power in the axe or the one who used the axe?
  2. Is the power in the saw or the one who wields the saw?
  3. Is the power in the club or the one who swings the club?
  4. Is the power in a scepter or in the one who lifts the scepter?

YHWH will judge him and his army in one day (Isa. 10:17). This refers to

  1. Tiglath-Pileser III
  2. specifically to Sennacherib (701 B.C.), recorded in Isaiah 36-38; 2 Kgs. 18:17-21:11; 2 Chr. 32:9-24, where 185,000 soldiers die before the walls of Jerusalem in response to the arrogance of the king of Assyria and his military leaders (#2 fits best, but did not happen until decades after Tiglath-Pileser III took Samaria). There is a difference between the God of Israel and the idols of the nations!

entries.title: Isaiah 10:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:16 YHWH is in control of history. This is the basic premise of monotheism linked to an involved Deity. He is present and active in His creation. In the OT all causality is attributed to YHWH (cf. Deut. 32:29; Job 5:18; Isa. 45:7; Hosea 6:1; Amos 3:6; see SPECIAL TOPIC: ONE CAUSALITY). It was a way to affirm monotheism. Exactly how, when, where He acts is unknown, but there is

  1. an eternal redemptive plan (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)
  2. a covenant people (see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT)
  3. a coming Messiah (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH)
  4. a heart for "the nations"

History is not cyclical, but teleological!

▣ "Lord" This is the Hebrew title Adon, which denoted "husband," "master," "owner." It is parallel to the Greek title kurios.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)

▣ "God of hosts" This is literally "YHWH of hosts" (BDB 217 and BDB 838).

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord of Hosts

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "send a wasting disease" Diseases were common among large armies (cf. v. 18). See IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 599.

▣ "His glory" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (OT)

▣ "fire" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

entries.title: Isaiah 10:17 "the light of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:17 "the light of Israel" This is a title for YHWH. Light (see note at Isa. 9:2) and fire are symbols of Deity (cf. Isa. 9:19; 29:6; 30:27; 31:9; 33:11-12,14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIGHT

▣ "and His Holy One" This title is usually restricted to YHWH (cf. v. 20 and Isa. 37:23), but here, it refers to the Messiah (or possibly the Death Angel, cf. 2 Kgs. 19:35; see SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS IN THE BIBLE

Notice that the NASB translation thinks "his Holy One" refers to the "flame." Notice in line 2, the use of the PRONOUN "it," but the PRONOUN "He" occurs again in v. 18.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:18 "both soul and body"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:18 "both soul and body" Mankind has both a physical component (i.e. nephesh; see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH) and a spiritual component. We as humans are prepared for life on this planet and for fellowship with a non-corporeal Deity! We share planet-life with animals, but we are also creatures of the spiritual realm (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; Dan. 12:2)!

entries.title: Isaiah 10:18-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:18-19 In these verses the Assyrian military is personified as trees in a forest (also note vv. 33-34).

Because of the mentioning "of his fruitful garden," these verses may also refer to the Assyrian palaces (i.e. imagery for the nation).

entries.title: Isaiah 10:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:19 I have no idea what this line of poetry is referring to. The JPSOA translates this as "what trees remain of it shrub, shall be so few that a boy may record them."

The Jewish Study Bible (Oxford) mentions that the remnant imagery used of God's faithful followers, is now used of the defeated Assyrian army.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:20 "in that day"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:20 "in that day" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

▣ "the remnant" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, three senses

▣ "will never again rely on the one who struck them" Ahaz trusted/relied on Assyria for help instead of YHWH, but not so in the future. The remnant (i.e. the covenant people) will rely on YHWH alone!

▣ "truly rely" See SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT

▣ "the Holy One"  See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

entries.title: Isaiah 10:20-23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:20-23 This paragraph focuses on two theological truths.

  1. YHWH will protect and restore a faithful remnant ("truly rely on the Lord," BDB 1043, KB 1612, Niphal PERFECT with waw) to accomplish His purposes with Abraham's seed.
  2. "In that day" refers to a day of deliverance. One is never sure if this promise is fulfilled in
    1. a return to Judah allowed by Persia (i.e. Cyrus II in 538 B.C.)
    2. the Maccabees (interbiblical period)
    3. the future time. The book that has really helped me understand the genre of Prophecy and Apocalyptic is D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:21 "A remnant will return"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:21 "A remnant will return" This remnant (BDB 984) is described as from Jacob and Israel. In this context it must refer to the Northern Ten Tribes that split off in 922 B.C. and were exiled by Assyria in 722 B.C. Few of them returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel and Joshua after Cyrus' edict in 538 B.C. allowed all the exiled people groups to return to their native lands. The phrase translates Isaiah's first son's name (Shear-jashub) who went with his father to confront King Ahaz (cf. Isa. 7:1-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, three senses

▣ "return" See SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ "to the mighty God" This is the same title (i.e. El, BDB 42 plus the ADJECTIVE "mighty" (BDB 150) used of the Messiah in Isa. 9:6. It is found only in these two places. In this context it refers to YHWH.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:22 "O Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:22 "O Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL

▣ "may be like the sand of the sea" This is a reference to the promise of many descendants, which was a major part of the Abrahamic covenant (cf. Gen. 13:16; 22:17; 32:12).

What a sad contrast occurs when the promises of YHWH to the Patriarchs of many descendants (see full note at Gen. 15:5).

  1. like the stars (cf. Gen. 15:5; 22:17; 26:4; Exod. 32:13; Deut. 1:10; 28:62)
  2. like the dust (cf. Gen. 13:16; 28:14)
  3. like the sand (cf. Gen. 22:17; 32:22)

is reduced through covenant disobedience and lack of personal trust (cf. Isa. 10:20) to only a few to return (cf. Isa. 10:21-22).

▣ "A destruction is determined, overflowing with righteousness" Israel's judgment has been

  1. determined by YHWH, Isa. 10:22
  2. decreed by YHWH, Isa. 10:23

Both "determined" and "decreed" translate the same VERB (BDB 358, KB 356, cf. Isa. 28:22; Dan. 9:26,27; 11:36). God will judge His people (Isa. 10:22). Isaiah 10:23 is (1) parallel to this or (2) YHWH will judge all the earth (LXX, Peshitta, NRSV. Paul quotes the LXX in Rom. 9:27-28). Context fits option #1 better. YHWH said He would do it; He did it!

entries.title: Isaiah 10:24 "do not fear the Assyrian"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:24 "do not fear the Assyrian" This VERB (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT) is used as a JUSSIVE. The implication is "fear YHWH who will bring judgment on them" (Isa. 10:25-27).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 10:24-27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:24-27 The paragraph again stresses YHWH's moral righteousness which is reflected in judgment against evil.

  1. Israel experienced YHWH's righteous anger (cf. Isa. 10:22)
  2. Assyria (cf. Isa. 37:26-28)
  3. Like His wrath in Egypt during the Exodus (cf. Exod. 14:16,27)
  4. Like Gideon against the Midianites (Judges 6-8)

YHWH's actions, past and future, described in Isa. 10:27, are parallel to His action (cf. Isa. 14:25) through the Messiah in Isa. 9:4, which also mentions the battle against Midian (an idiom of YHWH's total defeat of an enemy cf. Isa. 9:4; Ps. 83:9-11).

entries.title: Isaiah 10:26 "the rock of Oreb"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:26 "the rock of Oreb" Gideon summoned the Ephraimites to help him wipe out the remaining retreating Midianites. Two of the leaders were caught and killed (cf. Jdg. 7:24-25). The place where this occurred took on the names of the Midianite leaders, Oreb and Zeeb. The exact location is unknown.

▣ "His staff will be over the sea" As God delivered the Israelites at the Red Sea (Exodus), He will deliver them from Assyria (here, called "the sea").

10:27
NASB, JPSOA  "the yoke will be broken because of fatness"
NKJV  "the yoke will be destroyed because of the
 anointing oil"
LXX, REB  "the yoke will be destroyed from off your
 shoulders"
Peshitta  "the yoke shall be destroyed from your neck
 because of your strength"
NET  "the yoke will be taken off because
 your neck will be too large"

From these translations you can see the options.

  1. NASB, JPSOA follow MT (the UBS Text Project, p. 35, gives this a "C" rating)
  2. LXX, REB leave out the phrase "because of fatness"
  3. NKJV refers to the Messiah (i.e. anointed, BDB 1032)
  4. Peshitta sees it as a reference to strength and growth (cf. Deut. 32:15), which may contrast Isa. 10:16.
  5. the NET Bible, p. 1205, #10, gives possible emendation

Since Isaiah 7-12 relates to the special children of the New Age, including the Messiah, I like NKJV's understanding as the one that makes the most sense to me in this large literary unit, even though this is not in the Hebrew root for Messiah, but it is a root used of "anointing."

The UBS Text Project, p. 26, says that the original Hebrew text may have contained a place name.

  1. a place name which became an unknown place
  2. a proverbial location whose meaning is no longer recognized
  3. this links with place names in the next strophe

entries.title: Isaiah 10:28 "Aiath"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:28 "Aiath" This is Ai close to Jericho. The places mentioned show the movement of the Assyrians toward Jerusalem from the north.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:28-32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:28-32 H. C. Leupold, Exposition of Isaiah, vol. 1, p. 40, describes this stanza (strophe) as "The Strategic Assyrian Advance That Almost Took Zion Described in Terms of Bulletin-from-the-Front." Many geographical locations are mentioned and what was occurring at that location as the Assyrian mercenary army approached.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:30 "Cry aloud. . .Pay attention"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:30 "Cry aloud. . .Pay attention" These are both IMPERATIVES.

  1. BDB 843, KB 1007, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. BDB 904, KB 1151, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

This breaks the pattern of Isa. 10:28-32. If this stanza is "reports from the front lines," then Isa. 10:30 is a comment from the prophet, not an Assyrian messenger.

NASB  "wretched Anathoth"
NKJV  "poor Anathoth"
NRSV, NET  "Answer her, O Anathoth"
TEV  "Answer, people of Anathoth"
NJB, REB, LXX  "Anathoth will listen"
Peshitta  "Answer me, O Anathoth"
JPSOA  "Take up the cry, Anathoth"

This is from either

  1. the VERB "answer," BDB 772 I, Qal IMPERATIVE (MT)
  2. an ADJECTIVE "poor," BDB 776

They both have the same CONSONANTS. UBS Hebrew Text Project gives #2, translated "unfortunate,"a "C" rating (considerable doubt). It is surely possible that "poor" and "Anathoth" are a sound play (NASB Study Bible, p. 974).

entries.title: Isaiah 10:32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 10:32 The second line of poetry expresses the Assyrian's contempt for Judah's God and His temple.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:33
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:33 The second half of this verse has several terms found only here in the OT. This is why the central truth of the paragraph (prose) or stanza (poetry) is crucial. The main truth or imagery is key, not each and every detail or lexical option (often just an educated guess).

10:34
NASB, NKJV  "by the Mighty One"
NRSV  "with its majestic trees"
TEV  "the finest trees"
NJB  "of a Mighty One"
LXX  "with its lofty ones"
REB  "with its noble trees"
NET  "and mighty Lebanon"

This phrase can refer to

  1. God (cf. Isa. 10:33a; Isa. 10:34a)
  2. the tall trees of Lebanon (cf. Isa. 10:33b,c; LXX, JPSOA, NET)

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 10:33-34
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
10:33-34 Isa. 10:33-34 is hard to identify who is "lopped off." It seems to be a literary link between Isa. 10:16-19 and 11:1. Isaiah often used forestry imagery. Whoever compiled the scroll of Isaiah used word plays and themes as a way to link together Isaiah's recorded prophetic messages. We must remember that the major truth of the literary unit and stanzas are more important than

  1. the details
  2. the exact historical setting of each literary building block

Our love for the Bible and desire to know more have caused us to treat the Bible in non-contextual, literal ways, which destroy the literary nature of Scripture and especially Hebrew poetry and prophecy!

I think this is an elaboration of Isa. 10:16-19. The imagery is the destruction of a forest, which symbolizes the Assyrian army and its leadership.

entries.title: Isaiah 11:1 "a shoot"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:1 "a shoot" This rare word ( BDB 310, KB 307) can be translated "twig," "branch," or "shoot." It is translated "rod" in Prov. 14:3. It obviously refers to a supernatural Davidic descendant (cf. Isa. 6:13; 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17; Rev. 22:16) out of a seemingly dead stump (i.e. exiled Judah) will come a new king! This imagery (but different Hebrew word) is seen again in the Suffering Servant Song of Isaiah 52:13-53:12 (i.e. Isa. 11:2).

The Jewish Study Bible (p. 807) adds an interesting comment on this root.

"If the translation 'stump' is correct, then the passage may presume that the Davidic dynasty will (or has) come to an end; this reading would deviate significantly from Isaiah's notion that Davidic kings will reign eternally (cf. 2 Sam. 7:8-16; Ps. 89:20-37). But the Hebrew 'geza' refers not only to a stump of a tree that has been cut down but also to the trunk of a living tree."

I cannot confirm this meaning for "shoot" unless it is Isa. 40:24.

▣ "from the stem of Jesse" Jesse was King David's father. This future descendant is mentioned in Isa. 11:10; 9:7; 16:5.

The OT gives the lineage of the Special Coming One, the Anointed One.

  1. from the tribe of Judah, Gen. 49:8-12, esp. Isa. 11:10 and Rev. 5:5
  2. from the family of Jesse, 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17

The special child of the new age has now been identified as a special ruler. His character will characterize the new age (cf. Isa. 9:2-7; Jer. 23:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TITLES FOR THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

▣ "a branch from his roots" The NOUN "branch," "sprout," or "shoot" (BDB 666, cf. Isa. 14:19; 60:21; Dan. 11:7) is theologically parallel to "branch" or "sprout" (BDB 855, cf. Isa. 4:2; 61:11). New growth will come from what seemed to be dead! Notice lines 1 and 2 of v. 1 are in a synonymous parallel relationship.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BRANCH OF THE LORD

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY, III.

▣ "will bear fruit" The MT has the VERB "bear fruit" (פרה, BDB 826, KB 963, Qal IMPERFECT, Dead Sea Scrolls, NASB), but most ancient and modern versions assume a similar VERB, פרח (BDB 827, KB 966).

  1. NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta, "shall grow out"
  2. NJB, "will grow"
  3. LXX, Targums, "shall come up"
  4. REB, "will spring from"
  5. JPSOA, "shall sprout"

The second option fits the parallelism best!

entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BACKGROUND STUDY

  1. Isaiah 11 is in sharp contrast to Isa. 10:33-34, which describes the fall of Assyria (cf. Isa. 10:15-19).

  2. As Assyria is cut down as a great forest, so the Messiah will rise from the stump of Jesse. Isaiah often uses imagery from trees.

  3. Isaiah 11 reflects the promises to David's descendants found in 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17.

  4. This ideal eschatological period is also described in Isa. 2:2-4; 9:1-7. Isa. 11:10 could go with Isa. 11:1-9 or 11:11-16 depending on how one views the scope of the Messianic reign (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE END-TIME EVENTS SO CONTROVERSIAL?

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 11:2 "the Spirit of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:2 "the Spirit of the Lord" Many have tried to relate this passage to the seven-fold spirits of Rev. 1:4 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SEVEN SPIRITS IN REVELATION). This seems doubtful to me. The MT lists six characteristics, but the LXX adds a seventh, "piety," in place of "fear" in Isa. 11:2, but then adds "fear" from Isa. 11:3. However, this does relate to the titles of Isa. 9:6 and describes the king fully equipped by God in insight, administration, and piety. The Spirit of the Lord abides on Him as He did on David (cf. 1 Sam. 16:13).

The personality of the "Spirit" is not fully revealed in the OT. In the OT the Spirit is YHWH's personal influence to accomplish His purposes, much like the "Angel of the Lord." It is not until the NT that His full personality and Deity are revealed.

The other problem with the word "spirit" (BDB 924) is that it can refer to human characteristics or divine action.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Angel of the Lord

▣ "will rest on Him" The VERB (BDB 628, KB 679) is a Qal PERFECT with waw denoting a settled or continuing condition. He will abide and remain. This same truth is stated in different ways in Isa. 42:1; 59:21; 61:1; Matt. 3:16; Luke 4:18.

▣ "the spirit of. . ." Basically there are three groups of Spirit led human effectivenesses in this text of the Davidic Messiah:

  1. intellectual
    1. wisdom, BDB 315 (opposite of Isa. 10:13)
    2. understanding, BDB 108 (see first pair in Deut. 4:6)
  2. effective administration (cf. Isa. 9:6-7)
    1. counsel, BDB 420
    2. strength, BDB 150 (reign of peace through military power, cf. 2 Kgs. 18:20)
  3. personal piety
    1. knowledge of the Lord, BDB 395
    2. fear of the Lord, BDB 432 (cf. Isa. 11:3)

This same type of description is found in Isa. 2:2-4; 9:6-7; 42:1-4. It will be a time of justice, righteousness. and peace.

entries.title: Isaiah 11:3 "will delight"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:3 "will delight" This is literally "breathe in" (BDB 926, KB 1195, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT). This is used in the sense of the pleasing smell (Rotherham's Emphasized Bible has "fragrance," p. 658) of the sacrifice or incense rising to God (i.e. Gen. 8:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SOOTHING AROMA

▣ "in the fear of the Lord" This term "fear" (BDB 432) often denotes a respect for the awesomeness of God. It was meant as a deterrent to keep the covenant people from sinning (cf. Exod. 20:20; Deut. 4:10; 6:24). King David feared YHWH (cf. 2 Sam. 23:3). This Messiah, the new David, perfectly reflects this reverence as the ideal example of a "true Israelite." Note how it forms the introduction to Proverbs (cf. Prov. 1:7; also note 2:5; 14:26,27)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

▣ "He will not judge by what His eyes see" Because of the gifts of the Spirit this special Davidic ruler will be able to discern truth and not be tricked by false testimony. He will be the perfect righteous judge. The kings of Israel functioned as the last resort for justice.

entries.title: Isaiah 11:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:4 Does it surprise you that poverty and oppression will continue into the new age? This is the kind of literalism that causes confusion. This verse's purpose is the character of the Ruler, not a description of an eschatological society! It was meant to show that He will bring conformity to the ideals of God's revealed covenant. He will reflect YHWH's character Himself and project this onto human relationships!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (NT)

▣ "righteousness" See SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS.

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, LXX, Peshitta  "the earth"
NJB  "the country"
REB  "the ruthless"
JPSOA  "a land"

The first interpretive issue is the meaning of erets (BDB 75, KB 90; see the semantic field in SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH (OT).

The second issue is the possible emendation from REB.

  1. MT ‒ ארץ (BDB 75)
  2. NEB, REB ‒ עריץ (BDB 792)

The UBS Text Project, p. 27, gives the MT a "B" rating (some doubt).

The NEB/REB is an attempt to make the parallelism stronger.

▣ "with the rod of His mouth" This sounds very similar to the phrase used in Rev. 1:16; 2:16, which speaks of the power of the spoken word (cf. Genesis 1; Isa. 55:11; John 1:1-5) in the phrase "sword of my mouth." The last two lines of poetry speak of the ruler's effective power (cf. Isa. 11:2c).

entries.title: Isaiah 11:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:5 Clothing is imagery used to describe the qualities of the coming righteous Davidic ruler. Later Paul will use this to describe the believer's provisions for spiritual conflict (cf. Eph. 6:14).

▣ "faithfulness" Notice "faithfulness" is parallel to "righteousness." See SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFLNESS (OT), II. C.

entries.title: Isaiah 11:6-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:6-9 This is a picture of the Messianic era, described in terms of Genesis 1 and used as imagery in Revelation 22. Nature has been affected by mankind's sin, Genesis 3. It will also be affected by the Messiah's salvation (cf. Rom. 8:19-25). Notice the emphasis again on the small child of the new age.

The fellowship between humans and animals reflects the Garden of Eden (i.e. Genesis 2-3). Humans have so much in common with the animals that occupy the surface of this planet. They were also created for fellowship with God (cf. Job 38:39; 40:34) and us! The Bible starts with God, humans, and animals in a garden setting (Genesis 1-2) and it concludes with God, humans, and with these passages in Isaiah, animals (cf. Isa. 65:15; Hosea 2:18; Revelation 21-22). I personally do not think our pets will be in heaven, but I do think animals will be a part of eternity! They add a wonderful richness to life. They only became food and coverings after the Fall!

Another point about the inherent ambiguity involved in texts associated with the eschaton is the age of the persons mentioned. Little children (Isa. 11:6) and infants (Isa. 11:8) imply that physical birth continues. This assumes an earthly setting totally analogous to current life (cf. Matt. 24:38; Luke 17:27). However, Jesus asserts that there will be no sexual activity in the new age (cf. Matt. 22:29-30). Will humans in the eschaton be all different ages? Will they grow old? These are questions that have caused commentators to postulate a limited earthly period of restored righteousness (i.e. a millennium; see my exegetical notes on Rev. 20 online) and a future idealized state. Dispensationalists have even postulated a split between a group in heaven (Christians) and a group on earth (Jews). I prefer a single, visible Second Coming and an immediate idealized, eternal fellowship with God. If this is true, much of the OT and NT has to be viewed as accommodation related to the spiritual Kingdom of God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGDOM OF GOD). Please see my commentaries on Revelation (Partial Preterist), Daniel, Zechariah online free at www.freebiblecommentary.org

This new day of universal peace is described in idealistic, area-wide, inclusivistic terms. When is this new age to manifest itself?

  1. return from exile under Zerubbabel and Joshua (i.e. Ezra and Nehemiah)
  2. the Maccabean period (interbiblical)
  3. the inauguration of the Kingdom of God in Jesus' lifetime (Gospels)
  4. a millennial period (Rev. 20:1-10 only)
  5. an eternal kingdom (cf. Dan. 7:14; Rev. 20-22)

Each is viewed as a new opportunity, but with problems (#1-4). This is where different systematic (denominational) theologies take the ambiguous references and turn them into a "theological grid" through which to view all Scripture. The promises are sure! But the time frame and specifics are not.

One central question which deals with this issue is "how literal is the restoration of an earthly garden (i.e. Eden. see SPECIAL TOPIC: EDEN) to be taken (Genesis 1-3 and Revelation 21-22)"? Is

  1. this planet the focus
  2. the kosmos the focus
  3. a spiritual realm beyond time-space, possibly another dimension of reality (cf. John 4:21-24; 18:36)?

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

11:6
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA  "and the fatling"
TEV, REB  "will feed together"
NJB  "fat-stock beast"
LXX, NET  "graze together"

The LXX and Peshitta add "ox" and also add the VERB "feed together." The MT has "fatling" (BDB 597), but no VERB. With an emendation "and the fatling" (ומריא) can be changed to "will be fed" (ימרו, TEV). The UBS Hebrew Text Project, p. 27, gives the VERB "fed" a "C" rating (considerable doubt). With the parallelism of the first two and fourth lines of poetry having VERBS, one would expect the third line to have one also. The Dead Sea Scroll of Isaiah and the Septuagint have the VERB "fed" instead of "fatling."

The fatling would have sacrificial connotations (cf. Isa. 1:11; Amos 5:22). See SPECIAL TOPIC: SACRIFICIAL SYSTEMS OF THE ANE

entries.title: Isaiah 11:7 "lion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 11:7 "lion" See SPECIAL TOPIC: LIONS IN THE OT.

entries.title: Isaiah 11:8 "child"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:8 "child" This is another reference to the children (BDB 654) of the New Age (cf. Isa. 7:16; 8:4; 10:19; 11:6).

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA  "den"
NJB, LXX  "lair"
REB, NET  "nest"
Peshitta  "hole"

The MT has a NOUN (BDB 22), which occurs only here in the OT. BDB translates it "light hole," which means an opening of some type into a dark space where a serpent lives. It is parallel to "the hole of the cobra" in v. 8a.

entries.title: Isaiah 11:9 "My holy mountain"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:9 "My holy mountain" This does not refer to Jerusalem or Sinai, but to the entire earth as the parallel phrase in Isa. 11:4c, 9b, 10 shows. Also notice that the attributes of the Messiah have now been effectively communicated to all humans (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:15). He is the ideal covenant man!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 11:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:10 Verses like 4, 9, and 10 can be understood in one of two ways.

  1. YHWH will restore His covenant people to Canaan and the world will acknowledge them.
  2. The emphasis of a worldwide reign of a Davidic seed fulfills the promise of Gen. 3:15 for the restoration of the image and likeness of God in all humanity (i.e. Gen. 1:26-27), which was damaged by the Fall.

Are these Isaiah texts ultimately about Israel only or about the world (see Pau's view of the LXX of this verse in Rom. 15:12)? Are they literal, symbolic, or multiple fulfillment? Here is where one's overall view of Scripture begins to organize (for better or worse) texts. I have biases like everyone else! I have tried to list mine in the SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN. It is difficult to be faithful to texts and context and all texts at the same time! No one does it well!

▣ "that day" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

▣ "the root of Jesse" This same term (BDB 1057) is used in verse 1.

entries.title: Isaiah 11:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:11 This verse speaks of a climactic visitation by YHWH (cf. Isa. 2:2,11,12,20; 3:7,18; 4:1,2; 7:17,18,20; 9:14; 10:3,17,20,27). Here it is a day of restoration! Remember, God's "visitation" can be for blessing or judgment. The covenant people (i.e. in this case the Northern Ten Tribes), scattered across the ANE, will return home (a symbol of returning to faith in YHWH).

However, the rest of the literary unit (Isa. 7-12) has a universal element (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 9:1-7)! The OT has not been negated, but fulfilled (i.e. Matt. 5:17-19).

NASB, NRSV, NJB, REB  "a second time"
NKJV, Peshitta  "the second time"
TEV  "once again"
JPSOA  "again"
LXX  "further display"

This seems to be an allusion to the exodus (cf. vv. 15-16). As YHWH was faithful to His promises to Abraham (i.e. Gen. 15:12-21), He will do so again during the reign of the Messiah.

▣ "with His hand" This is an anthropomorphic idiom for divine activity within history. In Genesis 1 God speaks and things occur, but here He moves His hand (cf. Isa. 11:15; 1:25; 5:25; 8:11; 9:12,17,21; 10:4, etc.).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

▣ "The remnant" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, Three Senses

entries.title: Isaiah 11:12 "He will lift up a standard for the nations"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:12 "He will lift up a standard for the nations" In context this surely refers to the exiled seed of Abraham. They will be gathered from all the nations where they were scattered (i.e. v. 12d; Jer. 3:17-18).

Here, the focus is not on the inclusion of the nations (i.e. Ps. 2:8; 22:27; 86:9-10; 66:4; Isa. 2:2-4; 66:23; Micah 4:1-3; Rev. 15:4).

The standard that is lifted up is the righteous Davidic Messiah (cf. v. 10).

▣ "the four corners of the earth" Four is the symbolic number for the whole earth.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #2

SPECIAL TOPIC: WORLD (several terms), I. A.

entries.title: Isaiah 11:13 "Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:13 "Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah,

And Judah will not harass Ephraim"

Notice in the new era unity will be the keynote, not the tribal divisions that had characterized the people of God in the past.

The NET Bible, p. 1207, has an interesting comment (#21), which gives an alternate meaning to "those who harass Judah" (BDB 865, KB 1058, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE). It asserts that this phrase should be translated "those hostile toward Judah" will be destroyed.

entries.title: Isaiah 11:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:14 This verse is surprising! Is Isaiah prophesying a vindictive united Israel or is she to be the channel of revelation for "the nations" to come to YHWH in peace (cf. Isa. 2:2-4)?

▣ "sons of the east" This phrase can refer to several different people groups, depending on the context (cf. Gen. 29:1; Jdg. 6:3,33; 7:12; 8:10; 1 Kgs. 4:30; Job 1:3; Isa. 11:14; Jer. 49:28; Ezek. 25:4,10).

  1. Gen. 29:1 ‒ Aramean/Syrian
  2. Jdg. 6:3,33; 7:12; 8:10; Isa. 11:14; Jer. 49:28; Ezek. 25:4,10, desert tribes south and east of Canaan
  3. 1 Kgs. 4:30 ‒ all ANE
  4. Job 1:3 ‒ Edom, Moab, Ammon

entries.title: Isaiah 11:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
11:15 The covenant people's traditional enemies (i.e. vv. 14-15) will be utterly defeated.

NASB, NKJV, NRSV  "will utterly destroy"
TEV, NJB  "will dry up"
LXX  "make desolate"
Peshitta  "will utterly dry up"
REB, NET  "will divide"
JPSOA, NASB margin  "will dry up the tongue"

The NASB follows the MT "and he will devote to destruction" (והחרים, BDB 355, KB 353, Hiphil PERFECT with waw), which the UBS Hebrew Text Project gives a "B" rating (some doubt).

The other readings are

  1. והחריב, "and he will dry up," BDB 351, KB 349)
  2. the NEB and REB assume a proposed root (חרם, KB 354 II, Hiphil PERFECT), which means "split" or "divide" (cf. Exod. 14:16)

This is an allusion to a new universal exodus (cf. Isa. 11:11)!

NASB, NRSV  "scorching wind"
NKJV, REB, Peshitta  "a mighty wind"
TEV  "a hot wind"
NJB  "with the heat of his breath"
NET  "a strong wind"
JPSOA  "the might of His wind"
LXX  "a violent wind"

The MT has a NOUN (BDB 744), which is found only here. BDB suggests "glow." Most translations derive the meaning of the root from an Arabic root which means "to thirst" or "to be internally hot" (i.e. a dry, hot wind).

▣ "the seven streams" As YHWH dries up parts of the Gulf of Suez in v. 15b, so too, parts of the Euphrates, v. 15c,e. The stated purpose being that believers can come to Him with no barriers, v. 15f.

This imagery is parallel to YHWH providing a "highway" from Assyria (v. 16).

Notice supernatural access to the Holy One of Israel has been provided.

  1. from Egypt (i.e. new exodus, v. 16d)
  2. from Mesopotamia

The recurring question is, "Does this imagery apply to Israel only or all faithful followers?" I think this prophesies that a period of restoration has been universalized by the NT to include "whosoever will," "as many as," "all who"!

See Sandy and Giese, Cracking Old Testament Codes, "How to Interpret Oracles of Salvation," pp. 146-155.

These seven dried up streams offer easy access to YHWH, as does "the highway" in v. 16.

11:16 "a highway" See full note at Isa. 19:23.

▣"remnant"  See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, three senses.

▣"in the day" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Are the titles of the child used in Isa. 9 and 11 an assertion of his Deity?
  2. Explain the historical background of Isa. 7:1 through 10:4 and Isa. 10:4 through 34.
  3. Will nature be a part of heaven?

entries.title: Isaiah 12:1 "you will say"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:1 "you will say" The VERB (BDB 55, KB 65, Qal PERFECT with waw) denotes a settled attitude of an individual Israelite (SINGULAR). It is much like the song of victory found in Exod. 15:1-17. This is also a song of praise for YHWH's deliverance . One person speaks on behalf of the whole covenant community.

This brief poem was placed here because it connects to the return from exile mentioned in Isa. 11:11-16. It also has a relation to the theological goal of the nations knowing and coming to YHWH (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 11:10; 12:4-6; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 60:1-3; 66:23)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "on that day" This is an idiom for YHWH's action within history, either temporally or eschatologically. There is a time of reckoning coming. For some, a time of joy and victory, for others a time of judgment and rejection (cf. Dan. 12:2; John 5:28-29)! Covenant disobedience (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP) affects time and eternity!

Because this phrase appears in both Isa. 12:11 and Isa. 12:4 it is possible that this chapter is two hymns of praise (cf. JB).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

▣ "I will give thanks" This VERB (BDB 392, KB 389 II, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense) basically means "to throw" or "to cast." However, especially in the Psalms, in the Hiphil stem it denotes "to confess" or "to praise." It is also found in Isaiah in Isa. 12:1,4; 25:1; 38:18,19.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THANKSGIVING

▣ "O Lord" See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "although You were angry with me" This VERB (BDB 60 I, KB 72, Qal PERFECT) is used rarely in the OT (cf. Deut. 1:37). This line of poetry may be another allusion to Exod. 15 (i.e. Exod. 15:8), where the same root, "nostrils," is used of YHWH splitting the Red Sea. The VERB denotes a snort (cf. Ps. 2:12). BDB suggests several connotations: "nostril," "nose," "face," "anger." In this context, it denotes YHWH's anger at His covenant people's disobedience. He will punish them for this but will have mercy and forgive and restore them (cf. Ps. 30:5; 103:9; Isa. 54:7-8; Jer. 3:12; Micah 7:18).

This reflects YHWH's reaction to His covenant love being violated repeatedly (cf. Isa. 40:1-2; 54:8; and many others). God's wrath is difficult for many Bible readers to understand. For me a comparison of Deut. 5:9 with 5:10 and 7:9 helps. God's anger is best understood as parental discipline (cf. Heb. 12:5-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "Your anger is turned away" This VERB (BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal JUSSIVE) is often translated "repent," when used of humans. In a sense YHWH repents (i.e. changed His mind and actions) toward His covenant people (i.e. Hosea 11:8-9). In the OT it is often specifically connected to their repentance. However, in the NT (and new covenant, Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36) it is motivated by His grace and mercy, apart from fallen humanity's ability to perform/conform/reform!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ "And You comfort me" This VERB (BDB 636, KB 688, Piel IMPERFECT) means "comfort," or "console" (cf. Isa. 22:4; 40:1; 51:3,12,19; 61:2; 66:13). After judgment comes comfort; after discipline fellowship is restored (i.e. Isa. 54:7-10)! There is hope for rebels and sinners in the unchanging merciful character of YHWH (cf. Mal. 3:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COMFORT

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. This (or these) hymns of praise closes out "Immanuel's book" (i.e. Isa. 7-12).

  2. Because the opening phrase, "on that day" is repeated in Isa. 12:4, some (JB, NASB Study Bible) think there are two hymns.
    1. Isa. 12:1-3, cf. Exod. 15:1-17; Psalm 118
    2. Isa. 12:4-6, cf. Ps. 105:1; 148:13

  3. It is similar to Exodus 15 (the song of Moses) and Psalm 118. Often at times of great victory or deliverance, Israel composed hymns of praise to their God.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 12:2 "God is my salvation"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:2 "God is my salvation" There is no VERB in this line of poetry, which intensifies the phrase.

The term "salvation" (BDB 447) denotes deliverance which comes from a compassionate God (cf. Exod. 15:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

▣ "I will trust" This VERB (BDB 105, KB 120, Qal IMPERFECT) denotes that which is firm (i.e. reliable) or "to fall prostrate before." This VERB expresses a confident reliance on God (cf. Isa. 26:3,4; Ps. 78:22).

▣ "and not be afraid" This VERB (BDB 808, KB 922, Qal IMPERFECT) is the opposite of trust (cf. Deut. 28:66; Isa. 44:8,11). Because they trust YHWH, there is no reason to fear His wrath, but rely on His covenant love and promises (cf. 1 John 4:17-18)!

▣ "the Lord God" This is two related titles for Deity.

  1. יה, BDB 219 a contraction of YHWH (cf. Exod. 17:16; Ps. 118:14; Isa. 26:4; 38:11)
  2. יהוה, BDB 217 (YHWH)

For a full discussion of the theories connected to the covenant name of God from the VERB "to be," see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "my strength and song" Like Isa. 12:2a, there is no VERB with these two NOUNS, which are pointed by the Masoretic scholars.

  1. strength, BDB 738, describes the "Servant" in Isa. 49:5 and Israel's praise in Ps. 81:1
  2. song, BDB 274 I; these same two NOUNS are found in Moses' song of victory in Exod. 15:2, also in Ps. 118:14

The meaning of the second NOUN, זמרה is uncertain (BDB 275 II).

  1. song, NASB, NKJV, NJB, Peshitta (BDB 274 I, KB 274 I)
  2. might, NRSV, TEV, JPSOA (KB 274 II)
  3. LXX has "my glory and my praise"
  4. REB has "my refuge and defense"
  5. the same form (זמרת) as here appears in Gen. 43:11, where it is translated "the best products of the land"

▣ It is surprising that line 1 seems to affirm something that line 4 sees as progressive. It Might be a continuing quote from Exod. 15:2 (cf. Ps. 118:14,21). Hebrew poetry is ambiguous.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY

entries.title: Isaiah 12:3 "you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:3 "you" The SINGULAR of Isa. 12:1-2 changes to the PLURAL of collective joy (cf. Isa. 12:4-6).

▣ "draw water" The VERB (BDB 980, KB 1367, Qal PERFECT with waw has two orientations.

  1. God's gift of life-giving water, so important to those who depend on agriculture and livestock. Good water was seen as a blessing from God (cf. Deuteronomy 27-29).
  2. Salvation/deliverance is described as an abundant source of water (cf. Isa. 48:18; Ps. 36:9; Jer. 2:13; 17:13).

▣ "from springs of salvation" Compare with Jer. 2:13.

entries.title: Isaiah 12:4 "call on His name"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:4 "call on His name" This phrase implies participation in a worship setting (cf. Gen. 4:26; 12:8; 21:33; 26:25; Exod. 34:5-7; Rom. 10:9-13). The name would represent His person, His character! By calling on Him we acknowledge our need for Him and our desire to be like Him and pleasing to Him. This phrase denotes a desire for fellowship (cf. Isa. 43:1; 45:3,4)!

The NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 150, has a good list related to YHWH's name.

  1. it can be praised, Joel 2:26
  2. it can be loved, Ps. 5:11
  3. it can be declared, Ps. 22:22
  4. it can be feared, Mal. 4:2
  5. it can be waited on, Ps. 52:9
  6. it can be proclaimed, Isa. 12:4
  7. it can be walked on, Mic. 4:5
  8. it can be blasphemed, Isa. 52:5
  9. it can be polluted, Jer. 34:16
  10. it can be profaned, Ezek. 36:21-23

God's people's words and lives reflect Him positively or negatively, but we do reflect Him (cf. Matt. 5:13-16)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 12:4-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:4-6 These verses list the things God's joyful, grateful people (cf. Isa. 12:6b) should do and why (Isa. 12:5b; 6b)

  1. give thanks, BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 12:1 (i.e. worship setting; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)
  2. call on His name, BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal IMPERATIVE (i.e. worship setting; see SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME)
  3. make known His deeds among the peoples, BDB 393, KB 390, HIphil IMPERATIVE
  4. make them remember that His name is exalted, BDB 269, KB 269, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  5. praise the Lord in song, BDB 274 I, KB 273, Piel IMPERATIVE (i.e. worship setting)
  6. let this be known through the earth, Kethiv (it is written) BDB 393, KB 390, Pual PARTICIPLE; Qere (it is read) BDB 393, KB 390, Hophal PARTICIPLE (Owens, Analytical Key has Hiphil PARTICIPLE)
  7. cry aloud, BDB 843, KB 1007, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 54:1
  8. shout for joy, BDB 943, KB 1247, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 54:1

Again, notice the missionary mandate (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 51:4-5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 12:5 "Let this be known throughout the earth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:5 "Let this be known throughout the earth" YHWH's goal is that all humans made in His image and likeness (cf. Gen. 1:26, 27); created for fellowship with Himself (cf. Gen 3:8), return to an intimate, daily faith relationship with their Creator! This is the goal of revelation (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:6-8; 60:1-3; 66:23; Ps. 22:27; 66:24; 86:8-10; Mic. 4:1-4; Mal. 1:11; John 3:16; 4:42; 1 Tim. 2:4; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:1; 4:14).

For "earth" see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 12:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
12:6 This verse is set in the temple in Jerusalem. The space between the wings of the two Cherubim over the Ark of the Covenant in the Holy of Holies was seen as YHWH's footstool, the place where heaven and earth met. This description parallels the child's name, "Immanuel," which means "God is with us." There is no greater blessing than the presence of YHWH and a personal relationship with Him!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

▣ "the Holy One of Israel" See notes at Isa. 1:11,24 and SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Isaiah 13 marks a new division in the book of Isaiah that extends through Isa. 21:17 and the subject/genre also continuing in Isa. 23:1-8. This section of Isaiah deals with judgment of the surrounding nations. It is a genre in and of itself. It is very similar to Jeremiah 46-51; Ezekiel 25-32; Amos 1-2; Obadiah, Nahum, and Zephaniah 2.

  2. YHWH addresses the surrounding nations, both large and small, through His prophet; messages they will never hear or respond to. This demonstrates His universal sovereignty (cf. Isa. 2:1-4; 9:7; 11:9)! He is King of the earth; Lord of creation (cf. LXX Deut. 32:8)!

  3. The nations addressed are
    1. Old Babylon (or Assyria using Babylonian throne name "King of Babylon"), Isa. 13:1-14:23
    2. Assyria, Isa. 14:24-27
    3. Philistia, Isa. 14:28-32
    4. Moab, Isa. 15:1-16:14
    5. Syria, Isa. 17:1-3
    6. Israel, Isa. 17:4-14
    7. Ethiopia (Cush), Isa. 18:1-7; 20:1-6
    8. Egypt, Isa. 19:1-25; 20:1-6
    9. Neo-Babylon, Isa. 21:1-10
    10. Edom, Isa. 21:11-12
    11. Arabia, Isa. 21:13-17
    12. Jerusalem, Isa. 22:1-25
    13. Tyre, Isa. 23:1-18

  4. You will notice that Assyria seems to break into the context in Isa. 14:24-27. It is surprising that
    1. Babylon is addressed first when the problem in Isaiah's day was Assyria.
    2. Babylon is addressed again in Isa. 21:1-10.
    3. Assyria is abruptly mentioned only briefly in Isa. 14:24-27 with no new heading (i.e. "oracle").

      One way to contextually deal with these problems is to view all of Isa. 13:1-14:27 as directed toward Assyria. Assyria completely subjected and conquered Babylon in 689 B.C. and her kings took the title of "king of Babylon" (cf. Isa. 14:4). If this is right then it is not Neo-Babylon (i.e. Nebuchadnezzar), but earlier Babylon (Merodach-baladan) that fell to Assyria in 729 B.C. and the capital city of Babylon sacked and destroyed in 689 B.C. The NASB Study Bible (p. 976) notes that there is no new "oracle" heading at Isa. 14:24, which implies one literary unit from Isa. 13:1-14:32.
       The one problem with this approach is that "the Medes," who destroyed Neo-Babylon in 539 B.C., are mentioned in Isa. 13:17. However, with the weakening of Assyria in 660 B.C., Media and Babylon combined to rebel against the declining empire under Ashurbanipal (IVP Bible Background Commentary, p. 601). The capital of Assyria fell to a combined army of Media and Babylon in 612 B.C.
      SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA
      SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF NEO-BABYLON

  5. This is a good place to show how the poetic sections switch from first person (prophet speaking for God) to the third person (the prophet speaking about God).
    1. Isa. 13:1-3, first person
    2. Isa. 13:4-10, third person
    3. Isa. 13:11-16, first person
    4. Isa. 13:17-18, first person
    5. Isa. 13:19-22, third person

      But, Isa. 13:13 and 19 show how hard it is to follow this structure. In reality the prophet moves freely back and forth to reveal the message "poetically" (word plays, line beat, rare words, change of person).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

13:1
NASB, NRSV, REB  "oracle"
NKJV  "burden"
TEV  "a message"
NJB  "proclamation"
LXX  "a vision"
Peshitta  "the prophecy"
JPSOA  "a prophecy"

This term (BDB 672, KB 639) can mean "burden" or "load." It is used eleven times in this section of Isaiah (Isaiah 13-23) to describe oracles of future doom on the nations surrounding Israel. The term may simply denote

  1. a voice lifted to proclaim a message
  2. a message carried by someone to a recipient
  3. an emotional heaviness associated with a judgment oracle
  4. in Jer. 23:33 it may refer to sinful Judeans

▣ "Babylon" This was an empire of the Fertile Crescent that affected the people of God. The first major world power of the Fertile Crescent to affect Israel was Assyria, then Neo-Babylon, then Medo-Persia. Babylon is used in the Bible as a symbol of oppression and cruelty (cf. 1 Pet. 5:13; Rev. 14:8; 16:19; 17:5). The downfall of Babylon is revealed in Isa. 13:1-14:23 (old Babylon) and 21:1-10 (new Babylon).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF NEO-BABYLON

▣ "which Isaiah son of Amoz saw" The immediate contemporary enemy of Israel and Judah in Isaiah's day was Assyria. But as a prophet of God he was shown ("saw," BDB 302, KB 301, Qal PERFECT, cf. Isa. 1:1; 2:1; 13:1; Amos 1:1; Mic. 1:1; Hab. 1:1) the future demise of old Babylon, Assyria, Neo-Babylon, and the rise of Cyrus the Great (cf. Isa. 13:17; 44:28-45:1). Those who deny predictive prophecy exhibit a bias that affects all their interpretations!

Predictive prophecy is the main evidence of a unique supernaturally-inspired Bible. See my sermons "The Trustworthiness of the Old Testament" and "The Trustworthiness of the New Testament" online at www.freebiblecommentary.org in the "Video Sermons" section under Lakeside Baptist church.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

entries.title: Isaiah 13:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:2 This describes the gathering of a mighty army (cf. Isa. 13:9). From Isa. 13:17 we learn that it is the army of (1) Assyria or (2) Medo-Persia under Cyrus II gathered by God to defeat either "old" or "new" Babylon (cf. Isa. 44:28; 45:1).

Remember, Isaiah is an anthology of Isaiah's messages, but not in chronological order and usually with no specific historical setting.

▣ "Lift up a standard on a bare hill" This describes how ancient armies communicated.

  1. banners, flags in easily visible places, cf. Isa. 5:26; 31:9; Jer. 51:12
  2. shouts (whistle, cf. Isa. 5:26)
  3. hand movements, cf. Isa. 10:32; 19:16

There is a series of IMPERATIVES denoting YHWH's will.

  1. lift up, BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. raise, BDB 926, KB 1202, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  3. wave, BDB 631, KB 682, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 10:32; 11:15; 19:16
  4. enter, BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERFECT, but used in a JUSSIVE sense (NEB changes vowels and translates it as "draw your swords, you nobles")

▣ "enter the doors of the nobles" This is imagery for a city's defeat and plunder (cf. Isa. 45:1e). The doors are imagery for security of a city or a house. Old Babylon will fall to Assyria.

entries.title: Isaiah 13:3 "I have commanded my consecrated ones"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:3 "I have commanded my consecrated ones" YHWH is in control of history! These Median warriors are not consecrated in a moral or religious sense. For the most part they are unknowing servants of YHWH "set apart" ("consecrated ones," BDB 872, KB 1073, Pual PARTICIPLE) to do His bidding. This same concept can be seen in Cyrus being called "My anointed" in Isa. 44:28; "His anointed" in Isa. 45:1.

The Jewish Study Bible footnotes from JPSOA sees "My consecrated ones" (i.e. "My purified one," a COLLECTIVE SINGULAR) as a reference to a sacrificial meal (i.e. the impending slaughter) where the guests are told to prepare themselves (cf. Zeph. 1:7; p. 809).

Another option is to see this poem as expressing "Holy War" terminology and if so, then these could refer to angels (cf. Josh. 5:13-15; see SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY ONES).

entries.title: Isaiah 13:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:4 This describes the sounds of battle and victory!

entries.title: Isaiah 13:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:5 YHWH is bringing large mercenary armies from the Fertile Crescent to punish His people in Canaan (cf. Isa. 5:26; 7:18).

NASB  "farthest horizons"
NKJV, Peshitta  "the end of heaven"
NRSV  "the end of the heavens"
TEV  "the ends of the earth"
NJB  "from the far horizons"
LXX  "from the utmost foundation of heaven"
JPSOA  "from the end of the sky"

The NRSV and JPSOA are the most literal. It (BDB 892 CONSTRUCT BDB 1029) denotes the place where the sun rises, therefore, to the east, the very direction of the homelands of the Mesopotamian powers.

entries.title: Isaiah 13:6 "Wail"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:6 "Wail" This term (BDB 410, KB 413, Hiphil IMPERATIVE) refers to howling, wailing. Orientals are much more expressive of emotions in grieving than westerners. This term is used often in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 13:6; 14:31; 15:2,3; 16:7 [twice]; 23:1,6,14; 52:5; 65:14) and also in Jeremiah (cf. Isa. 4:8; 25:34; 47:2; 48:20,31,39; 49:3; 51:8).

▣ "for the day of the Lord is near" The creator God is a moral, ethical God. He approaches His creation and creatures in light of His character. Sometimes He approaches for affirmation and blessing, but other times (as here) He approaches for judgment (cf. Lev. 26 and Deut. 27-29). All moral creatures must give an account both temporally and eschatologically (cf. Matt. 25:31-46; Rev. 20:11-15) to the One who gave them life!

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Day of the Lord (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

▣ "the Almighty" This is the Hebrew title Shaddai. This was the patriarchal name for YHWH (cf. Exod. 6:3). See SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADDAI

There is a sound play (BDB 994) between "destruction" (כשׁד, BDB 994) and "the Almighty" (משׁדי, BDB 994). Note the connection with Joel 1:15. These types of Hebrew sound plays are very common in Isaiah.

entries.title: Isaiah 13:7-8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:7-8 The approach of YHWH will cause certain fearful responses.

  1. "wail," Isa. 13:6
  2. "all hands will fall limp," Isa. 13:7, cf. Ezek. 7:17; 21:7
  3. "every man's heart will melt," Isa. 13:7, cf. Isa. 19:1; Nah. 2:10
  4. "they will be terrified," Isa. 13:8
  5. "pain and anguish will take hold of them," Isa. 13:8
  6. "writhe like a woman in labor," Isa. 13:8, cf. Isa. 21:3; 26:17; 66:7; see SPECIAL TOPIC: BIRTH PAINS
  7. "look at one another in astonishment," Isa. 13:8
  8. "their faces aflame," Isa. 13:8
13:8
NASB  "Their faces aflame"
NKJV, Peshitta  "Their faces will be like flames"
NRSV  "their face will be aflame"
TEV  "their faces will burn with shame"
NJB  "with feverish faces"
REB, JPSOA  "their faces livid with fear"
NET  "their faces are flushed red"
LXX  "they will change their face like a flame"

The MT has two NOUNS in CONSTRUCT and no VERB

  1. aflame ‒ BDB 815
  2. faces ‒ BDB 529

This phrase is in a series of descriptive phrases on the fear and anguish of those who experience YHWH's judgment.

entries.title: Isaiah 13:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:9 This verse describes the day of the Lord as it relates to sinners (cf. Isa. 13:10). Note the threefold characterization.

  1. cruel
  2. with fury
  3. burning anger

A wasted and unpopulated land is exactly opposite to God's will for His creation (cf. Genesis 1-2).

entries.title: Isaiah 13:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:10 The approach of YHWH to His physical creation causes reactions in nature. These reactions are often referred to as apocalyptic, but in reality they are simply imagery in the OT prophets and only turn to apocalyptic imagery in the inter-biblical period and NT.

  1. stars and constellations cease to shine (the ancients thought these were life-controlling deities), Isa. 13:10
  2. sun and moon grow dark, Isa. 13:10
  3. the heavens tremble, Isa. 13:13
  4. the earth will be shaken from its place, Isa. 13:13

The heavens, the abode of God, become dark and fearful (cf. Isa. 24:23; 34:4; Ezek. 32:7-8; Joel 2:10,31; 3:15; Matt. 24:29; Acts 2:20; Rev. 6:12-13). But there is a new light coming (cf. Isa. 2:5; 9:2; 60:1-3,19-20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: DARKNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIGHT

entries.title: Isaiah 13:11 "the world"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:11 "the world" This (BDB 385) is a poetic synonym for ארץ (BDB 75, KB 90, i.e. "land," "earth," cf. Isa. 14:21; 24:4; 34:1). It is obviously a hyperbole (or maybe not, cf. Isa. 12:5; 24:4; 34:1), but it does express the theological concept of YHWH the creator and controller of this planet!

Notice how humans are characterized.

  1. evil
  2. wicked for their iniquity
  3. arrogance of the proud
  4. haughtiness of the ruthless

These same attributes describe the covenant people in Isa. 2:9,11,17; 5:15! The deadly tentacles (i.e. self, sin) of the Fall are everywhere (also note Gen. 6:5,11; 8:21; Rom. 3:9-18)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH

SPECIAL TOPIC: WORLD (several terms)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

▣ Notice how the people of old Babylon, who do not have the Law of YHWH, are characterized.

  1. evil
  2. wicked
  3. iniquity
  4. arrogance of the proud
  5. haughtiness of the ruthless

Fallen mankind, without the knowledge of God, is trapped by sin, self, and pride!

entries.title: Isaiah 13:12 "Ophir"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:12 "Ophir" This refers geographically to southern Arabia or east Africa. It was a symbol of refined purity in metals (i.e. gold). The allusion here is that living human beings will be very scarce on the day of judgment.

entries.title: Isaiah 13:14-16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:14-16 This is a vivid description of the horrors of invasion.

  1. hunted like gazelles
  2. sheep with no shepherd
  3. flee to family and homeland
  4. inhabitants thrust through
  5. inhabitants fall by the sword
  6. little ones dashed to pieces in sight of their parents, cf. Isa. 13:18; 2 Kgs. 8:12; 15:16; Hosea 13:16; Nah. 3:10
  7. houses plundered
  8. wives ravished (NASB), cf. Deut. 28:30

Judgment by invasion was a terrible experience. These warlike nations gave this treatment and received this treatment (cf. Ps. 137:8-9)! The worst of these violent invading armies was Assyria.

entries.title: Isaiah 13:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 13:16 The MT has the VERB "ravish" (BDB 993, KB 1415, Niphal IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 28:30; Jer. 3:2; Zech. 14:2), but the Masoretes suggested it be read (Qere) as "be lain with" (BDB 1011, KB 1486, Niphal IMPERFECT, cf. LXX; Lev. 15:20; Deut. 22:27; Micah 7:5).

entries.title: Isaiah 13:17 "the Medes"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:17 "the Medes" This is another major power of the Fertile Crescent north and east of Assyria. At first they were allied with "old" Babylon, but later they were incorporated with Persia under Cyrus II (cf. Isa. 44:28; 45:1; Jer. 51:11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF PERSIA

▣ "Who will not value silver or take pleasure in gold" This army will be so bent on revenge there will be no possibility of buying them off!

entries.title: Isaiah 13:18 "the fruit of the womb"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:18 "the fruit of the womb" This refers to unborn children and their mothers or young childen.

▣ "eye" It is used here to represent the attitudes/actions of a person (cf. Deut. 7:16; 13:8; 19:13; Ezek. 7:4; 16:5; 20:17). Here to denote that the invaders will have no pity even on children. This line of poetry is parallel with the line above!

The Median warriors had no compassion or pity (cf. Jer. 6:23; 21:7; 50:42).

entries.title: Isaiah 13:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:19 Old Babylon's cultural beauty and sophistication were renowned (i.e. Daniel 4 of Neo-Babylon), but it will all be lost and destroyed! However, if this refers to Babylon during the Assyrian period, it was totally destroyed in 689 B.C. by the Assyrian king, Sennacherib.

▣ "Chaldeans" This was the name of the tribe towards the mouth of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. The term is used in several senses. It is often used as a synonym for later nations (i.e. Neo-Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS.

▣ "Sodom and Gomorrah" These were cities of great wickedness, which God destroyed by fire and brimstone (cf. Gen. 19:24-28; Deut. 29:23).

entries.title: Isaiah 13:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:20 The destruction was so complete that

  1. it was uninhabited for generations
  2. Arabs do not camp there
  3. no flocks grazed there
  4. building remains used only by wild animals (possibly demons, cf. Isa. 13:21-22; 34:11-15; Rev. 18:2)
  5. no longer a national entity

This fits "old" Babylon better than "new" Babylon. The Medes abandoned their alliance with Merodach-baladan and joined the Assyrians in destroying the capital city of Old Babylon in 689 B.C.

entries.title: Isaiah 13:20-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:20-22 This is hyperbolic language describing cursed and deserted places (cf. Sumerian laments over Ur and visions of Nefertiti over the old Egyptian Kingdom). The city fell in Merodach-baladan's day to Assyria with total destruction. The city fell to the Medo-Persian army in 539 B.C. without widespread destruction.

The book that has really helped me, as a modern western person, to understand eastern prophetic and apocalyptic literature is D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic.

entries.title: Isaiah 13:21 "desert creatures"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
13:21 "desert creatures" Often the ruins of deserted cities or desert areas were considered to be haunts of the deomonic.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 14:1 "the Lord will have compassion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:1 "the Lord will have compassion" This VERB (BDB 933, KB 1216, Piel IMPERFECT, cf. Isa. 49:13,15; 54:7-8) denotes YHWH's special relationship with His covenant people (cf. Hosea 1-2; 11:8-11). This special relationship is also seen in the VERB "choose" (BDB 103, KB 119, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Isa. 41:8,9; 44:1; 49:7). In Isa. 9:17 Israel's God will have no compassion on His covenant people and in Isa. 13:18 the Medes will have no compassion on Old Babylon, but YHWH will again restore His unique relationship with Abraham's seed!

After YHWH uses the powers of Mesopotamia to punish His covenant people's disobedience, He will instigate a "new exodus."

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

▣ "Jacob. . .Israel" These two terms could be used for both the Northern Ten Tribes and the Southern Two Tribes being united again.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

entries.title: Isaiah 14:1-2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:1-2 There are two options for interpreting Isa. 14:1-2:

  1. either Isa. 14:1 and 2 go together and describe the same group (i.e. strangers. . .peoples)
  2. or Isa. 14:1 describes the blessings of non-Jews (i.e. strangers) and Isa. 14:2 describes the defeated enemies of Israel as being their servants

It is difficult in Isaiah and Micah to balance YHWH's attitude and actions towards the nations.

  1. He loves them and includes them into His covenant people (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 11:10, see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)
  2. He judges them and puts them in servitude (i.e. Isa. 60:10; 61:5)

Somehow both are true! The prophets move back and forth, often in the same context, between these two poles. Option #1 reflects Genesis 1-3; 12:3, while option #2 reflects Israel's history in Canaan.

In Isaiah the nations return the covenant people to their land (i.e. Canaan) and become one with them in the worship of YHWH (cf. Isa. 49:22; 60:4-9,10-14; 66:20). This may reflect the "new exodus." Many foreign people left Egypt with Israel and others joined her along the way (wilderness wanderings and conquest). Maybe the imagery of Isa. 14:2 reflects this. If so, it would solve the problem of #2 above.
