* Although they are not inspired, paragraph divisions are the key to understanding and following the original author's intent. Each modern translation has divided and summarized the paragraphs. Every paragraph has one central topic, truth, or thought. Each version encapsulates that topic in its own distinct way. As you read the text, ask yourself which translation fits your understanding of the subject and verse divisions.

In every chapter we must read the Bible first and try to identify its subjects (paragraphs), then compare our understanding with the modern versions. Only when we understand the original author's intent by following his logic and presentation can we truly understand the Bible. Only the original author is inspired—readers have no right to change or modify the message. Bible readers do have the responsibility of applying the inspired truth to their day and their lives.

Note that all technical terms and abbreviations are explained fully in the following Special Topics: Hebrew Grammatical Tems, Glossary, and Abbreviations.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Isaiah lived in the 8th century B.C. (the enemy was Assyria), yet Isaiah 40-66 fits into the historical setting of the return from Babylonian exile under Zerubbabel and Joshua recorded in Ezra 1-6, following the decree of Cyrus II in 538 B.C. (6th century B.C.) to allow all exiled people groups to return home and rebuild their national temples, so that each people group could pray for the Persian Empire..

  2. The book of Isaiah is a literary unity. God revealed His future plans to his faithful messenger. I reject the theory of two or three authors. I believe that the book was edited or compiled but that it is all inspired revelation through Isaiah.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: ISAIAH (authorship and unity)

  3. God had not forgotten His covenant promises, but He had established a new covenant by means of exile (cf. Jer. 31:31-34). His covenant people could not/did not keep His covenant (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30:15,19). This new covenant is ultimately defined in the life, ministry, death, and resurrection of Jesus.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

  4. The historical return from Neo-Babylon does not exhaust this prophecy. The ultimate focus of chapters 40-66 is the first and second comings of Messiah.
     Chapter 40 forms an introduction to the unique Messianic passages known as "the Servant Songs" (cf. Isa. 42:1-9; 49:1-7; 50:4-11; 52:13-53:12).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH
    SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

  5. As Isaiah 1-39 deals with Assyrian and Babylonian exiles, Isaiah 40-66 speaks to those who are returning to Judah and Jerusalem under Cyrus II's decree and the leadership of Ezra, Nehemiah, Zerubbabel, and Joshua. The geography of the audience has changed!

  6. Isaiah1:1-11 serves as an introduction and summary of the entire section. A new day has come!

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 40:3 "Clear the way"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:3 "Clear the way" This VERB (BDB 815, KB 937, Piel IMPERATIVE) basically means "turn," but here it is used in a specialized sense of "clear the path of objects" (cf. Isa. 40:3; 42:16; 49:11; 57:14; 62:10; Mal. 3:1).

The concept of "a highway of holiness" on which God's people (returning exiles) came to Him (i.e. to His temple) is recurrent in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 11:16; 26:7; 35:8; 40:3; 42:16).

In this context it is YHWH Himself who is returning to His people. They are to prepare the way, which denotes a spiritual/physical preparation.

This verse was John the Baptist's self-designation (cf. Matt. 3:3; Mark 1:3; Luke 3:4-6). This section is reflected in Zech. 14:10, where leveling of the physical terrain to Jerusalem is used as imagery for access to God (cf. Mal. 3:1; 4:5,6). It could be characterized as "prepare the road" for a royal visit.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "the Lord" This is a reference to YHWH. See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "in the wilderness" Ezekiel saw God's glory leaving the temple in Jerusalem and moving east (cf. Ezek. 10:18-19; 11:22-23; 43:1-3) because of Israel's idolatry (cf. Ezek. 8). God went with the exiles and this verse refers to His returning to Judah and Jerusalem.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:4 This context refers to a preparation by God's people for His return to Jerusalem. He will be accompanied by the returning exiles. He will protect, provide, and care for them (cf. Isa. 40:9-11). This is an extension and description of making a highway in the wilderness. It is imagery for people easily and freely coming to God. God has provided a new way (i.e. the new covenant, cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36). This new way is depicted as the new exodus

  1. here from physical exile
  2. imagery for the end-time recreation

For a good list of YHWH's actions toward His people, see note at Isa. 32:20.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:5 "the glory of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:5 "the glory of the Lord" The glory of the Lord is another link to Isaiah 6 (i.e. Isa. 40:3). Chapter 40 is functioning as a second call to Isaiah. See note at Isa. 40:25.

This is an allusion to "the cloud of glory" which appeared in the exodus and wilderness wanderings as a symbol of YHWH's personal presence. The rabbis called it the Shekinah, from the Hebrew term "to dwell" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH). The returning Jews needed the reassurance of God's continuing personal presence (i.e. Immanuel, Isa. 7:14; cf. Exod. 13:21-22; 14:19). A new exodus has come!

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT).

▣ "all flesh will see it together" "Flesh" (BDB 142) means human persons (cf. Isa. 40:7). This is the universal element so common in Isaiah. The good news for Israel has become good news for all people (i.e. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:6; 51:4-5; 52:10; 60:1-3; 66:23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "the mouth of the Lord has spoken" This is the Hebrew idiom for the power of the spoken word of YHWH (cf. Isa. 40:8; Gen. 1:3,6,9,11,14,20,26 and Isa. 55:11). What He wills, will be!

entries.title: Isaiah 40:6 "Call out"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:6 "Call out" See note at Isa. 40:1.

NASB  "he answered"
NKJV, Peshitta  "he said"
NRSV, NJB, LXX  "I said"
TEV, REB, DSS  "I asked"
JPSOA  "another asks"

Notice that two voices are involved. The UBS Text Project, p. 99, gives "he said" a "C" rating (considerable doubt). Following DSS, LXX it may be an angel or the Spirit speaking to Isaiah or Isaiah himself speaking (NRSV, NJB, LXX).

▣ "All flesh is grass" This recurrent imagery refers to the frailty and transitoriness of human corporal existence compared to the eternality of God (cf. Gen. 6:3; Job 10:4; 14:1-2; Ps. 78:39; 90:5-6; 103:15-18; 1 Pet.1:24-25).

To whom is the voice speaking?

  1. all humans
  2. world powers

It seems to be God's message to human governments. They may be temporarily powerful, but in time and in reality (i.e. in light of God's power) they are not!!

▣
NASB, NKJV  "loveliness"
NRSV, TEV  "constancy"
NJB, Peshitta  "beauty"
JPSOA  "goodness"
LXX  "glory of man"

This is translated from the Hebrew word hesed (cf. BDB 338, I, #4). This term is often used of God's covenant love and loyalty.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

entries.title: Isaiah 40:7-8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:7-8 All of the VERBS are PERFECT (i.e. completed action) except the concluding statement, "the word of our God stands forever" (IMPERFECT).

This was the truth that the returning exiles needed. It seemed that God's word of care and protection had failed (i.e. 2 Sam. 7; 1 Chr. 17)! However, the problem was not God's word, but God's sinful people! The curses of Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28 had been carried out as promised.

40:7
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, JPSOA, LXX, Peshitta  "the breath"
REB  "blast"
LXX  "word"

This Hebrew term ruah (BDB 924) can mean "wind," "breath," or "spirit."

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT

entries.title: Isaiah 40:8 "the word of our God stands forever"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:8 "the word of our God stands forever" God's promises are sure, even amidst divine discipline (cf. Ps. 103:17-18; Isa. 55:8-11; 59:21; Jer. 29:10; Matt. 5:17-20; 24:35). This statement is the confident faith hope/assurance of every believer. This phrase (BDB 182 CONSTRUCT BDB 43) is parallel to the breath of the Lord in v. 7.

For "forever," see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLICAL CONCEPT OF "FOREVER", II.
SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

entries.title: Isaiah 40:9 "a high mountain, O Zion. . .O Jerusalem"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:9 "a high mountain, O Zion. . .O Jerusalem" Both of these terms refer to Jerusalem. The temple was built on Mt. Moriah but the term "Zion" (another hill in the city where David built his palace) is an idiom for the whole city.

Who do these personifications refer to?

  1. God's prophets
  2. God's Levitical teachers
  3. the herald of the new age (i.e. John the Baptist)

Does this refer to

  1. return from Babylonian exile (i.e. Isa. 52:7-9; 62:10-12)
  2. Maccabean victories
  3. the first coming of Jesus (Isa. 62:11 quoted in Matt. 21:5)
  4. the second coming of Jesus (Isa. 40:10; 62:11, alluded to in Rev. 22:12)

There is a fluidity between (1) God's promise of restoration to Israel and (2) the new age in Christ. Here is where the mega-narrative must include the NT. Jesus fulfills these hopes, but the two comings of Christ (Savior, later King) causes a twofold fulfillment. These prophecies of the eschaton are still future. They were surely not fulfilled in the return of Zerubbabel and Joshua in 539 b.c. and not in the lifetime of Jesus of Nazareth.

Just one more thought, the paragraph, Isa. 40:9-11, is the proclamation of a "watchman" to a city of an approaching group/person/army. However, notice the powerful one (i.e. YHWH) comes, not as an invader but as a compassionate Shepherd. He comes to save, protect, and provide. The Shepherd of Israel (Psalm 23) returns to His land/people whom He abandoned because of their rebellion in Ezekiel 8-10!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, JERUSALEM, ZION

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE END-TIME EVENTS SO CONTROVERSIAL?

SPECIAL TOPIC: THIS AGE AND THE AGE TO COME

▣ "good news" This is the VERB בשׁר (BDB 142, KB 163; Piel PARTICIPLE) which means "bear glad tidings." Here it denotes the merciful message of YHWH's redemption and acceptance (cf. Isa. 40:9 [twice]; 41:27; 52:7 [twice]; 61:1; Nahum 1:15). Paul quotes Isa. 52:7 in Rom. 10:15 and relates it to Christ (Rom. 10:16 quotes Isa. 53:1). The gospel of Jesus Christ is characterized as "good news" in the NT.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

▣ "do not fear" This VERB (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT) is JUSSIVE in meaning, referring to Jerusalem (i.e. YHWH's people). Sin causes fear! How often God says "fear not" to His people! (cf. Isa. 41:10,13.14; 43:1,5; 44:2,8 [different words]; 51:7,12; 54:4,14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

▣ "Say to the cities of Judah" Judah's cities are personified. Those who hold to a later, post-exilic writer instead of Isaiah have trouble explaining this reference because all of the cities were destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar II in 586 B.C.

▣ "Here is your God" God is with His people (i.e. Immanuel, Isa. 7:14)! The wait is over (cf. Isa. 25:9; 26:8; 33:2; 40:31; 49:23; 51:5; 60:9)!

entries.title: Isaiah 40:10 "the Lord God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:10 "the Lord God" Literally this is "Adonai YHWH," which is literally translated "My Lord, Lord" (see Ps. 110:1, where both titles are used). "Lord" is the Hebrew word adon, which denotes master, owner, husband, lord.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)

▣ "With His arm ruling for Him" This is a Semitic anthropomorphic imagery for divine action and power. From Isa. 9:6-7; 11:1-5; and Micah 5:2-5a, we know this refers to the agency of the Messiah (cf. Psalm 110).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

▣ "His reward is with Him

  And His recompense before Him" This exact phrase is also found in Isa. 62:11 and alluded to in Rev. 22:12.

Verse 10 is speaking of the personal presence of Deity (41:10a). Immanuel has come (cf. Isa. 7:14)!

entries.title: Isaiah 40:11 "Like a shepherd"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 40:11 "Like a shepherd" YHWH, the mighty (cf. Isa. 40:10), is also a Shepherd (cf. Psalm 23; 80:1; Jer. 23:1-6; 31:10; Ezek. 34:11-16). Notice that also in Ezek. 34:23-24, YHWH appoints His Messiah to represent Himself! Jesus is the "good Shepherd" (cf. John 10). He is the "wounded" shepherd of Zechariah 11-12 and Isa. 52:13-53:12.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:12 "Who has measured the waters"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:12 "Who has measured the waters" All of the verbs of Isa. 40:12 are perfect (i.e. completed action). This is a series of questions which expect a "no" answer. It is similar to the book of Job 38-41, where God answered Job's questions by asserting His sovereignty and authority.

Notice the parallelism.

  1. measured ‒ BDB 551, KB 547]
  2. marked off ‒ BDB 1067, KB 1733
  3. calculated ‒ BDB 465, KB 463
  4. weighed ‒ BDB 1053, KB 1642

These are all symbolic actions of the Creator. The creation account of Genesis 1 is also imagery of God's control, ordering and maintaining the universe. I hope you will look at my exegetical verse-by-verse commentary on Gen. 1-11 online. Two new good books are John H. Walton, The Lost World of Genesis One and Genesis 1 As Ancient Cosmology.

▣ "span" For human body parts used to measure see SPECIAL TOPIC: CUBIT.

▣
NASB  "by the measure"
NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta  "in a measure"
REB  "in a bushel"
TEV  "in a cup"
NJB  "to the nearest bushel"
LXX  "in a handful"
JPSOA  "with a measure"

The term (BDB 1026 I) is found only here and in Ps. 80:6. Its basic meaning is "one third," but it does not specify of what unit of measurement. Most scholars assume it refers to a third of an ephah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES

entries.title: Isaiah 40:12-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:12-17 Verses 9-11 describe the message of YHWH's personal presence as Savior, while verses 12-17 describe Him (Elohim) as Creator.

  1. measured the waters (i.e. creator, controller, and organizer of water, fresh and salt), Isa. 40:12
  2. designed the atmosphere of this planet, Isa. 40:12
  3. ordered the dry land ("calculated the dust" and "weighed the mountains. . .hill" [Hebrew parallelism]"), Isa. 40:12
  4. directed the Spirit as agent, without counsel, Isa. 40:13-14
  5. in comparison with Elohim's creative power and intellect, humans are nothing (cf. Isa. 40:6-8, this is similar to Job 38-41), Isa. 40:15-17

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS/SEA

SPECIAL TOPIC: CIRCLE OF THE EARTH

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:13 "Who has directed the Spirit of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:13 "Who has directed the Spirit of the Lord" Verses 13 and 14 are parallel. This is not a Trinitarian passage but an OT passage, much like Genesis 1:2, which speaks of "the Spirit" as God's personal presence.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:13-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:13-14 The "who" of these verses may link back to the PLURALS of Isa. 40:1-3. If so, they relate to the heavenly council. These angelic servants can be seen in

  1. the "Us" passages of Genesis 1:26; 3:22; 11:7
  2. 1 Kings 22:19-23
  3. Job 1:6-12; 2:1-6,7
  4. Daniel 7:10,26

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

entries.title: Isaiah 40:14 "And who taught Him in the path of justice"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:14 "And who taught Him in the path of justice" Notice the parallelism. "Path" is the OT background to the NT concept of "The Way," which was used of the early church in Acts. This speaks of biblical faith as lifestyle fellowship with God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGE, JUDGMENT, AND JUSTICE (טפת) IN ISAIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ This verse in essence is asserting monotheism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:15-17 "the nations are like a drop from a bucket. . .a speck of dust on the scales. . .all nations are as nothing before Him"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:15-17 "the nations are like a drop from a bucket. . .a speck of dust on the scales. . .all nations are as nothing before Him" This is an emphasis on God's power (cf. Jer. 10:10), not on His lack of care or compassion for the nations. YHWH sent Jesus for the redemption of the whole human race. However, rebellious nations will be judged (cf. Isa. 17:13; 29:5,7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 40:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 40:16 The point of this verse is that even a place (i.e. Lebanon) which is heavily forested and full of wild animals would not provide an adequate sacrifice to the greatness of Israel's covenant God. For a similar extravagant attempt at an adequate sacrifice note 1 Kgs. 8:63.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:17 Notice the threefold characterization of organized human society (like Gen. 10-11).

  1. as nothing ‒ BDB 34 II
  2. less than nothing ‒ BDB 67 II
  3. meaningless ‒ BDB 1062
▣
NASB  "meaningless"
NKJV  "worthless"
NRSV, NJB  "emptiness"
LXX, Peshitta, JPSOA, REB  "nothing"
NET  "absolutely nothing"

This word, תהו (BDB 1062), is used of the formless earth in Gen. 1:2 (cf. Isa. 34:11; 45:18; Jer. 4:23). It is also used of the non-existence of idols (1 Sam. 12:21; Isa. 41:29; 44:9).

Isaiah uses it in this same chapter for the nothingness of human rulers (i.e. Egypt, Assyria, Babylon, Persia, and all enemies of God's people). Human organization and power are incomparable to YHWH's power and plan (i.e. Ps. 8).

entries.title: Isaiah 40:18 "To whom then will you liken God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:18 "To whom then will you liken God" This is the expression (cf. Isa. 40:25; 46:5; Exod. 8:10; 15:11; 1 Sam. 2:2; Mic. 7:18) of the Jews' major theological affirmation about the uniqueness of Israel's God, which we call monotheism (cf. Deut. 6:4-5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "Or what likeness will you compare with Him" This question goes back to YHWH revealing Himself to Moses and Israel on Mt. Sinai. He demanded that He not be visualized with any form. He is the ever present, invisible God of creation (cf. Exod. 20:4; Lev. 26:1; Deut. 4:15-19).

40:19
NASB  "fashions"
NKJV, NRSV, NJB, NET  "casts"
TEV  "set"
REB  "fits"
JPSOA  "forging"
LXX, Peshitta  "made"

This VERB (BDB 864, KB 1057, Qal PARTICIPLE) is used twice and refers to smelting metal into a specific form (cf. Isa. 41:7; 46:6). The NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 1000, prefers "forging" rather than the common translation "casting," because of the Hebrew synonymous parallelism,

entries.title: Isaiah 40:18-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 40:18-20 This section deals with the folly of idolatry similar to Isa. 44:9-20 and 46:1-7.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:20 "a tree"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 40:20 "a tree" This word (BDB 781) is used of a type of wood out of which idols are made (cf. Isa. 44:19; 45:20; Hosea 4:12). It may have been an especially hard wood but in time it would decay!

entries.title: Isaiah 40:21 "Do you not know"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:21 "Do you not know" This series of questions, like Isa. 40:28, is meant to remind the seed of Abraham of YHWH's previous revelations to them.

▣ "from the foundations of the earth" In context this is another allusion to creation (i.e. parallel "from the beginning"). Interestingly, a similar phrase is repeated five times in the NT referring to YHWH's actions before creation.

  1. Matt. 25:34 ‒ "inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundations of the world"
  2. John 17:24 ‒ "for You did love Me before the foundations of the world"
  3. Eph. 1:4 ‒ "He chose us in Him before the foundations of the world"
  4. 1 Pet. 1:19-20 ‒ He was foreknown before the foundation of the world"
  5. Rev. 13:8 (possible object)
    1. "everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world"
    2. "the Lamb who has been slain before the foundation of the world"

God was active before, in, and after physical creation. He was active in Adam, Noah, Abraham, Jacob, Israel, and Christ for the redemption of all humans.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BEGINNING (physical and spiritual)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 40:21-26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 40:21-26 This strophe is theologically related to Isa. 40:12-17. They both describe God as Creator, all else is small and insignificant in comparison. He is the only reality, the only truth, the only living One! Idols have no existence and humans have existence only by His will! But amazingly He wills to know those who believe and obey. What a God! Who is like Him?

entries.title: Isaiah 40:22 "It is He who sits above the circle of the earth. . .curtain. . .tent"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:22 "It is He who sits above the circle of the earth. . .curtain. . .tent" This is a common ancient Middle Eastern concept (cf. Isa. 42:5; Job 9:8; Ps. 104:2; Jer. 10:12; 51:15; Zech. 12:1). In the Egyptian Book of the Dead, heaven is described as a "skin." In the Rig Veda heaven is described as "stretched out like a hide." This is simply imagery for the vault of the heaven (i.e. the atmosphere of this planet) above the earth. It is phenomenological language (i.e. the way things appear to the five senses).

The term translated "curtain" (BDB 201) is used in this sense only here. The word means "to crush" (cf. Isa. 40:15, "fine dust"). Apparently it can also refer to something "thin" (KB 229, i.e. the dome that covers the earth). Remember interpreters look at

  1. the context
  2. other Hebrew roots
  3. cognate languages

but #1 has priority!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: CIRCLE OF THE EARTH

40:25 "the Holy One" See full note at Isa. 6:3 (see Isaiah 1-39, online free at www.freebiblecommentary.org). This title is another purposeful connection between the first call of Isaiah, where he is told Israel will not listen until destruction (cf. Isa. 6:9-11) and this second call, where he is told to "speak kindly" to her. She will listen now!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

entries.title: Isaiah 40:26 "Lift up your eyes. . .see"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:26 "Lift up your eyes. . .see" These are both Qal IMPERATIVES. Notice the parallel lines of Isa. 40:26 a,b.

▣ "And see who has created these stars. . .He calls all by name. . .not one of them is missing" This verse is very significant in light of Babylonian astral worship. Israel's God is depicted as the only creator, sustainer, and manipulator of the heavenly bodies (cf. Gen. 1:16; Ps. 8:3; Jer. 31:35).

The term "created" (BDB135, KB153, Qal PERFECT) is used in Genesis 1 of God creating. It is never used of anything or anyone except the creation of God. It occurs 20 times in Isaiah 40-66 (cf. Isa. 40:26,28; 41:20; 42:5; 43:1,7,15; 45:7 [twice],8,12,18 [twice]; 48:7; 54:16 [twice]; 57:19; 65:17,18 [twice]).

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord of Hosts

▣ "Not one of them is missing" This is a Hebrew idiom which means "not one of them fails to report to muster." YHWH controls the stars, planets, and comets. They are not gods. As the plagues of the Exodus depreciate the Egyptian gods, so too, this context and Genesis 1 depreciate the astral deities of the ANE.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:27 "Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:27 "Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name).

▣ "My way is hidden from the Lord,
  And the justice due me escapes the notice of my God"

The Israelites (i.e. "O Jacob. . .O Israel") felt that YHWH had abandoned them (cf. Isa. 49:14). YHWH had hid His face from them for a period (cf. Isa. 1:15; 8:17; 54:8; Romans 9-11).

entries.title: Isaiah 40:28
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:28 Notice the titles for God.

  1. the Everlasting God ‒ Gen. 21:33 and note Exod. 15:18; Deut. 32:40; Ps. 90:2; Jer. 10:10; see SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)
  2. the Lord ‒ YHWH (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)
  3. the Creator ‒ (this has been the thrust of chapter 40; see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.)
  4. also called "the Holy One" in Isa. 40:25 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE)

The God of promise is now again the God of presence!

▣ "Does not become weary or tired" This is a Hebrew imagery which means

  1. "He does not lose patience."
  2. He does not grow weary, as the ANE gods did

There is a word play related to "tiredness," "weariness" in Isa. 40:28-31.

  1. Isa. 40:28 ‒ weary, BDB 419, KB 421
    tired, BDB 388, KB 386
  2. Isa. 40:30 ‒ weary, BDB 419, KB 421
    tired, BDB 388, KB 386
  3. Isa. 40:30 ‒ stumble, INFINITIVE and IMPERFECT VERB (BDB 505, KB 502)
  4. Isa. 40:31 ‒ tired, BDB 388, KB 386
  5. weary, BDB 419, KB 421

YHWH brings strength and stability to those who wait on and trust in Him! The vitality of YHWH is transferred to His people (cf. Isa. 40:29-31). They are potent because He is potent!

NASB  "inscrutable"
NKJV, JPSOA, LXX  "no searching His understanding"
NRSV  "unsearchable"
NJB  "beyond fathoming"
JPSOA, REB, Peshitta  "cannot be fathomed"

The Hebrew word (BDB 350) basically means to search out. Here it is negated (cf. Job 5:9; 9:10; 36:26; Ps. 145:3). Paul expresses the same truth in Rom. 11:33 and quotes Isa. 40:13-14.

God is in control! His ways are sure and thought through (cf. Isa. 55:9-11). There are no surprises, no mistakes! He loves us, He is with us, He is for us (cf. Isa. 40:29-31)!

entries.title: Isaiah 40:29 "He gives strength to the weary"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 40:29 "He gives strength to the weary" YHWH comforts the very ones He judged (cf. Isa. 41:10; Ps. 107:9; Jer. 31:25). This is very similar to Jesus' statement, "Come unto Me, all who are weary and heavy-laden, and I will give you rest" in Matt. 11:28-30.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:30 "vigorous young men"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:30 "vigorous young men" This refers to the young men chosen for military service.

▣ "stumble badly" This is a Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a Niphal IMPERFECT of the same root (BDB 505, KB 502), which intensifies the concept.

entries.title: Isaiah 40:31 "wait"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
40:31 "wait" This is a Hebrew word (BDB 875, KB 1082, Qal PARTICIPLE) that speaks of active anticipation. It is used of

  1. farmers waiting for a crop (cf. Isa. 5:4,7)
  2. robbers waiting in ambush (cf. Ps. 56:6; 119:95)
  3. God's people waiting for Him (cf. Isa. 8:17; 25:9; 30:18; 33:2)

▣ "Will gain new strength" This VERB (BDB 322, KB 321, Hiphil IMPERFECT) means

  1. to exchange ‒ Lev. 27:10
  2. to change ‒ Gen. 31:7,41; 35:2
  3. to cause to succeed ‒ Isa. 40:31

▣ "like eagles" This term (BDB 676) could refer to several birds of prey, not just eagles. See UBS Fauna anda Flora of the Bible, pp. 82-88.

The Jewish Study Bible (p. 864) says there was a popular belief that when eagles molted they gained new strength as if younger (cf. Ps. 103:5).

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 41:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:1 Verse 1 is a literary technique used often in the OT (i.e. a court scene, cf. Isa. 1:18-20; 43:26; 50:8; Hosea 4; Micah 6). YHWH brings the nations, and in Isa. 41:21, their idols before His judgment seat.

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA  "coastlands"
TEV  "distant lands"
NJB, REB  "coasts and islands"
LXX  "O islands"
Peshitta  "O you islands"

The word (BDB 15) means "coast" or "region." Isaiah uses it often to refer to Gentile nations in the Mediterranean area (cf. Isa. 11:11; 24:15; 41:1,5; 42:4,10,12; 49:1; 51:5; 59:18; 60:9; 66:19).

It is parallel to "peoples" (BDB 522, cf. Isa. 49:1). It seems that the nation of Edom is used as a symbol for all "rebellious nations" (i.e. 34:5-17; 63:1-6; Jer. 49:7-22; Lam. 4:21-22; Ezek. 25:12-14; 35:1-15; Obadiah, Mal. 1:2-4). In Isaiah this term often stands for Gentile nations, like Philistia and Phoenicia (cf. Isa. 23:2-6).

▣ "in silence" This is another term related to a court scene (cf. Hab. 2:20; Zech. 2:13). There is nothing to say in light of YHWH's presence and power.

▣ "gain new strength" It is surprising (and uncertain in meaning) that the same VERB (BDB 322, KB 321, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) used of God's people in Isa. 40:31, is now used for "the peoples" (i.e. Gentiles).

▣ "come forward" This VERB, "draw near" (BDB 620, KB 670, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) can be used of priests approaching YHWH in sacrifice and worship, but here it is approaching the judge for a defense (cf. Isa. 34:1; 48:16).

41:2
NASB, NRSV, JPSOA, LXX  "has aroused"
NKJV, REB  "has raised up"
TEV  "brought"
NJB  "has raised"
Peshitta  "has stirred up"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 734, KB 802, Hiphil PERFECT), which expresses YHWH's activity in history.

  1. used of YHWH Himself ‒ Deut. 32:11; Isa. 42:13; 51:5
  2. used of Assyria ‒ 1 Chr. 5:26
  3. used of Neo-Babylon's enemies ‒ Jer. 50:9; 51:1
  4. used of Medo-Persia ‒ Ezra 1:1; Isa. 13:17; 41:25; 45:13; Dan. 11:2
  5. other nations
    1. Philistia ‒ 2 Chr. 21:16
    2. against Judah ‒ Ezek. 23:22
      for Judah ‒ Haggai 1:14

▣ "one from the east" This refers to Cyrus II (cf. "one from the north," Isa. 41:25). He is mentioned specifically by name in Isa. 44:28; 45:1. Cyrus II, known as Cyrus the Great

  1. became King of Anshan in 558 B.C.
  2. gained control of Media in 550 B.C.
  3. controlled Lydia in 546 B.C.
  4. controlled Neo-Babylon in 539 B.C.
  5. issued a decree in 538 B.C. that all the deported people groups exiled by Assyria and Babylon could go home, including the Jews

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF PERSIA

▣ "Whom He calls in righteousness" The JPSOA translates this by uniting the thoughts of lines 1 and 2, "who has roused a victor (BDB 841) from the east."

The Jewish Study Bible (864) mentions that the Targums translate this so as to refer to Abraham whom YHWH called from Ur of the Chaldees (i.e. Gen. 15:6, where the same root, BDB 842, is used of Abraham). If so, then the military part of Isa. 41:2 would refer to Genesis 14, Abraham's defeat of the kings.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "to His feet" It must be remembered that the Ark of the Covenant was viewed as the footstool for YHWH's feet (i.e. 1 Chr. 28:2; Ps. 132:7; Isa. 66:1) and, thereby, His presence. This is an anthropomorphic phrase.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "He" Notice all the things that YHWH does for Cyrus II.

  1. arouses from the east
  2. calls in righteousness
  3. delivers up nations before him
  4. subdues kings
    1. like dust
    2. like chaff

Verse 3 describes the swiftness of his victories. Verse 4 describes the Lord who accomplishes the victories for His own purposes of redemption and restoration for His people.

NASB  "subdues"
NKJV  "rule over"
NRSV, JPSOA  "tramples"
TEV  "victory"
NJB  "subjects"
REB  "overthrowing"
Peshitta  "confounded"

The problem is the rare VERB (BDB 921, KB 1190, Hiphil jussive). It basically means "have dominion over" or "rule" (NKJV). This does not seem to fit the context, so the various options. The VERB must refer to Cyrus.

41:3
NASB  "traversing with his feet"
NKJV  "he had not gone with his feet"
NRSV, NJB  "scarcely touching the path with his feet"
REB  "swifter than any traveler on foot"
JPSOA  "no shackle is placed on his feet"

The Hebrew phrase is ambiguous. The ancient versions did not understand it.

  1. LXX ‒ "the way of his feet shall proceed in peace"
  2. Peshitta ‒ "he shall not pass that way on foot"
  3. DSS ‒ "they do not discern the path of his feet"

Most modern English translations see it as imagery of speed. However, the JPSOA (p. 864) translates the word "path" (BDB 73) as "shackles" from an Old Aramaic root.

It could refer to new territory (NET Bible).

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. In this chapter YHWH displays His power and sovereignty by calling Cyrus II (i.e. the to be king of Persia, cf. Isa. 41:2,25) to take over the rule of the Fertile Crescent from Neo-Babylon. This regime change will show
    1. YHWH's plan of deliverance for His people (i.e. return from exile)
    2. YHWH's judgment of the idols of the peoples who cannot hear, see, or act

  2. Chapter 41 has an extensive number of commands used as a rhetorical literary device.
    1. directed to the "coastlands," Isa. 41:1
      1. "listen to Me" ‒ BDB 361, KB 357, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
      2. "let the peoples gain new strength" ‒ BDB 322, KB 321, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
      3. "let them come forward" ‒ BDB 620, KB 670, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
      4. "let them speak" ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, Piel IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
      5. "let us come together for judgment" ‒ BDB 897, KB 1132, Qal COHORTATIVE
    2. directed to "one from the east" (i.e. Cyrus II), Isa. 41:2 ‒ BDB 921, KB 1190, Hiphil JUSSIVE (i.e. Persia)
    3. the coastlands speak to each other, "be strong" Isa. 41:6 ‒ BDB 304, KB 302, Qal IMPERATIVE
    4. YHWH speaks to His people
      1. "do not fear" Isa. 41:10 ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense (also note Isa. 41:13, 14; see SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR)
      2. "do not anxiously look about you" Isa. 41:10 ‒ BDB 1043, KB 1609, Hithpael JUSSIVE
    5. YHWH (and the heavenly council; see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS) as Judge calls the idols to court (Isa. 41:21-24)
      1. "present your cases" ‒ BDB 897, KB 1132, Piel IMPERATIVE
      2. "bring forward your strong arguments" ‒ BDB 620, KB 670, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
      3. "let them bring forth" ‒ BDB 620, KB 670, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
      4. "let them declare to us" ‒ BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
      5. "as for the former events, declare what they were" ‒ BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
      6. "that we may consider them" ‒ BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal COHORTATIVE
      7. "that we may know their outcome" ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal COHORTATIVE
      8. "announce to us what is coming" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
      9. "declare the things that are going to come forward" ‒ BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
      10. "that we may know that you are gods" ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal COHORTATIVE
      11. "do good" ‒ BDB 405, KB 408, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
      12. "do evil" ‒ BDB 949, KB 1269, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
      13. "that we may anxiously look about us" ‒ BDB 1043, KB 1609, Hithpael COHORTATIVE
      14. "and fear together" ‒ BDB 431, KB 432 (or BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal COHORTATIVE), Qal JUSSIVE
    6. YHWH gives His verdict on the idols in Isa. 41:25-29
      1. "who has declared this" ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal COHORTATIVE
      2. "that we may say, 'he is right'?" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERFECT, but in a COHORTATIVE sense
      3. "when I look, there is no one" ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal JUSSIVE

  3. There is a symbolic trial where the nations are called to account (Isa. 41:1,21) because instead of repentance in the face of YHWH's presence, power and prediction, they make new idols.

  4. Notice the number of times "I" is used. YHWH chooses to act. This is similar to Ezek. 36:27-36.

  5. The new exodus from exile is described in agricultural terms as it was in Isaiah 35. The promises of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-29 are now realized.

  6. Israel has been restored to covenant status by YHWH's mercy and power.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 41:4 "Calling forth the generations from the beginning"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:4 "Calling forth the generations from the beginning" This is an idiom for YHWH's control of time and history (cf. Isa. 40:21; 41:26; 44:7; 45:21). YHWH directs creation, the call of Abraham, and his seed for His purposes. OT predictive prophecy is the strongest evidentiary basis for the inspired Bible!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ For "beginning" see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAD.

▣ "'I, the Lord, am the first, and with the last. I am He'" There is a series of Hebraic terms and forms used here to describe God.

  1. "the Lord" comes from the Hebrew VERB "to be" (cf. Exod. 3:14, see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)
  2. "the first and the last" (cf. Isa. 44:6; 48:12; Rev. 1:8; 21:6)
  3. "I am He" reflects the term "YHWH" (cf. Isa. 43:10; 44:4; John 8:24,28,57-58; 13:19; 18:5)

Collectively, these terms seem to reflect that God is the only-living, ever-living God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM). The imagery is used for Jesus, YHWH's Messiah, in Rev. 1:17; 2:8; 22:13. (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH)

entries.title: Isaiah 41:5 "The ends of the earth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 41:5 "The ends of the earth" This second line is parallel to "the coastlands," see note at Isa. 41:1. They both refer to the whole "known" Mediterranean and Near Eastern world.

entries.title: Isaiah 41:6-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:6-7 The Hebrew VERB "make strong" (BDB 304, KB 302) is used three times in these verses.

  1. Qal IMPERATIVE ‒ be strong, Isa. 41:6
  2. Piel IMPERFECT with waw ‒ encourage, Isa. 41:7
  3. Piel IMPERFECT with waw ‒ fastens it, Isa. 41:7

The nations looked to each other's deity for help, but in vain, for their gods could not see, hear, or act! Oh, the tragedy of human superstition and imagination!

entries.title: Isaiah 41:8 "But you, Israel, My servant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:8 "But you, Israel, My servant" There has been much discussion over the term "My servant." It seems to be used in three distinct ways in the OT.

  1. for an individual like the king or a prophet (cf. Num. 12:7)
  2. for the nation of Israel (cf. Isa. 42:19; 44:21)
  3. ultimately for the ideal Israelite, the Messiah (cf. Isa. 52:13-53:12)

In the book of Isaiah the second and third options are often merged.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

▣ "I have chosen" This VERB (BDB 103, KB 119, Qal perfect) is an emphasis on God's election (cf. Isa. 41:9; 43:10; 44:1,2; 49:7; Deut. 7:6; 14:2). In the OT election was for service (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6), while in the NT election is for salvation which leads to service.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

▣ "Descendant of Abraham My friend" Note YHWH's call and promise to Abraham in Genesis 12; 15; 22. This foundational Patriarchal covenant is emphasized by Paul in Romans 4 and Galatians 3. Abraham is also called YHWH's friend in 2 Chr. 20:7; James 2:23. They talked face to face in Genesis 18.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

entries.title: Isaiah 41:9 "You whom I have taken. . .called"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:9 "You whom I have taken. . .called" Both VERBS are PERFECTS (i.e. completed action).

  1. taken ‒ BDB 304, KB 302, Hiphil PERFECT
  2. called ‒ BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal PERFECT (see SPECIAL TOPIC: CALLED)

Also note the synonymous parallelism between

  1. from the ends of the earth
  2. its remotest parts

In context this refers to the places that Assyria resettled (i.e. exiled) the Israelites (722 B.C.) and Babylon resettled the Judeans (605, 597, 586, 582 B.C.).

▣ "I have chosen you and not rejected you" Judah felt that God had rejected them because of the exile and destruction of Jerusalem and the temple by Nebuchadnezzar II in 586 B.C. (i.e. 2 Sam. 7: 1 Chr. 17).

The VERB "reject" (BDB 549, KB 540, Qal PERFECT, NEGATED) is used in Lev. 26:44, where YHWH promises not to totally cut off His people because of their sin and covenant breaking. The question comes, how is this promise affected by the NT? It seems to me there are two main options.

  1. Israel still has a crucial place in end-time events (i.e. Zech. 12:10;Romans 9-11).
  2. God's people have always been those who trust Him and live for Him. In the OT this referred to the seed of Abraham, but also notice
    1. Melchizedek (Genesis 14)
    2. Job (Job 1)
    3. Jethro (Exodus)
    4. Caleb (Joshua)
    5. Uriah (2 Samuel 11)
    6. and others who were not Israelites
    7. In the NT this is widened to all believing Gentiles (i.e. Rom. 2:28-29; Galatians 3).

entries.title: Isaiah 41:10 "Do not fear"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:10 "Do not fear" This is a very common message from YHWH to His people (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, negated, cf. Isa. 41:13,14; 43:1,5; 44:2,8; 51:7,12; 54:4,14). See SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR

Notice why they should not fear.

  1. YHWH is personally with them
  2. YHWH is their covenant God
  3. He will strengthen them
  4. He will help them (Isa. 41:10,14)
  5. He will uphold them (Isa. 41:10,13)
  6. all who oppose them will
    1. be shamed
    2. be dishonored
    3. be brought to nothing (Isa. 41:11-12)
    4. perish

▣ "for I am with you" There is no stated verb in this phrase (see NKJV). There is an obvious intended word play (cf. Isa. 41:13) between the meaning of the needed verb (I am) and the name for God, YHWH (I Am that I Am, cf. Exod. 3:14). There is no greater promise in all the Bible (cf. Matt. 28:20; Acts 18:10). This truth is reflected in the Messianic title, "Emmanuel" (Isa. 7:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

NASB  "Do not anxiously look about you"
NKJV, Peshitta  "be not discourged"
NRSV, REB  "do not be afraid"
TEV  "let nothing terrify you"
NJB  "do not be alarmed"
LXX  "wander not"
JPSOA  "Be not frightened"

The Hebrew VERB (תשׁעה, BDB 1043, KB 1609) in the Hithpael, means "gaze not about (in anxiety)."

It is possible that the VERB is from another root (שׁתע), which is found in Ugaritic, meaning "fear" (NET Bible, p. 1250, #21), and therefore, a parallel with line 1.

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, REB, JPSOA  "with My righteous right hand"
TEV  "I will protect you and save you"
NJB  "with my saving right hand"
Peshitta  "with the right hand of my righteousness"
LXX  "with my just right hand"

The translation question is MASCULINE NOUN (BDB 841), which is the term usually translated "righteousness," but here, the connotation of "victorious" (BDB 842, #6. d., cf. Isa. 51:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

entries.title: Isaiah 41:11 "all those. . .those who contend"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:11 "all those. . .those who contend" Remember that YHWH has promised blessings to those who bless His people and curses to those who curse them (cf. Gen. 12:3). It must be remembered that Israel's strength, trust, and hope was in YHWH, not in themselves.

Notice how the returning Israelites' opponents are characterized.

  1. all those who are angered at you, Isa. 41:11
  2. those who contend with you, Isa. 41:11
  3. those who quarrel with you, Isa. 41:12
  4. those who war with you, Isa. 41:12

Also notice their fate.

  1. will be shamed, Isa. 41:11
  2. will be dishonored, Isa. 41:11
  3. will be as nothing, Isa. 41:11
  4. will perish, Isa. 41:11
  5. will not be found, Isa. 41:12
  6. will be as nothing, Isa. 41:12
  7. will be non-existent, Isa. 41:12

entries.title: Isaiah 41:14 "you worm Jacob"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:14 "you worm Jacob" This reference to Jacob as being a worm is not a derogatory term, but seems to be imagery for his helplessness (cf. Job 25:6; Ps. 22:6) without God's aid, similar to the imagery of Ezek. 16:6.

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA  "men"
NRSV  "insect"
NJB  "little handful"
REB, JPSOA footnote  "maggot"
NET footnote  "louse" or "weevil"

The MT has "men" (BDB 607) but modern translations emend it to an Akkadian root (NRSV, REB, NET Bible, p. 1250, #28).

▣ "your Redeemer" This (Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPIAL title, cf. Isa. 43:14; 44:6,24; 49:7; 59:20) reflects the Hebrew term Go'el (BDB 145, KB 169). This Hebrew term referred to the "kinsmen redeemer" or "avenger." It is used of one who buys a near relative back from slavery or a prisoner of war (cf. an example would be Boaz in Ruth 4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINSMAN REDEEMER

▣ "the Holy One of Israel" This is a favorite title for Israel's Deity in Isaiah (i.e. Assyrian period, cf. Isa. 1:4; 5:19; 10:17,20; 12:6; 17:7; 29:19,23; 30:11,12,15; 31:1; 37:23; also in the second part of Isaiah in the Neo-Babylonian period, Isa. 40:25; 41:14,16,20; 43:3,14, 15; 45:11; 47:4; 48:17; 49:7; 54:5; 55:5; 60:9,14). Because He is "holy," His people should be holy (cf. Lev. 19:2; Matt. 5:48; 1 Pet. 1:16).

This title, in a sense, expresses the impossible tension of a sinful, fallen people conforming to a holy standard. The Mosaic Covenant was impossible to keep (cf. Acts 15; Galatians 3; Hebrews). The old covenant was a way to show the impossibility of humans to conform to God's standard, yet He was with them, for them, preparing them for His answer to their fallen condition. He does not lower His standard, but provides it through His Messiah. The new covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36) is a covenant of faith and repentance, not human performance (cf. Eph. 2:8-9), though it issues in Christlikeness (cf. James 2:14-26). God wants a people who reflect His character to the nations (cf. Matt. 5:48).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANCTIFICATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SUPERIORITY OF THE NEW COVENANT OVER THE MOSAIC COVENANT

entries.title: Isaiah 41:15-16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:15-16 Israel's enemies are described as "mountains" (BDB 249) and "hills" (BDB 148) which will be "threshed," which is an agricultural term for harvesting by means of a heavy sledge (cf. Micah 4:13; Hab. 3:12). This is Hebrew poetry, be careful of literalism!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY

entries.title: Isaiah 41:17-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:17-20 These verses reflect God's presence and blessing with the Judean returnees with imagery from abundance in nature (cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 27; 28). This abundance was meant to attract the nations to YHWH.

As YHWH provided food, water, and protection (i.e. His presence with Israel during the Exodus), He will do it again. In a sense, this was a second exodus of Israel from foreign bondage.

For a good list of future prosperity promises, see Isa. 32:20. Prosperity was linked to

  1. covenant obedience (Lev. 26; Deut. 28)
  2. restoration of the covenant people to Canaan
  3. a way to attract the nations to YHWH

entries.title: Isaiah 41:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 41:19 For a good resource for identifying ancient plants and animals see UBS Fauna and Flora of the Bible.

entries.title: Isaiah 41:20 "the Holy One of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 41:20 "the Holy One of Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

entries.title: Isaiah 41:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:21 This is a court scene (cf. Isa. 41:1). This same type of imagery is found in Isa. 1:18-20).

▣ "The King of Jacob says" This title occurs only here. YHWH was the ideal King of the Covenant people (cf. Isa. 43:15; 44:6; Exod. 15:18; Num. 23:21; Jdg. 8:23; 1 Sam. 8:7; 12:12; 1 Kgs. 22:19; Isa. 6:5). Jacob's name (i.e. Israel) represents all the Covenant people, all thirteen tribes (cf. Isa. 45:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

entries.title: Isaiah 41:22-23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:22-23 Predictive prophecy is one of the strongest evidences of the inspiration of the Bible.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

entries.title: Isaiah 41:22-24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 41:22-24 This refers to the national gods. God calls on them to act or predict or do anything, but they cannot because they are vanity or nothingness (Isa. 41:24,28-29).

entries.title: Isaiah 41:23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:23 This verse is one of the places where the compilers of the MT recognized a Hebrew variant and suggested a change. The MT is not the oldest Hebrew MSS. It was not completed until A.D. 900 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT)

The MT has "and we shall see," 23c (Qere, ונראה, BDB 906, Qal IMPERFECT, NKJV, Leupold), but they suggest "and we shall be afraid" (ketiv, ונרא, BDB 431, Qal IMPERFECT, NASB). The UBS Text Project, p. 104, gives "see" a B rating (some doubt).

41:24b
NASB  "amounts to nothing"
NKJV  "is nothing"
NRSV  "is nothing at all"
NJB  "less than nothing"
REB  "none existant"
JPSOA  "less than nullify"
Peshitta  "corrupt"

The NOUN (BDB 67, KB 79) is found only here. Most translations take it as parallel to "nothing" (BDB 34 II) in line one.

KB Lexicon gives several guesses

  1. something worthless
  2. chaotic
  3. void
  4. illusion

The UBS Text Project, p. 104, lists two possible Hebrew roots.

  1. מאפע (BDB 67)
  2. מאפס (cf. v. 29b, BDB 67)

It gives option #1 only a "C" rating (considerable doubt). Please remember, even though we are not sure of the meaning of a word

  1. the larger context
  2. the Hebrew poetic prallelism

still provide the inspired message!

entries.title: Isaiah 41:24c "abomination"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 41:24c "abomination" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION

entries.title: Isaiah 41:25 "have aroused one from the north"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:25 "have aroused one from the north" This again refers to Cyrus II (cf. Isa. 41:2; 44:28; 45:1). The only direction that one could come into Palestine from the Fertile Crescent was from the north because a desert was directly to the east (i.e. "from the rising of the sun").

▣ "he will call on My name" This may refer to Cyrus' proclamation recorded in 2 Chr. 36:22-23 and Ezra 1:1-2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

NASB  "he will come upon rulers"
NKJV  "he will come against princes"
NRSV, TEV, NJB  "he shall trample on rulers"
REB  "he marches over rulers"
JPSOA  "he has trampled rulers"
NET  "he steps on rulers"

The MT has the common VERB "come" (בוא, BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERFECT) which several translations assume from context, means "step on." The UBS Textual Project, p. 106, suggests another possible root.

  1. ויבא ‒ he will come (MT)
  2. ויבס ‒ he will tread upon

However, the UBS Text Project put #1 in the text but gave it a "C" rating (considerable doubt). The NET Bible likes option #2 (p. 1251 #18).

entries.title: Isaiah 41:26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 41:26 YHWH shows His existence and power by His prophesied acts in history (cf. Isa. 43:9; 45:21). This may refer to Isa. 30:8, where YHWH tells the prophet to write down His prophecy so that the accuracy of His predictions prove His power, knowledge, and control over human history.

entries.title: Isaiah 41:27 "here they are"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 41:27 "here they are" This seems to refer to true prophets, as Isa. 41:28 and 29 refer to false prophets and the tragedy of people turning to helpless idols.

entries.title: Isaiah 41:29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
41:29 Isaiah describes the pagan national gods/idols (i.e. molten images, BDB 651) in four words.

  1. a delusion (BDB 19)
  2. nothing (BDB 67)
  3. their works are wind (BDB 924)
  4. empty (BDB 1062)

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 42:1 "Behold"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:1 "Behold" These two "beholds" (BDB 243), found in Isa. 41:29 and 42:1, contrast the lifeless idols of the nations with YHWH's activity, God's choice versus the nation's choice (cf. Isa. 41:29).

As in chapter 40, the question is asked "to whom is YHWH speaking?" It could be

  1. the prophet
  2. the heavenly council (see note at Gen. 1:26; see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS)
  3. just a literary technique for YHWH to express His thoughts to His covenant people

▣ "My Servant" This was a title of respect and calling (BDB 713).

  1. It was used in a collective sense
    1. the Patriarchs as a group ‒ Deut. 9:27
    2. the prophets ‒ 2 Kgs. 9:7; 17:13; Ezra 9:11; Jer. 7:25; 26:5; 29:19; 35:15; 44:4
    3. Israel ‒ Ps. 105:6; 136:22; Isa. 41:8-9; 42:18-19; 44:1,2,21; 45:4; 48:20; 49:3; Jer. 30:10; 46:27,28
    4. the Septuagint adds a phrase to Isa. 42:1, which makes it refer to national Israel ("Jacob is my servant, I will help him; Israel is my chosen")
  2. It was used in an individual sense
    1. Abraham ‒ Gen. 26:24; Ps. 105:6
    2. Job ‒ Job 1:8; 2:3; 42:7,8
    3. Isaac ‒ Gen. 24:14
    4. Jacob ‒ 1 Chr. 16:13; Ps. 105:6; Ezek. 28:25
    5. Moses ‒ Exod. 14:31; Num. 12:7-8; Deut. 34:5; Josh. 1:1-2,7,13,15
    6. Joshua ‒ Josh. 24:29; Jdg. 2:8
    7. Caleb ‒ Num 14:24
    8. David ‒ Ezek. 37:25
    9. Zerubbabel ‒ Hag. 2:23
    10. Solomon ‒ 1 Kgs. 3:8
    11. Isaiah ‒ Isa. 20:3; 44:26
    12. Jesus ‒ Matt. 12:15-21 quotes Isa. 42:1-4

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

▣ "whom I" Notice the things YHWH has done and will do for His special servant.

  1. whom I uphold, Isa. 42:1
  2. in whom My soul delights, Isa. 42:1
  3. I have put My Spirit upon Him, Isa. 42:1

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

▣ "He will. . ." Notice the things the Servant (the seed of David, the Messiah) will do (series of IMPERFECT VERBS).

  1. bring forth justice to the nations (i.e. universal implication, cf. Isa. 42:1; 4b,c)
  2. will not cry out, Isa. 42:2
  3. will not raise His voice, Isa. 42:2
  4. will not make His voice heard in the street, Isa. 42:2
  5. will not break a bruised reed, Isa. 42:3
  6. will not extinguish a dimly burning wick, Isa. 42:3
  7. will faithfully bring forth justice, Isa. 42:3
  8. will not be disheartened, Isa. 42:4
  9. will not be crushed, Isa. 42:4
  10. will establish justice in the earth, Isa. 42:4

▣ "My chosen one" This term (BDB 103, KB 119) denotes YHWH's choice of people, places, groups to serve Him.

  1. corporate choices
    1. the seed of the Patriarchs ‒ Deut. 4:37; 10:15
    2. Israel ‒ Deut. 7:7; Ps. 135:4; Isa. 44:1; Ezek. 20:5
    3. the people ‒ 1 Kgs. 3:8
    4. the tribe of Judah ‒ 1 Chr. 28:4; Ps. 78:68
    5. Levites ‒ 1 Chr. 15:2; 2 Chr. 29:11
  2. individuals
    1. Abraham ‒ Neh. 9:7
    2. Jacob ‒ Ps. 135:4
    3. Aaron ‒ Num. 16:5; 17:5; Ps. 105:26
    4. David ‒ 1 Sam. 10:24; 16:8,9,10; Ps. 78:70
    5. Solomon ‒ 1 Chr. 29:1
    6. Zerubabbel ‒ Hag. 2:23
  3. places (i.e. temple) ‒ Deut. 12:5,11,14,18,21,26; 14:23,24,25

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

▣ "My soul delights" This is similar to the title used by the Father for Jesus, "My Beloved" (cf. Matt. 3:17; 12:18; 17:5; Mark 9:7; Luke 9:35).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

▣ "I have put My Spirit upon Him" This refers to the Servant being anointed and equipped for a task (cf. Isa. 11:2; 59:21; 61:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

▣ "He will bring forth justice" See SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGE, JUDGMENT, JUSTICE and SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE.

▣ "to the nations" Notice the universal implications of this phrase and Isa. 42:4b and c, 6c and d, 10-12! Of all the prophets of Israel, it is Isaiah who saw the inclusion of the Gentiles in YHWH's future kingdom most clearly!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. This is the first of the special poems addressed to or about YHWH's Servant.
    1. Isa. 42:1-4 or 42:1-7 or 42:1-9
    2. Isa. 49:1-6 or 49:1-7 or 49:1-13
    3. Isa. 50:4-9 or 50:4-11
    4. Isa. 52:13-53:12
      Exactly where the first three stop is debatable.

  2. The Servant has both a corporate (i.e. Israel) and individual (i.e. the Messiah) orientation. Only context and/or description of the Servant's actions can differentiate the two. In a theological sense the Messiah is the "ideal Israelite" or "the Priest" of the kingdom of priests (see the NT book of Hebrews).

  3. The Aramaic translations and commentaries called the Targums assert that the Servant is the Messiah. He will be an individual Israelite accomplishing YHWH's will for the nation and the world. As Cyrus II was an instrument in the hand of YHWH for a new exodus/deliverance (i.e. return from exile), so too, will the Messiah bring a spiritual exodus or return from the alienation of the Fall (Genesis 3). He will restore the damaged image of God in mankind and allow for the intimate fellowship of Eden to be restored!
     The Messiah (cf. Luke 2:32) will be a light to the world that Israel was meant to be (cf. Isa. 42:6; 51:4; 60:1,3). Light is imagery for spiritual deliverance (cf. Isa. 49:6).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND
    SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN
    SPECIAL TOPIC: EDEN

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 42:2 "He will not cry out or raise His voice"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:2 "He will not cry out or raise His voice" This is either

  1. linked with Isa. 53:7, which refers to Jesus' trial
  2. a description of His quiet style of ministry
  3. a reference to a prayer for help which the Servant does not need (cf. Isa. 65:14)

The etymology of this term strongly favors #3.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:3 "A bruised reed. . .a dimly burning wick"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:3 "A bruised reed. . .a dimly burning wick" This describes a ministry of compassion, understanding, and patience to those who have somehow been wounded and stressed (cf. Isa. 57:15).

▣
NASB, NRSV, NJB  "faithfully"
NKJV, LXX  "truth"
JPSOA  "the true way"
REB  "unfailingly"
Peshitta  "truly"
NEB  "on every race"

This is the common Hebrew root אמן (BDB 52), which means confirm, support, secure. Here used of the Messiah's voice (v. 2). The UBS Text Project, p. 108, gives an "A" rating to "for truth" and not "for nations" (cf. NEB).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT

entries.title: Isaiah 42:4 ". . .Until. . ."
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:4 ". . .Until. . ." This seems to imply that a "crushing" (i.e. Isa. 52:13-53:12) will take place but at an appointed time (cf. Dan. 9:24-27).

▣ "in the earth. . .the coastlands" These are in a parallel relationship and, therefore, are synonymous. This again is a reference to Gentile nations. See note at Isa. 41:1,5.

For "earth" (erets, BDB 75) see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:5 "God the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:5 "God the Lord" These are two names for Israel's Deity (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, A., D.).

  1. El ‒ the general name for deity in the ANE (BDB 42). Here it has the DEFINITE ARTICLE and, therefore, refers to Israel's God, Elohim, and YHWH
  2. YHWH ‒ the covenant name for Deity from the VERB "to be" (BDB 217)

▣ "created" This VERB (BDB 135, KB 153, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) is used almost exclusively of God's (i.e. Elohim) creating (cf. Gen. 1:1).

▣ "the heavens" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

▣
NASB  "offspring"
NKJV, NRSV  "that which comes from it"
TEV  "all that lives there"
NJB  "what comes from it"
JPSOA  "what it brings forth"
REB  "everything that grows in it"
LXX, Peshitta  "all that is in it"

The term (KB 993) has two orientations.

  1. plants ‒ Job 31:8; Isa. 34:1; 42:5
  2. humans (imagery of descendants) ‒ Job 5:25; 21:8; 27:14; Isa. 22:24; 44:3; 48:19; 61:9; 65:23

Notice the series of "Who's"

  1. created the heavens
  2. stretched them out (see SPECIAL TOPIC: CIRCLE OF THE EARTH)
  3. spread out the earth (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORLD [several terms], I. A.)
  4. spread out its offspring
  5. gives "breath" (nephesh, BDB 675) to the people on it (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH)
  6. gives "spirit" (ruah, BDB 924) to those who walk in it (see SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT)

If this text is meant to form a chain like Genesis 1, then plants are the probable meanings. If they are synonymous parallelism, then people are the focus. Life, not just matter, is from YHWH. He is the ever-living, only-living God!

entries.title: Isaiah 42:5-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:5-9 This section is very similar to Isa. 40:12-17, which emphasizes YHWH as Creator and Sovereign over all physical creation and over His covenant people.

Notice God's acts in creation (v. 5, cf. Isa. 44:24).

  1. created the heavens and earth, BDB 135, KB 153, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS
  2. stretched them out, BDB 639, KB 692, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CIRCLE OF THE EARTH
  3. spread out the earth, BDB 955, KB. 1291, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE; parallel to #2
  4. spread out its vegetation, BDB 838 (lit. "what comes from it")
  5. created humans
    1. gave breath ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT
    2. gave spirit ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE, I.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:6-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:6-7 These verses describe what YHWH is doing for His covenant people. He chose them for the purpose of saving all mankind trapped in darkness (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

  1. called (BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal PARTICIPLE) them in righteousness (all the VERBS in v. 6 start with א, a sound play)
  2. held them by the hand (BDB 304, KB 302, Hiphil JUSSIVE but functioning as another IMPERFECT)
  3. watched over them (BDB 665, KB 718, Qal IMPERFECT)
    1. watch, guard, keep ‒ BDB 665, KB 718, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Isa. 27:3; 49:8 (NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NET)
    2. form, fashion ‒ BDB 427, cf. Isa. 41:25; 44:12 (NJB, REB, JPSOA)
    3. strengthen ‒ Pesitta, LXX
  4. appointed them as a covenant people (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERFECT; NET, "make you a covenant mediator for people")
    1. as a light to the nations (cf. Isa. 49:6; 51:4; 60:1-3; Luke 2:32; Acts 13:47; 26:23, see full note at Isa. 45:22)
    2. to open blind eyes (this may be parallel imagery for prisoners being freed from a dark dungeon, cf. Isa. 61:1)
    3. to bring out prisoners (i.e. spiritual slaves of sin)

Abraham's seed was both

  1. a kingdom of priests (PLURAL)
  2. a King/Priest (SINGULAR, Messiah, cf. Psalm 110)

who came to deliver the world from the darkness and prison of sin (Genesis 3).

There is some doubt about the Hebrew root of #3 above

  1. protect (נצר BDB 665) ‒ NASB, NKJV, NRSV
  2. form (יצר BDB 427) ‒ NJB, JPSOA, REB

Notice what the Messiah/Servant will accomplish.

  1. government in righteousness (cf. Isa. 9:6-7; 11:3-4)
  2. worldwide reign (cf. Isa. 45:22; 49:6; 52:10; Micah 5:4)
  3. open blind eyes (cf. Isa. 29:18; 32:3; 35:5)
  4. release prisoners (cf. Isa. 61:1)

entries.title: Isaiah 42:8 "I am the Lord, that is My name"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:8 "I am the Lord, that is My name" This is the covenant name of God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH, D.

▣ "My glory" "Glory" is a difficult term (BDB 458) to define.

  1. in Isa. 6:3 it fills the whole earth
  2. in Isa. 40:5 it will be revealed to the whole earth
  3. in a sense it represents YHWH's personal presence
  4. in the NT YHWH's glory is fully revealed in the person of the Messiah, Jesus (cf. John 1:14; 11:4,40; 17:4)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (doxa, NT)

▣ "I will not give My glory to another" See Isa. 40:18-26, which speaks of YHWH's reality vs. the idols' non-reality.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:9-10 "new things. . .new song"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:9-10 "new things. . .new song" The term "new" (BDB 294) is a recurrent theme in Isa. 43:19; 48:6; 62:2; 65:17; 66:22 and also in the NT book of the Revelation (see my new exegetical, verse-by-verse Partial Preterist commentary on the book of Revelation online). See full note at Isa. 62:2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: OLD THINGS. . .NEW THINGS

entries.title: Isaiah 42:9 "Before they spring forth I proclaim them to you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 42:9 "Before they spring forth I proclaim them to you" This also goes back to 40:18-26, where YHWH asks the idols to make a prediction to show their reality and they could not, but YHWH can! He is Lord of time and space. There is divine purpose and planning in human history.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:10 The last two lines of Isa. 42:10 refer to the same group as "coastlands" of Isa. 41:1 (cf. Isa. 42:12b).

  1. you who go down to the sea
  2. you islands

entries.title: Isaiah 42:10-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:10-13 These verses parallel the universal emphasis of the "Coastlands" of Isa. 41:1. The Gentiles eagerly wait for light (i.e. Isa. 2:2-4; 40:4,5,6; 49:6).

For those who seek light, YHWH is a refuge and help (Isa. 42:6-7), but for those who cling to idols He is a warrior (Isa. 42:13)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: "LIGHT"

▣ There are several commands in these verses.

  1. "sing" ‒ BDB 1010, KB 1479, Qal IMPERATIVE, Isa. 42:10
  2. "lift up their voices" ‒ BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, Isa. 42:11
  3. "sing aloud" ‒ BDB 943, KB 1247, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, Isa. 42:11
  4. "shout for joy" ‒ BDB 846, KB 1011, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, Isa. 42:11
  5. "give glory" - BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, Isa. 42:12
  6. "declare" ‒ BDB 619, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, Isa. 42:12

entries.title: Isaiah 42:10-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 42:10-17 The Jewish Study Bible, p. 867, thinks these verses are a concluding hymn to the Lord's words to His Servent, Judah.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:11 "Kedar"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:11 "Kedar" This (BDB 871) possibly refers to the Arab nations. The Hebrew root can refer to

  1. nomadic Arabian tribes ‒ Isa. 21:16; 42:11; 60:7; Jer. 2:10; 49:28; Ezek. 27:21
  2. descendants of Ishmael ‒ Gen. 25:13; 1 Chr. 1:29

▣ "Sela" This means "Rock" (BDB 709). This possibly refers to Petra, the capital of Edom (BDB 701, cf. Isa. 16:1).

▣ "sing aloud. . .shout for joy" What are they rejoicing about? The glory of YHWH has come to them (Isa. 42:12a). The light has come to the nations (Isa. 42:6d). That light is the covenant people and their knowledge of YHWH!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 42:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:13 This describes in military terms the Lord's attack (i.e. YHWH as Divine Warrior) against the idolatrous nations that oppose His will and His people's return.

  1. He will go forth like a warrior
  2. He will arouse His zeal like a man of war
  3. He will utter a shout
  4. He will raise a war cry
  5. He will prevail against His enemies (i.e. idolaters, cf. Isa. 42:17)

The term "zeal" (BDB 888) is also used in Isa. 9:7; 26:11; 37:32; 59:17 to show YHWH's purposeful actions that assure victory!

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUSY, ZEALOUS

entries.title: Isaiah 42:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:14 This possibly refers to the exilic period. YHWH endured the exile of His covenant people with deep emotions.

  1. I have kept silent for a long time (unusual usage of 'olam)
  2. I have kept still and restrained Myself
  3. I waited in anguish like a woman in labor
    1. a groan (BDB 821, KB 949)
    2. a gasp (BDB 983, KB 1375)
    3. a pant (BDB 675, KB 730)

YHWH chooses a feminine image to describe Himself. This is not the only place He does this (cf. Isa. 66:12-13). Remember, God is an eternal Spirit present throughout time and space. He uses human vocabulary to communicate with His highest creation, mankind made in His image. He is neither male nor female, but incorporates the best of each in Himself. The only part of the Trinity that has had a body is Jesus, the Son. Please listen to my audio sermon entitled, "The Femininity of God," second green box on my homepage, #111.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE USED TO DESCRIBE GOD

entries.title: Isaiah 42:15-16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:15-16 YHWH describes His aid for the returning covenant people.

  1. v. 15 is imagery of preparing a smooth and level highway for the return (also Isa. 42:16d)
  2. v. 16a-c describes His care for the returnees
  3. v. 16e-f describes YHWH's sure commitment to act (two Qal PERFECTS)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

42:15
NASB, NKJV  "coastlands"
NRSV, JPSOA, LXX, Peshitta  "islands"
TEV, JPSOA emendation  "deserts"
NJB  "firm ground"
REB  "desert wastes"

The MT has "coastlands" (BDB 15 I, cf. Isa. 11:11; 24:15; 41:1,15; 42:4,10,15; 49:1; 51:5; 59:18; 60:9; 66:19; Jer. 31:10), sometimes translated "islands" (i.e. Isa. 40:15). It is an idiom for Gentile nations (cf. Zeph. 2:11). See note at v. 4.

Here, it denotes YHWH leading His people back to Canaan by destroying the nations who oppose Him (i.e. vv. 13-17).

entries.title: Isaiah 42:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:17 This continues YHWH's rejection and condemnation of idolatry (i.e. Isa. 1:28-31; 44:9-11; 45:16).

The term "shame" (DB 102) is intensified by joining it to its VERB form (BDB 101, KB 116, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Isa. 44:9,11).

▣ "shame" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME

entries.title: Isaiah 42:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:18 Note the two IMPERATIVES

  1. hear ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. look ‒ BDB 613, KB 661, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

▣ "deaf. . .blind" These words occur several times in this context and are an allusion to Isa. 6:9-10.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:18-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:18-22 This strophe describes the covenant people. The shock is that they too had become idolaters! Yet they were even more responsible for their spiritual condition because they had

  1. the Patriarchs
  2. the covenants
  3. the promises (cf. Rom. 9:4-5)

The ones who were to bring light to the nations in darkness had themselves become darkness! They epitomized the curse of Isa. 6:9-10, but there was hope in Isa. 35:5!

entries.title: Isaiah 42:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:19 Notice the parallel between the titles

  1. "My Servant," line 1
  2. "My messenger," line 2
  3. "the servant of the Lord" in line 4
  4. also notice the threefold repetition of "blind" (BDB 734). The irony is that the "blind" one is described as:
▣
NASB  "he that is at peace with Me"
NKJV  "he who is perfect"
NRSV  "my dedicated one"
JPSOA  "the chosen one"
REB  "the one who has trust"
LXX  "the ruler"
NET  "My covenant partner"

The Hebrew word שׁלם (BDB 1023, KB 1532, Pual PARTICIPLE; see SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE [OT]) is uncertain in this context. There have been several theories. It seems to

  1. be parallel to the other titles for Israel (see above, v. 19)
  2. a title that showed how far Israel was from her calling and true self (i.e. she is blind and deaf, v. 18)

entries.title: Isaiah 42:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:20 There is an obvious parallelism between the two parts of line 1 (related to sight) and line 2 (related to hearing). Verses 19-20 describe Judah in their spiritual blindness.

The first pair is one which the MT compilers identified as a variant.

  1. the MT had "you have seen," BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal PERFECT (ketiv), also in Dead Sea Scrolls
  2. the Masoretic Jewish scholars suggested "to see," Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE (qere)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE MASORETIC TEXT

entries.title: Isaiah 42:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:21 The problem with Israel was not God's law but Israel's inability to do it (cf. Gal. 3; the book of Hebrews)! The Fall affected all humans (cf. Isa. 42:22; i.e. Ezek. 36:22-38). Israel's sin had consequences! The New Covenant of Jer. 31:31-34 was meant to answer this human inability (cf. Isa. 42:23-25; Eph. 2:8-9)

42:22
NASB, NJB  "in caves"
NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA, REB  "in holes"
LXX  "in secret rooms"
Peshitta  "in prison houses"
NET  "in pits"

The MT has "young men" (BDB 104), but the context implies a similar form "in holes" (BDB 359).

  1. בחורים ‒ young men
  2. בהורים ‒ in holes

It is possible that this term refers to special "pits" dug to keep prisoners for a limited period of time. Note the parallelism between line 2 and line 3. See IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 628.

Context, context, context is crucial! Hebrew parallelism in poetry is crucial in interpretation!

entries.title: Isaiah 42:23-25
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 42:23-25 I think 42:18-25 should be one paragraph which describes Judah's (i.e. My Servant) unfaithfulness to the Mosaic Covenant and the warnings of the prophets. They failed in their mission to be "a light to the nations." This resulted in the "curses" of Lev. 26 and Deut. 28 falling on both the northern Kingdom (722 B.C.) and the southern Kingdom (586 B.C.). But, YHWH wants to forgive and restore them, not because they are worthy or repentant, but because of His greater purpose, which is the coming birth, life, teachings, death, resurrection of His Faithful Servant, the Messiah (Isa. 52:13-53:12).

entries.title: Isaiah 42:24 "walk"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
42:24 "walk" This is used in the Bible to show that biblical faith is a lifestyle commitment (i.e. Eph. 1:4; 2:10; 4:1,17; 5:2,25), not a theology alone. This is possibly a source of the early title of Christianity in Acts, "the Way" (cf. Acts 9:2; 19:9,23; 22:4; 24:14,22; and John 14:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why did Israel and Judah need this message so badly? (cf. Isa. 40:27)
  2. Why is God's power stressed?
  3. Does the title "My Servant" refer to the Jews or to the Messiah?
  4. Why are the numerous references to the Gentiles' inclusion so significant in this passage?
  5. Why did God choose the Jews?

entries.title: Isaiah 43:1 "Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:1 "Lord" This is from the word YHWH. In Exod. 3:14 it is translated "I Am." This form is from the Hebrew VERB "to be." He is the ever-living, only-living One.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "your Creator" This is a Qal PARTICIPLE (BDB 135, KB 153, used only of divine creation, Gen. 1). This is a common theme throughout the Servant Songs. Here it refers to the establishment of the nation of Israel (cf. Genesis 12; 15; 22).

The second line of chapter 43 has the parallel VERB "formed" (BDB 427, KB 428, Qal PARTICIPLE, cf. Isa. 43:21; 44:2,21,24). YHWH was not only the Creator of the physical realm but also the covenant people (cf. Genesis 12; 15; 18; 22).

▣ "O Jacob. . .O Israel" These two VOCATIVES both refer to the collective covenant people, the seed of Abraham.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣ "Do not fear" This is a command (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense). So often this is God's word for His people, especially after the exile and destruction of Jerusalem and the temple (cf. Isa. 40:9; 41:10,13,14; 44:2; 54:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

▣ "redeemed" See SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM.

▣ "I have called you by name" This (both "redeemed" and "called" are Qal PERFECTS) refers to God's choice of Israel (cf. Isa. 43:7; 45:3-4). This was a special calling through Abraham (cf. Genesis 12; 15; 18; 22).

Naming something shows ones power and authority.

  1. Adam names the animals ‒ Gen. 2:19-20
  2. Adam names Eve ‒ Gen. 2:23; 3:20
  3. YHWH names the stars ‒ Ps. 147:4; Isa. 40:26; 48:12-13
  4. YHWH names His people ‒ Isa. 43:1,7; 45:3-4

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "you are Mine" See Isa. 43:21 and Exod. 19:5-6. Israel was uniquely YHWH's people.
