READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Israel's unique position as YHWH's covenant people is clearly revealed in Isa. 43:1-7.
    1. He formed them, Isa. 43:1,7
    2. He redeemed them, Isa. 43:1
    3. He called them by His name, Isa. 43:1,7
    4. He protected them, Isa. 43:2
    5. He is their covenant God, Isa. 43:3
    6. They are precious in His sight, Isa. 43:4
    7. He honored them, Isa. 43:4
    8. He loved them, Isa. 43:4
    9. He is with them, Isa. 43:5
      SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

  2. YHWH wants to use them to reveal Himself to the nations, Isa. 43:8-10 (esp. Isa. 43:10c).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

  3. Verses 10d-f ‒ 13 are a theological affirmation of YHWH's uniqueness.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

  4. YHWH will bring His people back from exile (Isa. 43:5-6,14,16,19-20)
    1. through Cyrus II's decree in 538 B.C. (imagery of a second Exodus)
    2. ultimately through the Messiah (a third and final exodus from sin)

  5. YHWH will redeem Israel even though they do not deserve it (cf. Isa. 43:22-24). However, this will involve a "new covenant" (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 35:22-36). YHWH has a worldwide redemptive plan
    SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

  6. YHWH as Israel's redeemer is the focus of this chapter (cf. Isa. 43:1,3,11,14,25-26). YHWH acts because of who He is and for His greater purpose. Israel is a precious tool in the hand of God for universal redemption.

  7. Names for God used in chapter 43 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. D.)
    1. "the Lord" (Isa. 43:1,3,11,14) YHWH ‒ The covenant name for God (cf. Exod. 3:14), "I Am," is from the Hebrew VERB "to be."
    2. "God" (Isa. 43:3; "El in Isa. 43:13) Elohim ‒ This is a PLURAL word. The rabbis say YHWH is God's name for mercy, while Elohim deals with the world in general (i.e. creator, sustainer). These two names for God are the most common in the OT.
       I reject the modern western model of "Source Criticism" that turns these names into separate authors.
      SPECIAL TOPIC: PENTATEUCH SOURCE CRITICISM (J.E.D.P.)
    3. "The Holy One of Israel" (Isa. 43:3,15) ‒ This title expresses God's purity and transcendance (see note at Isa. 40:25; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE).
    4. "Savior" (Isa. 43:3,11,12) Yasha ‒ This is from the same root as Joshua and Jesus. The basic meaning is "to be wide" or "spacious" (cf. Isa. 19:20; 45:15,21; 49:26; 60:16; 63:8; see SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR).
    5. "Redeemer" (Isa. 43:14) ‒ This is from the same root as Go'el, the kinsman redeemer or avenger (cf. Ruth 4:4,6). This term depicts God as our near kinsman (cf. Isa. 41:14; 44:6,24; 47:4; 48:17; 49:7,26; 54:5,8; 59:20; 60:16; 63:16). It is another example of God's personal relationship with us. Other examples are God as parent or husband. See SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM
    6. "The Creator" (Isa. 43:15) ‒ YHWH the creator (cf. Isa. 40:28) is also the special covenant God of Israel. This (the VERB bara, cf. Isa. 43:1) is a common theme (cf. Isaiah 40-66).
    7. "King" (Isa. 43:15) ‒ God is the true King of Israel. The earthly king is merely His representative (cf. 1 Samuel 8). See See SPECIAL TOPIC: TITLES FOR THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 43:2 "the waters. . .the fire. . .the flame"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:2 "the waters. . .the fire. . .the flame" This is such a wonderful text! These are used as imagery of problems, fears, and foes! Oh, what wonderful truth for believers in a fallen world!

▣ "will be with you" This is God's greatest promise (i.e. His personal presence, cf. Isa. 43:5; Deut. 31:6,8; Ps. 23:4; Matt. 28:20). This is what the Messianic title "Immanauel" means (cf. Isa. 7:14).

▣ "Nor will the flame burn you" For a powerful example see Daniel 3.

entries.title: Isaiah 43:3 "Savior"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:3 "Savior" This root's basic meaning can be translated "to be wide" (BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil PARTICIPLE). The names Joshua, Hosea, and Jesus are based on this root.

SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR

▣ "ransom" This speaks of the high cost of redemption. The object of this verse seems to be Cyrus II's conquests.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

entries.title: Isaiah 43:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:4 There is an apparent parallel between

  1. Isa. 43:3 ‒ a Divine ransom involving Egypt, Cush, and Seba instead of Israel
  2. Isa. 43:4 ‒ a Divine ransom involving
    1. other men (Adam, BDB 9)
    2. other peoples (BDB 522)
  3. The UBS Text Project (p. 111) gives another option (i.e. Assyria. . .Edom), which is found in the REB. This change is possible without a change of consonants. However, the UBS Text Project rates option #1 as A (very high probability).

Verses 3 and 4 are a literary way of showing YHWH's great love for Israel and His willingness for Cyrus' military victories to assure Israel's return to Palestine.

43: 5-7 This reflects the return from Neo-Babylonian exile allowed by Cyrus II's decree (538 B.C.), which allowed all the exiled people groups to return to their homeland.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF PERSIA, C.

entries.title: Isaiah 43:7 "called. . .created. . .formed. . .made"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:7 "called. . .created. . .formed. . .made" God had a purpose for Israel (cf. Isa. 43:10; Gen. 12:1-3; Exod. 19:5-6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 43:8 "the people who are blind"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 43:8 "the people who are blind" This was because of their continuing unbelief and covenant disobedience (cf. Isa. 6:9-10 and 42:18-22).

entries.title: Isaiah 43:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:9 There is a series of Qal IMPERFECTS used as JUSSIVES (cf. NRSV and NJB, "let. . .").

  1. let them bring their witness (BDB 678, KB 733)
  2. let them justify themselves (BDB 842, KB 1003)
  3. let them hear (BDB 1033, KB 1570)
  4. let them say (BDB 55, KB 65)

The nations, like the idols of Isaiah 40, do not know the future. Only YHWH holds time and history in His hand (i.e. many predictions in Isaiah of the fall of Assyria and Babylon). He will use Israel to reveal Himself and ultimately He will use the Messiah, His special Servant to bring the nations to faith (i.e. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8).

entries.title: Isaiah 43:10 "You are My witnesses"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:10 "You are My witnesses" This is imagery for a court scene (cf. Isa. 43:12; 1:18; 41:21; 44:8; Rom. 8:31-39; Matt. 25:31-46), where all the nations are gathered (cf. Isa. 43:9).

▣ "Before Me there was no God" This refers to monotheism (cf. Isa. 43:10-13). This is reflected in Exod. 20:5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

entries.title: Isaiah 43:10-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:10-13 Notice the many ways YHWH's uniqueness, power, and eternality are expressed.

  1. He wants humans, made in His image (cf. Gen. 1:26-27), to
    1. know (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal IMPERFECT; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW)
    2. believe (BDB 52, KB 63, Hiphil IMPERFECT; see SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS [OT])
    3. understand (BDB 106, KB 122, Qal IMPERFECT)
  2. He is the only God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM)
    1. I am He, Isa. 43:10,11,12,13
    2. before Me there was no God formed, Isa. 43:10
    3. after Me no God formed, Isa. 43:10
    4. no savior beside Me, Isa. 43:11; 45:22
  3. His acts (all Hiphil IMPERFECTS; see wonderful parallel at Ps. 103:6-14)
    1. He has spoken (BDB 616, KB 665)
    2. He has saved (BDB 446, KB 448)
    3. He has proclaimed (BDB 1033, KB 1570)
  4. He is from eternity, Isa. 43:13a; Micah 5:3; Ps. 90:2
  5. His power, Isa. 43:13b,c

These truths are what the nations need to know and affirm, Isa. 43:9.

entries.title: Isaiah 43:13 "eternity"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:13 "eternity" This follows the Septuagint. The MT has "from the day."

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE MASORETIC TEXT

entries.title: Isaiah 43:14 "the Lord your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:14 "the Lord your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel" See Contextual Insights, G.

▣ "will bring them all down as fugitives" This refers to the fall of Neo-Babylon by Cyrus II. It was not Cyrus' power that defeated Neo-Babylonians but YHWH's power and purpose (i.e. "for your sake").

There is a possible revocalization of the Hebrew consonants (BDB 138).

  1. "fugitives," מברחים, Peshitta, NASB, NKJV, NET, cf. Ezek. 17:21 only, but possibly Isa. 15:5
  2. "bars," MT, Ezek. 38:11, בריחים, JPSOA, cf. Isa. 45:2

The UBS Text Project, p. 112, gives option #1 a B rating.

▣ "the Chaldeans" Herodotus (450 B.C.), Hist. I, uses this term (BDB 505) to refer to an ethnic group (cf. 2 Kgs. 24:1-4; Dan. 5:30) as well as a priestly class (cf. Dan. 2:2; 3:8; 4:7; 5:7,11) whose usage goes back to Cyrus II. Even before this time period Assyrian records used the term (BDB 505) in an ethnic sense (cf. R. K. Harrison, Introduction to the Old Testament, p. 1113). Also read the good discussion of the possibility of a confusion of two similar terms (i.e. Kal-du vs. Kasdu) in The Expositors Bible Commentary, vol. 7, pp. 14-15 or Robert Dick Wilson, Studies in the Book of Daniel, series 1.

Because Gen. 11:28 states that Ur of the Chaldeans was the home of Terah and his family, Chaldeans may have been ethnically Semitic (i.e. same racial group as the Hebrews).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS

▣ There is another possible revocalization of the Hebrew consonants.

  1. into the ships (BDB 58, NASB, NKJV)
  2. in lamentation (change of vowels, JPSOA, NRSV, NJB, TEV, REB, NET Bible)
  3. the LXX has "bound in ships"

It is possible that Isa. 43:14 should be taken as Neo-Babylonian people thinking they could escape the Persian army by floating down river (i.e. Euphrates) in the ships they were so proud of, yet now they will be ships of mourning!

entries.title: Isaiah 43:15 "your King"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 43:15 "your King" This is possible linked to 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17. See Contextual Insights, G.

entries.title: Isaiah 43:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:16 This uses

  1. the Exodus from Egypt (cf. Isa. 43:17; Exodus 14-15) as imagery for the return from Neo-Babylon
  2. YHWH's control of the waters of chaos. See SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

▣ "I will do something new" This theme of something "new" is so common in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 41:15; 42:9,10; 48:6; 62:2; 65:17; 66:22). See full note at Isa. 62:2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: OLD THINGS. . .NEW THINGS

entries.title: Isaiah 43:19 "I will even make a roadway in the wilderness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:19 "I will even make a roadway in the wilderness" This is a very common biblical theme (cf. Isa. 40:1-4).

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, JPSOA, LXX, Peshitta  "Rivers"
REB, DSS  "Paths"

The UBS Text Project, p. 113, cannot decide between the MT, "rivers/streams" and DSS "paths."

  1. נהרות ‒ BDB 625, "rivers"
  2. נתיבות ‒ BDB 677, "paths"

I think option #2 is a better poetic parallel to the previous line of poetry (notice "path," BDB 677, in v. 16, as well as "a way," BDB 292).

However, v. 20 does involve YHWH bringing water (i.e. rivers, BDB 677) to the desert.

entries.title: Isaiah 43:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:20 Instead of curses (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28) the beasts became tame. Nature blooms and produces in light of YHWH's presence and blessings, imagery of a restored Garden of Eden.

See Isa. 32:20 for a list of passages like this.

entries.title: Isaiah 43:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 43:22 These are acts of worship done at the temple.

entries.title: Isaiah 43:22-24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 43:22-24 This is not a condemnation of sacrifice in general but of false motives (JPOSOA footnote, cf. Jeremiah 7; Amos 5). The VERBS are all PERFECTS which show a settled attitude of rebellion.

entries.title: Isaiah 43:24 "sweet cane"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:24 "sweet cane" This (BDB 889) refers to holy anointing oil (cf. Exod. 30:23; Jer. 6:20).

▣ "sins. . .iniquities" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, A. #1, #2

entries.title: Isaiah 43:25 "I, even I, am the one who wipes out your transgressions for My own sake"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:25 "I, even I, am the one who wipes out your transgressions for My own sake" God's forgiveness is an act of pure grace, not merit (cf. Isa. 37:35; 48:9,11; Ezek. 36:22-36; Eph. 2:8-9).

▣ "I will not remember your sins" When God forgives, God forgets (cf. Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 44:22; Ps. 103:12; Micah 7:19)! What a needed truth in light of Satan's continuing condemnations! Oh the mercy and grace of God!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WORDS FOR FORGIVENESS

entries.title: Isaiah 43:26 "let us argue our case together"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:26 "let us argue our case together" This reflects a legal imagery of a court room (cf. Isa. 1:18; 41:21; Rom. 8:31-39). This verse has a series of commands by the judge.

  1. put Me in remembrance ‒ BDB 269, KB 269, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  2. let us argue our case together ‒ BDB 1047, KB 1627, Niphal COHORTATIVE
  3. state your case ‒ BDB 707, KB 765, Piel IMPERATIVE

entries.title: Isaiah 43:27 "Your first forefather sinned"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:27 "Your first forefather sinned" Literally it is "father." It could refer to Adam or Jacob or any Jewish ancestor. It shows that God's love is undeserved. The OT does not dwell on the origin of sin, but acknowledges its presence and pervasiveness. On the origin of "sin" some rabbis, like Paul, emphasize Genesis 3, but most emphasize Genesis 6 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: "sons of God" in Genesis 6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE AGE OF ACCOUNTABILITY

▣ "spokesmen" This is a reference to either

  1. the prophets
  2. the priests or Levites (cf. 2 Chr. 30:22)
  3. the civil leaders

entries.title: Isaiah 43:28 "I will pollute the princes of the sanctuary"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
43:28 "I will pollute the princes of the sanctuary" The VERB "pollute" (BDB 320 III, KB 319, Piel IMPERFECT with waw) can mean "pollute," defile," or "profane." The NEB and REB slightly change the Hebrew consonants to "your princes profaned my sanctuary," which follows the LXX.

It is uncertain whether the two VERBS of Isa. 43:28 refer to the past or the future. The Hebrew text links verses 27 and 28. Verse 28 obviously refers to the past. Most of chapter 43 deals with YHWH's current deliverance of Israel from exile. Hebrew TENSES do not give time, just action; time must be ascertained from the context.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW GRAMMAR, II. A.

▣ "the ban" This is from the word herem (BDB 356). Something was "holy," so unusable by fallen humanity, therefore, it must be destroyed. An example would be Jericho (cf. Joshua 6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CURSE (OT)

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 44:1 "listen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:1 "listen" This is an IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570) which characterizes many oracles in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 1:2,10; 6:8,9,10; 7:13; 28:14; 32:9; 33:13; 34:1; 36:13; 39:5; 42:18; 46:3,12; 47:8; 48:1,12,14, 16; 51:1,7,21; 55:2,3; 59:1; 66:5).

This word means "to hear so as to perform" (cf. James 1:22-25). It became the name (the Shema) of the famous Jewish prayer in Deut. 6:4-5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR

▣ "O Jacob, My servant" Notice the parellelism between lines 1 and 2. YHWH is addressing corporate Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

▣ "whom I have chosen" YHWH

  1. chose Israel, Isa. 44:1,2
  2. made Israel, Isa. 44:2
  3. formed Israel, Isa. 44:2 (cf. Isa. 27:11; 37:26; 43:1,7,21; 44:2,21-24; 45:11)
  4. helped Israel, Isa. 44:2

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 44:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:2 Notice the parallelism between lines 1 and 2.

  1. "made you" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal PARTICIPLE, line 1, cf. Isa. 17:7
  2. "formed you" ‒ BDB 427, KB 428, Qal PARTICIPLE, line 2, cf. Gen. 2:7,8 (see #3 above)

There are several Hebrew words used to describe YHWH's creative acts.

▣ "Do not fear" This phrase (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) is used often in chapters 40-66 (cf. Isa. 40:9; 41:10,13,14; 43:1,5; 44:3; 51:7; 54:4,14; 57:11). They were not to fear because

  1. they were God's people
  2. He was with them
  3. their punishment was over
  4. He would provide all they needed

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

▣ "Jeshurun" This (BDB 449) was a rare title for Israel meaning "the upright one" (cf. Deut. 32:15; 33:5,26). It is parallel to "O Jacob My servant."

entries.title: Isaiah 44:3 "I will pour"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:3 "I will pour" This VERB (BDB 427, KB 428, Qal IMPERFECT) is often used in connection with anointings or sacrifices. In this verse it is repeated twice.

  1. once for the miraculous water of abundance
  2. once for the Spirit (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE)
    1. Isa. 32:15, different word (BDB 788)
    2. Joel 2:28, different word (BDB 1049)

YHWH is the source of blessings and for desert people water was the symbol of life and abundance (cf. Isa. 44:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS/SEA, I. A. #4

▣ "on your offspring" Blessings, like curses, moved through families (cf. Deut. 5:9-10; 7:9).

These future generations will know who they are in YHWH, i.e. if their parents teach them (cf. Deut. 4:9,10; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 32:46), rejoice in it (Isa. 44:5), and live it!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

entries.title: Isaiah 44:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:5 The textual question is to whom this verse refers.

  1. proud descendants of Abraham (v. 2)
  2. foreigners who claim and extol Israel's God (cf. v. 5; 56:3-6)

The VERB "call" (BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal VERB) is translated

  1. PASSIVE in the Aramaic Targums, "shall be called"
  2. REFLEXIVE (Niphal) in the LXX and the Peshitta, "shall call himself"
  3. ACTIVE in the Hebrew, "shall call on" (i.e. act of worship; see SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME)

It seems to me from the context of the parallelism of lines 2 and 3 that it is talking about foreigners (see UBS Text Project, p. 116). If so, then this is one of those texts that assures non-Jews of access to the one true God (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:41-43)! Not only is the servant a light to the nations (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:6-7; 60:1-3; 66:23), but a savior of the nations! Genesis 3:15 is fulfilled, as well as Gen. 12:3!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "write on his hand, 'Belonging to the Lord'" This seems to reflect the ANE custom of slaves being tattooed with the name of their owner. This would be similar imagery to God marking His followers' foreheads.

  1. Paul, in Gal. 6:17, mentions a "brand/mark of Jesus"
  2. God marks His faithful followers who believe in Jesus on their hand or forehead in Rev. 7:3
  3. Satan mimics this in Rev. 13:16; 14:9; 20:4

For a fuller discussion see my new Partial Preterist commentary on Revelation (2024) online free at www.freebiblecommentary.org. Click on the second blue box on homepage and then, "written commentaries."

entries.title: Isaiah 44:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:6 Notice the titles for God in this context (similar to 43:3,15).

  1. the Lord (YHWH); see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.
  2. the King of Israel; cf. Exod. 15:18; Num. 23:21; Jdgs. 8:23; 1 Sam. 8:7; 12:12; 1 Kgs. 22:19; Ps. 10:16; 29:10; Isa. 6:5; 41:21; 43:15; Jer. 46:18; 48:15; 51:57
  3. Redeemer (BDB 145 I, cf. Isa. 41:14; see SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM)
  4. the Lord of hosts; see SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS
  5. I am the first and I am the last (cf. Isa. 41:4; 43:10; 48:12; Rev. 1:8,17; 21:6; 22:13)
  6. God (Elohim), see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.
  7. Rock, Isa. 44:8 (cf. Isa. 17:10; 26:4; 30:29; Ps. 18:2)

These titles emphasize the uniqueness, eternality, faithfulness, and power of Israel's God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (NT)

▣ "there is no God besides Me" This is an affirmation of uniqueness and monotheism. This is a recurrent theme in Isaiah (i.e. Isa. 43:11; 45:5,6,21; 46:6,8; Deut. 4:35,38; 1 Sam. 2:2; Mark 12:32).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

entries.title: Isaiah 44:7 "Let him proclaim and declare it"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:7 "Let him proclaim and declare it" This is an allusion to the court scene again. YHWH is challenging the idols to prove their existence and power but they cannot (cf. Isa. 41:21-24; 45:21; 46:10). They cannot predict the future.

Notice the number of commands addressed to the false gods (i.e. the idols of the nations).

  1. proclaim ‒ BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  2. declare ‒ BDB 616, KB 615, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  3. recount ‒ BDB 789, KB 884, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  4. declare ‒ same as #2

entries.title: Isaiah 44:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:8 In light of the impotence of the false gods of the nations, Israel is not to

  1. tremble ‒ BDB 808, KB 922, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  2. fear ‒ BDB 923, KB 437 (רהה), Qal IMPERFECT (NEGATED) used in a JUSSIVE sense (different root from Isa. 44:2 (ירה) BDB 431, KB 432)

▣ "you are My witnesses" YHWH had a specific revelatory purpose for His servants/servant (see note at v. 23; 43:10-12; 55:4,6-13). Predictive prophecy is a major part of establishing the uniqueness and inspiration of the Bible.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

▣ "I know of none" YHWH answers His own question. The VERB (BDB 393, KB 390) is Qal PERFECT; there is no other god or gods, only Him.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

entries.title: Isaiah 44:9-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:9-20 This is a prose section dealing with the folly of idolatry (cf. Ps. 115:2-8; Isa. 40:18-20; 41:7; 45:20; 46:5-7; Jer. 10:2-16). See a good brief discussion in John H. Walton, ANE Thought and the OT, pp. 116-117.

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

44:9
NASB  "futile"
NKJV  "useless"
NRSV  "nothing"
TEV  "worthless"
NJB  "nothingness"
REB  "less than nothing"
JPSOA  "to no purpose"
LXX, Peshitta  "vain, vanity"

This is the Hebrew word (BDB 1062) translated

  1. "formless" in Gen. 1:2; Jer. 4:23
  2. "desolation" in Isa. 34:11
  3. "emptiness" in Isa. 41:29
  4. here it denotes unreality (i.e. idols, cf. 1 Sam. 12:21; Isa. 41:29)

This term (BDB 1062) is parallel to "vain" (BDB 996). It is used in Isaiah often.

  1. Isa. 24:10 ‒ ruined cities
  2. Isa. 25:21 ‒ false/empty testimony
  3. Isa. 34:11 ‒ chaos/desolation
  4. Isa. 40:17 ‒ worthless
  5. Isa. 40:23 ‒ nothing/void
  6. Isa. 41:29 ‒ confusion caused by idols
  7. Isa. 44:9 ‒ idols are nothing
  8. Isa. 45:18 ‒ the earth as unformed, Gen. 1:2; Jer. 4:23
  9. Isa. 45:19 ‒ waste place
  10. Isa. 49:4 ‒ of disobedient Judah's nothingness are vanity
  11. Isa. 59:4 ‒ empty arguments

Here the idols of the nations are non-existent, vain, worthless things! Other texts suggest that these idols are used by the demonic to seduce and trick fallen humans (cf. Deut. 32:16-17; Ps. 106:37; 1 Cor. 8:4-6; 10:20; Gal. 4:8; Rev. 9:20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEMONS (fallen angels)

entries.title: Isaiah 44:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 44:10 This is a rhetorical, sarcastic question.

entries.title: Isaiah 44:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:11 There is a series of IMPERFECTS used as JUSSIVES describing the idol maker and worshiper.

  1. let them assemble ‒ BDB 867, KB 1062, Hithpael IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  2. let them stand up ‒ BDB 763, KB 840, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  3. let them tremble ‒ BDB 808, KB 922, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  4. let them be put to shame ‒ BDB 101, KB 116, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

entries.title: Isaiah 44:14-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:14-20 This shows the folly of idolatry (cf. Jer. 10:2-16).

  1. plants a tree
  2. cut it for
    1. warmth
    2. cooking food
    3. making a god
    4. falls down in worship before a helpless god, the remainder of a cut log. He asks the log to help him, save him!
    5. the maker forgets all this preparation because he has deceived himself (Isa. 44:20)

entries.title: Isaiah 44:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:18 Is the unbelief and superstition a result of

  1. the Fall (cf. Isa. 1:3; Jer.10:8,14; 2 Cor. 4:4; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND)
  2. YHWH's hand (cf. Ps. 81:12; Isa. 6:9-10; Jer. 10:29; Rom. 11:7-8; 2 Cor. 3:14; see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD HARDENED

The OT relates all causality to God (i.e. see full note at Isa. 14:24-27; also note Isa. 6:9-10; 29:10), but still humans are responsible for their acts. This is the mystery of God's sovereignty and humanity's free will (i.e. necessary human acts for God's forgiveness, cf. Isa. 55:7). Maybe Ps. 81:12 sums it up best (cf. Rom. 1:24,26,28; Phil. 2:12-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: ONE CAUSALITY

entries.title: Isaiah 44:19 "an abomination"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 44:19 "an abomination" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION.

entries.title: Isaiah 44:20 "He feeds on ashes"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:20 "He feeds on ashes" Ashes (BDB 68) has several connotations here.

  1. part of the wood the idolater used to make his idol/god, he now uses to cook his food, Ps. 102:9
  2. symbol of insignificance ‒ Gen. 18:27; Ezek. 28:18; Mal. 4:3
  3. symbol of mourning ‒ 2 Sam. 13:19; Esther 4:1,3; Ps. 102:9; Isa. 61:3
  4. symbol of worthlessness ‒ Job 13:12; BDB 68 lists Isa. 44:20 here
  5. symbol of that which is unclear, loathsome ‒ Job 30:19
  6. NET Bible, p. 1256, #9, suggests "he eats on an ash heap."

entries.title: Isaiah 44:21 "My servant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:21 "My servant" See SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV  "you will not be forgotten by Me"
REB, LXX, Peshitta, JPSOA  "never forget me"

The interpretive question is, "Does this line of poetry match v. 21a, "remember" (Qal IMPERATIVE) or does it refer to "YHWH's memory?" The MT has a Niphal IMPERFECT (BDB 674, KB 728) VERB which is normally viewed as PASSIVE (NASB). Most ancient versions view it as a Qal IMPERFECT which parallels the call of v. 1 for Judah to remember YHWH.

Theologically speaking both are crucial to a covenant relationship.

The UBS Text Project, p. 121, gives the PASSIVE a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

entries.title: Isaiah 44:21-23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:21-23 In light of the false witness of idolatry, the true witness of YHWH's people is crucial! They are commanded to

  1. remember, Isa. 44:21 ‒ BDB 269, KB 269, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. return, Isa. 44:22 ‒ BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal IMPERATIVE (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT))

YHWH's creation is also to witness

  1. shout for joy, O heavens, Isa. 44:23 ‒ BDB 943, KB 1247, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. shout joyfully O depths of the earth, Isa. 44:23 ‒ BDB 929, KB 1206, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  3. break forth with a shout of joy you mountains and forests, Isa. 44:23 ‒ BDB 822 KB 953, Qal IMPERATIVE

It is ironic that the idol makers burn and form the trees, but the trees rejoice over YHWH's redemption and Israel's witness to His glory.

entries.title: Isaiah 44:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:22 This is another tremendous promise of complete forgiveness. The VERB "wipe out" (BDB 562, KB 567, Qal PERFECT) is also used in Isa. 43:25; Ps. 51:1,2,9. When God forgives, God forgets (cf. Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; Micah 7:19).

The bases for this complete blotting out of our transgressions are

  1. YHWH's redemption (i.e. "I wipe away your sins")
  2. a believer's repentance (i.e. "come back to Me")

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 44:23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:23 Notice how all creation rejoices at YHWH's forgiveness (cf. Rom. 8:18-22)

  1. heavens, cf. Ps. 69:34; 96:11 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN)
  2. Sheol, cf. Deut. 33:13; Ps. 148:7; Hab. 3:10 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEOL)
  3. mountains, cf. Ps. 65:12; 98:8; 148:9; Isa. 55:12; Hab. 3:10
  4. forests, cf. Ps. 96:12; Isa. 55:12; Hab. 3:10 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES)
▣
NASB, NKJV  "lower parts of the earth"
NKJV, JPSOA  "depths of the earth"
TEV  "deep places of the earth"
NJB  "underworld"
LXX, Peshitta  "foundations of the earth"

This apparently refers to Sheol (BDB 982).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, I. B.

entries.title: Isaiah 44:24 Redeemer"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:24 Redeemer" This is the term Go'el, which has the same definition as "ransom" with the added idea of a near kinsman as the agent. It is often a title for God (cf. Job 19:25; Ps. 19:15; 78:35; Isa. 41:14; 43:14; 44:6,24; 49:7; 59:20; Jer. 50:34); it is used in this personal sense to reveal God's character and Israel as His chosen special family.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "the one who formed you from the womb" This is imagery referring to the formation of the nation of Israel (cf. Isa. 45:2). It is used uniquely of the Exodus experience. This concept of birthing also lends itself to the concept of the people of God as the children of God.

▣ "I, the Lord, am. . ." This is literally the phrase, "I am YHWH," which is a key phrase in the OT. It is a play on the covenant name for God, from the VERB "to be" (cf. Exod. 3:14). Its basic meaning is "I am the ever-existing, only-existing God."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "maker of all things" This is the emphasis of God as both Creator (cf. Psalm 104) and Redeemer (cf. Isa. 45:12,18; Psalm 103).

▣ "Stretching out the heavens by Myself" Here again is God as Creator. This phraseology is used in Isa. 40:22; 42:5; 45:12,18; 51:13.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CIRCLE OF THE EARTH

▣
NASB  "all alone"
NKJV, Peshitta (Qere)  "by Myself"
NRSV, DSS, LXX, TEV  "no one helped me"
NJB  "who was with me?"
REB  "alone"
JPSOA  "unaided"
NET  "all by myself"

The MT has "who with me" (Ketiv), which parallels "alone" (BDB 94 II) in the previous line of poetry. The Masoretic Text scholars suggested "by myself" (Qere). No one gave YHWH counsel or suggestions when He created the earth (cf. Job 38:4ff).

Some scholars see the "Us" of Gen. 1:26; 3:22; 11:7, as referring to an angelic council, but even if this is true, this text asserts YHWH Himself created and performed these things (cf. "by myself" and "all alone").

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

entries.title: Isaiah 44:24 "His glory"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:24 "His glory" YHWH's glory, in this context, is the truth that He is the only true God, the Creator, the Redeemer. Israel was to witness to the nations of this great truth (cf. v. 8). They were trapped in idolatry, superstition, and manipulated by the demonic. Only Israel had true revelation. They were called into being as the covenant people to share this message with the world.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDMPTIVE PLAN

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 44:24-28
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:24-28 This is one sentence in Hebrew. It is a series of relative clauses which are translated by the NIV as "who. . ." It is significant that this is a structured unit (i.e. Isa. 44:24-45:13) because the climax is found in the mention of Cyrus II by name in Isa. 45:28. It is basically a unit dealing with "the God who can" versus the idols who cannot. YHWH announces beforehand what will occur to prove His existence and power (cf. Isa. 41:22-23; 44:7,26).

Notice the list of "who. . ." in NIV (i.e. Qal PARTICIPLES).

  1. who formed you in the womb, Isa. 45:24
  2. who has made all things, Isa. 45:24
  3. who alone stretched out the heavens, Isa. 45:24
  4. who spread out the earth by Myself, Isa. 45:24
  5. who foils the signs of false prophets, Isa. 45:25
  6. who overthrows the learning of the wise, Isa. 45:25
  7. who carries out the words of his servants, Isa. 45:26
  8. who says of Jerusalem, "it shall be inhabited," Isa. 45:26
  9. who says to the watery deep, "Be dry," Isa. 45:27
  10. who says of Cyrus, "He is my shepherd," Isa. 45:28

entries.title: Isaiah 44:25 "omens. . .diviners. . .wise men"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:25 "omens. . .diviners. . .wise men" This verse is an exposure of the occult practices of the surrounding nations, particularly Neo-Babylon. It is a literary foil for God to discuss His true prophets in Isa. 45:26. Biblically, the way to determine a true prophet is found in Deut. 13:1-3; 18:22. The false prophets and the true prophets are going to be contrasted in order to reveal that God is the only God.

It is possible that the Hebrew word translated "boasters" in the NASB can mean (i.e. "the omens of boasters")

  1. liars, vain talkers (BDB 95 III)
  2. soothsayers, from an Akkadian root (AB, vol. 20, p. 72), which would make it parallel to "diviners" (line 2). The Barim priests of Neo-Babylon were known for their predictions (Leupold, p. 133).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

entries.title: Isaiah 44:26 "Confirming the word of His servant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:26 "Confirming the word of His servant" God is in control of history. His forth-telling of future events is one way to prove to all mankind that YHWH is the only Creator, Redeemer God (cf. Isa. 41:22-23; 45:7,26; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE [its uniqueness and inspiration]). Throughout this section of Isaiah prophecy is used as a means of God demonstrating His ability over against the inability of the occult practices to determine future events.

The words "servant" (BDB 712) and "messengers" (BDB 521) are parallel. The first is SINGULAR (UBS Text Project, p. 122, gives the SINGULAR a "B" rating) and the second PLURAL. Is this meant to refer to

  1. the Servant
  2. the prophets (NET Bible)

or are both to be understood as the prophet? Thereby, "servant" would be a way to characterize all prophets.

This verse may be an allusion to Isa. 2:2-4 or Micah 4:1-4.

▣ "It is I who says of Jerusalem, 'she shall be inhabited'" This is a very specific prophecy of not only the restoration of Jerusalem but also of the cities of Judah (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; Dan. 2:24-27; Mic. 4:1-3).

entries.title: Isaiah 44:27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:27 There has been much discussion on the meaning of this verse. These are the theories:

  1. YHWH controls the waters of chaos (cf. Genesis 1; Psalm 74:12-17; Isa. 51:10).
  2. It is a reference to God's splitting of the Red Sea and the Jordan River and, therefore, is a reference to the Exodus.
  3. It shows that God can overcome any barrier and is used in the sense of God drying up or overcoming the Euphrates River (i.e. note Isa. 11:15-16) so that Cyrus can defeat Babylon.
  4. This is used in some sense that God is the controller of moisture which proves that He, and not Ba'al, is the true fertility God, the God of abundance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS/SEA

entries.title: Isaiah 44:28 "It is I who says of Cyrus"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
44:28 "It is I who says of Cyrus" Cyrus is mentioned by name for the first time in this context. He is also mentioned by name in Isa. 45:1. Josephus, in his book, Antiquities of the Jews, 11.1.2, says that Jewish tradition believes that these prophecies were shown to Cyrus and because of them he allowed the Jews to return to Judah. We also learn that Cyrus was impressed by these prophecies in 2 Chr. 36:22-23.

▣ "He is My shepherd" This term primarily speaks of a leader or administrator. There are two very strong kingly terms used here, "shepherd" (BDB 944 I) in Isa. 44:28 and "anointed one" (BDB 603) in Isa. 45:1. Both of these terms show that God will use Cyrus to accomplish His larger purposes. This does not imply that Cyrus became a believer (cf. Isa. 45:5c), but that God uses human instrumentality in order to accomplish His purposes (i.e. Exod. 3:7-10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE, F. #4

▣ "Your foundation will be laid" The fulfillment of this prophecy, related to both the city of Jerusalem and the temple, is found in the books of Ezra, Nehemiah, Daniel (i.e. Dan. 9:24-27), and Haggai.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:1 "anointed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:1 "anointed" This is a title in the OT used for several kinds of people.

  1. for King Saul, 1 Sam. 12:3; 24:6
  2. for the people of God, Hab. 3:13
  3. for the Patriarchs, Ps. 105:15
  4. for the priests, Lev. 4:3,5,16
  5. for "the Coming One," Dan. 9:25; Ps. 2:2

It is used as a Messianic title developed during the inter-biblical period. The term "Messiah" comes from the Hebrew term "Anointed One." Cyrus being called by this term shows that election in the OT was primarily for service, not salvation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE

▣ "by the right hand" YHWH is actively guiding Cyrus II. See SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "to loose the loins of kings" This imagery ("loose," BDB 834, KB 986, Piel IMPERFECT) refers to loosening the sash, which either

  1. implies a man's garments were free-flowing which made it difficult to move (JPSOA footnote, "I made them helpless")
  2. the sash may have held weapons and they, therefore, dropped to the ground (cf. Isa. 45:5; NET Bible, "disarm Kings")
45:2
NASB  "rough places smooth"
NKJV  "crooked places straight"
NRSV, TEV  "level the mountains"
NJB  "open gateways"
JPSOA  "level the hills that loom up"
REB, Peshitta  "level the swelling hill"

The NRSV is literal ("make straight," BDB 448, KB 449, Qere, Piel IMPERFECT). It is also found in the DSS and LXX. "Mountain" may be imagery of problems or fears (JPSOA, cf. Isa. 40:4; 41:15; 42:15; 49:11).

▣ "shatter the doors of bronze, and cut through their iron bars" These are all imagery that YHWH will cause Cyrus II to succeed in his conquest over the walled cities of Mesopotamia and Palestine.

It is interesting that the historian, Herodotus, 1:179, mentions that the city of Babylon had over 100 brass gates.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS TO ISAIAH 44:24-45:25

  1. This is a very specific prophecy. Cyrus II, also known as Cyrus "the Great," is mentioned by name in Isa. 44:28 and 45:1. YHWH has claimed several times that He knows and controls events (cf. Isa. 41:22-23; 44:7,26). This prophecy is the major impetus for the theory of multiple authorship of Isaiah. I believe that Isaiah is written by only one author and that God not only reveals the future of the Assyrian Empire, but also that of the Neo-Babylonian and the Persian Empires through this 8th century B.C. prophet.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)
    SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

  2. This particular reference to Cyrus has to do with his decree of 538 B.C. that allowed all of the exiled people (exiled by Assyria and Neo-Babylon) to return to their native lands and rebuild their national temples with the help of the Persian treasury. For the specific reference to the Jewish return see Ezra 1:2-4; 6:3-5. Cyrus' primary motivation for this was for each of the nations to pray to their own god on Persia's behalf and Cyrus' successors (cf. Ezra 6:10; 7:23).

  3. I think that Isaiah 45:6 is extremely significant. It shows again not only the purpose of God choosing Israel, but also of God choosing Cyrus. God chose Abraham to choose the world and He chose Cyrus for the same larger purpose.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

  4. Notice the number of times the different words for create are used.
    1. BDB 427, KB 428 ‒ form, create, Isa. 44:24; 45:7,9 (twice), 18 (twice)
    2. BDB 793, KB 889 ‒ do, make, Isa. 44:24; 45:7,9,11,18
    3. BDB 135, KB 153 ‒ create, Isa. 45:7 (twice), 8,12,18 (twice)

    The theological emphases of this "new age" section are

    1. YHWH alone created everything
    2. YHWH formed Israel for a purpose
    3. YHWH is alone and unique (monotheism)
    4. YHWH proves His existence by
      1. predictive prophecy
      2. Israel's existence

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 45:3 "treasures of darkness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 45:3 "treasures of darkness" This is the hidden wealth of the empires of Mesopotamia and the Near East.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:4 "For the sake of Jacob My servant,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:4 "For the sake of Jacob My servant,

 And Israel My chosen one" Here we have the first of two reasons why YHWH used Cyrus:

  1. the restoration of His chosen people to Palestine
  2. He wanted the people of Israel to be a light to the world, Isa. 45:6. Israel was not a light so God used Cyrus II (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

▣ "Though you have not known Me" YHWH used Cyrus even though he did not know Him. There is a play on the word "know" in Isa. 45:4,5,6. In Hebrew the term "know" speaks of intimate personal relationship (cf. Gen. 4:1; Jer. 1:5), not only cognitive knowledge. There is no merit on Cyrus' part that God should choose him, but God used him for divine purposes.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW (using mostly Deuteronomy as a paradigm)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN, D.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:5 "I am the Lord, and there is no other"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:5 "I am the Lord, and there is no other" This is an affirmation of monotheism (cf. Isa. 44:24; 45:6-7,14,18,21,22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "Besides Me there is no God" This is another way of referring to monotheism (cf. Isa. 44:6,8; 43:11). See Special Topic above.

▣ "I will gird you" This means "arm you." The weapons were worn on the girdle (cf. Isa. 45:1). This is the opposite of Isa. 45:1d.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:6 "That men may know from the rising to the setting of the sun
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:6 "That men may know from the rising to the setting of the sun

  That there is no one besides Me" Here again is the astonishing prophecy that YHWH chose Cyrus II for the same purpose that He chose Israel, which was to reveal Himself to all the world so that all the world might come to know Him (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 60:1-3; 66:23).

entries.title: Isaiah 45:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:7 This verse has caused much consternation among commentators because it seems to make God the creator of evil. Basically, what is seen here is the denial of a dualism in the universe. This may reflect the Persian influence of Zoroastrianism, but we are uncertain of Cyrus' relationship to this developed dualism. This verse is basically saying that there is only one causality in the universe (see full note at Isa. 14:24-27). God is in control of all things. He uses evil for His purposes! This is another way of affirming monotheism.

Verse 7 is a series of Qal PARTICIPLES relating to God's creating activities put in contrasting pairs.

  1. forming ‒ BDB 427, KB 428
  2. creating ‒ BDB 135, KB 153 (see John Walton, ANE Thought and the OT, p. 183)
  3. causing ‒ BDB 793, KB 889
  4. creating ‒ BDB 135, KB 153
  5. doing ‒ BDB 793, KB 889

Be careful of taking one verse out of a poetic context and using it as the basis of a doctrinal statement. Genre and context are crucial in proper interpretation!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ONE CAUSALITY

entries.title: Isaiah 45:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:8 The prophet is using the crisis of his own day to foreshadow the future kingdom of God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY [OT]). In context, this verse is influenced by Isa. 45:6, which means that this is the idealistic future when all believing humans will know and worship God, which was the purpose of the original creation (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KINGDOM OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ Verse 8 is a series of IMPERATIVES (i.e. prayers) directed toward God's created order.

  1. drip down ‒ BDB 950, KB 1271, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  2. pour ‒ BDB 633, KB 683, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  3. open ‒ BDB 834, KB 986, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  4. bear fruit ‒ BDB 826, KB 963, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  5. spring up ‒ BDB 855, KB 1033, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

YHWH ends the paragraph/verse with His summary statement of His creating power (BDB 135, KB 153, Qal PERFECT)! This emphasis on God as creator introduces the rest of the chapter (esp. Isa. 45:18). As He created the earth, so too, Israel. Creation has a relational purpose (i.e. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8).

Notice the goal is righteousness and salvation!

entries.title: Isaiah 45:9 "Woe to the one who quarrels with his Maker ‒"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:9 "Woe to the one who quarrels with his Maker ‒" We have seen several allusions to the court scene literary model in Isaiah. Now "woe" identifies another prophetic literary model, "the funeral dirge." It was a "grave" warning to those (Jews or Gentiles) who question YHWH. In context, this strophe would refer to the shock felt by Judeans at the inclusion of Gentiles!

This shows the presence of some Judeans who reacted negatively to God's way of handling restoration to Palestine (cf. Isa. 10:15; 29:16; 45:11; also note Jonah). They were upset that God would use an unbelieving ruler such as Cyrus II (cf. Isa. 45:13). This is very similar to the prophet Habakkuk's incredulous thoughts about God using Neo-Babylon.

▣ "Will the clay say to the potter" This concept of humans as clay and YHWH as potter is common in the Bible, probably because

  1. humans are made from the dust or clay and will return to dust (cf. Gen. 2:7; 3:19; Isa. 29:16; Jer. 18:1ff; Rom. 9:20-21)
  2. it highlights YHWH's freedom to do with His creation whatever He desires and purposes (cf. Romans 9-11)

There are MSS variants here.

  1. with the potsherds of clay (MT)
  2. with the potters of clay (NEB, JPSOA)
  3. with the potter of clay (RSV, NRSV)

The UBS Text Project, p. 123, gives a "C" rating to #1. This means the committee could not decide which option was original.

▣
NASB, NKJV  "He has no hands"
NRSV, JPSOA  "Your work has no handles"
REV, REB  "you have no skill"
NJB  "your work has no hands"
Peshitta  "am I not the work of your hands"
NAB  "what you are making has no hands"
LXX  "nor do you have hands"
NET  "Your work lacks skill"

This can mean

  1. the idols have no hands
  2. the craftsmen have no skill
  3. the vessel has no handles

It is best just to recognize the ambiguity and look to the other lines of poetry in Isa. 45:9 and Isa. 45:10 for a general contextual meaning. That which is created (i.e. a pot or an idol) cannot question the creator!

entries.title: Isaiah 45:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:11 This verse starts out with several titles for God.

  1. YHWH (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)
  2. the Holy One of Israel (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE)
  3. Israel's Maker (BDB 427, KB 428, Qal PARTICIPLE)

It then continues the emphasis on YHWH as the predictor of future events (i.e. Cyrus' conquest).

The UBS Text Project (p. 125) suggests, "questions me about the things to come, (but) as to my sons and the work of my hands, let me take care of them!" (JPSOA, "will you question Me").

▣ "My hands" SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

entries.title: Isaiah 45:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:12 Line 1 reflects Genesis 1.

▣ "stretched out the heavens" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CIRCLE OF THE EARTH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

▣ "with My hands" SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "And I ordained all their host" Here again YHWH is magnifying His unique place as Creator of heaven and earth. The Babylonians worshiped the stars and planets. This is a strong statement that YHWH commanded (BDB 845, KB 1010, Piel PERFECT) all their hosts (cf. Isa. 40:26; 48:13; Ps. 33:6). This emphasis on YHWH as the creator and controller of the heavenly bodies (i.e. sun, moon, stars, planets, comets) functions like Genesis 1 in showing the folly of astral worship.

In Isa. 24:21-22 the word "host" is used for the angelic powers behind the nations (cf. the LXX of Deut. 32:8 and Daniel 10). Whether it is angelic or planetary, YHWH is in control of all the lesser spiritual beings of the universe called elohim. There is no other Supreme Being but YHWH, but there are other spiritual forces.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND THE DEMONS

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

entries.title: Isaiah 45:13 "I have aroused him in righteousness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:13 "I have aroused him in righteousness" The NIV translates the "him" as Cyrus. YHWH stirred up Cyrus to do His will. This refers to

  1. the rapid and complete conquests by Cyrus II
  2. the decree of Cyrus II, which allowed all the exiled people groups to go home and rebuild their national temples. This decree was given in 538 B.C., one year after the fall of Neo-Babylon.

▣ "My city" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO CITIES IN ISAIAH

▣ "Without any payment or reward" YHWH will give Cyrus II victory and he in turn will let Israel return to Judah without a bribe or payment (TEV).

The Jewish Study Bible (p. 876) says that Isa. 45:14 refers to YHWH's reward to Cyrus.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:14 It is uncertain if Isa. 45:14-17 comprises a literary unit. It is obvious that Isa. 45:15-17 is referring to Judah (cf. Isa. 43:3). It is possible that Isa. 45:14 may refer to Cyrus II and not to Judah.

However, these same nations are given as a ransom for God's people in Isa. 43:3. All the world was meant to come to God in Isa. 45:20-22. Therefore, Judah could be the subject of Isa. 45:14. This is very similar to the prophecies that all the nations will stream to a restored Zion (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 60:1ff; Ps. 72:8-11; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

The summary line of Isa. 45:14, "No other God," carries over to Isa. 45:16 (i.e. "they"). Both the idols and their worshipers shall be

  1. put to shame ‒ BDB 101, KB 116, Qal PERFECT
  2. humiliated ‒ BDB 487, KB 480, Niphal PERFECT

But Israel will not (cf. Isa. 45:17)!

▣
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "men of stature"
NRSV, NJB  "tall of stature"
TEV  "tall men"
REB, JPSOA footnote  "bringing tribute"
JPSOA  "long of limb"
LXX  "lofty men"

The MT has "men of stature." The JPSOA footnote mentions Ezra 4:20; 8:6; Neh. 5:4 as corroborative historical evidence for the emendation.

  1. "men of" ‒ אנשׁו (BDB 60)
  2. "tribute" ‒ אשׁכר (NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 552)

Option #2 fits the context best but there are no textual examples.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:15 Notice the names for God

  1. God (El, BDB 42)
  2. God (Eloah, BDB 43) of Israel
  3. Savior (BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil PARTICIPLE)

The Savior of Israel did hide Himself from His people for a period of time because of their sin and rebellion (cf. Isa. 1:15; 8:17; 54:8; 57:17; Ps. 44:24; 88:14, also note Job 13:24). But that period of judgment has passed (cf. Isa. 40:2) and now the return and restoration has begun through Cyrus II.

The AB, vol. 20, p. 82, suggests this hiddenness is because Judah was a small and insignificant nation at this period of time.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:16 See note at Isa. 45:14. Verse 16 is theologically parallel to Isa. 44:11.

▣ "put to shame" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME

entries.title: Isaiah 45:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:17 This is a wonderful promise but readers need to remember it is conditional on Judah's covenant obedience. Just to read this and forget that Israel was again conquered and destroyed by both Greece and Rome shows the limits of proof-texting.

The problem was not YHWH's love, power, and promises, but Israel's inability to keep His commandments. See SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

The Hebrew terms "everlasting" (BDB 761) and "eternity" (BDB 761) are from a Hebrew root that has a wide range of meaning (i.e. semantic field).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

entries.title: Isaiah 45:18 "He established it and did not create it a waste place"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:18 "He established it and did not create it a waste place" This is an allusion to Gen. 1:2. It could be translated "without form" (BDB 1062). YHWH always had a purpose for this planet. That purpose is that it would be inhabited (i.e. Gen. 1:28; 9:1,7). There was a purposful, planned development in God's creation. This does not prove some kind of destruction between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2 (i.e. the Gap Theory). See full note at Gen. 1:1-2 online. I have been blessed by a new understanding of Genesis 1; see John H. Walton, The Lost World of Genesis One: An Ancient Cosmology. This book sees Genesis 1 as Elohim preparing this planet for human population. Dr. Walton views this text in light of other ANE cosmologies and concludes that it is not addressing initial creation, but organization.

▣ "But formed it to be inhabited)" This is used by the rabbis to stress that everyone should marry (cf. Gen. 1:28; 9:1,7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CELIBACY AND MARRIAGE

entries.title: Isaiah 45:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 45:19 YHWH has asserted over and over in this section of Isaiah that He is the God who hears and acts; Who knows the future and sets its course! This theological assertion is a primary evidence of His existence! The other evidence is the existence of Israel and her return to the Promised Land.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:20 "Gather yourselves and come;
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:20 "Gather yourselves and come;

Draw near together, you fugitives of the nations;

They have no knowledge"

Some say this refers to scattered, exiled Israelites returning home (i.e.,"you fugitives of the nations," also note Isa. 45:25), while others believe it is another general invitation to the Gentile nations, as in Isa. 45:6,22,23 (cf. Rom. 14:11; Phil. 2:10). Both are possible in this context.

There is a series of commands in Isa. 45:20-22 related to how humans are to approach YHWH and respond to His offer of availability.

  1. gather yourselves ‒ BDB 867, KB 1062, Niphal IMPERATIVE, Isa. 45:20
  2. come ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE, Isa. 45:20
  3. draw near ‒ BDB 620, KB 670, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, Isa. 45:20
  4. turn to Me ‒ BDB 815, KB 937, Qal IMPERATIVE, Isa. 45:22
  5. be saved ‒ BDB 446, KB 448, Niphal IMPERATIVE, Isa. 45:22

The NT uses Isa. 45:23 in two quotes that refer to all humans (i.e. Rom. 14:11 and esp. Phil. 2:10)! What a wonderful invitation and fulfillment of Gen. 3:15 and 12:3.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "Who carry about their wooden idol" This is a recurrent call on the nations to reject their idols who cannot see, hear, or act, and come to the God of Israel who can act and who will save them.

entries.title: Isaiah 45:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:21 This is the imagery of a court scene. It predicts

  1. Cyrus II and his success
  2. the return of Israel as an evangelistic tool to bring the world to God

Here, God is called a "Savior" and in this context implies not of Jews only but of the entire world (cf. Isa. 45:22; 49:6; 51:4; 52:10; Acts 13:47). The obvious implication of monotheism is that the One God loves all humans created in His image (cf. Gen. 1:26-27).

entries.title: Isaiah 45:22 "Turn to Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:22 "Turn to Me" This is the Hebrew word that is used for worship (BDB 815, KB 937, Qal IMPERATIVE PLURAL). As the people turn to God they leave their idolatry and sin (cf. Isa. 55:7).

Humans have a choice. They can turn to YHWH and be saved or turn to idols (cf. Lev. 19:4,31; 20:6; Deut. 31:18,20) and have no hope!

This is a wonderful invitation for the nations to be included in the Family of God!

▣ "and be saved, all the ends of the earth" This is a reference to the universal salvation offered to all humans who will repent and trust in YHWH because there is no other God (cf. Isa. 45:21). This universal offer is so characteristic of Isaiah (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 60:1-3; 66:23).

This can be translated "save themselves" (Niphal IMPERATIVE), which would be a play on Gen. 12:3 (see exegetical notes online).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 45:23 "I have sworn by Myself"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:23 "I have sworn by Myself" There is no higher oath possible! This, of course, is imagery for God's truthfulness

▣ "The word has gone forth from My mouth in righteousness

  And will not turn back"  This is the ancient belief in the power of the spoken word (cf. Isa. 24:3; 25:8; 40:8; 55:10-11). God said it; He wants the world to be saved (i.e. John 3:16; 4:42; 1 Tim. 2:4; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:2; 4:14)!

▣ "That to Me every knee will bow, every tongue will swear allegiance" There are several different ways (i.e. physical positions) that ANE people worshiped.

  1. standing up ‒ 1 Sam. 1:26; 1 Kgs. 8:22; Jer. 18:20
  2. kneeling ‒ 1 Kgs. 8:54; 2 Chr. 6:13; Ps. 95:6; Isa. 45:23; Dan. 6:10-11
  3. prostrated ‒ Ps. 5:7; 95:6; 99:5,9; 138:2

A good example of multiple positions based on which part of the worship event is Nehemiah 9:2-5.

  1. they stood while Torah was read
  2. they knelt down to confess their sin
  3. they stood up again at the direction of the Levite leaders

This is used in this context of YHWH. However, in Phil. 2:10 it is used of all conscious creation confessing Jesus Christ as Lord. The context again shows that God wants the whole world to come to Him and later revelation will show it is through His Messiah, Jesus Christ, that this universal offer is accomplished (cf. Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL).

The theological issue is very clear. If the NT is revelation, then the OT promises to national Israel have been widened. Neither Jesus nor any NT writer ever reaffirms a national promise to Israel!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE OT COVENANT PROMISES SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

45:24
NASB, NRSV  "will come to Him"
NKJV  "To Him men shall come"
TEV  "all who hate me"
NJB  "who used to rage at him"
REB  "All who defy him"
NET  "all who are angry at him"
JPSOA  "trust in Him"

The MT has "shall come and be shamed" (two Qal IMPERFECTS). The question is, "To whom does 'will come to Him' refer?"

  1. those who acknowledge YHWH (v. 23d, JPSOA, cf. Ps. 65:2b)
  2. those who are angry (v. 24c, TEV, NJB, NET, REB)

▣ "And all who are angry at Him shall be put to shame" This does show that one day all peoples, whether they believe in YHWH or not, will acknowledge Him as Lord (cf. Phil. 2:10-11). Some will have previously acknowledged Him and be saved, but some will acknowledge Him just before judgment and separation (cf. Matt. 25:31-46; Rev. 20:11-15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT

entries.title: Isaiah 45:25
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
45:25 YHWH not only desires the worship of the nations, but the vindication and glory of Abraham's seed.

As a Christian, this terminology, "all the offspring of Israel," causes me to note Rom. 2:28-29; 9-11, esp. 9:6; 11:26; also see Gal. 3:7-9,29; 6:16; 1 Pet. 3:6.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. List the characteristics of God mentioned in Isa. 44:24-28. (there are nine relative clauses)
  2. Why did God choose Cyrus?
  3. What is the significance of the Hebrew word "know" (cf. Isa. 45:4-6)?
  4. Why is Isa. 45:6 so significant?
  5. List the number of times and ways the doctrine of monotheism is mentioned in this passage.
  6. Does Isa. 45:8 refer to the return from exile or the Messianic kingdom? Why?
  7. What is the significance of Isa. 45:22?
  8. How is Isa. 45:23 used in the NT and what significance does it have for this passage?

entries.title: Isaiah 46:1 "Bel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:1 "Bel" Bel (BDB128, KB 132, Akkadian for "lord" is a similar title to the Canaanite title Ba'al). This is a reference to the chief god of the Akkadian pantheon (Enlil, who was called "lord"). As Babylon came to power the chief deity's name was changed to Marduk (BDB 597, cf. Jer. 50:2).

▣ "Nebo" This was the son of Marduk (named only here in the OT) who was the god of learning and writing (BDB 612). He was the chief deity of the city of Borsippa. Bel and Nebo can be seen in many of the Babylonian names of the period.

  1. Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:1)
  2. Nebushazban (Jer. 39:13)
  3. Nebuzaradan (Jer. 39:9)
  4. Nabopolassar (first king of Neo-Babylon, and Nebuchadnezzar's father)
  5. Nebuchadnezzar
  6. Nabonidus (Belshazzar's father, last king of Neo-Babylon)
  7. Belteshazzar (Dan. 1:7)
  8. Belshazzar (Dan. 5:1)

These were the two chief gods of the Babylonian pantheon.

▣ "bowed down. . .stoops over" There is a play on the concept "bow down" (BDB 505, KB 499). It relates to 45:23, the deities of Babylon are bowing before YHWH the Creator.

▣ "you carry. . .load. . .the burden" There is a play on the word "carry" in Isa. 46:1-2 and 3-4. First of all the idols of Babylon must be carried on beasts of burden to try to escape the Persians or in ritual marches through the streets of the large cities. God carries His children, both metaphorically in the womb and later, throughout their lives (cf. Isa. 46:4). It is the inability of the Babylon gods to hear, to act versus the care, provision, and grace acts of the God of Israel, with which they are contrasted in Isa. 46:1-4.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. H. C. Leupold, in his commentary on Isaiah, p. 147, reminded me that
    1. in Isaiah 14 the kingdom of old Babylon is judged
    2. in Isaiah 46 the idols of Neo-Babylon are judged
    3. in Isaiah 47 the nation, personified as a queen, is judged

  2. "Babylon," in the Bible, is imagery for all human society organized and functioning apart from God (as is Edom in Isaiah 34). It is mankind's attempt to meet his needs with his own resources. Babylon is personified as the great whore in Revelation 18 (which, by the way, I think refers to faithless Jerusalem. See my new 2024 exegetical, verse-by-verse commentary of Revelation [i.e. Partial Preterist]).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 46:2 "They stooped over"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:2 "They stooped over" This is a play between the animals that carried the heavy cast idols (v. 6) bowing down just like the idol's makers.

▣ "They could not rescue the burden" The idols could not save themselves (i.e. taken by conquerors), nor could those who worshiped them.

▣ "But have themselves gone into captivity" Here these Neo-Babylonian idols are personified as going into captivity with their people.

entries.title: Isaiah 46:3 "Listen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:3 "Listen" This, like Isa. 46:12, is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570). See note at Isa. 44:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "the remnant" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES

▣ "have been carried from the womb" This primarily is a reference to God as parent and Israel as child. However, it also refers to the formation of the nation of Israel beginning with the Exodus (cf. Deut. 1:31; Isa. 63:9).

entries.title: Isaiah 46:4 "Even to your old age"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:4 "Even to your old age" God not only created Israel but will sustain her (i.e. "carry" or "bear" them, cf. Exod. 19:4; Deut. 1:31; 32:11).

▣ "I shall be the same" This (lit. I Am He, cf. NKJV) is the concept that God does not change (cf. NJB, cf. Mal. 3:6 and James 1:7). Even though Israel has been unfaithful to the covenant, God remains faithful. He is the God of covenant loyalty. He is the same yesterday, today, and forever!

For a discussion of "covenant loyalty" see SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "And I will bear you and I will deliver you" This is a reference to the nation of Israel, but it is individualized also to every believer (SINGULAR VERBS). Notice the VERBS in Isa. 46:4.

  1. God had created Israel (Qal PERFECT, BDB 793, KB 889)
  2. God will continue to provide and protect
    1. bear you ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 687, KB 741 (twice)
    2. carry you ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 669, KB 724 (twice)
    3. deliver you ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 572, KB 589

entries.title: Isaiah 46:5 "To whom would you liken Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:5 "To whom would you liken Me" This is the theological emphasis that no one can be compared with YHWH (cf. Isa. 43:11; 44:6,8; 45:6). This is a comparison between YHWH and the idols of the nations (cf. Isa. 40:18-20; 44:9-20).

Notice the parallelism.

  1. to whom would you liken Me ‒ Piel IMPERFECT (BDB 197, KB 225)
  2. and make Me equal ‒ Hiphil IMPERFECT (BDB 1000, KB 1436)
  3. and compare Me ‒ Hiphil IMPERFECT (BDB 605, KB 647)
  4. that we should be alike ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 197, KB 225)

YHWH is unique! He is the ever-living, only-living, one true God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM). Also note the surprising NT theological revelation of Trinity, see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

entries.title: Isaiah 46:6-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:6-7 These two verses are the contrast between the one true God of Isa. 46:5 and the idols of the nations.

  1. people give money to make images and then bow down and worship them (Isa. 46:6)
  2. they then move them here and there but they cannot move themselves; the idols cannot deliver (Isa. 46:7)

entries.title: Isaiah 46:8 "Remember"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:8 "Remember" This verse and the first line of Isa. 46:9 contain a series of IMPERATIVES.

  1. remember, Isa. 46:8 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 269, KB 269)
  2. be assured, Isa. 46:8 ‒ Hithpoel IMPERATIVE (BDB 84, KB 100)
  3. recall, Isa. 46:8 ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE (BDB 996, KB 1427)
  4. remember, Isa. 46:9 ‒ same as #1

Number 2 is a rare form found only here in the OT. The Aramaic Targums translate it as "take courage," possibly from a related Arabic root (cf. Leupold, p. 145).

▣
NASB  "be assured"
NKJV  "show yourselves men"
NRSV  "consider"
Peshitta  "discern"
NJB, JPSOA  "stand firm"
REB  "abandon hope"
LXX  "groan"
NET  "so you can be brave"

This Hebrew term (BDB 84, KB 100 II) is found only here.

  1. BDB ‒ found, establish
  2. KB ‒ to pluck up courage
  3. Arabic related root
  4. NIV Lexicon ‒ fix in mind
  5. Owens, Analytical Key to the OT ‒ consider

▣ "you transgressors" This shows that some in Israel still had doubts about the way God was performing His task of restoration (cf. Isa. 45:9-11, the book of Habakkuk). This same group is referred to in Isa. 46:12 as "the stubborn minded" of the Jewish people.

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 46:9 "the former things long past"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:9 "the former things long past" This could refer to

  1. YHWH's ancient covenant with Abraham (cf. Gen. 12; 15; 17; 22; Isa. 43:18; 65:17; Jer. 16:14; 23:7)
  2. YHWH's acts of birthing (i.e. the Exodus) them
  3. Israel's ancient promise to be loyal and abide by the covenant (cf. Exod. 19:8; 24:3,7; Deut. 5:27)
  4. YHWH's proof of His existence by predicting the future (cf. Isa. 46:10,11; 42:9; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE [its uniqueness and inspiration])

▣ "For I am God" This verse uses two titles for "God."

  1. El ‒ BDB 42, cf. Isa. 40:18-42:5; 43:10; 44:10,15,17; 45:14,15,20,21,22; 46:6
  2. Elohim ‒ BDB 43, cf. Isa. 40:1,3,8,9,27,28; 41:10,13,17; 43:3; 44:6; 45:3,5,14,15,18,21

This, like v. 5, is a continuing emphasis on monotheism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, A., C.

entries.title: Isaiah 46:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:10-11 Again, God is using the example of predictive prophecy (i.e. the summoning of Cyrus II) to show that He is in control of history. The emphasis on His purposes, mentioned so often in Isa. 46:10-11, shows that history is not random but has a divine purpose (i.e. teleological; cf. Isa. 14:24,26; 25:1). This assurance of YHWH fulfilling His Divine Plan is also seen in Isa. 14:24; 25:1; 40:8; 55:11 (see Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed., pp. 371-390).

The phrase in 10a is theologically parallel to Isa. 41:4; 44:6; 48:12. YHWH is the "present one" from the "very" beginning to the "very" end (i.e. the first and last)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 46:12 "Who are far from"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:12 "Who are far from" This description of God's covenant people is contrasted with the nearness ("it is not far off," Isa. 46:13b) of YHWH's deliverance

  1. through Cyrus II (temporal)
  2. through the Messiah (eschatological)
▣
NASB, NKJV, LXX, Peshitta  "righteousness"
NRSV  "deliverance"
TEV, JPSOA, REB  "victory"
NJB  "saving justice. . .justice"

The Hebrew word used twice is "righteousness" (BDB 842 see SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS). BDB says it is used of the salvation of God (#6a) in Isa. 45:8; 46:13; 51:6.

entries.title: Isaiah 46:12-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 46:12-13 This is a very important passage and shows that God will have mercy even on unbelieving Israel. This shows that the Israelite people did not deserve God's love and mercy. Many of them were still stubborn and stiff-necked (see SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORN, cf. Isa. 48:4), but God brought salvation to them because of Who He is and not because of who they are (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36). This is the New Covenant model (cf. Jer. 31:31-34).

entries.title: Isaiah 46:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
46:13 The Hebrew term "deliverance" (BDB 842) is parallel to "salvation" (BDB 448).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS (BDB 842)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT) (BDB 447)

entries.title: Isaiah 47:1 "Come down"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:1 "Come down" This funeral dirge is one of three literary models used by the Hebrew prophets to communicate their divine messages.

  1. funeral dirge
  2. court scene
  3. promise oracle

▣ "sit in the dust" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "O virgin daughter of Babylon" This was a Semitic idiom of security and preciousness in family imagery. She (the Neo-Babylonian Empire) who was so secure and protected, has now become vulnerable.

▣ "sit in the dust. . .sit on the ground without a throne" This is literally "sit" (BDB 442, KB 444, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 47:1 [twice],5,8 [twice]). It was one of the physical signs of mourning.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "O daughter of the Chaldeans" This is parallel to "Babylon," see full note at Isa. 43:14. It is repeated in v. 5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS

▣ "shall no longer be called tender and delicate" These two terms (BDB 940 and 772) are used in Deut. 28:56 for luxurious, extravagant living. This is contrasted with Isa. 47:2-3, where she is now

  1. a slave
  2. a prostitute
