READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. If chapter 46 emphasized the fall of the Neo-Babylonian idols, then chapter 47 describes the fall of the empire itself (i.e. the city of Babylon) along with its occult prophets and priests.

  2. Verses 1-7 have a series of IMPERATIVES directed at Neo-Babylon, depicted as a prostitute/queen.
    1. come down, Isa. 47:1 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 432, KB 434)
    2. sit in the dust, Isa. 47:1 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 442, KB 444)
    3. sit on the ground, Isa. 47:1 ‒ same as #2 (notice the number of times this term is used in Isa. 47:1 [twice],5, 8 [twice])
    4. take, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 542, KB 534)
    5. grind, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 377, KB 374)
    6. remove your veil, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Piel IMPERATIVE (BDB 162, KB 191)
    7. strip off the skirt, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 362, KB 359)
    8. uncover the leg, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Piel IMPERATIVE (BDB 162, KB 191)
    9. cross the river, Isa. 47:2 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 716, KB 778)
    10. let your nakedness be uncovered, Isa. 47:3 ‒ Niphal JUSSIVE (BDB 162, KB 191)
    11. sit silently, Isa. 47:5 ‒ same as #3,4
    12. go into darkness, Isa. 47:5 ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 97, KB 112)

  3. The prophetic literary form of this chapter is a "funeral dirge." It is recognized by its unique beat/meter in Hebrew (3, 2 beat, like the poems of Lamentations). It is a funeral lament but in a sarcastic sense (Taunt Song).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 47:2-3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:2-3 This is a series of phrases used to describe one who used to be the queen of the nations (Isa. 47:5,7) and is now a slave.

  1. she grinds meal, Isa. 47:2
  2. she removes her veil, Isa. 47:2
  3. she had to prepare her clothes for hard labor, Isa. 47:2
  4. she had to cross the rivers herself and not be carried (possibly into exile), Isa. 47:2
  5. her nakedness was uncovered, Isa. 47:3 (cf. Jer. 13:26)
    1. as a punishment for sin (cf. Isa. 20:4)
    2. simply the lot of slaves who were poorly clad and sexually vulnerable
47:3
NASB  "and will not spare a man"
NKJV  "I will not arbitrate with a man"
NRSV  "I will spare no one"
TEV  "no one will stop me"
NJB  "no one stands in My way"
REB  "show clemency to none"
JPSOA  "let no man intercede"
LXX  "I will no longer deliver you over to men"
Peshitta  "I will not meet you as a man"

This is a somewhat ambiguous phrase but the VERB "I will not spare" (BDB 803, KB 910, Qal IMPERFECT), had an etymological relationship to prayerful intercession (BDB 803, KB 910, cf. Isa. 53:12; 59:16; Jer. 36:25). It seems to mean that no one could intercede for Neo-Babylon or that no human was powerful enough in prayer to stop YHWH's predetermined plan for her judgment.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:4 This is an exclamation from the author who interjects himself into the flow of poetry (REB adds "says" to the MT, making these statements come from YHWH. The UBS Text Project, p. 127, gives this option a "B" rating). Three of the beautiful titles for God are seen here as the prophet praises YHWH for Who He is. The titles are:

  1. Redeemer ‒ an emphasis on God as Savior; He is the One who buys people back from slavery (see SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM)
  2. Lord of hosts ‒ a Persian title which focuses on one of two areas (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS)
    1. the angelic council, Isa. 24:21-22 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS)
    2. the astral deities of Babylon, Isa. 40:26
  3. the Holy One of Israel ‒ the title for God who will bring this to pass on behalf of His people (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

entries.title: Isaiah 47:5 "Sit silently, and go into darkness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:5 "Sit silently, and go into darkness" This major world power has now become a peasant. This verse tells her to seek obscurity and be silent (two IMPERATIVES).

▣ "The queen of kingdoms" This is an idiom of Neo-Babylon's view of itself and its power (cf. Isa. 47:7). The queen has become a sex slave (cf. Isa. 47:2-3,8a). What she did to exiles will now happen to her (i.e. divinely caused role reversal).

It is just possible that this idiom relates to Nabonidus leading Neo-Babylon away from Marduk to the worship of the moon goddess called "the Queen of heaven." She was called Sin (Akkadian) or Nanna (Sumerian).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP

entries.title: Isaiah 47:6 "I was angry with My people"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:6 "I was angry with My people" This explains why the covenant people were taken into exile. In the ancient world the deity of the individual nations protected them. The fact that both Israel and Judah were taken captive was seen by the ANE world as the gods of the Fertile Crescent being more powerful than the God of Israel, but this was not the case. God was using the powers of the Fertile Crescent to judge His people for their sin (cf. Isa. 10:5; 42:24). This was clearly foreshadowed in Lev. 26 and Deut. 28.

▣ "You did not show mercy on them" Although God gave His people to Assyria and Babylon in order to punish them, these pagan nations went too far and now they will be judged for their lack of mercy.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:7 "These things you did not consider
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:7 "These things you did not consider

 Nor remember the outcome of them"

The two VERBS are Qal PERFECTS, which denote a settled attitude.

  1. did not consider, lit. "did not lay these things to heart"
  2. did not remember their end

Notice how Isa. 47:8 continues the thought.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:8-9 "Who dwells securely. . .but these two things shall come upon you suddenly"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:8-9 "Who dwells securely. . .but these two things shall come upon you suddenly" It seems from Daniel 5 and from Herodotus that the people of Neo-Babylon laughed at the approaching Persian army. However, the Persian army rechanneled the waters of the Euphrates River, went under the walls of this magnificent city, and in one day the city fell (cf. Daniel 5). The common people of the city of Babylon saw the Persians as liberators because Belshazzar and his father, Nabonidus, had begun to worship a strange moon goddess called Sin (Nanna, see SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP) and Cyrus II allowed them to return to their traditional deities—Bel, Marduk, and Nebo.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MARDUK

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEBO

47:8
NASB  "sensual one"
NKJV, Peshitta  "you who are given to pleasure"
REB  "lover of luxury"
JPSOA  "pampered one"
NJB  "voluptuous woman"
TEV, NRSV  "lover of pleasure"
LXX  "luxurious one"

This is a rare Hebrew ADJECTIVE (BDB 726, KB 792) which denotes one accustomed to an easy, pampered life.

▣ "I am, and there is no one beside me" This is an obvious challenge to the uniqueness of YHWH (cf. Isa. 47:10; same language used by Nineveh in Zeph. 2:5). Which One delivered His people? Which One is the true, unique God who possesses power?

entries.title: Isaiah 47:9 "Loss of children"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:9 "Loss of children" Note Isa. 13:16,18. What she did to others will happen to her!

▣ "many sorceries. . .the great power of your spells" The emphasis on Neo-Babylon's occultic practices, made so specific here, is continued in Isa. 47:11-13. These practices are condemned in Deuteronomy 18. For all her magical arts Neo-Babylon could not protect herself, which shows the ineffectiveness of occult practices (i.e. the weakness of her gods).

  1. sorceries ‒ BDB 506
  2. spells ‒ BDB 288 I

The NET Bible, p. 1260, #23, thinks these terms refer to spells and amulets that were worn by most people in the ANE to ward off evil spells, demons, bad luck, or danger.

See a good brief discussion in IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 631.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

entries.title: Isaiah 47:10 "secure in your wickedness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:10 "secure in your wickedness" The Dead Sea Scrolls change "wickedness" (BDB 949) by changing a "d" to an "r," which makes it mean "knowledge" (BDB 395, which occurs in line c of v. 10). Either of these words fits the context.

▣ "No one sees me" This implies that they knew what they were doing was wicked and were trying to hide themselves (cf. Isa. 29:15).

47:11
NASB, NRSV, NJB, JPSOA, NET  "charm away"
NKJV, Peshitta  "from where it arises"
TEV  "your magic can not stop it"
JPSOA footnote  "bribe"
REB  "conjure it away"

The MT, "you cannot know her dawn," thus the Peshitta and NKJV translations. There have been several suggested emendations.

  1. from the root (KB 1466 III) "to cause to disappear by magic," thus NASB, REB, NET trandslations
  2. from a root (JPSOA footnote) "to bribe" or "buy off," from BDB 1005

▣ "atone" This is the Hebrew word "to cover" (BDB 497, KB 493, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) and is used of the OT concept of atonement as being a blood covering on the mercy seat (cf. Leviticus 16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ATONEMENT

▣ "suddenly" This certainly describes the fall of the city of Babylon.

entries.title: Isaiah 47:12 "Perhaps you may cause trembling"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 47:12 "Perhaps you may cause trembling" H. C. Leupold adds the word "me" to show the possibility that God is telling them to see if their spells threaten Him or cause Him to tremble. This seems to be the meaning of the passage. It may, however, refer to the Persian army (NJB).

entries.title: Isaiah 47:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:13 Not only are Neo-Babylon's deities helpless and humiliated (cf. Isa. 47:1-3,5), but also her prophets and counselors/sorcerers (cf. Isa. 47:14).

▣
NASB, NKJV, LXX  "counsels"
NRSV, NJB  "consultations"
TEV  "advise"
JPSOA  "art"

This is the same Hebrew word, "counsel" (BDB 420 calls it "political consultation") that is translated "purpose" (REB) in Isa. 46:10,11. This may be a contrast between YHWH's plans/purposes that will come to pass and the faulty, weak, ineffective plans/purposes of the Neo-Babylonian religious elite!

No one "counseled" YHWH (cf. Isa. 40:13). He always fulfills His plans (cf. Isa. 44:26; 46:10,11).

▣
NASB, NKJV, TEV, NJB, LXX  "astrologers"
NRSV  "those who study the heavens"
JPSOA  "scanners of heavens"
Peshitta  "Chaldeans"
Emphasized Bible  "the dividers of the heavens"

The MT has the Qal PERFECT of BDB 211, KB 237 (ketiv), which seems to mean "to divide" from an Arabic root. The Masoretic scholars suggested that the Qal PARTICIPLE of the same root be read (qere). If this is accurate then it is parallel with "those who prophesy by the stars" (i.e. astrologers).

entries.title: Isaiah 47:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
47:14 Verse 14 has one unified theme (i.e. judgment by fire) or the first three lines are judgment but the last two may relate to astrologers, the false prophets or enchanters finding a place of comfort from the cold weather by the fire they made from the scraps of their wooden idols (i.e. Isa. 44:16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. What is the play between Isa. 45:23 and 46:1-2?
  2. What is the word play between Isa. 46:1-2 and 46:3-4?
  3. List the number of ways that monotheism is emphasized in Isaiah 46 and 47.
  4. What does 46:8 have in common with Isa. 46:12?
  5. How does one reconcile God's control over history and human freedom?
  6. Why is Isa. 46:12-13 important to our concept of justification by faith?
  7. List the number of ways that Babylon has fallen from luxury to slavery.
  8. List the types of occult practices found in Isa. 47:9-13.

entries.title: Isaiah 48:1 "Hear"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:1 "Hear" This is a common IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570) for Isaiah, as well as Deuteronomy, Kings, Job, Psalm, and Amos, to begin a new section (cf. Isa. 1:2,10; 7:13; 28:23; 36:13; 37:17; 47:8; 46:3,12; 47:8; 48:1,14,16; 49:1; 51:1,7; 55:2; 66:5). YHWH wants His message "heard" and "lived out." Divine revelation demands obedience! Truth is not only mental but lifestyle!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣
NASB, NRSV, Peshitta  "from the loins of Judah"
NKJV  "from the wellsprings of Judah"
TEV  "you who are descended from Judah"
NJB  "issued from the waters of Judah"
REB  "from the seed of Judah"
LXX  "came forth out of Judah"
JPSOA  "have issued from the waters of Judah"

There are three Hebrew roots used by commentators to attempt to explain this text.

  1. "waters," מי (BDB 565, the UBS Text Project, p. 128, gives the MT a "B" rating)
  2. "loins," מעי (BDB 588, NASB, NRSV, AB; DSS, "from the inward parts")
  3. "seed," זרע (BDB 281, REB)

All of these Hebrew terms are imagery for the descendants by natural means of a group, tribe, family. The UBS Text Project, p. 128, gives "from the waters" a B rating.

Notice that all the descendants are designated by

  1. Jacob
  2. Israel
  3. Judah

This implies the returnees were mostly from the southern three tribes called Judah. "Israel" now refers to all of Abraham's seed, as it did before the United Monarchy split in 922 B.C.

▣ "Who swear. . .invoke" Both of these VERBS refer to worship acts.

  1. swear by the name (BDB 989, KB 1396, Niphal PARTICIPLE, cf. Isa. 19:18; 65:16)
  2. invoke (lit. "cause to remember," BDB 269, KB 269, Hiphil IMPERFECT, cf. Isa. 12:4; 26:13; 62:6)
▣
NASB. NKJV, LXX  "But not in truth nor in righteousness"
NRSV  "But not in truth or right"
TEV  "But you don't mean a word you say"
NJB  "Though not in good faith or uprightness"
JPSOA  "Though not in truth and sincerity"
REB  "But not with honesty and sincerity"

Wow, what a condemning evaluation of Israel's worship!

  1. The term "truth" is אמת (BDB 54) and means "faithfulness." See SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT
  2. For the second word, צדקה (BDB 842) see SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. As YHWH addressed Neo-Babylon in Isaiah 46 and 47, He now addresses His people, His returnees, His faithful remnant.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses)

  2. Notice the different ways Israel is referred to.
    1. O house of Jacob, Isa. 48:1
    2. who are named Israel, Isa. 48:1
    3. who came from the loins of Judah, Isa. 48:1
    4. who swear by the name of the Lord, Isa. 48:1
    5. who invoke the God of Israel, Isa. 48:1
    6. you are obstinate, Isa. 48:4
    7. you have been called a rebel from birth, Isa. 48:8
    8. O Jacob, Isa. 48:12,20

  3. Notice the different titles and descriptions of YHWH
    1. the name of the Lord, Isa. 48:1
    2. the God of Israel, Isa. 48:1,2
    3. I am He, Isa. 48:12
    4. I am the first, I am the last, Isa. 48:12
    5. the Lord (YHWH), Isa. 48:14,17,20,22
    6. the Lord God (Adon YHWH), Isa. 48:16
    7. Redeemer, Isa. 48:17
    8. the Holy One, Isa. 48:17
    9. the Lord your God, Isa. 48:17

  4. There are several significant and theologically important verses in this section of Isaiah that will be developed in the NT.
    1. Isa. 45:23
    2. Isa. 46:8-11
    3. Isa. 48:8-11
    4. Isa. 48:16

  5. H. C. Leupold entitles this chapter "A Sharp Rebuke and a Gracious Challenge" (p. 158). This fluctuation between judgment and mercy characterizes prophetic literature and it happens side by side with little or no textual transition markers.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 48:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:2 The first two lines remind me of Jeremiah's "Temple Sermon" in Jeremiah 7, where the Israelites trust in the temple but not in YHWH.

  1. call themselves after the holy city (BDB 894, KB 1128, Niphal PERFECT, cf. Isa. 48:1)
  2. lean on the God of Israel (BDB 701, KB 759, Niphal PERFECT)

Their worship looked orthodox and pious but it was false and directed to the wrong source.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

entries.title: Isaiah 48:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:3 YHWH again speaks (notice the number of "I's") of His control of time and history. He uses predictive prophecy to show His people His existence and power (v. 5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

entries.title: Isaiah 48:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:4 YHWH describes His people as

  1. obstinate (cf. Ezek. 2:4; 3:7)
  2. neck is an iron sinew
  3. forehead is bronze

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

▣ "know" This word (BDB 393, KB 390) is used several times in this chapter (cf. Isa. 48:4,6,7,8 [twice]), where it means "knowledge about," but it should mean "intimate fellowship with."

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

entries.title: Isaiah 48:5 "idol"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:5 "idol" This verse mentions two kinds of false images of deities (cf. Isa. 40:20; 46:5-7).

  1. carved from wood (cf. Isa. 44:9-17; Jer. 10:1-10)
  2. cast of metal in a mold (cf. Isa. 30:22; 40:19; 41:7)

entries.title: Isaiah 48:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:6 There is some question about how the VERBS of the first two lines should be translated. I like the NJB's version, "You have heard and seen all this, why won't you admit it?"

The "it" refers to YHWH's predictions (cf. Isa. 42:9; 43:19; 48:5). YHWH proves His existence by His knowledge of and control of future events affecting all nations not just Israel/Judah.

For "new things" see full note at Isa. 62:2.

entries.title: Isaiah 48:8 "deal very treacherously"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:8 "deal very treacherously" This intensified grammatical form is a Qal IMPERFECT and a Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same root (BDB 93, KB 108). A good example is Jer. 44:15-19.

▣ "a rebel from birth" See Deut. 9:7. Even in the exit from Egypt, Israel was idolatrous (i.e. Ezek. 20:8,13; Amos 5:25-26).

entries.title: Isaiah 48:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:9 This is a good summary of YHWH's problem with Abraham's seed. He wanted to use them so that the world would know Him and come to Him (cf. Gen. 12:3). But they were not faithful. He had declared, "the soul that sins it will die" (i.e. Gen. 2:16,17; Ezek. 18:4,20). Now God's word and God's purpose come into conflict. He will choose to act for the greater good (i.e. salvation of all humans, cf. 1 Sam. 12:22; Ps. 106:8; Jer. 14:7; Ezek. 20:8-9,14,17). The text that describes this so well is Ezek. 36:22-36! YHWH acts for Israel for His greater purpose! Is this not what Isa. 48:11 is affirming? This is the wonderful message of Isaiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

48:10
NASB, NKJV, JPSOA  "tested"
NRSV, Peshitta  "refined"
NJB  "chosen"
REB  "purified"
LXX  "delivered"

The MT has the VERB "choose" (בחר, BDB 103, KB 119, Qal PERFECT, NJB), but the DSS scroll of Isaiah has a similar VERB "tested" (בחן, BDB 103, KB 119), which fits the context better. The UBS Text Project gives "refined" a "B" rating.

entries.title: Isaiah 48:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:11 This verse is similar in content to Ezek. 36:22-36. The last line is reflected in Isa. 42:8.

▣
NASB  "how can My name be profaned?"
NKJV  "how should My name be profaned?""
NRSV, NJB  "why should My name be profaned?"
TEV  "I will not let my name be dishonored"
REB  "I will not let my name be profaned"
JPSOA  "Lest [My name} be dishonored!"
Peshitta  "that my name may not be polluted"
LXX  "because my name is profaned"

In the UBS Text Project, p. 130, the committee gives four possible textual options, but it cannot decide which one is original.

  1. how should it be profaned
  2. how should my name be profaned
  3. how should I be profaned
  4. how should my praise be profaned

It chose option 3 as the best guess.

entries.title: Isaiah 48:12 "Listen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:12 "Listen" See full note at v. 1.

▣ "I am He, I am the first, I am also the last" This is a recurrent idiom in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 41:4; 44:6) and becomes a common designation for Christ in Rev. 1:17; 2:8; 22:13! It is theologically parallel to "I am the Alpha and Omega" (cf. Rev. 1:8). It denotes the God of creation (Isa. 48:13; Jesus was the Father's agent in creation, cf. John 1:3,10; 1 Cor. 8:6; Col. 1:16; Heb. 1:2) and eternity—eternity past, eternity future (i.e. time). The only God is YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

entries.title: Isaiah 48:14 "Assemble, all of you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:14 "Assemble, all of you" This command to gather (BDB 867, KB 1062, Niphal IMPERATIVE) refers to "O Jacob, even Israel" of v. 12.

▣ "listen" See note at 48:1.

▣ "Who among them has declared these things" The "who" seems, in context, to refer to the astrologers, false propehts, and enchanters of Isa. 42:11. YHWH shows His reality by His predictions and actions, which surprised the hearers.

The things delcared have to do with His judgment on Neo-Babylon by Cyrus II (Persia).

  1. YHWH loves him
  2. YHWH will carry out His good pleasure through him

entries.title: Isaiah 48:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:15 The first phrase ("I, even I, have spoken," BDB 180, KB 210, Piel PERFECT) is a way of accepting the power of YHWH's spoken word (cf. Isa. 55:11). His purposes cannot be thwarted!

▣ Notice YHWH's actions toward His instrument (i.e. Cyrus II) for His covenant people's release from exile

  1. I have spoken ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, Piel PERFECT
  2. I have called him ‒ BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal PERFECT
  3. I have brought him ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Hiphil PERFECT
  4. He will make his ways successful ‒ BDB 852, KB 1026, Hiphil PERFECT with waw

entries.title: Isaiah 48:16 "Come near to Me, listen to this"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:16 "Come near to Me, listen to this" These two IMPERATIVES match/parallel the two IMPERATIVES of v. 14, "assemble, all of you and listen."

▣ "From the first I have not spoken in secret" YHWH made His plans, will, and future events known through

  1. revelation to Moses
  2. revelation from the prophets

Israel/Judah knew exactly what YHWH wanted and expected from them.

▣
NASB  "now the Lord God has sent Me, and His Spirit"
NKJV  "and now the Lord God and HIs Spirit have sent Me"
NRSV  "and now the Lord God has sent me and his spirit"
TEV  "Now the Sovereign Lord has given me his power
  and sent Me"
NJB  "and now Lord Yahweh has sent me with his spirit "
JPSOA  "and now the Lord God has sent me, endowed
  with His Spirit"
LXX  "and now the Lord has sent me and his spirit"
REB    omit

Wow! How many persons and who are they who are being mentioned? Who is the speaker? Obviously, the first is YHWH. His Spirit is probably the same as Gen. 1:2; Isa. 11:2; 42:1; 61:1. But who is the "me"?

  1. the prophet Isaiah speaking for YHWH
  2. the Messiah (or the Servant)
  3. Cyrus II (as if speaking, vv. 14-15)

Christians can easily see the Trinity in this text (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY, II>). The same three persons are mentioned again in Isa. 61:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

entries.title: Isaiah 48:17 "the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:17 "the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel" This is a recurrent use of divine title in this section of Isaiah (cf. Isa. 41:14; 43:14; 49:7,26; 54:5,8). It is expressed in a slightly different but parallel way in Isa. 49:26, "I the Lord, am your Savior, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D. (YHWH)

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

▣ "your God" See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D. (Eloah)

▣ "who teaches you to profit" This is the use of the root "profit" (BDB 418 I, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) in the sense of advantage (cf. Job 21:15; 35:3; Jer. 12:13; Isa. 47:12). Often it is used of what idols cannot do for the worshiper (cf. Isa. 44:9,10; 57:12; 1 Sam. 12:21; Jer. 2:8; 7:8,11; 23:32; Hab. 2:18).

▣ "Who leads you in the way you should go" This is the Semitic idiom of the righteous life as a "good path" (cf. Ps. 32:8; 119:105; Prov. 1:1-6). Here it probably refers to YHWH's presence and provisions on the way home from exile (cf. Isa. 48:20; 49:9-10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

entries.title: Isaiah 48:18-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 48:18-19 This is a "what if. . ." text that reflects the covenant blessing and cursing of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28. Israel sinned and reaped the terrible consequences. She was created for righteousness and revelation, but disobedience and idolatry led to darkness and confusion.

entries.title: Isaiah 48:19 "Like the sand"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:19 "Like the sand" The OT uses these images for Israel's descendants.

  1. dust
  2. stars
  3. sand

See full list of texts at Gen. 13:16 and 15:5 online.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

entries.title: Isaiah 48:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:20 This is a series of commands to the returning exiles.

  1. Go forth from Babylon ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 422, KB 425)
  2. Flee from the Chaldeans ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 137, KB 156)
  3. Declare with the sound of joyful shouting ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE (BDB 616, KB 665)
  4. Proclaim this ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570)
  5. Send it out to the end of the earth ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE (BDB 422, KB 425)
  6. Say. . . ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 55, KB 65)

YHWH announces to His people to leave exile and go home. To the world He announces His purpose (cf. Isa. 62:11; Jer. 31:10; 50:2) and that He has accomplished it! He wants the world to know so they will come to know Him (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 42:6; 45:22-23; 51:4-5; 60:1,3; Acts 13:46-49)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 48:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 48:21 The return from Assyrian and Babylonian exile was seen as a new exodus (i.e. Isa. 35:6; 49:10) and wilderness wandering (i.e. Exod. 17:6; Deut. 8:15). YHWH will provide their every need. He will be with them as He was with the Israelites during the exodus.

entries.title: Isaiah 48:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
48:22 This is a summary statement related to unbelievers and idolaters (cf. Isa. 57:21; 59:8). Any path without YHWH is a path of destruction and ruin. This decision-making process is known in the OT as "the two ways" (cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Ps. 1:1; Prov. 4:10-19; Jer. 21:8; Matt. 7:13-14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 49:1 "Listen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:1 "Listen" See full note on the introductory IMPERATIVE at Isa. 48:1.

There are two IMPERATIVES that introduce this new literary unit.

  1. listen ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570)
  2. pay attention ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE (BDB 904, KB 1151)

God's revelation of Himself and His purposes was meant to be heard, understood, and acted on!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (Shema)

▣ "O islands. . .peoples from afar" These parallel phrases show the universal implications of the "servant's" task (cf. Isa. 42:6-7). The love of God

  1. remembers its covenant with Abraham's descendants (cf. Isa. 49:5-6b)
  2. remembers the promise to all humans, Gen. 3:15; 12:3 (cf. Isa. 49:6c; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDMPTIVE PLAN)

There is a dual aspect to YHWH's message

  1. to the returning covenant people from exile by Cyrus' decree
  2. to the returning nations under the Servant/Messiah

There is always in Isaiah an eye on the present (Assyria); the near Future (Neo-Babylon, Persia), and the distant future (gospel age). YHWH's desires for Israel's

  1. righteousness
  2. revelation to the nations

was never fulfilled. The evangelistic mandate (see note at Isa. 40:15) was transferred to the NT people of God (cf. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT PREDICTIONS OF THE FUTURE vs. NT PREDICTIONS

▣ "The Lord called Me from the womb" The NASB has the PRONOUNS capitalized to show that they think they refer to the Messiah, the individualized Servant (i.e. LXX of Isa. 52:14). God's special call is expressed in the Servant's prenatal call (cf. v. 5, as was Jeremiah, cf. Jer. 1:5). There is an obvious tension in these "Servant" passages between the individual and corporate aspects of the Servant. It is clear from Isa. 41:8-9; 42:19; 43:10; 49:3 that the title is used for corporate Israel. However, the individual focus of the SINGULAR PRONOUNS of chapter 49 and the work of the individual in Isa. 52:13-53:12 show that these passages have a dual focus. This dual focus can also be seen in chapter 42. Verses 1-4 relate to the Messiah, while Isa. 49:19-21 are obviously corporate Israel. Israel was called to be a kingdom of priests to bring the world to God, Gen. 12:1-3; Exod. 19:4-6. She failed because she did not and could not keep the covenant. God fulfilled His universal redemptive task through one faithful Israelite-Jesus! This same tension between the individual and corporate can be seen in that Isa. 49:6 is quoted in Luke 2:32 to refer to Jesus' ministry and in Acts 13:46-49 referring to the ministry of Paul and Barnabas.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "From the body of My mother" The word "body" is literally "inward parts" (BDB 588). This speaks of the creation and development of a baby (cf. Ps. 139:13). This same word is used in Isa. 48:19 for "offspring" (also note Gen. 15:4).

▣ "He named Me" The Servant is called and named before birth by YHWH. He is His special representative.

This parallels what YHWH did for national Israel in Isa. 43:1. There is a real and continuing fluidity between the corporate and individual imagery related to the Servant!

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. The literary unit of Isaiah 40-66 focuses on God's restoration of His people through the work of "His Servant" (esp. Isa. 49-57).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

  2. This passage is known as the second Servant Song. See full list of the Songs/Poems at the Introduction to Isa. 42, A.

  3. This chapter has several important truths.
    1. YHWH has prepared a special Savior/Servant
    2. This special Servant will bring all people to Him
    3. YHWH has not forgotten His Servant nation, Israel

      Who is this Servant?

      1. obviously some contests must refer to Israel/Judah (cf. v. 3a)
      2. some contexts, such as Isa. 52:13-53:12 refer to the ideal Israelite, the Messiah
        SPECIAL TOPIC: A SUFFERING MESSIAH
      3. Isaiah himself and his own mission (v. 4)
      4. a faithful remnant of Israel; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses)
      5. The NT uses several texts from Isaiah and applies them to Jesus (i.e. Matt. 12:18-21; Acts 8:21-35; 1 Pet. 2:21-25).

        Remember, there is a fluidity in Isaiah 40-66 between the corporate and the individual.

  4. Note the parallel themes and imagery between Isa. 40 and 49.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 49:2 "He has made My mouth like a sharp sword"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:2 "He has made My mouth like a sharp sword" This is imagery describing a powerful speaker, and here and in Eph. 6:17; Heb. 4:12 it speaks of divine revelation. It is used to describe the glorified Christ as Judge in Isa. 11:4; Rev. 1:16; 2:12-16; 19:15,21.

▣ "In the shadow of His hand" This verse has two images of protection and concealment (cf. Isa. 51:16) until the right time. The Servant's task is specialized and specific. This thought is captured by the recurrent NT phrase "in the fullness of time" (cf. Mark 1:15; Gal. 4:4; Eph. 1:10; 1 Tim. 2:6; Titus 1:3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW, SHADE

entries.title: Isaiah 49:3 "My glory"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 49:3 "My glory" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod)

entries.title: Isaiah 49:3-4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 49:3-4 The focus of these verses is that the Servant is corporate Israel, but the corporate Servant has failed its assigned task! Israel was to be YHWH's chosen instrument of world redemption, Isa. 49:6c,d, but now she herself must be redeemed (cf. Isa. 49:5-6a,b; 53:8d). Verses 5-6 speak of an individual Israelite sent by YHWH to accomplish His redemptive task.

entries.title: Isaiah 49:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:4 There is a contextual question if these verses relate to the failure of Israel or the suffering of the Messiah. All the VERBS are PERFECT. The ambiguity may be purposeful!

The closing two lines of Isa. 49:4 express an ultimate trust in God's justice and reward (cf. Isa. 49:5c).

▣ "My reward with My God" I think this links up with Isa. 53:10-11. The reward will be redemption on a global scale!

entries.title: Isaiah 49:5 "To bring Jacob back to Him"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:5 "To bring Jacob back to Him" This verse and Isa. 49:6b show that the Servant must restore Israel, therefore, the Servant cannot be Israel (see LXX of Isa. 52:14)

▣  "(For I am honored in the sight of the Lord,

 And My God is My strength)

This is a comment from the Servant. It may be a way of encouraging the Servant amidst the disappointments and opposition He will encounter during His ministry (cf. Isa. 53:1-12).

entries.title: Isaiah 49:6 "to restore the preserved ones of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:6 "to restore the preserved ones of Israel" This phrase refers to the faithful remnant of the Chosen People, the chosen instrument of revelation. The hope of a restored, believing Israel is seen in Zech. 12:10 and Romans 9-11 (see the free commentaries on these books at www.freebiblecommentary.org).

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

▣ "I will also make You a light of the nations

So that My salvation may reach to the end of the earth"

Notice the Servant/Messiah had two purposes. If Isa. 49:5 reflects the Israel-focused ministry of the Gospels, then Isa. 49:6 represents the worldwide expansion of the early church. This universal spread of the gospel is an oft-repeated theme in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 60:1,3; 66:23; Acts 13:46-49). Oh what great news for humanity (cf. Gen. 3:15)!

entries.title: Isaiah 49:7 "the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel, and its Holy One"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:7 "the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel, and its Holy One" This series of titles (see note at Isa. 48:17) shows us the tension between

  1. the transcendent and immanent God
  2. God as Savior and God as Judge
  3. God as friend and God as boss

We must hold together justification and sanctification. They form one purpose! YHWH wants a people who display His character.

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)

▣ "To the despised One,

To the One abhorred by the nation,

To the Servant of rulers"

This implies the lowliness of the Servant, even the rejection of the Servant (cf. Isa. 50:4-11; 52:14-53:6; Psalm 22). The MT has the SINGULAR "nation," but used in a collective sense. It is parallel to "rulers," "Kings," and "princes." But ultimately all earthly authority will acknowledge Him (cf. Phil. 2:6-11, which alludes to Isa. 45:22-23). Matthew 12:18-21; Acts 8:26-35; and 1 Pet. 2:21-25 quote Isaiah as referring to Jesus.

Is it not ironical that the one despised and abhorred by the nations (cf. Psalm 2) is the very one that will bring salvation to the nations!

▣ "Kings shall see and arise,

  Princes shall also bow down" These are VERBS of homage.

  1. arise ‒ BDB 877, KB 1056, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Gen. 19:1; 23:7; Exod. 33:10; 1 Sam. 20:41
  2. bow down ‒ BDB 1105, KB 295, Hishtaphel IMPERFECT, cf. Gen. 19:1; 23:7; Exod. 33:10; Lev. 19:32; 1 Sam. 20:4

The One despised and abhorred has now, by YHWH's help, become the respected, honored One!

▣ "Because of the Lord who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel who has chosen You" Here is the key to our hope, YHWH's faithfulness. Our hope is in the character of the One who calls, promises, and redeems!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY ONE

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 49:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:8 Notice that "in a favorable time" and "in a day of salvation" are parallel. This text is quoted in 2 Cor. 6:2. It is used in Ps. 69:13-15 for a day of deliverance. It can denote physical or spiritual deliverance/salvation (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION [OT]). The Year of Jubilee (Lev. 25:10) symbolized this radical forgiveness of debts. In this context they are talking about the return to Palestine, which began with Cyrus' decree in 538 B.C. and was accomplished in several waves.

  1. Sheshbazzar ‒ Ezra 1
  2. Zerubbabel and Joshua ‒ Ezra 2
  3. Nehemiah ‒ Nehemiah 1
  4. Ezra ‒ Nehemiah 8

Notice the VERBS in Isa. 49:8 that describe YHWH's actions.

  1. I have answered You ‒ Qal PERFECT (BDB 772, KB 851)
  2. I have helped You ‒ Qal PERFECT (BDB 740, KB 810)
  3. I will keep You ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 665, KB 718, "watch," "guard," "keep")
  4. I will give You ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 678, KB 733)
    1. to restore the land ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 877, KB 1086)
    2. to make them inherit ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB635, KB 686)

These personal redemptive actions of YHWH are also highlighted in Ezek. 36:21-36.

▣
NASB  "give You for a covenant of the people"
NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta  "give You as a covenant to the people"
TEV  "through you make a covenant with all peoples"
JPSOA  "appoionted you a covenant people"
REB  "destined you to be a light for peoples"
LXX  "given you for a covenant of the nations"
NJB  "have appointed you to be the covenant for a people"
NET  "and make you a covenant mediator for people"

This phrase was used earlier in Isa. 42:6 in which the themes of Isa. 49:6,8 coincide. YHWH's covenant with Abraham and his seed had a wider orientation than just Israel (cf. Gen. 12:3; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN). It was also for the whole world (i.e. the nations; see the different translations of this line of poetry). This is the logical and theological implication of monotheism-only one God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM), all humans created in God's image (cf. Gen. 1:26-27), and a promise to redeem all humans in Gen. 3:15, long before there was a nation of Israel.

entries.title: Isaiah 49:8d-12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 49:8d-12 These verses are imagery of sheep feeding in abundant pastures. They reflect the covenant blessing of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-28. God's people have been restored to the Promised Land! Paul uses this text for the New Age in 2 Cor. 6:2. Verse 10 is also used in Rev. 7:16, which shows Gentiles are included.

entries.title: Isaiah 49:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:9 The Israelites are described as being in prison (i.e. prisoners, BDB 63, cf. Isa. 42:7; 61:1).

  1. to those who are bound
  2. to those who are in darkness

They are told to

  1. go forth ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 422, KB 425)
  2. show yourselves ‒ Niphal IMPERATIVE (lit. "uncover yourself," BDB162, KB 191)

entries.title: Isaiah 49:10 "He who has compassion on them will lead them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:10 "He who has compassion on them will lead them" These are descriptive titles for YHWH.

  1. the one who has compassion ‒ Piel PARTICIPLE (BDB 933, KB 1216)
  2. the one who leads them ‒ Piel IMPERFECT (BDB 624, KB 675)
  3. the one who will guide them ‒ Piel IMPERFECT (BDB 624, KB 675)

SPECIAL TOPIC: DESCRIPTIVE TITLES FOR GOD

▣ The agricultural imagery of provision is from Isa. 49:9 continue.

  1. no hunger
  2. no thirst
  3. no heat stroke (used only here and Isa. 35:7)

The return home will be easy, protected and with abundant provisions (i.e. new Exodus and Wildeness Wandering Period). This same imagery is used in Rev. 7:16 of the Messianic period. YHWH's Messiah is their shepherd (cf. Ps. 121:5-6).

entries.title: Isaiah 49:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:11 Access to Jerusalem is metaphorically assured by the removal of all obstacles and the provision of a repaired, even raised, roadway (cf. Isa. 11:16; 19:23; 35:8; 62:10).

There will be a free-flowing movement between nations for the purpose of worshiping YHWH. The nations have come!

It is interesting how many times Isaiah uses the imagery of a highway.

  1. a highway for the exiled Jews to return, Isa. 11:16; 57:14
  2. a highway for Gentile worshipers to come, Isa. 19:23
  3. a highway of holiness, Isa. 26:7; 35:8; 43:19; 49:11; 51:10
  4. a Messianic highway, Isa. 40:3; 42:16

entries.title: Isaiah 49:12 ". . .And these from the land of Sinim"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:12 ". . .And these from the land of Sinim" The exact location is uncertain. The thrust of the text is that God will bring all His people home, even from the farthest land. Notice the variety in the following translations.

  1. MT, NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta ‒ "Sinim"
  2. NRSV, REB ‒ "Syene" (BDB 696, cf. Ezek. 30:6)
  3. TEV, NIV, NJB ‒ "Aswan"
  4. DSS of Isaiah ‒ "Syenians"
  5. LXX ‒ "Syenians"

All of these are various spellings (except the LXX) of the ancient and modern city in southern Egypt which had a large Jewish population (cf. Ezek. 30:6, #2), also known in Greek literature as Elephantine. Today its name is Aswan.

entries.title: Isaiah 49:13 "O heaven. . .O earth. . .O mountains"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:13 "O heaven. . .O earth. . .O mountains" These have served as witnesses to YHWH's judgment against His people (Isaiah 48). Now they serve as joyful witnesses of God's faithfulness (cf. Isa. 44:23)!

Notice the series of IMPERATIVES.

  1. shout ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 943, KB 1247)
  2. rejoice ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 162, KB 189)
  3. break forth ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 822, KB 953)

▣ "comforted" See SPECIAL TOPIC: COMFORT

entries.title: Isaiah 49:14-21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:14-21 These verses are words of encouragement by YHWH to a discouraged and barren Jerusalem (i.e. Zion). Notice the number of times the word "forget' (BDB 1013, KB 1489) is used.

  1. "the Lord has forgotten me" ‒ Qal PERFECT
  2. "can a woman forget her nursing child" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT
  3. "even these may forget" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT
  4. "I will not forget you" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT

YHWH uses anthropomorphic language to describe His love and faithful protection to the returnees by means of a feminine imagery (hear sermon online at www.freebiblecommentary.org under "Difficult and Controversial Texts," number 111, "The Femininity of God."

entries.title: Isaiah 49:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:15 This is powerful imagery of YHWH's covenant love (cf. Isa. 66:9-13). YHWH is described in terms of a nursing mother.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

entries.title: Isaiah 49:16a
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:16a This may reflect Isa. 44:5. The covenant people, Abraham's descendants, are always on YHWH's mind and heart. This is also true of the city of Jerusalem (v. 16b).

49:17
NASB  "Your builders hurry"
NKJV  "your sons make haste"
NJB  "your rebuilders are hurrying"
JPSOA  "swiftly your children are coming"
NET  "Your children hurry back"

The UBS Text Project (p. 134-135) shows the two options.

  1. your sons, בניך ‒ MT, DSS, Peshitta (cf. Isa. 49:25e)
  2. your builders, בוניך ‒ which the UBS calls "Babylonian vocalization"

The UBS Text Project, pp. 134-135, gives option #2 a C rating (considerable doubt), p. 134.

The second line is also in question.

  1. REV ‒ "Your builders outstrip your destroyers"
  2. NEB ‒ "Those who are to rebuild you make better speed than those who pulled you down"

This difference involves only a revocalization of the Hebrew consonants (UBS Text Project, p. 135).

entries.title: Isaiah 49:16-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:16-17 This is more powerful imagery of YHWH's constant remembrance of His covenant with Abraham's descendants. Even when Jerusalem is in ruins, YHWH's people envision the new day of restoration (cf. Dan. 9:24-27)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

entries.title: Isaiah 49:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:18 Jerusalem was destroyed! She is personified as a mother without children (cf. Isa. 49:20-21). Her husband, YHWH, has now restored her and provided numerous children as the crown of her old age!

YHWH challenges the returnees to

  1. lift up your eyes ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 669, KB 724)
  2. look around ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 906, KB 1157)

▣ "As I live, declares the Lord" This is an oath statement with a play on the Hebrew VERB "to be," which is Israel's God's chosen title (cf. Exod. 3:13-14). YHWH is the ever-living, only-living One!

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "all of them" Tis could refer to

  1. the childen of the returnees (v. 17)
  2. the former destroyers who are now rebuilders (v. 17)

entries.title: Isaiah 49:19-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 49:19-20 These verses are imagery of the large number of returnees and their children who fill up the Promsed Land. This reflects God's stated purpose, "be fruitful and multiply," in Genesis 1 and 9.

entries.title: Isaiah 49:21-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 49:21-22 Those who return to Jerusalem, which symbolizes the worship of YHWH (i.e. the temple), will be so many that the city cannot physically contain them all!

entries.title: Isaiah 49:22 "set up My standard to the peoples"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:22 "set up My standard to the peoples" This is parallel to "lift up My hand to the nations." The Servant will be a signal/flag for the nations (i.e. Gentiles) to rally (cf. Isa. 11:10,12). The ultimate goal of the covenant people's restoration is the restoration of all humanity!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE END-TIME EVENTS SO CONTROVERSIAL?

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 49:22-23
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 49:22-23 In Isa. 49:7 the leaders of the Gentile nations rejected and rebelled against God's Messiah (cf. Psalm 2). Now they come repentantly to Jerusalem bringing God's covenant people with them. This verse is not meant to magnify the Old Covenant, but the covenant-making God! The Gentiles' reverence for YHWH will be seen in their respect for His people (cf. Isa. 45:14).

entries.title: Isaiah 49:23 "And you will know that I am the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:23 "And you will know that I am the Lord" Israel was meant to be a witness to the nations. Now the nations will be a witness to Israel. As Gentiles trust in YHWH and are converted in large numbers, this is a sign to Israel that God is with them but that they must also have faith (cf. Romans 9-11).

▣ "Those who hopefully wait for Me will not be put to shame" The concept of "wait" is found often in Isaiah: 25:9; 26:8; 40:31 (Ps. 37:9). This is analogous to those who "trust in" the Servant! Notice the personal element (i.e. "Me").

The phrase "put to shame" is another theme of the OT (cf. Isa. 45:17; Ps. 25:3; Joel 2:27). Those who wait/trust will not be shamed/disappointed!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME

entries.title: Isaiah 49:24-26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:24-26 These verses are imagery for a second exodus experience. God is delivering His people again from powerful world empires. It is significant that God's purpose in this deliverance, like His first deliverance, is not only that His covenant people might go free but that all nations will know Him (cf. Isa. 49:26c; 45:6; Mal. 1:11).

As a Christian, I wonder if this context was in Jesus' mind in Matt. 12:22-29; Luke 11:14-22. Jesus' exorcisms clearly show His power over evil. The third, and most important, Exodus imagery is Jesus' defeat of sin and Satan! Often, Jesus' ministry uses Exodus imagery.

49:24b
NASB, NRSV, NJB, TEV  "a tyrant"
NKJV  "the righteous"
REB  "the ruthless"
JPSOA  "victor"
Peshitta  "giants"
NET  "a warrior"
DSS  "violent ones"
LXX  "mighty one"

The MT translation is followed by NKJV, but the others come from the DSS, Syriac, and Vulgate.

  1. righteous ‒ צדיק (BDB 843)
  2. tyrant ‒ עריץ (BDB 792)

The UBS Text Project, p. 136, gives option #2 a C rating (considerable doubt). However, #1 makes no sense in this context, unless it is used as an ADJECTIVE for YHWH's people. See Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT, p. 207.

entries.title: Isaiah 49:25 "For I will contend"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:25 "For I will contend" This is "court scene" imagery. Possibly its use in Jer. 50:34 sheds light on this verse.

YHWH/Servant has changed from Prosecutor to Advocate (i.e. legal terminology)!

entries.title: Isaiah 49:26a-b
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:26a-b Israel's enemies (i.e. Assyria, Neo-Babylon) are completely defeated.

  1. eat their own flesh
  2. drink their own blood

This imagery refers to the horrors of siege warfare in the ANE.

entries.title: Isaiah 49:26c "And all flesh will know that I, the Lord, am your Savior"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:26c "And all flesh will know that I, the Lord, am your Savior" It is theologically difficult to know if these Servant Songs refer to the restoration and salvation of national Israel or to the restoration and salvation of all mankind.

In the immediate context, it must refer to corporate Israel, YHWH's covenant people. But, NT authors use these verses to describe the ministry of Jesus. So, these are multiple fulfillment prophecies. I have mentioned how this section of Isaiah (i.e. Isaiah 40-66) often moves between promises to the returning exiles and promises of a universal Messiah.

Jesus fulfilled the OT (cf. Matt. 5:17-19). He opened the door for all the children of Adam and Eve to find Him (i.e. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 49:26c-d
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
49:26c-d Notice again the powerful titles for the Deity of Israel (cf. Isa. 41:14; 43:14; 44:6,24; 47:4; 48:17; 49:7,26; 54:5,8; 59:20; 60:16; 63:16).

  1. Your Savior
  2. Your Redeemer
  3. the Mighty One of Jacob, cf. Isa. 1:4

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 50:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
50:1 There are two ancient legal situations used to highlight Israel's legal standing.

  1. divorce of a faithless wife (cf. Isa. 54:6-7; Jer. 3:1,8; Hosea 2:4; see SPECIAL TOPIC: CERTIFICATE OF DIVORCE)
  2. the selling of someone into slavery for a debt (cf. Deut. 32:30; 2 Kgs. 4:1; Neh. 5:5)

For Israel's "iniquities" and "transgressions" she was judged and exiled. It was not the weakness of YHWH, but the rebellion of His people (cf. Isa. 59:2).

▣ "you were sold for your iniquities" This is the exact opposite of the imagery of ransom/redeem.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. This chapter contains the third Servant Song (Isa. 50:4-11).

  2. In Isa. 49:25d the court imagery is used with the Servant as the defense advocate. Here the court imagery is used of YHWH as divorcing His covenant people for their faithlessness.

  3. In contrast to the faithlessness of the covenant people, the faithfulness of the Servant, the ideal Israelite, is stressed. He will accomplish what Israel could not!

  4. Notice that most English translations see three paragraphs in Isa. 50:4-11, which would denote three main truths.
    1. Isa. 50:4-6
    2. Isa. 50:7-9
    3. Isa. 50:10-11

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 50:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
50:2 This verse starts with a series of four rhetorical questions, as Isa. 50:1 had two. The first two deal with YHWH, surprised at the lack of intercession and faith response.

He asks if Israel had lost confidence in His ability to save!

▣ "Is My hand so short" This is a Qal PERFECT and a Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same root (BDB 894, KB 1126), which intensifies a concept, here a question.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

▣ "ransom" See SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM. It is parallel to "deliver."

▣ "sea. . .rivers" See SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS/SEA.

entries.title: Isaiah 50:3 "I clothe the heavens with blackness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
50:3 "I clothe the heavens with blackness" This probably relates to YHWH creating the heavenly lights in Genesis 1. Often in the Bible, when He visits His creation for blessing or judgment, these heavenly lights are affected (cf. Job 9:5-9; Isa. 13:10; 24:23; 50:3; Ezek. 32:7; Joel 2:2,10,31; 3:15; Matt. 13:24-25; 24:29; Luke 21:25; Rev. 6:12-13).

▣ "make sackcloth their covering" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES.

entries.title: Isaiah 50:4a "The Lord God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
50:4a "The Lord God" This is literally two words.

  1. Adon ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)
  2. YHWH ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

The reason to translate them in this way is because they are both often translated, "Lord." Lord Lord would be confusing to English speakers (e.g. Ps. 110:1, "The Lord says to my Lord," which is quoted in Matt. 22:44; Mark 12:36; Luke 20:42; Acts 2:34,35; Heb. 1:13).

▣ "disciples" This is a rare word (BDB 541), found only here (twice) and Isa. 8:16 in this sense. Usually it is translated "taught" (Isa. 54:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DISCIPLES

50:4b
NASB, NRSV  "sustain the weary one"
NKJV  "speak a word in season to him who is weary"
TEV  "strengthen the weary"
NJB  "to give a word of comfort to the weary"
JPSOA  "speak timely words to the weary"
REB  "to console the weary"

The MT (reflected in the NASB) has a rare Hebrew VERBAL (BDB 736, KB 804, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT), which occurs only here in this form. BDB suggests the text is corrupt and may have originally read "edify."

  1. לעות ‒ BDB 736, "help"
  2. לרעות ‒ BDB, KB, "edify"

But, the DSS and the Vulgate support the MT. The NET Bible mentions that cognate roots in Arabic and Aramaic mean "help" or "sustain."

Remember, in these cases of rare roots or stems, the context, especially parallelism, helps to suggest the meanings. The central truth of the strophe is the important issue in interpretation.

entries.title: Isaiah 50:4c,d
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
50:4c,d There is a repeated Hiphil IMPERFECT (BDB 734, KB 802), "awakens." In the Hiphil it is used to rouse or stir up activity.

  1. Isa. 13:17 ‒ the Medes (Jer. 51:11)
  2. Isa. 41:2,25 ‒ Cyrus II
  3. Isa. 45:13 ‒ Cyrus II
  4. here ‒ the Servant
  5. Dan. 11:2 ‒ inter-biblical ruler

YHWH is in control of world history and world redemption!

entries.title: Isaiah 50:4-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
50:4-6 These verses describe aspects of the Servant's ministry (in His own words).

  1. gifted to listen
  2. gifted to encourage, Isa. 50:4a
  3. He listens to
    1. hurting, weary ones (cf. Jer. 31:25), Isa. 50:4b
    2. YHWH, Isa. 50:4c,d,5a
  4. He was not disobedient, Isa. 50:5b
  5. He did not turn back, Isa. 50:5c
  6. He yielded Himself to abuse by leaders (cf. Matt. 26:67; 27:30; Mark 15:19)
    1. whipped His back
    2. plucked out His beard
    3. spit in His face

The Servant's verbal skills will lead to a rejection of His message and person by those who refuse to listen (cf. Isa. 50:11).

entries.title: Isaiah 50:5a
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
50:5a This is literally "has opened my ear," which seems to refer to

  1. a clear message received
  2. an allusion to obedience, to which the next two parallel poetic lines attest

This would surely describe Jesus' obedience to the Father's will (i.e. Matt. 26:39; John 8:29; 14:31; 15:10; Phil. 2:8; Heb. 5:8; 10:7 [quotes Ps. 40:8]).

entries.title: Isaiah 50:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
50:6 The specific treatment of the obedient Servant is a foreshadowing of the treatment of Jesus. This introduces the fourth Servant Song in Isa. 52:13-53:12, esp. Isa. 50:3,4-5,7-9. The Servant will pay a high price for His loyalty, trust, and obedience to YHWH (cf. Psalm 2; 22). There is a divine purpose in suffering for Him (cf. Isaiah 53; Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21; the book of Hebrews).

SPECIAL TOPIC: A SUFFERING MESSIAH

entries.title: Isaiah 50:7-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
50:7-9 The first verse of this strophe is repeated in Isa. 50:9a, "the Lord (Adon) God (YHWH) helps me."

Because of this the Servant will

  1. not be disgraced
  2. set His face like flint (cf. Luke 9:51)
  3. be ashamed

Why, because YHWH acts on His behalf, introduced by another series of questions (Isa. 50:8-9). The grammatical structure (i.e. "Who. . .?") runs through Isa. 50:10.

50:8
NASB, NRSV  "vindicates"
NKJV, LXX, Peshitta  "justifies"
TEV  "prove me innocent"
NJB  "saving justice"
JPSOA  "My vindicator"
REB  "will clear my name"

As Isa. 50:6-7 describe an unjust trial, so Isa. 50:8 describes a just verdict. The VERB (BDB 842, KB 1003) is a Hiphil PARTICIPLE which means "declare righteous" (cf. Exod. 23:7; Deut. 25:1; 1 Kgs. 8:32; Prov. 17:15). It is used in a negative context in Isa. 5:23. It describes

  1. God in this context
  2. the Servant in Isa. 53:11

▣ "Let him draw near to Me" This is a Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense. The VERB (BDB 620, KB 670) is used of approaching a judge at trial. Notice here the Servant is the Judge (i.e. "Let him draw near to Me").

The imagery of a court scene is one of three prophetic models. Often YHWH is depicted in various roles.

  1. as the Judge ‒ 1 Sam. 24:15; Ps. 9:4; 43:1; 140:12; Lam. 3:58; Micah 7:9
  2. as the accused ‒ Isa. 50:1-3; 49:14
  3. as advocate of the weak ‒ Prov. 23:11
  4. as advocate of Israel ‒ Ps. 119:54; Isa. 50:8-9; 51:22; Jer. 50:34; 51:36
  5. as litigant ‒ Ps. 74:22; Isa. 41:21; 43:5; Jer. 25:9
  6. against Israel ‒ Ps. 103:9; Isa. 3:13-15; Jer. 2:9; Hosea 4:1-4; 12:2; Micah 6:1-5

entries.title: Isaiah 50:9a.b
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 50:9a.b These first two lines of poetry express a repeated truth (cf. Ps. 118:6; Rom. 8:31-39; Heb. 13:6).

entries.title: Isaiah 50:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
50:10-11 AB takes these two verses as a response to the Servant (p. 116), apparently by YHWH (Leupold, p. 196). There is a contrast between two kinds of "light."

  1. the darkness (PLURAL for intensity) of those who have faith in God and His Messiah but do not fully understand (Isa. 50:10)
    1. let him trust in the name of the Lord ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 105, KB 120) used in a JUSSIVE sense (see SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH)
    2. let him rely on his God ‒ Niphal IMPERFECT (BDB 1043, KB 1612) used in a JUSSIVE sense
  2. those who make their own light (i.e. fire, see SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE) and walk in it (Qal IMPERATIVE) which will eventually consume them (i.e. lie down in torment, Isa. 50:11)

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 51:1 "Listen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
51:1 "Listen" This is the Hebrew word Shema (BDB 1033, KB 1570). It means "hear so as to do." The IMPERATIVE is recurrent in Isaiah! This same word starts the famous monotheistic prayer of Deuteronomy 6:4-6.

▣ "you who. . ." This is speaking to the faithful covenant people (cf. Isa. 50:10). There are three descriptive phrases.

  1. who pursue righteousness, Isa. 51:1
  2. who seek the Lord, Isa. 51:1
  3. who have the law in their hearts, Isa. 51:7

It is possible that the MT "deliverance" (BDB 841, NASB, "righteousness") is parallel to YHWH in line 2, therefore, it may be a title, "The Righteous One" (SPECIAL TOPIC: DESCRIPTIVE TITLES FOR GOD). The "you who. . ." would speak of the faithful who

  1. pursue God, line 1
  2. seek God, line 2 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord [OT])

▣ "the rock. . .the quarry" This refers to Abraham and Sarah (cf. Isa. 51:2; Gen. 17:15-17) The geographical location of Abraham's call (i.e. Ur of the Chaldees) was the same as the location of the Babylonian captives (Channel Chebar). YHWH had promised to bless Abraham and his seed (cf. Gen. 12:1-3; 15:1-11; 18:18; 22:16-18).
