READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

PRELIMINARY QUESTIONS

  1. To whom is this chapter speaking? (the covenant people in Exile or all humans)
  2. What is it offering to them: (restoration to the Promised Land or spiritual salvation of all repentant believers [i.e. Ibn Ezra, Radak])
  3. This is where two hermeneutical principles collide!
    1. Every passage should be interpreted in light of the original, inspired author's intent. The way to judge a proper interpretation is, "What would the original hearers (i.e. the target audience) have understood?" Every text has only one meaning.
    2. The NT is the proper fulfillment and interpreter of the OT (cf. Matt. 5:17-48). Jesus is the goal and purpose of the OT promises. In Him and in Him alone should the OT be interpreted. The NT is about Jesus and universal redemption, not about national Israel. Paul used OT texts like this to refer to Gentiles (i.e. Rom. 9:24-26; Eph. 2:13). The NT gives the proper understanding to OT texts. The NT reveals the mind of the Spirit who is the true author of revelation.
  4. Notice that the return from exile is not specifically mentioned (unless Isa. 55:12a,b) or even alluded to. The invitation is more general, more broad!

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. This setting is either the
    1. Messianic banquet, Matt. 25:6-8; Luke 14:15-24; 22:16,18; Rev. 19:9, which I have come to believe is the wedding feast of Jesus and the church. See my new (2024) exegetical commentary on the book of Revelation.
    2. market place of Jerusalem

  2. The OT Prophets often used the historical events of their own day to foreshadow eschatological events.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

  3. As a Great Commission Christian (i.e. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:47; Acts 1:8) who believes in the priority of evangelism and discipleship, this chapter holds a dear place in my heart and ministry. YHWH, through His prophet, pleads for fallen humanity to return to Him so that He can give them full and free forgiveness (cf. Isa. 55:1-5; also note the universal invitation of Jesus in Matt. 11:28; Rev. 22:17). This is the goal of Gen. 3:15 (i.e. a restored Garden of Eden; see SPECIAL TOPIC: EDEN)!
     However, there is a mandated covenant response (cf. Isa. 55:6-7, see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT). Humans must repent, believe, obey, and persevere.
     YHWH has an eternal redemptive plan (cf. Isa. 55:8-11). See SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN! God's revelation through Abraham's seed was a message for the whole world. Abraham's seed is now all believers in Christ (cf. Rom. 2:28-29; 9:6; Gal. 3:7-9,29; 6:16; Eph. 2:11-3:13; 1 Pet. 3:6).

  4. Notice the speaker in the poem is YHWH (or Personified Wisdom of Prov. 8:22-9:6). Only the invitation of Isa. 55:6-7 is spoken by the prophet who was overwhelmed at the mercy of YHWH.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 55:1-3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
55:1-3 YHWH's invitation to humanity (i.e. "everyone who thirsts," cf. Isa. 55:1a) has many commands which are mostly emphatic divine invitations.

  1. come to the waters ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 229, KB 246)
  2. come ‒ same as #1
  3. buy ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 991, KB 1404)
  4. eat ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 37, KB 46)
  5. come ‒ same as #1 and 2
  6. buy ‒ same as #3
  7. listen carefully ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE and an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same root (BDB 1033, KB 1570) for emphasis
  8. eat ‒ same as #4
  9. delight yourself ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 772, KB 851) used in a JUSSIVE sense
  10. incline your ear ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE (BDB 639, KB 692)
  11. come to Me ‒ same as #1,2,5; notice the personal element
  12. listen ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570; see SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR)
  13. that you may live ‒ Qal JUSSIVE (BDB 310, KB 309)
  14. I will make an everlasting covenant with you ‒ Qal COHORTATIVE (BDB 503, KB 560)
    SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT
    SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

entries.title: Isaiah 55:2 "Why do you spend money. . .for what does not satisfy"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
55:2 "Why do you spend money. . .for what does not satisfy" This reflects mankind's continuing search for happiness in things, pleasure, or power (cf. the book of Ecclesiastes). Hear my audio sermon, "Where Is Happiness Found?"; second green box on www.freebiblecommentary.org, tape #2014.

▣ "delight yourself in abundance" God wants humanity made in His image to be happy and content in fellowship with Himself (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28; John 5:11). The earth with its beauty and abundance is for mankind's enjoyment! But, the Fall of Genesis 3 turned this wonderful gift into "greed."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NATURAL RESOURCES

entries.title: Isaiah 55:3 "come to Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
55:3 "come to Me" Personal relationship is the key to biblical faith! YHWH Himself is the goal, not just truths about Him!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

▣ "Listen" This is from the word Shema (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 6:4-5). It means "listen and do." All OT promises to Israel and individuals are conditional covenants.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR

▣ "that you may live" I agree with the NET Bible footnote #7, sn, p. 1272, that "to live" (BDB 310, KB 309, Qal JUSSIVE) would refer, in this context, to

  1. prosperity
  2. security

These were part of YHWH's covenant promises (i.e. Lev. 18:5; Deut. 30:6,15,19-20; Rom. 10:5) to David (v. 3d promises).

▣ "an everlasting covenant" "Everlasting" (BDB 761, see SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios) is used to describe many things in Isaiah 40-66. This is parallel phrasing to the "new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34 described in Ezek. 36:22-36.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "faithful mercies" This is from the word hesed (BDB 338 I, KB 336 II). It means "covenant loyalty."

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

▣ "David" This is an example of God's love and care even to the undeserving (cf. Psalm 32,51). Also this reference has Messianic implications (cf. 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17), which have an eternal aspect. God's promises related to the salvation of Adam's seed are unconditional (i.e. Gen. 15:12-22).

55:4
NASB, NRSV  "a leader and commander for the peoples"
NKJV  "a leader and commander for the people"
NJB  "a leader andf lawgiver to peoples"
TEV, NET  "a leader and commander of nations"
REB  "a prince ruling over them"
Peshitta  "a ruler and leader to the nations"
LXX  "a prince and commander to the Gentiles"
JPSOA  "a prince and commander of peoples"

The MT has three functions for this new David for "the peoples."

  1. a witness to the peoples (BDB 729)
  2. a leader (BDB 617)
  3. a commander (BDB 845)

This points beyond David to the Messiah (cf. 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17) because the object is the Gentiles (i.e. "to the peoples," cf. Isa. 55:4-5).

The MT and LXX have "him" referring to David's seed (i.e. the Messiah), but for some reason, the Syrian versions have "you." This is the same theological issue of who is the "Suffering Servant"? (cf. Isa. 52:14).

See full notes in Contextual Insights to Isa. 52:13-53:12.

entries.title: Isaiah 55:4-5 "the peoples. . .a nation"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
55:4-5 "the peoples. . .a nation" Gentiles are included (notice the PLURALS, cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:6-7; 60:1-3; 66:23)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 55:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
55:5 The nations will come to the God of Israel and honor His people (cf. Isa. 45:14,22-25; 49:6,12,23; Zech. 8:20-23). The question remains: Is this a reference to a believing, restored Israel (not the secular state of modern Israel) or is this an eschatological reference to the Great Commission?

▣ Notice the names of Israel's Deity

  1. YHWH (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)
  2. your Elohim (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.)
  3. the Holy One of Israel (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE)

entries.title: Isaiah 55:6 "Seek the Lord while He may be found"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
55:6 "Seek the Lord while He may be found" "Seek" is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 205, KB 233). This VERB is often used of seeking God in a personal sense (cf. Deut. 4:29; Isa. 58:2; 65:10). This seeking is described well in Deut. 30:1-3,10; Jer. 29:13-14; and Amos 5:14-15.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord

▣ "while He may be found" No one can come to God unless He draws them (cf. Isa. 45:22; John 6:44,65), but when He draws, humans must respond. God never forsakes His creation (cf. Ps. 103:8-14), but there is a time to choose. If that time passes, a hardness of the human heart develops into an inability to hear God and respond to Him.

Salvation involves God's initiation and mankind's appropriate response.

  1. repentance (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [NT])
  2. faith (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST)
  3. obedience (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
  4. worship (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)
  5. service (growing toward Christlikeness)
  6. perseverance (see SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE)

▣ "Call upon Him while He is near" "Call" is also a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 894, KB 1128). This line of poetry is parallel to the line above. This language denotes a worship setting, as does Rom. 10:9-13 or John 1:12. Humans must respond in repentance and faith (cf. Jer. 3:12-13; 4:1-4; Joel 2:12-13; Amos 5:4-7,14-15; Mark 1:15; John 3:16; Acts 20:21). This appropriate covenant response is true for the OT as well as the NT. YHWH desires a fellowship, a people! A people who reflect His character, so as to attract the whole world to Himself!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO "RECEIVE," "BELIEVE," "CONFESS/PROFESS," "CALL UPON"?

entries.title: Isaiah 55:7 "Let the wicked forsake his way"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
55:7 "Let the wicked forsake his way" Lifestyle repentance is crucial. Biblical faith is an initial, personal decision followed by lifestyle faith and repentance. Eternal life haas observable characteristics!
SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

The term "wicked" (BDB 957) is parallel with "unrighteous" (BDB 19, cf. Isa. 10:1). These two terms describe the spiritual state of unbelieving mankind. The second term has two possible origins (i.e. Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT, p. 83).

  1. from root "to desire"
  2. from root "nothingness"

The first dentoes the selfish tendancies related to the Fall (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND). The second denotes the superstition and resulting idolatry of human beings.

  1. SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY
  2. SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY, VAIN, NOTHINGNESS (i.e. different root ‒ BDB 996)

▣ Notice the parallelism between the first two lines. Evil is described in two ways.

  1. lifestyle actions
  2. the thought life

The rabbis have a helpful thought about this. They describe the thought life as a garden ready for seed. What we let in through our eyes and ears falls on that ready soil. If we choose to dwell on it then it becomes who we are. Sin begins in the thought life, but in time reaches the hand/foot/mouth! Guard your thought life (cf. 1 Pet. 1:13)!

The first three VERBS of Isa. 55:7 are JUSSIVES.

  1. forsake ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 736, KB 806) used in a JUSSIVE sense
  2. return ‒ Qal JUSSIVE (BDB 996, KB 1427, cf. Isa. 31:6; 44:22
  3. will have compassion ‒ Piel IMPERFECT (BDB 933, KB 1216) used in a JUSSIVE sense, 49:10,13; 54:8

▣ "He will have compassion. . .abundantly pardon" When God forgives, He forgets (cf. Ps. 103:12; Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; Micah 7:19). What a wonderful truth of the love and forgiveness of God (cf. Heb. 9:14; 1 John 1:7). YHWH is willing, ready, and able to accept, forgive, and restore His fallen creation made in His image!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS IN THE OT

▣ "He will abundantly pardon" Wow, I love this chapter! It is a wonderful invitation to spiritually hungry people who are being aggressively sought after by a loving, forgiving, creator God!

Notice the powerful VERBALS.

  1. "He will abundantly" ‒ BDB 915, KB 1176, Hiphil IMPERFECT
  2. pardon ‒ Qal BDB 699, KB 757, INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT. This word is always used of God's forgiveness. Notice its usage:
    1. in the context of YHWH's characteristics ‒ Exod. 34:9
    2. in a negative sense related to idolatry ‒ Deut. 29:19-20
    3. part of Moses' intercession for Israel ‒ Num. 14:20
    4. part of the promise of a "new covenant" ‒ Jer. 31:34
      SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS IN THE OT, #1

Those who have experienced God's love and forgiveness have a powerful, wonderful message to share with a frightened, confused, hurting, discouraged, sinful world!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 55:8-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
55:8-11 These verses have a unified theme, YHWH's redemptive purposes! The parallel lines of Isa. 55:8 speak of the uniqueness of His gracious character. Humans deserve death but He gives life, peace, and His personal presence! He is totally different from humans, but He loves humans. He created them like Himself (cf. Gen. 1:26-27) for fellowship (cf. Gen. 3:8; Lev. 26:12). He will not let us go! He is pursuing us in mercy and in Christ!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 55:11 "My word. . .will not return to Me empty"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
55:11 "My word. . .will not return to Me empty" God is sovereign (cf. Isa. 40:8). God's spoken word had great power in the OT (cf. Genesis 1; Isa. 53:11). In this chapter His powerful, purposeful word is for mercy, forgiveness, and fellowship (cf. Isa. 14:24; 25:1; 45:23; 46:10; 59:21; Matt. 24:35)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOGOS (WORD)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRISTIAN ASSURANCE

entries.title: Isaiah 55:12-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
55:12-13 In this OT context the visible sign of God's presence and blessing was agricultural abundance (i.e. Isa. 55:1-2). Creation is often personified as rejoicing at the presence of God. The idyllic fellowship of the Garden of Eden (see SPECIAL TOPIC: EDEN) is restored!

An interpreter must ask, was this fulfilled in the return under Zerubbabel, Joshua, Ezra, Nehemiah? The answer clearly is, it was not (cf. Dan. 9:24-27)! Therefore, this must be viewed as an eschatological setting, not just the return from Neo-Babylonian exile.

  1. go out with joy ‒ Isa. 51:11; 52:9; Ps. 105:43
  2. led forth in peace ‒ Isa. 54:10,13; Jer. 29:11

entries.title: Isaiah 56:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:1 This chapter starts out with two commands related to an appropriate life of faith (cf. Isa. 55:7).

  1. preserve justice ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 1036, KB 1581, cf. Isa. 1:17); for "justice," see SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGE, JUDGMENT, JUSTICE
  2. do righteousness ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 793, KB 889); for "righteousness," see SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ The reason for the life of faith is

  1. My salvation is about to come ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 97, KB 112, cf. Isa. 46:13; 51:5; Ps. 85:9)
  2. My righteousness to be revealed ‒ Niphal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 162, KB 191, see same first two references as #1)

NT Believers must live every day as if the Lord was returning! This attitude and lifestyle keeps us close to God (cf. Ps. 85:9), as it did the faithful followers under the Old Covenant (i.e. Ps. 1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT) TERM

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

There is a change from Isaiah's message to the returnees from Mesopotamian exile (Isaiah 40-55) to the faithless, covenant people in Palestine (Isaiah 56-66).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 56:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:2 Notice the first two lines are parallel. Also the "blessed man" (cf. Ps. 1:1-3; 112:1; 119:1-2; 128:1) is the one who obeys/observes God's law.

▣ The second two lines describe two specific things that "the blessed man" will not do.

  1. keeps from profaning the sabbath (cf. Exod. 20:8-11; 31:16-17; 35:2-3; Isa. 58:13; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH)
  2. keeps his hand from doing any evil (summary phrase)

The VERB "keep" (BDB 1036, KB 1581) occurs four times in this chapter (Isa. 56:2 [twice],4,6). Lifestyle faith and obedience are vital and crucial aspects of a personal relationship with YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Isaiah 56:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:3 This verse assures those who were normally excluded from Israel's God that they would be included.

  1. the physically damaged person (cf. Isa. 56:6-8, Deut. 23:1-8)
  2. the non-Israelite worshiper (cf. Isa. 56:4-5)

The word "says," which is repeated twice (foreigner, eunuch) is a Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 55, KB 65) used in a JUSSIVE sense.

▣ "surely separate" This is a Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a Hiphil IMPERFECT from the same root (BDB 95, KB 110) used for emphasis. However, the great emphasis is that this statement is not true!

▣ "the eunuch" This refers to a person

  1. with damaged testicles
  2. a castrated person
  3. a royal servant (i.e. Potiphar and Daniel)

The account of the Ethiopian eunuch in Acts 8 being fully accepted into the people of God by faith in Jesus Christ, the Suffering Servant, is a great example of this type of persons' inclusion!

entries.title: Isaiah 56:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:4 Notice the qualifications of a faithful eunuch.

  1. keeps My sabbaths ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT
  2. chooses what pleases Me ‒ BDB 103, KB 119, Qal PERFECT with waw
  3. holds fast My covenant ‒ BDB 304, KB 302, Hiphil ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

entries.title: Isaiah 56:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:5 Eunuchs could have no natural children (i.e. "a dry tree," v. 3) so YHWH will give the faithful eunuchs a memorial in His house (i.e. temple). He will give them "an everlasting name" (i.e. Hebrew idiom for descendants).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

▣
NASB, REB  "memorial"
NRSV, LXX, Peshitta  "a place"
NJB, JPSOA  "monument"

The Hebrew term is literally "hand" (BDB 388, #4) but used idiomatically for memorial (cf. 1 Sam. 15:12; 2 Sam. 18:18).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

entries.title: Isaiah 56:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:6 Notice how the faithful foreigners are characterized.

  1. join themselves to the Lord ‒ Niphal PARTICIPLE (BDB 530, KB 522)
  2. minister to Him ‒ Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 1058, KB 1661)
  3. love the name of the Lord ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 12, KB 17; see SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH)
  4. be His servants ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 224, KB 243)
  5. keep from profaning the sabbath ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE (BDB 1036, KB 1581, cf. vv 2,4) and a Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 320, KB 319)
  6. holds fast My covenant ‒ Hiphil PARTICIPLE (BDB 304, KB 302)

YHWH's true followers are known by their lifestyle faith (cf. Matthew 5-7, esp. Matt. 7:15-23,24-27; Eph. 1:4; 2:10; James 2:14-26).

entries.title: Isaiah 56:7 "My house will be called a house of prayer for all the peoples"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:7 "My house will be called a house of prayer for all the peoples" This was the stated purpose of Solomon's temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:41-43,60). Jesus quotes this verse in Matt. 21:13; Mark 11:17; Luke 19:46 as He cleansed Herod's temple (i.e. the court of the Gentiles) of the animal sellers and money changers. For a complete listing of this universal element in Isaiah see Isa. 45:22.

▣ "burnt offering" See SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERING.

56:8
NASB  "Yet others I will gather to them"
NKJV  "Yet I will gather to him others besides"
NRSV, Peshitta  "I will gather others to them"
  (Peshitta, "to him")
TEV  "has promised that he will bring still
  other people to join them"
NJB  "there are others I shall gather"
JPSOA  "I will gather still more to those gathered"
REB  "I shall add to those who have already
  been gathered"
LXX  "I will gather to him a congregation"

There are two possibilities.

  1. YHWH will gather even more of the exiled descendants of Abraham (JPSOA, LXX, NET, cf. Isa. 60:4-14)
  2. YHWH will gather other outcasts (i.e. foreigners, eunuchs, cf. Isa. 19:24-25; 60:3; 66:18-21; Joel 2:28-32)

Jesus' use of this text in Mark 11:17, following the LXX, shows its wider intended scope; also note John 10:16. This is the thrust of Joel 2:28-32 (quoted by Paul in Rom. 10:13).

entries.title: Isaiah 56:7-8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:7-8 As Isa. 56:6 described the faithful foreigners' actions, so Isa. 56:7-8 describe what the faithful God will do for them.

  1. I will bring to My holy mountain (i.e. temple, cf. Isa. 27:13; 57:13; 65:14; 66:20; Jer. 31:23; Ezek. 20:40; Dan. 9:16,20)
  2. I will make them joyful in My house of prayer
  3. I will accept their sacrifices on My altar
  4. I will gather them and others

entries.title: Isaiah 56:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:9 This is a parody of the invitation to the Divine supper (cf. Isa. 56:12; 55:1-2), but here in the context of judgment (Isa. 56:10-12) it is a command ("come" ‒ BDB 87, KB 102, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT). This will be a banquet of judgment!

There is an interpretive question related to Isa. 56:9-12, as to when this occurs.

  1. pre-exilic
  2. exilic
  3. post-exilic

The issue is to which period of Israel's history do these verses refer? Possibly it relates to some in each period (i.e. multiple fulfillment prophecy, or at least the historical ambiguity of Isaiah's poems can relate to different periods). There were always faithless leaders and people.

entries.title: Isaiah 56:10 "His watchmen are blind"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 56:10 "His watchmen are blind" The MT scholars noted a problem in the Hebrew text. It reads a Qal PERFECT (BDB 859, KB 1044), but they suggest a Qal PARTICIPLE. Either one does not change the sense of the text.

entries.title: Isaiah 56:10-12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:10-12 These verses are in sharp contrast to the faithful outcasts of Isa. 56:1-8. These describe Israel's spiritual condition (mostly her leaders).

  1. the watchmen (spiritual leaders) are blind
  2. all of them know nothing
  3. all of them are dumb dogs
  4. dream/rave
    1. from Arabic root or "pant" (KB 243), referring to "dogs" of Isa. 56:10c
    2. DSS has "seers," referring to prophets
  5. love to sleep
  6. greedy
  7. never satisfied
  8. shepherds without understanding
  9. all tuned to their own ways (cf. Isa. 53:6)
  10. each one turned to unjust gain
  11. drunkards
  12. no plans or motive to change their evil ways

Wow! What a terrible description of the covenant people. Their leaders are corrupt and the proverb is true, like leader, like people! God's revelation, temple, and godly leaders had made no difference (i.e. Roim. 9:4-5). Their fruit is obvious (i.e. self)!

entries.title: Isaiah 56:12 "Come"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
56:12 "Come" This IMPERATIVE (Qal, BDB 87, KB 102) matches the one in Isa. 56:9c! The humans come to get drunk and ignore God (Isa. 56:12b), so now the animals are invited by God to come and devour His covenant people (cf. Isa. 18:6; Jer. 7:33; 12:9; 15:3; 34:20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WINE AND STRONG DRINK, II. A. #4,5,6

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 57:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:1 Evil triumphs when the righteous are persecuted and murdered, and no one seems to care!

  1. no man takes it to heart
  2. no one understands

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "is taken away from evil" As the wicked seek self and sin, the righteous are delivered from the terrible influence of the Fall (cf. Genesis 3; 6:5,11-12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

▣ The last line of v. 1 (NASB) seems in conflict with the meaning of the first two lines.

  1. The JPSOA adjusts this by translating, "That because of evil the righteous are taken away."
  2. The TEV has "But when they die, no calamity can hurt them."
  3. The NJB has "Yes, because of the evil times the upright is taken off."
  4. The REB has "The righteous are swept away by the onset of evil."

However, v. 2 implies that it is YHWH who takes them away to a place of blessing. Death for faithful followers is a reunion, not a separation (i.e. 2 Cor. 5:6,8; Heb. 11:13-16).

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Obviously the context of Israel's sin continues from Isaiah 56.

  2. This describes the OT theological concept of "the two ways"; one of life and peace and the other of self, sin, and ruin (cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1).

  3. H. C. Leupold makes the interesting comment (p. 271) that as Isaiah 56 ended on faithless leaders, Isaiah 57 deals with faithless people.

  4. The setting of the idolatry is not Mesopotamia but Canaan's fertility cults (i.e. Ba'al, Asherah, Molech). This reached its apex under King Manasseh.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 57:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:2 This verse describes the spiritual condition of the righteous man.

  1. enters into peace (because of Isa. 57:1 this must be mental; see SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE [OT])
  2. rest in their beds (BDB 1012). There is a word play on this word used here of the righteous, but in Isa. 57:7,8, of the wicked (i.e. "they rest in their beds").
    1. bed for sleep (JPSOA, NRSV, NJB)
    2. bed for sex (cf. vv. 7,8)
    3. the grave (NET, REB, TEV, LXX)
  3. walked in his upright way (i.e. lifestyle faithfulness; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)

entries.title: Isaiah 57:3-4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:3-4 These verses describe the wicked ones mentioned in Isa. 57:1. They are characterized as

  1. sons of a sorcerer (BDB 778 II, cf. Isa. 2:6; Jer. 27:9; Micah 5:12; see SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC, #10)
  2. offspring of an adulterer (BDB 610)
  3. offspring of a prostitute (BDB 275)
    YHWH calls them to approach (Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 897, KB 1132) His presence for judgment.
  4. offspring of deceit (BDB 833)
    1. against whom do you jest
    2. against whom do you open wide your mouth
    3. against whom do you stick out your tongue (these described their accusations against the righteous)
  5. children of rebellion (BDB 1055)

entries.title: Isaiah 57:5-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:5-6 The idolatry is described as

  1. inflame yourself among the oaks (Niphal PARTICIPLE, BDB 328, KB 328). This refers to the fertility worship of Ba'al and Asherah, i.e. Deut. 12:2; 1 Kgs. 14:23; 2 Kgs. 17:10; Jer. 2:20; 23-28; 31:6-13; Ezek. 6:13; 20:28; Hosea 4:13)
  2. slaughter the children (Qal PARTICIPLE, BDB 1006, KB 1458, this refers to the worship of Molech; see SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH)
  3. pour out a libation (Qal PERFECT, BB 1049, KB 1629)
  4. make a grain offering (Hiphil PERFECT, BDB 748, KB 828)

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST

entries.title: Isaiah 57:6a
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:6a The reference to which this line relates is uncertain.

  1. the cultic trees of Asherah worship, v. 5a,b
  2. the place of sacrificing children (i.e. valley of Hinnom), v. 5c
  3. associated with the "clefts of the crags," v. 5d
  4. another place of fertility worship (i.e. sacrifice), v. 7c
    1. drink offerings, v. 6c
    2. grain offerings, v. 6d
  5. the promiscuity of v. 7a,b
  6. Rotherham's Emphasized Bible, p. 701, suggests the meaning is "in open places in the valley," these fertility worshipers expose themselves (i.e. no modesty or sense of morality).
57:6e
NASB  "Shall I relent concerning these things"
NKJV  "Should I receive comfort in these"
NRSV  "Shall I be appeased for these things"
TEV  "Do you think I am pleased with all this"
LXX  "Shall I not therefore be angry for these things"
Peshitta  "Should I receive comfort in these things"
JPSOA  "Should I relent in the face of these"
REB  "In spite of this am I to relent"

The Israelites' fertility worship, even if done in YHWH's name (i.e. the golden calves at Dan and Bethel), was unacceptable! God had no choice but to judge His people in order to restore proper worship. This is possibly a rhetorical question (see NET Bible, p. 1274, #13)

entries.title: Isaiah 57:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:7 This refers to the Ba'al and Asherah altars which were placed on the tops of hills (cf. Deut. 12:2; 2 Kgs. 17:10; Jer. 3:6; 17:2; Hosea 4:13). The phrase "made their bed" refers to the ritual sexual activities offerred for the fertility of the land, herds, and human population (cf. Isa. 57:8b-d).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

entries.title: Isaiah 57:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:8 The first two lines are ambiguous. This could refer to an idolatrous image set up

  1. in their homes
  2. on their village walls
  3. in the temple itself (cf. Ezekiel 8-10)
  4. in secret, v. 6

One wonders if this is somehow related to political/military alliances with pagan nations who demanded the worship of foreign gods (cf. Isa. 57:8d-e, 9).

57:8c
NASB, NKJV, NRSV  "uncovered yourself"
TEV  "take off your clothes"
NJB  "you exposed yourself"
REB  "you have stripped"
LXX, NET  "depart from me"

The MT has the Piel form of the VERB (BDB 162, KB 191), but the NET Bible, p. 1274, #16, suggests the Qal meaning of "depart" instead of the Piel "uncover."

The first relates to the first phrase of the line, "far removed from Me"; the second option, "depart," relates to the rest of v. 8.

It seems to me option #2 fits the context best.

57:8e
NASB  "you have made an agreement for yourself with them"
NKJV, JPSOA  "made a covenant with them"
NRSV  "you have made a bargain for yourself with them"
TEV  "whom you pay to sleep with you"
REB  "you drove bargains with men"
NJB  "you struck a profitable bargain"

The MT has "cut" (BDB 503, #4; KB 500, Qal IMPERFECT with waw), which often refers to "cutting a covenant" (cf. Gen. 26:28; 31:44; 1 Sam. 11:1; Ps. 83:5; Isa. 55:3; 61:8; Hosea 12:1), but here, it does not seem to fit. The NET Bible assumes an emendation.

  1. ותכות ‒ MT, "to cut"
  2. וכרית ‒ NET, "you purchase"

Context, context, context must determine meaning.

57:8g
NASB  "you have looked on their manhood"
NKJV  "where you saw their hand"
TEV  "there you satisfy your lust"
NJB  "with your eyes on the sacred symbol"
JPSOA  "you have chosen lust"
NRSV, NIV, Peshitta  "where you saw their nakedness"
NET Bible  "gaze longingly on their genitals"

The problem is the word יד (BDB 388, KB 386), which is literally "hand."

  1. In Ugaritic ידד means "love" or "genitals."
  2. In Arabic ידו means "penis" (cf. NIDOTTE, vol 2, p. 56).
  3. It could refer to "sexual strength" here in a fertility worship sense.

There are several euphemisms used by Hebrew authors to refer to the sex organs (another example is "feet," BDB 919, cf. Exod. 4:25; Deut. 28:57; Jdg. 3:24; Ruth 3:8; 1 Sam. 24:3; Ezek. 16:25).

entries.title: Isaiah 57:9-10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 57:9-10 This seems to refer to the political gifts to assure their safety against foreign invasion.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:9a "king"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:9a "king" This could be understood as referring to the fertility god Molech (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH), whose name has the same consonants as "king" (mlk) in Hebrew. The UBS Text Project, p. 150, gives "king" a B rating (some doubt).

57:9c
NASB, NRSV, NJB, JPSOA  "your envoys"
NKJV, TEV, Peshitta  "your messengers"
REB  "your procurers"
LXX  "your ambassadors"

This term (BDB 851 II) usually refers to ambassador type messengers (cf. Isa. 18:2; Jer. 49:14), but sometimes, a personal messenger (i.e. Prov. 13:17; 25:13). But, in this context, there are so many unusual words that seem to relate to worship of dead family members. Therefore, it may relate to necromancers (i.e. the witch of Endor, 1 Sam. 28:3-7). The JPSOA translates this as "and you have sent your envoys afar, even down to the netherworld."

Molech was the god of the netherworld.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

▣ "Sheol" The OT holding place of the dead.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, I. B.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:11-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:11-13 This strophe starts with a series of questions from YHWH to His faithless covenant people. The tragedy was that they were "religious" (cf. Isa. 57:12,13a) but had

  1. not remembered (Qal PERFECT, BDB 269, KB 269, negated) Him
  2. nor give Me a thought (lit. "lay it to heart of you," Qal PERFECT, BDB 962, KB 1321, negated)

The reasons they had neglected YHWH was His silence (Isa. 57:11d). This may refer to true prophets who were not sent or at least not heard.

The idols are "vanity" and "emptiness." The wind will carry them away and along with them, those who trust in them.

57:11
NASB, NJB  "for a long time"
NKJV  "from of old"
TEV  "for so long"
JPSOA  "so long"
REB  "look away"
NAB  "unseeing"

The JPSOA mentions an emendation that results in "and shut my eyes" (p. 898), which is followed by REB and NAB. The same Hebrew consonants ומעלם can be translated "and from eternity" or "and being hidden" (UBS Text Project, p. 151; it refers to "and from eternity").

The immediate context does not make sense using "eternity." For a period of time (i.e. 70 years), YHWH refused to help His covenant people because of their covenant disobedience and idolatry. He hid His face from them and did not respond to their prayers. It may have seemed to them to be an eternity!

57:13a,b
NASB, NKJV, NRSV  "Let your collection of idols"
NJB  "let those thronging round"
Peshitta  "let those who gather around"
JPSOA  "your assorted [idols]"

The MT has a NOUN (BDB 868) that occurs only here. It is formed from the VERB (BDB 867) "to gather" or "to assemble." The translations above interpret this in two ways.

  1. Israel's idols (JPSOA)
  2. fellow worshipers

In context #1 fits best.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:13d-e
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:13d-e But those few faithful ones who trust in YHWH and take "refuge" (Qal PARTICIPLE, BDB 340, KB 337) in Him will be preserved and rewarded by the giving of

  1. the Promised Land
  2. YHWH's presence (i.e. the temple)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 57:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:14 There is a series of IMPERATIVES whereby YHWH commands that all necessary preparations be made for His faithful ones to return from exile (cf. Isa. 40:3-4; 62:10).

  1. build up (twice) ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 699, KB 757
  2. prepare the way ‒ Piel IMPERATIVE, BDB 815, KB 937
  3. remove every obstacle ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE, BDB 926, KB 1202

entries.title: Isaiah 57:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:15 Notice the titles and characterizations of God.

  1. the high One ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE, BDB 926, KB 1202 (same VERB used in Isa. 57:14 translated "remove," i.e. lift up)
  2. the exalted One ‒ Niphal PARTICIPLE, BDB 669, KB 724 (same VERB used in Isa. 57:7,13, but in different senses)
  3. who lives forever ‒ Qal PARTICIPLE, BDB 1014, KB 1496, (lit. "who inhabits eternity"). The NET Bible [p. 1275] thinks in this context it should be understood as "the One who rules forever." This may be true because of Exod. 15:18; Ps. 10:16.
  4. whose name is Holy (see SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY)
  5. dwells on a high and holy place ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 1014, KB 1496 (in contrast to the fertility gods)
  6. with a contrite (BDB 194 I) and lowly (BDB 1050) spirit (BDB 924)
  7. to revive the heart of the contrite ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, BDB 310, KB 309, used twice
    1. of YHWH, #6
    2. of His faithful

Notice in the great covenant God wants to dwell with believing, faithful followers (v. 15d).

entries.title: Isaiah 57:16a-b
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:16a-b This continues a description of YHWH by YHWH.

  1. "I will not contend forever" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 936, KB 1224, cf. Gen. 6:3
  2. "neither will I always be angry" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 893, KB 1124, cf. Ps. 79:5; 85:5; 103:9; Micah 7:18-19

This should not be interpreted as a period of time set by God after which His grace ceases, but the reality that when humans ignore and violate His word and will, there is a terrible consequence of hardening. The human heart becomes unable to hear and respond!

It is interesting that the OT contrasts the human emotions of love and anger when describing God.

  1. love is long lasting and sure ‒ Deut. 5:10; 7:9; Ps. 30:5; Isa. 54:7-8; Jer. 31:3
  2. anger is short lived ‒ Deut. 5:9; Ps. 30:5; Isa. 26:20; 54:7-8; 57:16-19

entries.title: Isaiah 57:16c-d
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:16c-d YHWH reveals the reasons why He does not remain angry (see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN [anthropomorphism]). This is very similar to Ps. 103:8-14.

  1. for the spirit (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE) would grow faint before Me
  2. the breath would grow faint

Notice the parallelism of "spirit" (BDB 924) and "breath" (BDB 675) as in Isa. 42:5. The frail physical and now psychological condition of fallen mankind cannot endure the silence (Isa. 57:11,17) and anger (Isa. 57:16,17) of their Creator and Redeemer!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT

entries.title: Isaiah 57:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 57:17 YHWH's judgment is analogous to a parent's punishment (cf. Hosea 11; Heb. 12:5-13). He does it so His children will learn and turn from it, but sadly some will not, cannot (Isa. 57:17c; 1:3,4).

entries.title: Isaiah 57:18-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:18-19 Notice what YHWH will do for the contrite and lowly of spirit (Isa. 57:15), those both near and far (Isa. 57:19).

  1. revive, Isa. 57:15 ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 310, KB 309)
  2. I will not contend, Isa. 57:16 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 936, KB 1224)
  3. I will not always be angry, Isa. 57:16 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 893, KB 1124)
  4. I will heal, Isa. 57:18 ‒ Qal IMPERFECT with waw (BDB 950, KB 1272, cf. Isa. 19:22; 30:26; 53:5; see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING)
  5. I will lead, Isa. 57:18 ‒ Hiphil IMPERFECT (BDB 634, KB 685)
  6. I will restore comfort, Isa. 57:18 ‒ Piel IMPERFECT with waw (BDB 1022, KB 1532)
  7. I will create their praise of peace, Isa. 57:19 Qal PARTICIPLE (BDB 135, KB 153)
  8. I will heal them, Isa. 57:19 Qal IMPERFECT with waw (BDB 950, KB 1272)

entries.title: Isaiah 57:18-21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:18-21 There is an obvious contrast between the way YHWH will treat the contrite and the rebellious.

  1. contrite ‒ Isa. 57:15-16,18-19
  2. rebellious ‒ Isa. 57:17,20-21

entries.title: Isaiah 57:19a "creating the praise of the lips"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:19a "creating the praise of the lips" Literally, "the fruit of the lips." This, and similar phrases like it (i.e. Lev. 7:12), became the Jewish community's way to speak of sacrifice when there was no temple or temple access. Modern Judaism cannot do Mosaic practice because there is no place to offer sacrifice or approach Him on feast days.

The Jewish believer, whoever it was, of the book of Hebrews uses this same sacrificial terminology in Heb. 13:15 to denote Christian worship.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:19b
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:19b In context, this refers to the faithful remnant who are in Palestine and those still in exile.

In the NT, this text relates to

  1. Jewish pilgrims to Jerusalen at Passover and residents of Jerusalem ‒ Acts 2:37-42
  2. all believng human beings ‒ Eph. 2:11-3:13 (esp. Eph. 2:17)

This transfer of promises to the faithful OT remnant is expanded in the NT to all human beings.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 57:20-21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
57:20-21 The rebellious, faithless covenant people are described as

  1. the tossing sea
  2. sea that cannot be quiet
  3. sea that tosses up refuse
  4. sea that tosses up mud
  5. no peace

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 58:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:1 This chapter, like many chapters in Isaiah (i.e. a typical literary marker for a new poem), starts with a series of IMPERATIVES. The questions of interpretation are:

  1. who is the speaker?
  2. who is the recipient?

Here is the list of what is commanded (note the parallelism):

  1. cry loudly ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 894, KB 1128
  2. do not hold back ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 362, KB 359, used in a JUSSIVE sense
  3. raise your voice ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE, BDB 926. KB 1202
  4. declare ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE, BDB 616, KB 665

The speaker is YHWH by the mouth of His prophet and the recipients are:

  1. pre-exilic Israel/Judah
  2. exilic Israel/Judah
  3. returning Judah
  4. eschatological people of God (i.e. believers, both Jew and Gentile, cf. Rom. 2:28-29; Gal. 3:7-9,29; 6:16; Eph. 2:11-3:13)

▣ "trumpet" This is BDB 1051 and denotes the prophet raising his voice like a trumpet so all could hear YHWH's message. See SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL

▣ "their transgression. . .their sins" Formal ritual had replaced personal righteousness. They were religious but far from YHWH (cf. Isa. 29:13-14; Jer. 7; 2 Tim. 3:5; Titus 1:16). Religion can be a barrier to true personal faith!

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BACKGROUND

  1. This chapter is a condemnation of religious ritual without personal faith (cf. Isa. 29:13; Jeremiah 7).

  2. This is the spiritual problem that caused the Exile, and in my opinion, the fall of Jerusalem in A.D. 70. See my exegetical notes on the Olivet Discourse online (i.e. Matthew 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 58:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:2 Notice how the false faith is characterized.

  1. They seek Me day by day (see SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek The Lord).
  2. They delight to know My ways.
  3. A nation. . .has not forsaken the ordinance (BDB 1048) of their God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION, II. F) .
  4. They ask Me for just decisions.
  5. They delight in the nearness of God.

All of this sounds great but it was a show, a farce, a religious game; words, not deeds (cf. Isa. 29:13; Jer. 7).

▣ "As a nation that has done righteousness" This is sarcasm.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "ask Me for just decisions" This refers to ways to know God's will.

  1. the Urim and Thummim (i.e. the High Priest, cf. Exod. 28:30; Num. 27:23; Deut. 33:8; Neh. 7:65
  2. the prophets (covenant mediators)
  3. local Levites (teachers of the application of Mosaic laws)

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

entries.title: Isaiah 58:3 "fasted. . .humbled ourselves"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:3 "fasted. . .humbled ourselves" The word "fasted" (Qal PERFECT, BDB 847, KB 1012) parallels "humbled" (Piel PERFECT, BDB 776, KB 853, cf. Lev. 16:29,31). They thought God must bless their religious acts. The OT has only one fast a year (Leviticus 16), the Day of Atonement (cf. Isa. 58:6a). During the Exile the Jews had multiplied this to four fast days to commemorate tragic events in their national life (i.e. the fall of Jerusalem, the destruction of the Temple, etc., cf. Zech. 7:3,5; 8:19).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FASTING

▣ "on the day of your fast you find your desire

  And drive hard all your workers" They fasted for "religious" reasons and would not allow their laborers off to participate! The effects of the Fall continue!

entries.title: Isaiah 58:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:4 The fast days produced irritation not faith.

▣
NASB, NKJV, JPSOA  "to strike with a wicked fist"
AB  "strike the poor with the fist"
LXX  "strike a humble person with your fists"
Peshitta  "to strike violently with the fists
  of wickedness"
NJB  "to strike viciously with your fist"

The MT has "to hit with fist wicked," but notice how the LXX takes a clue from Isa. 58:3c-d.

▣ "to make your voice heard on high" One purpose of fasting was to help with prayers, but it caused the opposite reaction (cf. Isa. 1:15; 59:2).

entries.title: Isaiah 58:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:5 This is a list of outward signs of mourning, like sackcloth and ashes, but in reality these were only for show (cf. Matt. 6:5,16-18).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

entries.title: Isaiah 58:6-7 "Is this not the fast which I chose"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:6-7 "Is this not the fast which I chose" God lists what He really wants from His people (i.e. daily social justice, cf. Exod. 21:2; Lev. 25:39-41; Deut. 15:12; and Jer. 34:8-11, which refers to the year of Jubilee; Titus 1:16).

  1. to loosen the bonds of wickedness ‒ Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE, BDB 834, KB 986
  2. to undo the bonds of the yoke ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE, BDB 684, KB 736
  3. to let the oppressed go free ‒ Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE, BDB 1018, KB 1511
  4. to break every yoke ‒ Piel PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, BDB 954, KB 1285 (i.e. indentured servitude)
  5. to divide your bread with the hungry ‒ Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE, BDB 828, KB 969
  6. to bring the homeless poor into the house ‒ Hiphil IMPERFECT, BDB 97, KB 112, cf. Matt. 25:35; Rom. 12:13; 1 Tim. 3:2; Titus 1:8; Heb. 13:2; 1 Pet. 4:9
  7. to cover the naked ‒ Piel PERFECT with waw, BDB 491, KB 487, cf. James 2:14-18
  8. not to hide yourself from your own flesh ‒ Hithpael PERFECT, BDB 761, KB 834, cf. 1 Tim. 5:8 (i.e. help your relatives)

This is the origin of the glorified Messiah's criteria for dividing the sheep (faithful believers) from the goats (unbelievers who act selfishly) in Matt. 25:31-46. This is not a works-righteousness, but lifestyle evidence that the results of the Fall (i.e. self) have been reversed (i.e. others).

entries.title: Isaiah 58:8-9b
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:8-9b This is the promised restoration if they will repent and exhibit lifestyle faith. Notice what true faithfulness brings.

  1. your light will break out like the dawn
  2. your recovery will speedily spring forth
  3. your righteousness will go before you
  4. the glory of the Lord will be your rear guard
  5. you will call and the Lord will answer
  6. you will cry, and He will say "Here I am" (cf. Isa. 65:1)

This is what God wanted to do for His people, but their sin and rebellion caused judgment and separation!

▣ "the glory of the Lord will be your rear guard" This refers to the Shekinah cloud of glory being their protection as it was during the Exodus period (cf. Exod. 14:19 and Isa. 52:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 58:9a,b
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:9a,b These lines of poetry emphasize YHWH's availability to an obedient covenant people.

  1. He will hear their prayers
  2. He will be available (i.e. "Here I am," cf. Isa. 6:8)

entries.title: Isaiah 58:9c-10 "If"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:9c-10 "If" This (cf. Isa. 58:9 and 10) shows the conditional element of God's reciprocal covenantal relationship ("if. . .then," often assumed but not stated) with His people. Note the conditions.

  1. remove the yoke (i.e. indentured servants/slaves)
  2. stop the pointing of the finger, cf. Prov. 6:13
  3. stop speaking wickedness
  4. give yourself to the hungry (Hiphil JUSSIVE, BDB 807, KB 920)
  5. satisfy the desire of the afflicted

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Isaiah 58:9 "The pointing of the finger"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:9 "The pointing of the finger" This refers to evil gestures or words (cf. Prov. 6:13).

  1. formal legal accusation
  2. announce a curse
  3. social slander

entries.title: Isaiah 58:10c-12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:10c-12 The "then" (blessing) part of the conditional covenant (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28-29) is spelled out.

  1. your light will rise in darkness
  2. your gloom will become like midday
  3. the Lord will continually guide you
  4. the Lord will satisfy your desire
  5. the Lord will give strength to your bones
  6. you will be like a watered garden
  7. you will be like a spring of water whose waters do not fail
  8. you will rebuild the ancient ruins
  9. you will raise up the age old foundations
  10. you will be called the repairer of the breach
  11. you will be called the restorer of the streets

The prophet uses several sources of imagery to describe YHWH's presence and blessing.

  1. light vs. darkness
  2. shepherd imagery
  3. agricultural blessing
  4. rebuilding imagery

entries.title: Isaiah 58:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:11 There are two textual issues in this verse.

  1. Isa. 58:11b
    NASB  "satisfy your desire"
    NKJV  "satisfy your soul in drought"
    TEV  "satisfy you with good things"
    NJB  "will satisfy your needs in the scorched land"
    JPSOA  "He will slake your thirst in parched places"
    Peshitta  "satisfy your soul with rich food"
    LXX  "you shall be satisfied exactly as your soul
      desires"

    The word "desire" is nephesh (BDB 659) which has many connotations (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH).
     The "scorched places" is found only here (BDB 850, KB 1019) and the meaning is uncertain.

  2. Isa. 58:11e
    NASB, NKJV  "whose waters do not fail"

    The MT's VERB (BDB 469, KB 467, Piel IMPERFECT) means "to lie" or "to deceive." The sense seems to be "the waters God provides; they never 'lie' or 'deceive'" (i.e. always flows [NJB])

entries.title: Isaiah 58:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:12 YHWH promises that the returnees from exile will rebuild their land, but this seems to contradict Isa. 32:14 (as well as Jer. 25:9). There are two issues here.

  1. the eastern peoples' use of hyperbole (see SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE)
  2. the ambiguity of the Bible's use of "forever," "everlasting" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

Prophecies were meant to effect change in the way God's people were living. If they did not change, the prophecies were sure! However, if repentance and rightoues living occurred, the prophecies were canceled (i.e. Jonah)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣
NASB  "the restorer of the streets in which to dwell"
JPSOA  "restorer of lanes for habitation"
LXX  "you shall cause the paths between them to rest"
Peshitta  "the restorer of paths to dwell in"
REB  "the restorer of houses in ruins"

The MT has "paths" (BDB 677), probably to be understood as "streets" because of the VERB "to dwell" (Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, BDB 442, KB 444).

entries.title: Isaiah 58:13 "the sabbath"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:13 "the sabbath" See Exodus 20:8-11 and Isaiah 56.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH

entries.title: Isaiah 58:13-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:13-14 This strophe uses obedience to the Sabbath requirements as a way to know a person's attitude and faithfulness.

  1. turn your foot from doing your own pleasure, to YHWH's sabbath (cf. Isa. 58:13)
  2. delight in the sabbath by calling it "honorable" (BDB 457, KB 455, is used twice in Isa. 58:13)

Notice again the conditional covenant ("if. . .then"). The benefits are listed in Isa. 58:14b,c.

entries.title: Isaiah 58:14 "For the mouth of the Lord has spoken"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:14 "For the mouth of the Lord has spoken" This expresses the trustworthiness and power of God's promises (cf. Genesis 1; Isa. 55:11)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

entries.title: Isaiah 58:14b "I will make you ride on the heights of the earth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
58:14b "I will make you ride on the heights of the earth" There are two interpretive issues.

  1. meaning of the VERB "ride on the heights"
    1. imagery for military victory and security (i.e. cities, forts built on hills)
    2. imagery of God-given abundance (cf. Deut. 32:13-14), v. 14c
  2. "the earth" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH)
    1. Palestine/Canaan
    2. universal implications for a new day of YHWH's blessing on the planet

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. What is the difference between biblical faith and religiosity?
  2. How is ethics related to theology?
  3. What is the purpose of fasting?
  4. What is the purpose of the Sabbath? Is it valid in our day?

entries.title: Isaiah 59:1 "hand"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:1 "hand" This is often a Hebrew idiom for activity (cf. Isa. 51:9). See SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND.

Notice the number of human body parts used to describe Deity (see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN).

  1. hand
  2. ear
  3. face

 Also notice how many human body parts describe human evil.

  1. hands, Isa. 59:3
  2. fingers, Isa. 59:3
  3. lips, Isa. 59:3
  4. tongue, Isa. 59:3
  5. feet alluded to in Isa. 59:7-8

▣ "save" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT).

▣ "dull" This word (BDB 457, KB 455, Qal PERFECT) means "to be heavy," "to be burdensome," or "to be honored." In this context it refers to an inability to hear (cf. Isa. 6:9-10). It is used in this same way as the "eyes" in Gen. 48:10 and of Pharaoh's "heart" in Exod. 9:7.

entries.title: Isaiah 59:1-2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:1-2 These opening phrases clearly show the problem with God's promises to Israel; it was not His word, character, or power but their repeated and continuing sin.

Verse 1 reflects the prophet's reaction to the questioning he hears from the Israelites of his day (i.e. where are the Lord's promises?). Isaiah records the murmurings of the people several times (i.e. Isa. 40:27; 49:4,14).

entries.title: Isaiah Contextual Insights
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. It is difficult to see how the different poems (i.e. chapters) relate in this section of Isaiah. I agree with R. K. Harrison that Isaiah is an anthology of Isaiah's preaching/teaching/writing assembled after his death. It is organized in an eastern way (thematic, word play) not a western chronological way.

  2. One wonders about these prophecies.
    1. Are they multiple fulfillment (i.e. Isa. 7:14; and Dan. 11:31; 12:11)?
    2. Do they express God's heart and desire for Israel, knowing that even with all the benefits of covenant (cf. Rom. 9:4-5) they could not keep it (i.e. Dan. 9:24-27)?
    3. Are they poems/prophecies from different periods of Isaiah's ministry, addressing different periods of Israel's history, but now arranged in a pattern that moderns do not comprehend? They are given without historical setting and written in powerful Hebraic poetry. They could fit the 8thcentury, or the 7th, or the eschaton.

  3. Modern interpreters must remember
    1. this is poetry, not historical narrative (see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY)
    2. these poems are presented without their specific historical setting (often Old Babylon and Neo-Babylon are not clearly differentiated)
    3. many of the words are used only once in the Bible or known Semitic literature (no cognate roots)
    4. Be careful of dogmatic doctrinal assertions from limited lines of poetry. Attempt to see
      1. parallelism
      2. parallel passages especially in Isaiah and Micah (8th century prophets)
      3. NT usage of the text/concept (cf. F. F. Bruce, Answers To Questions, pp. 87-88)

  4. The Jewish Study Bible (p. 901) sees this chapter in three parts.
    1. the prophet addresses the peoples' sin (i.e. corporately)
    2. the faithful in the nation acknowledge their sin (individually)
    3. the prophet announces YHWH's
      1. mercy to the faithful who repent (cf. Isa. 59:20,21)
      2. judgment to the hardened
        (1) Jews
        (2) the coastlands (i.e. Gentiles)

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 59:2 "iniquities"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:2 "iniquities" This term (BDB 730), from a root "to bend" or "to twist," is used of breaking God's laws.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, A. #2

▣ "made a separation between you and your God" The VERB (BDB 95, KB 110, Hiphil PARTICIPLE) is used in several senses.

  1. God separating light from dark in Gen. 1:4
  2. God setting Israel apart from other peoples
  3. making a distinction between clean and unclean
  4. dividing into parts (i.e. sacrifices)
  5. YHWH and Moses setting apart Levites (especially Aaron, 1 Chr. 23:13)
  6. cutting off a person from Israel (cf. Deut. 29:20)
  7. excluding foreigners (cf. Neh. 13:3)
  8. setting apart musicians
  9. separating oneself from foreigners and pagans in one's society (cf. Ezra 6:21; 9:1; 10:11; Neh. 9:2)
  10. separating oneself to a specific leader (i.e. David, 1 Chr. 12:8)

In this context it is used in a unique sense. Israel's sins had emotionally and spiritually separated the covenant people from the covenant God and His presence, promises, provisions, and protection! The exile of the covenant people was not a sign of YHWH's weakness, but of their covenant disobedience!

One way to illustrate this terrible spiritual condition is the next parallel line of poetry. God hid His face from them (i.e. He would not hear their prayers)! This is the opposite of Isa. 58:9.

entries.title: Isaiah 59:3-8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:3-8 These verses list (in parallel lines) the sins of Israel that had caused the separation (BDB 95).

  1. your hands are defiled with blood, Isa. 59:3
  2. your fingers defiled with iniquity, Isa. 59:3
  3. your lips have spoken falsehood, Isa. 59:3
  4. your tongue mutters wickedness, Isa. 59:3 (the VERB, BDB 211 I, is often connected to the occult, cf. Isa. 8:19; 29:4; 47:12-13)
  5. courts are corrupt, Isa. 59:4 (notice the four INFINITIVE ABSOLUTES)
  6. you plan evil and violence, Isa. 59:5-7 (cf. Job 8:14-15; 15:35; Prov. 1:16; for Isa. 59:7 see Rom. 3:15-17)
  7. they did not know the way of peace (cf. Isa. 26:3,12; 57:20-21; Luke 1:79) or justice, Isa. 59:8 (notice the four PERFECT VERBS)
    SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 59:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:4 Verse 4, like Isa. 59:13, uses a series of INFINITIVE ABSOLUTES to describe evil human behavior.

  1. they trust in confusion, Qal. BDB 105, KB 120
  2. they speak lies, Piel, BDB 180, KB 210
  3. they conceive mischief, Qal, BDB 247, KB 255 (cf. Job 15:35)
  4. they bring forth iniquity, Hiphil BDB 408, KB 411

entries.title: Isaiah 59:9-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:9-11 These verses describe the results of Israel's sins (Isa. 59:3-8). This explains why YHWH's promises of abundant restoration have been delayed.

  1. justice is far from us (see SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE)
  2. righteousness does not overtake us (see SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS)
  3. hope for light, but darkness comes (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LIGHT and SPECIAL TOPIC: DARKNESS)
  4. hope for brightness but walk in gloom (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)
  5. grope along the wall like blind men (BDB 178, KB 206, Piel COHORTATIVE, twice, cf. Deut. 28:29; Jer. 13:16; Amos 5:18,20; also note Isa. 6:9-10)
  6. growl like bears
  7. moan like doves
  8. hope for justice, but none comes
  9. hope for salvation but it is far away (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION [OT])

Number 6 is a metaphor, found only here in the OT. The TEV translates (paraphrases) it and the next line as "we are frightened and distressed." The NASB Study Bible footnote characterizes it as "impatient and frustrated."

Number 7's imagery is found in Isa. 38:14; Ezek. 7:16; and Nahum 2:7.

59:10d
NASB, NRSV  "among those who are vigorous"
NKJV, Rotherham  "in desolate places"
NJB  "among the robust"
REB  "in the desolate underworld"
JPSOA  "among the sturdy"
JPSOA footnote  "In the daytime"
LXX, Peshitta  "they will groan"

The MT has a PREPOSITION and the NOUN (BDB 1032, KB 96). This root can mean

  1. robust, healthy
  2. fertile place
  3. among the stout (only here)
  4. desolate places (cf. Hosea 14:1 conjecture from BDB 79); KB 96 suggests "graveyard."

Obviously, the Hebrew is uncertain. JPSOA footnote emendation fits the parallelism of v. 10 best.

entries.title: Isaiah 59:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:12 Verse 12 describes the current spiritual situation (cf. Isa. 1:2-4; 6:5).

  1. Israel's transgressions are multiplied before YHWH
  2. Israel's sins testify against them
  3. Israel's transgressions are present with them
  4. Israel knows her sins

Notice that Isaiah, like Ezra, confesses the corporate sin of the covenant people (cf. Ezra 9:6-7). This is what the High Priest did on the Day of Atonement (cf. Leviticus 16). There is corporate guilt with consequences, as there is individual sin and its consequences!

This may be a separate literary unit (TEV, NJB) which records the faithful remnants' confession of sin. These repentant ones, and not all of Israel/Judah, are forgiven and restored.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

entries.title: Isaiah 59:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:13 Verse 13 describes the sins.

  1. transgressing ‒ BDB 833, KB 981, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  2. denying the Lord ‒ BDB 471, KB 469, Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  3. turning away from God ‒ BDB 690, KB 744, Niphal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  4. speaking oppression and revolt ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  5. conceiving from the heart lying words ‒ BDB 247, KB 255, Poel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  6. speaking/uttering from the heart lying words ‒ BDB 211, KB 237, Poel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

Notice how the author artistically uses the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTES in Isa. 59:4 and 13! The faithless seed of Abraham show their true orientation (i.e. self) by their lifestyle (cf. Titus 1:16). They speak of YHWH but live for self (cf. Isa. 6:9-10; 29:13; Matt. 7:15-29).

entries.title: Isaiah 59:14-15a
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:14-15a What are the results of these premeditated spiritual rebellions?

  1. justice is turned back
  2. righteousness stands far away
  3. truth stumbles in the street
  4. uprightness cannot enter
  5. truth is lacking

Notice the personifications! The one who tries to be righteous is a target and prey for the sinful!

entries.title: Isaiah 59:15b-16b
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:15b-16b Israel, the covenant people, was YHWH's means of revealing Himself to the world (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN). They had miserably failed. They, like all fallen humans, were incapable of following God.

  1. their actions and attitudes were displeasing
  2. there was no justice
  3. there was no righteous man
  4. there was no one to intercede (cf. Ezek. 22:30)

Therefore, YHWH must act Himself. This is similar theologically to Ezek. 36:22-36, which describes the "new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34.

Notice that the prophet speaks about YHWH in Isa. 59:15b-20. YHWH speaks for Himself in Isa. 59:21.

entries.title: Isaiah 59:16c-d
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:16c-d In light of fallen humanity's (even covenant humanity) ability YHWH chooses to act.

  1. His own arm brought salvation to Him, cf. Isa. 52:10; 63:5
  2. His righteousness upheld Him

Who is the "Him"? In context it could be the Suffering Servant (i.e. Messiah) or YHWH's prophet (i.e. Isaiah).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: SUFFERING MESSIAH

entries.title: Isaiah 59:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:17 YHWH is described as a "warrior" preparing for battle (i.e. the Divine Warrior, cf. Exod. 15:3; Josh. 5:13-15; Ps. 24:8; Isa. 42:13; Rev. 19:11-16). This text is the OT background for Paul's use of this military imagery in Eph. 6:10-17 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRITUAL WARFARE).

  1. He puts on righteousness like a breastplate
  2. He puts on a helmet of salvation
  3. He puts on garments of vengeance
  4. He wrapped Himself with zeal as a mantle

entries.title: Isaiah 59:18 "According to their deeds, so He will repay"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:18 "According to their deeds, so He will repay" This is a recurrent truth in Scripture (cf. Job 34:11,25; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 12:14; 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:19; Ezek. 33:20; Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12). All humans reap what they sow! There are consequences to choices and actions that follow us through time. Thank God for divine forgiveness and forgetfulness!

Just an added thought; without choice, how can there be responsibility? Human choice can be clearly seen in

  1. YHWH forbiding eating of the tree of knowledge, Genesis 3
  2. YHWH's words to Cain in Gen. 4:7
  3. the call of Abraham, Gen. 12:1-3
  4. the consequences for blessing and cursing in Lev. 26; Deut. 28 (i.e. to the Mosaic covenant)
  5. the powerful call of Deut. 30:15,19 (i.e. "choose life")

These are just isolated, limited examples. How can humans be responsible for their actions, if all is determined before by God's choices?

▣ "the coastlands" This word (BDB 15 I) is used often in this section of Isaiah (cf. Isa. 40:15; 41:1,5; 42:4,10,12,15; 49:1; 51:5; 59:18; 60:9; 66:19) in the sense of other nations or Gentile nations.

entries.title: Isaiah 59:19 "the name of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:19 "the name of the Lord" See SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH.

▣ "His glory" This is a recurrent theme (cf. Isa. 40:5; 58:8; 60:1; see fuller note at 60:1).

▣ "the wind of the Lord" See SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT and SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D. (YHWH).

entries.title: Isaiah 59:19-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:19-20 The purpose of YHWH's recompense (BDB 168) is for redemption (i.e. fear the name of the Lord). A Redeemer (cf. Isa. 41:14; 43:1; 44:22) comes from Israel (i.e. the Messiah). He comes for all who "turn" (BDB 996, KB1427, Qal PARTICIPLE, see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT]).

In the NT the context that struggles with Jewish unbelief and rebellion is Romans 9-11. Paul uses Isa. 59:20 in Rom. 11:26-27. I think that Rom. 3:21-31; 9-10; Galatians 3; and the book of Hebrews are the best NT texts to understand how the Old Covenant and New Covenant diverge and merge again!

For a good brief discussion of this text, please look at F. F. Bruce, Answers To Questions, pp. 87-88. This is one of my favorite books!

entries.title: Isaiah 59:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 59:20 Only the faithful remnant, those who turn from their sin (i.e. vv. 9-15a), are redeemed.

entries.title: Isaiah 59:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
59:21 YHWH speaks ("as for Me") to Israel (or the spiritual faith seed of Abraham, cf. Rom. 2:28-29; 9:6; Gal. 6:16). He promises

  1. His Spirit
  2. His revelation
  3. His influence through generations

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

▣ "from now and forever" One of my favorite books on interpreting prophecy is D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks. He has a good discussion of the metaphorical use of "forever," see pp. 99-101. He states that often it "serves to intensify the verb it modifies." Please look at the Special Topic below!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

entries.title: Isaiah 60:1 "Arise, shine"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:1 "Arise, shine" Two Qal IMPERATIVES implore the covenant people to be what they were called to be for themselves and for the world (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

Light is recurrent imagery in this chapter to describe:

  1. God's presence, Isa. 60:1,2,9-20; Rev. 21:23; 22:5
  2. spiritual holiness, Isa. 60:1,3,5,21; 62:1
  3. recurring imagery of light in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 9:2; 42:6; 49:6; 58:8; 59:9)

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIGHT

▣ "your light has come" The subject of Isa. 60:1-22 is "Zion" (cf. Isa. 60:14), which symbolizes the people of God.

The common VERB "come" (BDB 97, KB 112) is used several times in this chapter.

  1. has come ‒ Qal PERFECT, Isa. 60:1
  2. come ‒ Qal PERFECT, Isa. 60:4
  3. will come ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 60:4
  4. will come ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 60:5
  5. will come ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 60:6
  6. will bring ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, Isa. 60:6
  7. bring ‒ same as #6, Isa. 60:11
  8. will come ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 60:13
  9. will bring ‒ Hiphil IMPERFECT, twice, Isa. 60:17
  10. same as #9
  11. will set ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 60:20

Remember the time element is not in the Hebrew VERB but in its use in context.

▣ "the glory of the Lord" This is parallel to "light" in line 1. It is used in other places in Isaiah connected to light/lights (cf. Isa. 24:23; 58:8) and agricultural abundance (cf. Isa. 35:2). The Hebrew term for "glory" (BDB 458), because of its association with the Shekinah cloud of glory (cf. Exod. 13:21-22; 14:19,20,24; 19:16-18; 20:21), symbolized YHWH's personal presence with the Israelites during the Exodus. Fire and lightning were associated with the coming of YHWH to Mt. Sinai (cf. Exodus 19-20), so brightness became an aspect of "glory."

Notice YHWH's glory.

  1. will rise ‒ BDB 280, KB 281, Qal IMPERFECT
  2. will appear ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERFECT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (OT)
