READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. There is a radical change in the mood between Isaiah 59 and Isaiah 60-62.

  2. Isaiah 60-62 form a unit that deals with the glorious future of God's people as depicted in the restoration of Jerusalem.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 60:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:2 This has some allusion to the physical darkness of Gen. 1:1-2 or Exod. 10:21-23 or even Isa. 9:2, and the spiritual darkness caused by sin. YHWH will not allow the darkness of the Fall (cf. Genesis 3), which covers all humans, to remain. His "light" of revelation and salvation will rise (Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 280, KB 281).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: DARKNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "earth" Erets (BDB 75, KB 90) has a wide semantic field.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH

entries.title: Isaiah 60:3 "Nations will come to your light"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:3 "Nations will come to your light" It is obvious that God's original purpose for Israel was to bring the world to Himself (cf. Isa. 61:6,11b; 62:2,11; Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6).

Of all the prophets, with the possible exceptions of Micah and Jonah, it is Isaiah who saw the universal implications of

  1. monotheism (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM)
  2. OT Patriarchal promises (see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS)
  3. Israel's evangelistic purpose (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)

Note Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 42:6-12; 45:14,22-25; 49:23; 51:4-5; 56:6-7; 60:1-3; 66:23. This is surely the precursor of John 3:16; 4:42; 1 Tim. 2:4; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; I John 2:2; 4:14. The NT, following the teachings of Jesus, universalized the OT promises to Israel (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5), to the whole world (cf. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:47; Acts 1:8). Neither Jesus nor any NT Apostle ever reaffirms a national promise to Israel. The OT has been fulfilled and overflowed in the Gospel (cf. Matt. 5:17-19; Eph. 2:11-3:13).

entries.title: Isaiah 60:4 "Lift up. . .see"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:4 "Lift up. . .see" These are two Qal IMPERATIVES (cf. Isa. 49:18; John 4:35). In this section of Isaiah IMPERATIVES often begin a new strophe.

▣ "Your sons will come from afar" In Isaiah 60-62, there are two major eschatological signs that deal with traveling.

  1. the people of God will return to their ancestral home, symbolized by the city of Jerusalem
  2. the nations, instead of taking the Jews prisoner and deporting them, will come to the people of God with gifts and praise

entries.title: Isaiah 60:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:5 As a result of God's repentant people "seeing" (Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 906, KB 1157), notice the stated consequences of seeing the light of God (cf. Isa. 60:1,4,19,20).

  1. be radiant ‒ Qal PERFECT with waw, BDB 626, KB 676
  2. thrill (lit. tremble) ‒ Qal PERFECT with waw, BDB 808, KB 922
  3. rejoice ‒ Qal PERFECT with waw, BDB 931, KB 1210

The reasons for this hope and joy are God's gracious acts.

  1. the abundance of the seas will be turned to you (i.e. the wealth of the seafaring peoples)
  2. the wealth of the nations will come to you (cf. Isa. 60:6-7,11; 61:6)

These parallel lines of poetry describe the gratitude of the nations for Israel's

  1. revealing of YHWH
  2. bringing the reality of YHWH's presence to earth
  3. opening a way for their inclusion to God's covenant family (cf. Isa. 56:7)

In some ways, this parallels what happened when Israel left Egypt. Egyptians gave them gifts (cf. Exod. 12:35-36).

60:5b
NASB, NRSV, Peshitta  "rejoice"
NKJV, TEV  "with joy"
NJB  "dilate"
REB  "with gladness"
JPSOA  "thrill"

The MT has two paralleled Qal PERFECT VERBS.

  1. BDB 808, KB 922, "in awe"
  2. BDB 931, KB 931, "to be wide" or "large"

The second one is a Hebrew idiom. It referred to the excitement of a calf released from a pen into a wide, green pasture. The joy can be expressed by a similar Hebrew root (BDB 923), but the UBS Text Project, p. 153, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt). However, the meaning of the line of poetry is the same.

entries.title: Isaiah 60:6 "will bear good news of the praises of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:6 "will bear good news of the praises of the Lord" The VERB (Piel IMPERFECT, BDB 142, KB 163) refers to the grace of God to Israel and to all nations (cf. Isa. 40:9-10; 41:27; 42:10-13; 52:7). Isn't it shocking to hear of the pagan nations praising the God of Israel? This is the obvious theological goal of monotheism. There is one God and all humans are created in His image and likeness (cf. Gen. 1:26-27) for fellowship (implication of Gen. 3:8; Lev. 26:12). The promise of Gen. 3:15 to all humans and the hope of covenant blessings to the families of the earth in Gen. 12:3 have come to fruition.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 60:7 "Nabaioth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:7 "Nabaioth" This refers to Arabian tribes, as the phrase, "the flocks of Kedar," does. This tribe is mentioned in Gen. 25:13. They are called the Nabateans by the Greeks and Romans.

▣ The last two poetic lines seem to imply Gentiles acting as priests at YHWH's altar. Wow! What a new day of inclusion (possibly linked to Isa. 56:7; 61:6-7; 66:21; 1 Pet. 2:5,9; Rev. 1:6; 5:10; 20:6).

entries.title: Isaiah 60:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 60:8 This refers to sails of ships on the horizon coming (i.e. v. 9) to the restored and renewed Jerusalem (cf. v. 7c, d).

entries.title: Isaiah 60:9 "Surely the coastlands will wait for Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:9 "Surely the coastlands will wait for Me" The term "coastlands" (or "islands," BDB 15 I) is used in this section of Isaiah as a metaphor for all Gentiles.

The VERB "wait" (Piel IMPERFECT, BDB 875, KB 1082) is often used of trusting in YHWH (cf. Isa. 8:17; 25:9; 26:8; 33:2). Notice how it is used of YHWH in Isa. 30:18!

▣ "the ships of Tarshish" Tarshish could refer to

  1. Southern Spain
  2. Sardinia
  3. a proverbial use of the ends of the earth

SPECIAL TOPIC: TARSHISH

▣ Notice the covenant names for Deity (also notice Isa. 60:14,16).

  1. YHWH (God as Savior and Redeemer)
  2. Elohim (God as creator and provider)
  3. Holy One of Israel (covenant God)

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C., D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

entries.title: Isaiah 60:10 "For in My wrath I struck you,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:10 "For in My wrath I struck you,

 And in My favor I have had compassion on you" Here we see the two major actions of YHWH in the Bible:

  1. His grace (long term, cf. Ps. 103:10-14)
  2. His wrath (short term, cf. Isa. 57:16; Ps. 103:9)

His judgment is parental in nature and meant to cause His creation to return to Him (cf. Romans 1-3; Heb. 12:1-13).

entries.title: Isaiah 60:11 "Your gates will be open continually"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:11 "Your gates will be open continually" This phrase is used to show

  1. security is assured
  2. availability is certain (cf. Rev. 21:25)

entries.title: Isaiah 60:12 "the nation and the kingdom which will not serve you will perish"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 60:12 "the nation and the kingdom which will not serve you will perish" This warning is similar to God's covenant with Abraham in Gen. 12:3.

entries.title: Isaiah 60:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:13 This verse speaks of the construction of a new Holy Place (i.e. temple) with the beautiful lumber from Lebanon (cf. 1 Kgs. 5:15-25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE OF THE WILDERNESS

▣  "the place of My sanctuary;

And I shall make the place of My feet glorious" The Ark of the Covenant in the Holy of Holies symbolizes God's presence on earth. The Jews conceived of the space between the wings of the Cherubim as the footstool of God (cf. 1 Chr. 28:2; Ps. 99:5; 132:7; Ezek. 43:7); His throne was in heaven.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

entries.title: Isaiah 60:14 "Zion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:14 "Zion" The term "Zion" (BDB 851) is synonymous with the City of Jerusalem. The temple was built on Mt. Moriah, but the city was seldom referred to by this term (cf. Isa. 62:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, JERUSALEM, ZION

entries.title: Isaiah 60:15 "you have been forsaken and hated"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:15 "you have been forsaken and hated" This phrase is a Hebrew idiom relating to marriage. We can see this in the terms to describe "Leah" in Gen. 29:21ff. This same idiom of marriage is continued in Isa. 62:4-5 and in the NT as the church in Eph. 5:22-33.

"Hate" is a Hebrew idiom of comparison.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HATE

entries.title: Isaiah 60:15-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:15-22 This passage is very similar to Rev. 21:1-27, which describes "New Jerusalem." There have been two major opinions on the relationship of the OT promises to the NT:

  1. They are meant to be taken literally and Jerusalem will be rebuilt with its central sacrificial temple, i.e. dispensational premillennialism.
  2. These passages are symbolic of the church and their significance is caught up in the NT as the new people of God, i.e. amillennialism.

The same ambiguity can be seen in Isa. 61:6, where Israel is referred to as a "Priests of the Lord" (cf. Exod. 19:6 "a Kingdom of Priests"). But these same terms are used in 1 Pet. 2:5,9 and Rev. 1:6 to describe the church. Israel's purpose has always been to bring the world to God (cf. Isa. 62:2,11). However, they failed and God has chosen the church to fulfill this task.

I have recently (2024) changed my eschatological opinion about

  1. Jesus' Olivet Discourse (Matt. 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21)
  2. 2 Thessalonians 2
  3. the book of Revelation

I have changed from a Futurist/Idealist to a Partial-Preterist/Idealist. Because of this, I have rewritten my exegetical notes on those Scripture texts. I hope you will look at the new videos and written commentary on Revelation. All of these Bible Studies are free online at www.freebiblecommentary.org. Click on the second blue box and then either "Written Bible Commentaries" or "Video Bible Commentaries."

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SECOND COMING

SPECIAL TOPIC: DISCIPLES' QUESTIONS ABOUT THE TEMPLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION OF DESOLATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANTICHRIST

SPECIAL TOPIC: SOON RETURN

SPECIAL TOPIC: DELAYED RETURN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANY MOMENT RETURN OF JESUS vs. THE NOT YET

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE END-TIME EVENTS SO CONTROVERSIAL?

entries.title: Isaiah 60:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:16 This imagery mixes

  1. royal images (from David and Solomon)
  2. with iternational rulers

Instead of the nations being enemies, they will come as nurses and servants. Their coming will bring

  1. salvation to them
  2. encouragement to the covenant people

▣ Notice the names/titles of Israel's God in v. 16.

  1. the Lord ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.
  2. your Savior ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR
  3. your Redeemer ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM
  4. the Mighty One of Jacob ‒ Gen. 49:24; Ps. 132:2,5; Isa. 1:24; 49:26; 60:16

entries.title: Isaiah 60:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:17 This is possibly an allusion to 1 Kgs. 14:26-27 relating to the stripping of precious metals from the temple to pay a tribute to Egypt.

▣ "And I will make peace your administrators
  And righteousness your overseers" This may reflect the Messianic government mentioned in Isaiah 7-14.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

entries.title: Isaiah 60:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:18 This prophecy is surely not applicable to Israel's subsequent history (cf. Dan. 9:24-27)! This seems to show the absence of social violence and problems in the Messianic Age.

▣ "salvation" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 60:19-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 60:19-20 John the Apostle uses this imagery in Rev. 21:23; 22:5. YHWH's presence is the true light! This may reflect Gen. 1:3.

entries.title: Isaiah 60:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:20 The first three poetic lines emphasize the eternality of God's restoration promises to His covenant people. But, the problem is that they will be in trouble from foreigners again in the future.

  1. Greeks (Seleucids)
  2. Romans (cf. Dan. 9:24-27)

With this in mind, two possibilities come to mind.

  1. this is a conditional covenant promise (see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT)
  2. this refers to an eschatological time

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

▣ "your mourning will be over" A new day has/will dawn, cf. Isa. 35:10; 65:19; Rev. 21:4.

entries.title: Isaiah 60:21 "all your people will be righteous"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:21 "all your people will be righteous" God's blessings will come only when the people repent and obey. This is why the modern state of Israel cannot be a prophetic fulfillment. See Steve Gregg's YouTube video, "The Modern State of Israel," and while you are on this web site, see his "Deconstructing Dispensationalism" and "Deconstructing Calvinism." He, Himself, will provide a new heart, a new spirit, and a new mind (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36).

This type of promise is the source of the theological debate over sovereignty and free will. Can fallen mankind do anything toward their own salvation or is everything (i.e. faith, repentance) a gift from God (cf. Acts 5:31; 11:18; 2 Tim. 2:25). Other texts point toward a preaching that draws humans to repent (i.e. free will response to a Divine offer, cf. Matt. 3:8; Luke 3:8; John 1:12; Acts 2:38; Rom. 10:9-13). Somehow both are biblical! This is the western problem with eastern paradox!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

▣ "They will possess the land forever" This may be an allusion to Gen. 17:8. The word "forever" is the interpretive problem because the Mosaic covenant is conditional on human obedience.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW

▣ "The branch of My planting" This same imagery is used in Isa. 61:3. It seems to reflect Psalm 1, but is also seen in Isa. 11:1. The OT uses agricultural imageries often.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BRANCH OF THE LORD

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE

▣ "The work of My hands" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

entries.title: Isaiah 60:22 "clan"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
60:22 "clan" This term can mean "thousands."

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

▣
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "hasten it in its time"
NRSV  "in its time I will accomplish
   it quickly"
TEV  "I will make this happen quickly"
NJB  "when the time is ripe. . .shall
   quickly bring it about"
REB  "at its appointed time. . .shall bring
   this swiftly to pass"
LXX  "gather them in due time"
JPSOA  "will speed it in due time"

When is this prediction of return, restoration, and blessed prosperity to occur?

  1. in 538 B.C. by Cyrus II's decree
  2. in Dan. 9:24-27
  3. in the eschaton

Isaiah's prophetic poems purposely do not state the historical setting, so as to allow his predictions to fit different periods of time. History is in God's hands (cf. Isa. 45:23; 61:11).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why is this chapter replete with metaphors that describe "brightness" or "light"?
  2. Will there be a literal restoration of the Jews or does this refer to the Messianic Age?
  3. Why would the Gentiles flow into Jerusalem?
  4. What is the connection between Isa. 60:15-22 and the book of Revelation?

entries.title: Isaiah 61:1 "The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:1 "The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me" Jesus used this verse for Himself in Luke 4:18-21. He also used this verse to answer John the Baptist's question. cf. Luke 7:18-23. This occurred visibly in Jesus' life at His baptism (cf. Isa. 11:1-2; 42:1; Matt. 3:13-17; Mark 1:9-11; Luke 3:21,22; John 1:31-34), but the Spirit had always been with Jesus.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE NT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

▣ "anointed" This is the same Hebrew root from which the title "Messiah" (BDB 602) or "the Anointed One" comes. This was a sign of God's unique blessing and equipping for a task (cf. Ps. 23:5). In the OT prophets, priests, and kings were anointed as a symbolic act of God's unique presence and call upon their lives. From this John Calvin derived his threefold category for describing Christ's ministry as prophet, priest, and king (cf. Heb. 1:2-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE (BDB 603)

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

▣ "To bring good news to the afflicted" The Messiah's message will be one of hope and forgiveness to the outcast, ostracized, and socially oppressed (cf. Isa. 35:5-6; note Matt. 11:5; 12:15-22; Luke 4:18-21; 7:18-23; John 3:16).

Notice the series of INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS in Isa. 61:1-3 that describe the Messiah's task.

  1. to bring good news to the afflicted ‒ Piel, BDB 142, KB 163
  2. to proclaim liberty to captives ‒ Qal, BDB 894, KB 1128
  3. to proclaim the favorable year of the Lord ‒ same as #2
  4. to comfort all who mourn ‒ Piel BDB 636, KB 688
  5. to grant those who mourn in Zion a garland instead of ashes
    1. grant ‒ Qal, BDB 962, KB 1321
    2. give ‒ Qal BDB 678, KB 733
  6. another INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT but directed towards the Messiah, Himself ‒ "that He may be glorified" ‒ Hithpael, BDB 802, KB 908

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Isaiah 60 describes the end result, while Isa. 61 describes the means of God's blessing.

  2. Jesus uses this passage of Himself in Luke 4:16-21; 7:18-23. This was meant to be the task of Israel's king. Because of this, this passage must be Messianic (i.e. the Servant).
     Those of us who are Christian must continue to remember that Jesus is the ultimate revelation of God (cf. Matt. 5:17-19). His life, teachings, death, and resurrection changed everything! The OT must now be reinterpreted through NT revelation (cf. 2 Tim. 3:15-17). Neither Jesus nor any Apostle ever reaffirmed a national promise to Israel. By divine act Jerusalem and the temple were destroyed by Rome (A.D. 66-70). As a consequence of this, the Jewish believers totally separated from the synagogue and became a truly international church (cf. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8)!
     I have come to believe that the Olivet Discourse of Jesus (i.e. Matt. 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21; 2 Thess. 2; and the book of Revelation) predict the Jewish war with Rome and not far future events and persons. Please check my exegetical verse-by-verse commentary on these verses free online at www.freebiblecommentary.org.

  3. The Spirit of the Lord here is obviously analogous (i.e. foreshadowing) to the Holy Spirit in the NT Trinitarian sense.
    1. see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE
    2. see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY
    3. see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

  4. It is obvious that this is an example of a local historical situation in the life of Israel being used to depict future events in the time of the Messiah (i.e. typology).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: TYPOLOGY

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 61:2 "the favorable year of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:2 "the favorable year of the Lord" This is an allusion to the year of Jubilee (cf. Lev. 25:10,13,28,54). This was a year of release from all debts (i.e. an example of YHWH's mercy; note King Zedekiah's decree in Jer. 34:8-10) and a return of all lands to the original owners every fifty years (i.e. an example of YHWH dividing the land in Joshua. The land belonged to YHWH). There is not one example in the OT that this was ever historically enacted. See Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 175-177.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, II. C.

▣ "the day of vengeance of our God" It is significant to notice that the favorable year and the day of vengeance occur at the same time (cf. Isa. 63:4). For those who know God in the Messiah, it is a day of reward. To those who do not know our Christ, it is a day of judgment and great sorrow (cf. Matt. 25:36-46; Rev. 20:11-15). There must be bad news of human rebellion before there is good news of God's mercy in Christ! (cf. Romans 1-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT

entries.title: Isaiah 61:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:3 Notice the contrasts (i.e. "instead").

  1. a garland instead of ashes
  2. oil of gladness instead of mourning
  3. the mantle of praise instead of a spirit of fainting

Also notice the same contrast in Isa. 61:7.

  1. double portion instead of shame
  2. shout of joy instead of humiliation

▣ "garland. . .ashes" These are examples of types of things put on the head (cf. Ezek. 24:17).

▣ "The oil of gladness" The ancients lacked the availability of makeup, therefore, to prepare themselves for times of joy and festival, they anointed themselves with olive oil (cf. Ps. 45:7).

▣ "The mantle of praise" Here is an OT example of clothing used as imagery for an attitude and spiritual position.

▣ "oaks of righteousness. . .The planting of the Lord" In Psalm 1 it refers to God's initiating love, ongoing support, and provision (cf. Jer. 17:7-8). Here it refers to the Messiah (cf. Isa. 60:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "that He may be glorified" YHWH is glorified when His leaders and people are treated appropriately (i.e. Mosaic Covenant).

entries.title: Isaiah 61:4 "they will rebuild the ancient ruins"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:4 "they will rebuild the ancient ruins" It is hard for a non-Jew to imagine the intensity of the feeling that is connected with the Promised Land and Jersualem (cf. Isa. 49:8; 58:12; 60:10).

This verse lists several things the ones set free will do.

  1. rebuild the ancient ruins
  2. raise up the former devastations
  3. repair the ruined cities

The last line of Isa. 61:4 shows that the author is addressing those returning from Mesopotamian exile. As in all of Isaiah's ambiguous poems, the historical setting is not given. The revelatory truths can apply to multiple historical situations.

entries.title: Isaiah 61:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:5 Verse 5 continues the theme of foreigners coming to Jerusalem with gifts and service, to worship the God of Israel.

From NT revelation we now know that this refers to the new covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36) in Christ available for all through repentance and faith (cf. Mark 1:15; Acts 3:16,19; 20:21)!

I interpret the OT promises to national Israel as multiple fulfillment prophecies. They were never fulfilled in Israel's history because of their sin and rebellion. They only find fulfilment in Christ.

See note at Contextual Insights, B.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE END-TIME EVENTS SO CONTROVERSIAL?

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 61:6 "you will be called the priests of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:6 "you will be called the priests of the Lord" Israel was meant to be a nation of priests, now they will be! Peter uses this very same phrase to describe the church in 1 Pet. 2:5,9 (cf. Exod. 19:56-6; also see John's usage in Rev. 1:6).

▣
NASB  "in their riches you will boast"
NKJV  "in their glory you shall boast"
NRSV  "in their riches you shall glory"
TEV  "and be proud that it is yours"
NJB  "you will supplant them in their glory"
JPSOA  "and succeed to their riches"
Peshitta  "in their glory shall you boast yourselves"
LXX  "and shall be admired because of their wealth"
NET  "and boast about the riches you receive from them"

The textual issue is over the last word in v. 6 of the MT.

  1. תתימרו ‒ you shall glory (MT)
  2. תתאמרו ‒ you shall boast (DSS)

See KB 67 compared with 416.

entries.title: Isaiah 61:7 "double portion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:7 "double portion" This refers to the inheritance of the eldest son in the inheritance structure of ancient Israel (cf. Deut 21:17). As Israel had a double portion of YHWH's wrath (cf. Isa. 40:2), now a double reward.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVERS' INHERITANCE

▣ "Everlasting joy will be theirs" This same wonderful promise is also found in Ps. 16:11. The question is when will this happen.

  1. it did not happen to the returnees from Mesopotanian exile
  2. it did not happen to the Jews under Greece or Rome
  3. the future then
    1. Israel after the Messiah comes
    2. the church (spiritually)
    3. the millennium (physically)
    4. restored Garden of Eden (i.e. Rev. 21-22)

This is ancient, inspired poetry! It does not address all the modern questions. It is best to take the central meaning of the strophe and view it through NT revelation (i.e. Jesus is the ultimate revelation of the unseen God; see Contextual Insights, B)!

entries.title: Isaiah 61:8 "For I, the Lord, love justice"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:8 "For I, the Lord, love justice" YHWH is an ethical, moral being. He demands ethical, moral actions from His people!

Note His listed characteristics.

  1. loves justice
  2. hates robbery in sacrifices (i.e. burnt offerings)

Other wonderful texts that describe YHWH's character are Exod. 34:6; Num. 14:18; Neh. 9:17; Ps. 86:15; 103:8-14; 145:8-9!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE

▣ "in burnt offerings" The Septuagint and possibly some variations of the Masoretic Text have "with iniquity" (same consonants, NRSV, Peshitta, NEB, REB). The UBS Text Project, p. 156, gives the sacrificial phrase a B rating (some doubt).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERINGS

▣ "I will. . .make an everlasting covenant with them" The children of Abraham continually broke the first covenant, as a reading of I and 2 Kings and I and 2 Chr. will show. Because of this (i.e. Lev. 26; Deut. 28), God finally allowed the Covenant to be terminated (He left the temple, cf. Ezek. 1; 8-10). The purpose of this termination was the beginning of a new covenant with even greater spiritual significance (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36). This new covenant begins with the birth of Jesus.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Isaiah 61:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:9 Here is another forever promise to Israel as a sign and message (i.e. a light, cf. Isa. 42:6; 49:6; 51:4; Acts 13:47) about the nature of YHWH and other nations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 61:10 "I will rejoice greatly in the Lord,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:10 "I will rejoice greatly in the Lord,

  My soul will exult in my God" This verse could refer to the Messiah or the nation (cf. Isa. 12:1-2; 25:9; 41:16) rejoicing in YHWH's provision. The AB suggests that this chapter has three speakers.

  1. the prophet, Isa. 61:1-7 (possibly the Servant)
  2. YHWH, Isa. 61:8-9
  3. personified Zion, Isa. 61:10-11 (p. 181)

This shows the ambiguity of these poems as to speakers and recipients (i.e. period of time). Many commentators think Isa. 61:1-3 is a fifth Servant Song.

I think Isa. 61:10-11 are the restored and redeemed humanity (cf. Gen. 3:15), which is described in Eph. 2:11-3:13; Romans 9-11.

The VERBAL PHRASE, "I will rejoice greatly," is a Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a Qal IMPERFECT VERB of the same root (BDB 965, KB 1314). It was a Hebraic grammatical way of showing intensity.

The next line is parallel and the VERB "exalt" is a Qal JUSSIVE (BDB 162, KB 189).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

▣ "He has clothed me with garments of salvation" Here is an example of the joy of a wedding feast used as imagery for the spiritual joy of knowing YHWH. This imagery is extended in the NT to refer to believers as having Christ's robes of righteousness (cf. 2 Cor. 5:21).

Notice all the different ways of referring to festival clothing.

  1. clothed me with garments of salvation ‒ BDB 527, KB 519, Hiphil PERFECT
  2. wrapped me with a robe of righteousness ‒ BDB 418, KB 420, Qal PERFECT
  3. as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland ‒ BDB 464, KB 461, Piel IMPERFECT. This is the Hebrew root, cahan, which usually refers to priests putting on their priestly garments. It is occasions such as this that we must remember context, not lexicons, determines word meaning.
  4. as a bride adorns herself ‒ BDb 224, KB 243, Qal PERFECT with waw

entries.title: Isaiah 61:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
61:11 See Isa. 40:8 and 55:10-11.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. If this refers to the Messiah, why is it phrased in such nationalistic terms?
  2. Define the term Messiah.
  3. In what sense and to what purpose are the Jews a kingdom of priests?
  4. Why did God break His first everlasting covenant with the Jewish nation?
  5. Why is the use of a clothing metaphor in Isa. 61:10 so significant? How is it used in the NT for the believer standing before God?

entries.title: Isaiah 62:1 "Zion. . .Jerusalem"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:1 "Zion. . .Jerusalem" These are in a Hebrew parallel relationship. Jerusalem was built on seven hills. Mount Zion was not the site of the Temple, but the location of David's palace and came to be a reference to the whole city of Jerusalem.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, ZION, JERUSALEM

▣ The VERBS "be silent" (Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 364, KB 361) and "be quiet" (Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 1052, KB 1641), both negated, are related to the positive statement of Isa. 61:1.

The "I" could refer to the prophet or the Servant/Messiah (Deity breaks the silence mentioned in Isa. 42:14; 57:11; 64:12; 65:6). Obviously Isaiah 60-62 are a literary unit.

▣ "righteousness. . .salvation" These two words also are in a parallel relationship. Righteousness speaks of the position and lifestyle of the people of God which results in their physical deliverance from their enemies. In the OT the term "salvation" primarily refers to a physical deliverance, while in the NT the term refers primarily to spiritual forgiveness and a standing before God. Zion's (cf. Isa. 61:10-11) new day has come and will affect the whole world (cf. Isa. 62:2; 60:3)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

▣ "brightness. . .burning" Again the presence of YHWH is connected to light, as it was on Mt. Sinai (cf. Exodus 19-20). See note at Isa. 60:1.

Israel was meant to be "the light" of YHWH to the darkness of paganism and fertility worship. However, she was captured by them. The NT gives this same mission of revelation (i.e. Jesus is God's ultimate Light, cf. John 1:4; 8:12; 12:35) and evangelism as the believers' task (cf. Matt. 5:14-16; 28:19-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIGHT

SPECIAL TOPIC: DARKNESS

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS ‒ Isaiah 60-62 is a literary unit and should be read and interpreted together.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 62:2 "The nations will see your righteousness"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:2 "The nations will see your righteousness" Israel was chosen by YHWH to be a witness to the entire world to bring them to Himself (cf. Isa. 62:11; 52:10; 60:3; 61:6,11; 1 Pet. 2:5,9; Rev. 1:6). This is the true meaning of the phrase "a kingdom of priests" (cf. Exod. 19:5-6).

▣ "And you will be called by a new name" The imparting of a new name implies the new age of the Spirit. The new covenant is realized.

The term "new" (BDB 294 I) is used extensively in the second part of Isaiah to describe the new day of righteousness.

  1. new things, Isa. 42:9; 48:6
  2. new song, Isa. 42:10 (cf. Rev. 5:9; 14:3)
  3. something new, Isa. 43:19 (cf. Rev. 3:12)
  4. new name, Isa. 62:2 (cf. Isa. 56:5)
  5. new heavens and a new earth, Isa. 65:17; 66:22 (cf. 2 Pet 3:13)

The "new" day (cf. Rev. 21:5) was, in reality, the day that God always wanted for humans, but the Fall in Genesis 3 caused a terrible disruption! It is surely possible that the Bible's imagery of heaven is a restored Garden of Eden (cf. Rev. 21:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: OLD THINGS. . .NEW THINGS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: EDEN

entries.title: Isaiah 62:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:3 The Jerome Bible Commentary, vol. 1, p. 383, mentions that ancient eastern people believed their gods wore a crown shaped like the city that worshiped them. If so, then this may be a cultural allusion to this concept. This view depends on

  1. YHWH being the speaker of chapter 62
  2. how widespread this pagan concept was known

The Bible does use pagan imagery to describe and magnify YHWH. Four of many possible examples:

  1. "God of Heaven" in Nehemiah
  2. allusion to Persian Zoroastrian deity, Mal. 4:2
  3. allusion to the twelve signs of the zodiac in Rev. 12:1
  4. allusion to evil as a dragon

In Isa. 28:5 YHWH Himself is the crown of the covenant people. He is their glory, light, provision, protection, and victory!

In Zech. 9:16 the covenant people are the jewels in YHWH's crown.

▣ "in the hand of the Lord. . .in the hand of your God" Notice the parallelism.

  1. Lord (BDB 217) = YHWH, SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.
  2. God (BDB 43) = Eloah, SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

The eternal, non-corporal Deity is described in human terms. We have no other option to describe God but

  1. human terms
  2. negations ‒ what He is not
  3. analogy ‒ what He is like

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

entries.title: Isaiah 62:4 "Forsaken (BDB 736 I). . .Desolate (BDB 1031)"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:4 "Forsaken (BDB 736 I). . .Desolate (BDB 1031)" This describes Israel's own interpretation of the Exile (i.e. these are their titles for themselves). They felt they had been forsaken (cf. Isa. 49:14-21; 54:6-7) by YHWH and wondered if He would ever love them again (cf. v. 12).

▣ "My delight is in her" This is their true title! "Delight" may be the name "Hephzi-bah" (BDB 343, cf. 2 Kgs. 21:1). This is the beginning of sustained imagery about YHWH as marriage partner (cf. Isa. 62:4-5). It is hard to describe an infinite Holy Creator God, therefore, we have to use human analogies. It is common in the Bible to describe God as Father, as husband, as near kinsman.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINSMAN REDEEMER

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "married" This can also be translated "Beulah" (BDB 127). Lines 4 and 5 may be the "new name" of Isa. 62:2c.

This VERB (BDB 127, KB 42) is used four times in Isa. 62:4-5.

  1. Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, Isa. 62:4
  2. Niphal IMPERFECT, Isa. 62:4
  3. Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 62:5
  4. same as #3

Obviously, marriage is a good analogy for biblical faith (cf. Eph. 5:22-33).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SEXUALITY

entries.title: Isaiah 62:5 "virgin"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:5 "virgin" All women in Israel/Judah were expected to be virgins when they married.

SPECIAL TOPIC: VIRGIN

▣
NASB, NKJV  "so your sons will marry you"
NRSV  "so shall your builder marry you"
TEV  "He who formed you will marry you"
NJB  "your rebuilder will wed you"
REB  "so will you be wedded to him who rebuilds you"
LXX  "so shall your son dwell with you"
Peshitta  "so shall your sons husband you"

By a revocalization of the consonants (בניך) "sons" (MT) becomes "builder" (NRSV, JPSOA footnote, cf. Ps. 51:18; 102:16; 147:2), which fits the marriage imagery of the strophe better. However, the UBS Text Project, p. 156, gives the MT "sons" an A rating. YHWH is the builder!

The LXX has a VERB that means "to dwell with."

The Expositor's Bible Commentary, vol. 1, p. 336, says of this verse

"Verse 5 presents as strange an analogy as that in Isa. 60:16. In both cases there seems to be an intentional breach in the normal application of the analogy, perhaps in the interests of vivid impression. Such analogies puzzle us, but we do not forget them!"

entries.title: Isaiah 62:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:6 "Watchmen" refers to the prophets (cf. Isa. 52:8; 56:10 [negated]; Jer. 6:17; Ezek. 3:17; 33:7), although the rabbis see it referring to angels (cf. Dan. 4:13-17; Zech. 1:12-17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS IN THE BIBLE

entries.title: Isaiah 62:6-7 "You who remind the Lord. . .give Him no rest until He establishes. . .Jerusalem"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:6-7 "You who remind the Lord. . .give Him no rest until He establishes. . .Jerusalem" This may refer to the theological truth that God has limited Himself to the prayers of His children (cf. James 4:2). It is not overcoming the reluctance of an apathetic Deity, but it is the intercessory ministry of the people of God claiming the promises of God.

The VERBS "appointed" and "remind" are both Hiphils.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW GRAMMAR, II. B. #6

entries.title: Isaiah 62:8 "The Lord has sworn by His right hand and by His strong arm"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:8 "The Lord has sworn by His right hand and by His strong arm" This is an anthropomorphic phrase (see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)). God does not have a body. He is Spirit (cf. John 4:24), yet He swears by His own ability to act! YHWH is a God who has, will, and does act in individual lives, as well as nations.

YHWH's oath is a significant promise (cf. Isa. 54:9; Heb. 6:13-20; 7:20-28). It reminds us of

  1. the power of God's word, Isa. 55:11; 66:2d
  2. the trustworthy character of God, Isa. 45:22-23 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD [OT])

God has an eternal redemptive plan for all humans made in His image and likeness (cf. Acts 2:23; 3:18; 4:28; 1 Pet. 1:20, see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN). The Suffering Servant of Isa. 52:13-53:12 is the mechanism for universal redemption (cf. Rom. 5:12-21). The fellowship of Eden will be restored for those who repent and believe in God's Messiah.

▣ "enemies. . .foreigners" This refers to the invasion of Palestine by foreigners. It is a direct reference to the blessing versus cursing action of Lev. 26:16 and Deut. 28:30-33. Israel broke the Covenant. Israel suffered the consequences. YHWH promises a future day when the blessings will be a reality (i.e. 1 Pet. 1:4).

Just a reminder, these are conditional promises. If Abraham's seed is faithful and obedient to YHWH's covenant, blessing will flow. The purpose of these blessings is to reach the nations' attention so they can come to Him and find peace, security, and abundance.

The unconditional promises are related to YHWH's promises regarding salvation and restoration, but every individual must respond and continue to respond in an appropriate way (conditional covenant, see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT).

  1. repentance (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT])
  2. faith (see SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT)
  3. sevice
  4. obedience (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
  5. worship (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)
  6. perseverance (see SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE)

entries.title: Isaiah 62:9 "will drink it in the courts of My sanctuary"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:9 "will drink it in the courts of My sanctuary" This refers to the fellowship meal between YHWH and His covenant partner (cf. Deut. 12:18). These people are back in the land and the temple is restored.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING

entries.title: Isaiah 62:10 "go through the gates"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:10 "go through the gates" This could refer to

  1. the gates of the cities of Mesopotamia where the Israelites and Judeans were exiled (esp. Babylon)
  2. the gates of the rebuilt (i.e. Cyrus II's decree in 538 B.C.)
    1. Jerusalem (Zerubbabel, Joshua, Ezra, Nehemiah)
    2. the temple

▣ "Clear the way for the people;

 Build up, build up the highway"

This is common imagery of preparing the road for a royal visit (cf. Isa. 11:16; 19:23; 35:6-10; 40:3-4; 49:11; 57:14). This is used several ways in the Bible.

  1. it is used of the return of the exiled
  2. it is used by John the Baptist as a self-designation of his own ministry (i.e. Isa. 40:3 quoted in Matt. 3:1-3)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "lift up a standard" This refers to the flag of a tribe or military unit. Notice here the standard is over "the peoples" and Isa. 62:11a "to the end of the earth." The insignia of Israel is now the flag of all who believe, receive, and acknowledge YHWH (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:6-7; 60:1-3: 66:23).

entries.title: Isaiah 62:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:10-11 This is a message for the exiled people of God given by the prophet on YHWH's behalf. There is a series of eight IMPERATIVES.

  1. go through ‒ Qal, BDB 716, KB 778
  2. go through ‒ same as #1
  3. clear the way ‒ Piel, BDB 815, KB 937
  4. build up ‒ Qal, BDB 699, KB 757
  5. build up ‒ same as #4 (repeating VERBS is a common way of emphasis in Isaiah)
  6. remove the stones ‒ Piel, BDB 709, KB 768
  7. lift up a standard ‒ Hiphil, BDB 926, KB 1202
  8. say ‒ Qal, BDB 55, KB 65

entries.title: Isaiah 62:11 "to the end of the earth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:11 "to the end of the earth" It is this universal aspect of YHWH's promises that signal that His love and salvation are for all humans, not just Israel. Please look at the important Special Topic below!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "Say. . ." There are three truths to be spoken (Qal IMPERATIVES) by the prophet about YHWH's coming (cf. Isa. 40:3) in blessing.

  1. your salvation comes (cf. Isa. 49:6)
  2. His reward is with Him
  3. His recompense before Him (cf. Isa. 40:10)

entries.title: Isaiah 62:12 "they will call them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
62:12 "they will call them" This is an allusion to "the new name" of Isa. 62:2. The non-Israelites will now call them, not "Forsaken" or "Desolate" (Isa. 62:4), but

  1. the holy people
  2. the redeemed of the Lord
  3. sought out

▣ "The redeemed of the Lord" "Redeemed" (BDB 145 I) is related to the concept of Go'el. This was the kinsman redeemer who bought back his relative from poverty or capture. YHWH as a go'el is another example of Deity described in close intimate personal family terms.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

▣ "Sought out, a city not forsaken" This title was very significant because it states the truth that God was not running from the covenant people but running toward them!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Does Isaiah 62 refer only to the Exile or is it a typology referring to the reign of the Messiah?
  2. Define the OT terms "righteousness" and "salvation."
  3. Why does God have to be reminded in Isa. 62:6 of His promises?
  4. Does God have a special love for Israel that He does not have for other nations?

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 63:1 "Edom"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:1 "Edom" This neighboring nation is often a symbol for all pagan Gentile nations (cf. Isa. 34:5-15) that are judged by YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: EDOM AND ISRAEL

▣ "Bozrah" This was a major city in Edom, often its capital. It is mentioned often in the "Woe" oracles of judgment (cf. Isa. 34:6; 63:1; Jer. 49:13,22; Amos 1:12).

▣
NASB, NRSV, NJB, TEV, Peshitta  "marching"
NKJV  "tetravelingxt"
JPSOA  "pressing forward"
REB, JPSOA footnote  "striding along"
LXX    omit

In Isa. 51:14 the word (צעה, BDB 858, KB 1040, Qal PARTICIPLE) is understood as "stooping," but here that connotation does not fit. Some suggest an emendation to the root, צעד (BDB 1040, KB 1040), which means "marching" or "striding." The UBS Text Project, p. 157, gives "stooping" a B rating (some doubt), but it does not fit the parallelism.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 63:1-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:1-6 This is a dialogue or diatribe (question-answer) format between the prophet/Servant and YHWH.

  1. Prophet asks the first question, Isa. 63:1 ‒ YHWH is described as coming from Edom in majestic apparel, Isa. 63:1a-d,2
  2. YHWH speaks, Isa. 63:1e
    1. speak in righteousness
    2. mighty to save
  3. Prophet asks a second question, Isa. 63:2
  4. YHWH answers, Isa. 63:3-6
    1. trodden the wine trough alone (i.e. judgment)
    2. no one from the peoples with Him (cf. Isa. 63:5; 59:16)

entries.title: Isaiah 63:3 "the wine trough"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 63:3 "the wine trough" This imagery of judgment (i.e. red apparel) is also found in Lam. 1:15; Joel 3:13; Rev. 14:19,20; 19:15. This is YHWH/Messiah as the Divine Warrior (i.e. Isa. 42:13; 59:17; Exod. 15:3; Josh. 5:11-15; Ps.24:8; Jer. 20:11; Rev. 19:11-15).

entries.title: Isaiah 63:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:4 Notice how the day of vengeance (cf. Isa. 34:8; 35:4,8; 61:2) is a necessary precursor to the day (year) of redemption!

The Day of the Lord and the day of salvation are two sides of one coming! For the faithful God's coming is a great reunion of fellowship; for those who are unfaithful His coming is the final act of separation and rejection (cf. Matt. 25:31-46; Rev. 20:11-15)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Day of the Lord (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT

▣ "redemption" This (BDB 145 I) denotes YHWH acting as a Go'el (i.e. Kinsman Redeemer) who paid the price for national Israel/Judah's salvation/deliverance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINSMAN REDEEMER

entries.title: Isaiah 63:5 "So My own arm brought salvation to Me,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:5 "So My own arm brought salvation to Me,

  And My wrath upheld Me" This is related to lines 1-2. YHWH could depend on no human help in bringing salvation (cf. Isa. 59:16). He and He alone could do it (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36). This text may be the imagery the Apostle John used in Revelation 5, only one is worthy to open the book, only one, the crucified, risen Lamb of God/Messiah/Servant!

entries.title: Isaiah 63:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:6 YHWH's judgment is described by the use of three metaphors (i.e. YHWH as the Divine Warrior, cf. Isa. 59:17; see list at v. 3).

  1. "trod down" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 100, KB 115 (parallel to "tread," used three times in Isa. 63:2-3; note Isa. 51:23)
  2. "made them drunk" ‒ Piel IMPERFECT, BDB 1016, KB 1500 (judgment as drunkenness, cf. Isa. 51:22-23; Ps. 75:8; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WINE AND STRONG DRINK)
  3. "poured out their life blood on the earth" (lit. "brought down their juice to the earth"; see Isa. 49:26) ‒ Hiphil IMPERFECT, BDB 432, KB 434 (people lying dead on the ground)

entries.title: Isaiah 63:7 "the lovingkindness of the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:7 "the lovingkindness of the Lord" This is the special covenant NOUN (BDB 338) that denotes YHWH's covenant loyalty.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

▣ "According to all that the Lord has granted us" Notice how the NASB uses this word three times to describe YHWH.

  1. the great goodness (BDB 378)
  2. His compassion (BDB 933)
  3. abundance of His lovingkindness (hesed, BDB 338)

entries.title: Isaiah 63:8 "they are My people"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:8 "they are My people" This is covenant language (cf. Exod. 6:7; Isa. 3:15; 51:4).

▣ "Sons who will not deal falsely" This is the exact opposite of Isa. 1:2-3 (cf. Jer. 3:22). Repentance has occurred!

▣ "So He became their Savior" Notice the contrast between Isa. 63:5 and 8b. Although God's sovereignty is emphasized, still there is a place for Israel's faithfulness (i.e. Romans 9-11)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

63:9
NASB, NKJV, NRSV footnote  "In all their affliction He
  was afflicted"
NRSV, NJB, TEV  "In all their distress. It was
  no messenger or angel. . ."
REB, LXX  "in all their troubles,
  no envoy, no angel. . ."
JPSOA  "In all their troubles He
  was troubled"
Peshitta  "In all their troubles he
  did not afflict them"

In English this is a powerful statement of the unity between YHWH and His covenant people (cf. Isa. 57:15), but the MT is difficult to follow.

  1. This phrase may relate with the last line of Isa. 63:8.
  2. This phrase may relate to the second line of Isa. 63:9.

The MT has "not" (לא) but the Masoretic scholars suggest לו, "him" (Qere, JPSOA). The UBS Text Project, p. 158, gives the Qere a "C" rating, as to be original, but it does not make an understandable line of poetry.

The NASB marginal note says, "Another reading is, 'He was not an adversary'; while the JPSOA footnote says, 'Ancient versions read, "so He was their Deliverer."'"

▣ "the angel of His presence" This is a direct allusion to Exod. 23:20-23; 33:14,15. It refers to events during the Wilderness Wandering Period. Israel's sin caused YHWH to replace Himself with a personal representative (i.e. the angel of the Lord).

YHWH affirmed His personal presence (cf. Deut. 32:9-14).

  1. He redeemed them ‒ Qal PERFECT, BDB 145, KB 169
  2. He lifted them ‒ Piel IMPERFECT with waw, BDB 642, KB 694
  3. He carried them ‒ Piel IMPERFECT with waw, BDB 669, KB 724 (cf. Isa. 46:3; Deut. 1:31)

Also note the three NT Divine Persons in Isa. 63:9-10.

  1. the Father, Isa. 63:9a
  2. the pre-incarnate Messiah, Isa. 63:9b
  3. the Holy Spirit, Isa. 63:10b

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANGEL OF THE LORD

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

entries.title: Isaiah 63:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:10 Notice two VERBS describe Israel's sin and two VERBS describe YHWH's reaction (synonymous parallelism).

  1. rebelled ‒ Qal PERFECT, BDB 598, KB 632
  2. grieved His Holy Spirit ‒ Piel PERFECT with waw, BDB 780, KB 864 (cf. Acts 7:51; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT; for a good article entitled "Who Is the OT Holy Spirit?" see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 273-274, also pp. 306-307)
  3. He turned Himself to become their enemy ‒ Niphal PERFECT with waw, BDB 245, KB 253, cf. Lam. 2:4-5
  4. He fought against them ‒ Niphal PERFECT, BDB 535, KB 526

entries.title: Isaiah 63:11-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:11-14 This lists the things that YHWH did for Israel during the Exodus.

  1. brought them up out of the sea using Moses (cf. Exodus 14-15; play on Moses' name)
  2. put His Holy Spirit in the midst of them (cf. Num. 11:17,25,29; Haggai 2:5; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT)
  3. caused His glorious arm to go at the right hand of Moses (cf. Exod. 6:6; 15:16)
  4. divided the waters before them (SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS)
    1. Red Sea ‒ Exodus 14-15 (Isa. 11:15; 51:10; see SPECIAL TOPIC: RED SEA)
    2. Jordan River ‒ Joshua 3
  5. led them through the depths (same as #4; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS/SEA)
  6. gave them rest (i.e. the Spirit, cf. Josh. 21:44; 23:1; JPSOA footnote suggests an emendation to "guided them," but, the UBS Text Project, p. 160, gives "rest" a "B" rating)
  7. shepherded Your people

YHWH did all of this for Israel "to make Yourself a glorious name." YHWH wanted to reveal Himself to all humanity through Israel. His acts toward them were for the greater good (i.e. eternal redemptive plan).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 63:15 "Look. . .see"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:15 "Look. . .see" These are two IMPERATIVES seeking YHWH's attention.

  1. look ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE, BDB 613, KB 661, cf. Deut. 26:15
  2. see ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 906, KB 1157, cf. Ps. 80:14

▣ "from heaven" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

▣ "Your holy and glorious habitation" This is a way of speaking about the temple. For the ancient Israelites, the Ark of the Covenant was a footstool for YHWH, who dwelt in heaven (cf. 1 Chr. 28:2; Ps. 99:5; 132:7; Isa. 66:1; Lam. 2:1; Matt. 5:35; Acts 7:49).

A new book by John Walton, The Lost World of Genesis One: An Ancient Cosmology, asserts that Gen. 1:1-2:3 is YHWH organizing and building His temple (i.e. a functioning planet prepared for mankind).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "The stirrings of Your heart and Your compassion are restrained toward me" This powerful poetry is personifying Jerusalem pleading for YHWH to again recognize and return to her.

  1. where is Your zeal (BDB 888)
  2. where are Your mighty deeds (BDB 150)
  3. where are the stirrings (lit. "yearnings," BDB 242) of Your heart
  4. where is Your compassion (BDB 933)

entries.title: Isaiah 63:16 "You are our Father"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:16 "You are our Father" This is the logical conclusion from Israel being called "sons" (i.e. Isa. 1:2). The phrase is repeated in Isa. 64:8.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD

▣ ". . .though Abraham does not know us

  And Israel does not recognize us"

The Patriarchs would not know/recognize these Judeans because of

  1. the time between their generations
  2. the sin of these descendants

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "Redeemer" See note at Isa. 41:14.

For the concept of "redeem" see SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM.

entries.title: Isaiah 63:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:17 The first two lines of this verse show how the concept of the sovereignty of God can be used to diminish personal responsibility (i.e. Adam and Eve in Gen. 3:8-13).

  1. You cause us to stray
  2. You hardened our hearts

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALVINISM versus ARMINIANISM (human free will)

▣ "return for the sake of Your servants" This is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 996, KB 1427) used as a prayer.

entries.title: Isaiah 63:18-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
63:18-19 These verses show how the Judeans perceived themselves.

  1. they had the temple for only a short time
  2. their enemies had taken control of it
  3. they had become like "just another nation"
  4. they had become like the nations who were never called by YHWH's name

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Isaiah 64:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
64:1 The first two lines are labeled as Isa. 63:19 in the MT. There is a series of PERFECT VERBS from Isa. 64:18 through Isa. 64:19.

YHWH, who lives on high, "rends" (Qal PERFECT, BDB 902, KB 1146, cf. Isa. 34:4; Rev. 6:14) the atmosphere of the earth (i.e. heavens, cf. Gen. 1:1).

As the creator approaches the creation quakes (Niphal PERFECT, BDB 272, KB 272 [this form occurs only here and Jdg. 5:5, which is Deborah's praise/psalm of the defeat of Hazor and its army], cf. Isa. 64:2; Ps. 18:7-15; 68:8; 77:18; 144:5)

For "heavens" see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 64:2 "fire"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
64:2 "fire" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

▣ Notice the purpose of YHWH is that His name be known and that the nations tremble (hopefully in repentance, cf. Ps. 99:1-5; Jer. 33:9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

64:3
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, REB  "awesome things"
TEV  "terrible things"
NJB  "unexpected miracles"
JPSOA  "wonders"
LXX  "glorious deeds"
Peshitta  "wonderous things"

The Hebrew word (BDB 431, KB 432, Niphal PARTICIPLE) literally means "fear," but in this form it can denote the majestic, awesome miracles of YHWH on behalf of Israel (cf. Deut. 10:21; 2 Sam. 7:23; 1 Chr. 17:21; Ps. 66:3,5-6; 106:22; 145:6).

In Ps. 139:14 several Hebrew words are used in parallel.

  1. BDB 431 ‒ fearful
  2. BDB 811 and 810 ‒ wonderful

SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS

entries.title: Isaiah 64:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
64:4 The interpretive question is to whom does the PRONOUN "they" refer.

  1. national Israel/Judah
  2. the faithful returnees (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses))
  3. the nations (cf. Isa. 64:2)
  4. #2 and #3 together

entries.title: Isaiah 64:4 "ear. . .eye"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
64:4 "ear. . .eye" The covenant people's rebellion was predicted by YHWH in Isa. 6:9-10. Paul seems to build on this in 1 Cor. 2:9, but uses it in a positive sense.

▣ "a God besides you" See SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM.

▣ "Who acts. . ." The word is "works" (Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 793, KB 889). This is the theological distinction between YHWH and the idols.

  1. They cannot see, hear, act, speak, but He can and does!
  2. He does not have a consort or a pantheon.
  3. He cannot be bribed.

▣ "the one who waits for Him" This describes the person of faith. He/she waits (Piel PARTICIPLE, BDB 314, KB 313). This word has the connotation of "hoping, trusting, waiting" for God (cf. Isa. 8:17; 30:18; Hab. 2:3).

Another root (BDB 875 I) is also translated "wait," but often not as theologically significant (cf Isa. 25:9; 26:8; 33:2; 40:31; Ps. 25:3; 27:14; 37:34; 40:1; 130:5; Prov. 20:22).

entries.title: Isaiah 64:5 "You meet him who. . ."
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
64:5 "You meet him who. . ." The VERB (Qal PERFECT, BDB 803, KB 910) in this context denotes an encounter of/for fellowship and/or kindness.

Notice the kind of people YHWH "meets" with.

  1. him who rejoices in doing righteous
  2. him who remembers You in Your ways
▣
NASB  "We continued in them a long time
  And shall we be saved?"
NKJV  "In these ways we continue
  And we need to be saved"
NRSV  "Because you hid yourself we transgressed"
NJB  "now we persist in your ways and we shall be saved"
JPSOA  "We have been steeped in them from of old
  And can we be saved?"
LXX  "therefore we went away"

The MT is uncertain. AB suggests an emendation involving two consonants which yields, "we have long been rebels" (p. 190).

▣ Lines 3-5 ask a pertinent question. Israel/Judah are covenant-breaking people. Can a sinful people be "saved" (i.e. "delivered," BDB 446, KB 448)

  1. from the physical consequences of sin
  2. from the spiritual consequences of sin

I want to believe, "Yes, yes, yes" (cf. Isa. 64:8-9)! But only divine mercy and grace (this chapter is a prayer for YHWH's intervention) can do it (recommended translation of UBS Text Project, p. 164). The consequences of Genesis 3 are staggering and relentless.

However, in this context (i.e. Isa. 64:4-7) this verse is not redemptive but condemnatory (Isa. 64:8-12 are a cry for mercy). Israel sinned in the past and the present. If this is to be accepted as the meaning then the VERB "delivered" (ישׁע, BDB 446, KB 448, Niphal IMPERFECT) must be changed to "and we were evil" (רשׁע, BDB 957; LXX, NRSV, TEV).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

entries.title: Isaiah 64:6-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
64:6-7 Notice the consequences of sin.

  1. all of us ‒ scope of the problem (cf. Rom. 3:9-18,23; 11:32; Gal. 3:22)
  2. unclean (BDB 379)
  3. our righteousness is a polluted garment (cloth of menstruation, BDB 723, cf. Lev. 15:19-24)
  4. wither (BDB 615, KB 663, Qal IMPERFECT with waw, cf. Isa. 1:30; 34:4) like a leaf
  5. the wind takes us away
  6. none call on the name of the Lord (i.e. worship; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)

YHWH reacts to this tragedy of a sinful covenant people, meant to promote and clarify His own character.

  1. He hid His face (cf. Isa. 1:15; 54:8; Deut. 31:18)
  2. He delivered us (MT, מוג, "melted," BDB 556, KB 555, an emendation to the root מגו, "hand over," [BDB 171, KB 545 I], fits better) into the power (i.e. consequences) of our iniquities (this is theologically parallel to Rom. 1:24,26,28!)

These verses serve as a petition of confession. There is no reason why YHWH should forgive/forget, but He does (cf. Ps. 103:11-12; Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; 55:6-7; Micah 7:19)! The new covenant is in view here (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36). YHWH will deal with them (i.e. Israel) and with all humans in a new way based on His character, His acts, His purposes, and through His Son's actions and Spirit's drawing!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

entries.title: Isaiah 64:8-12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
64:8-12 This is a prayer of hope for YHWH to remember His covenant and not His children's sin.

  1. You are our Father (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD)
  2. You are the potter
  3. we are the work of Your hand (cf. Isa. 29:16; 45:9)

entries.title: Isaiah 64:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
64:9 There is a series of commands in the sense of prayer requests.

  1. do not be angry beyond measure ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 893, KB 1124) used in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Isa. 54:7-8
  2. do not remember iniquity forever ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 269, KB 269) used in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Isa. 43:25
  3. look, all of us are Your people ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE (BDB 613, KB 661)

All of these are similar to Isa. 57:16-17; Ps. 103:8-14.

entries.title: Isaiah 64:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
64:10-11 All of the VERBS are PERFECTS ("become" used four times). They describe the complete destruction of YHWH's wrath.

  1. the cities of Palestine are a wilderness
  2. Jerusalem is desolate
  3. the temple burnt with fire (i.e. Babylon in 586 B.C. and Titus in A.D. 70)
  4. all Israel's precious things are in ruin

entries.title: Isaiah 64:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
64:12 God's people cry out for restraint and compassion. Please, please, no more, they cry. Please come to us again!

ISAIAH 65
