READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. These last two chapters are contained in a literary unit which runs from Isaiah 56 to Isaiah 66. It could be characterized as "A New Day" or "The New Age." See my new (2024) exegetical, verse-by-verse commentary on Revelation 21-22, free online.

  2. OT prophets used contemporary occurrences to foreshadow future events. The return of the exiles seems to be the foreshadowing of the spiritual return of all of God's human creation to an original Adamic fellowship of Eden
    SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN
    SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

  3. Isaiah. 65 is possibly a response to Isaiah's corporate prayer for help and mercy which is recorded in Isa. 63:7-64:12. God's basic answer is that He has always been ready (cf. Isa. 55:6-7), but His people have always turned away from Him (Isa. 65:5).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT
    SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

  4. It is quite interesting that Paul uses Isa. 65:1-2 in Rom. 10:20-21. Paul interprets Isa. 65:1 as referring to the Gentiles and Isa. 65:2 as referring to the Jews. In context they both seem to be related to the returning Judeans of Ezra's and Nehemiah's day. However, Isa. 65:1d, which contains the phrase, "to a nation which did not call on My name," could refer to the Jewish nation unless it is used in some kind of idolatrous, sarcastic, ironical way.

  5. Isaiah 65 is also unique in prophecy because it takes the concept of corporality into the area of individual response. The two groups can be clearly seen in Isa. 65:10c and 11a. God will make a distinction within the nation between those who know Him and those who reject Him (cf. Ezek. 18:1-21; 33:10-20; and Jer. 31:29-30.

  6. Isaiah 65 culminates Isaiah's unique emphasis on the universal love of God and its inclusion of the Gentiles (i.e. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:7; 60:1,3; 66:23). He goes so far as to say that God will even make some Gentiles priests and Levites (cf. Isa. 61:6; 66:21). This is very significant in light of the obvious conclusions of Jewish monotheism and the call of Abraham in Gen. 12:1-3, which also included all of the world (i.e. Exod. 19:5-6).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM
    SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

  7. It is surprising that this New Age is described without any allusions to the Messiah of Isaiah 9 and 11.

  8. For a good brief discussion of ANE views of the afterlife, see John H. Walton, ANE Thought and the OT, pp. 314-329.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 65:2 "I permitted Myself to be sought. . .to be found"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:2 "I permitted Myself to be sought. . .to be found" God always takes the initiative in spiritual matters (i.e. John 6:44,65). Humans are only responders in the spiritual realm, not initiators! Even in this context He is allowing Himself to be found, revealing Himself to the children of Abraham and to the other children of Adam (cf. Isa. 55:6-7; John 10:16; see SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord). These opening verses remind me of Romans 11.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

▣ "Here am I, here am I" The doubling is for emphasis! These are words of a Hebrew idiom of availability (i.e. Isa. 6:8; 52:6). God was always available but His people would not respond ("ask," "seek").

▣ "To a nation which did not call on My name" In context this refers either to

  1. the covenant people who called upon idols, particularly the fertility gods
  2. the Gentiles (cf. Rom. 10:20-21)

The concept of calling upon someone's name is the idea of responding to them in a worship setting. Paul uses this same concept of calling upon the name of the Lord in Rom. 10:9-13 (cf. Acts 7:59; 9:14,21; 22:16; 1 Cor. 1:2; 2 Tim. 2:22; see SPECIAL TOPIC: The Name of the Lord [NT]). This was considered an act of trust and worship.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

entries.title: Isaiah 65:2 "I spread out My hands all day long to a rebellious people"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:2 "I spread out My hands all day long to a rebellious people" This is anthropomorphic imagery which shows the intensity and openness of God's love (cf. Rom. 10:21). Usually it is a gesture of prayer but here of welcome.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

▣ "Who walk in the way which is not good, following their own thoughts" The following verses list several aspects of idolatry which characterize the covenant people. It is very difficult in this period of history to completely understand each one of these aspects in detail (cf. Isa. 65:3-7). Some say that they are all caught up in the garden worship mentioned in Isa. 65:3, while others differentiate between the groups. What is obvious is that God's people had turned to other gods. Some possible enumerations of these idolatrous traits are

  1. offering sacrifice in gardens
  2. burning incense on bricks
  3. sitting among graves
  4. spending nights in secret places
  5. eating swine's flesh
  6. having the broth of unclean meat in their pots
  7. burning incense on mountains
  8. scorning Me on the hills
  9. setting a table for "Fortune," Isa. 65:11
  10. filling cups of mixed wine for "Destiny"

entries.title: Isaiah 65:3 "A people who continually provoke Me to My face"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:3 "A people who continually provoke Me to My face" This is Hebrew imagery of repeated, open defiance to God. Sin is primarily against God (cf. 2 Sam. 12:13; Ps. 41:4; 51:4; also note Gen. 20:6; 39:9). Idolatry had become so common and accepted that it was not even hidden.

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

▣ "Offering sacrifice in gardens" We are not sure if this is

  1. the ancient veneration of trees that can be seen in Isa. 1:29; Hosea 4:13 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES)
  2. a particularized worship within a garden setting (cf. Isa. 66:17)

▣ "burning incense on bricks" It has been suggested that the term "bricks" can simply refer to

  1. an altar made with cut stones (cf. Lev. 20:24-25)
  2. the pillars of Ba'al worship (cf. Lev. 26:1)
  3. the roof tiles which relate to the worship of Babylonian astral deities
  4. incense altars (see IVP Bible Background Commentary: OT, p. 640)

These numerous possibilities show us that we simply do not know what this really means.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:4 "Who sit among graves"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:4 "Who sit among graves" This seems to be some kind of worship or communication with the dead, possibly necromancy or ancestral worship (cf. Lev. 19:31; 20:6,27; Deut. 18:10-12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

▣
NASB, NRSV  "spend the night in secret places"
NKJV  "spend the night in the tombs"
TEV  "at night they go to caves and tombs"
REB  "keeping vigil all night long"
NJB  "spending the night in dark corners"
Peshitta  "who sit in tombs and lodge in caves"
LXX  "and in the caves for the sake of dreams"
JPSOA  "and pass the night in secret places"

The MT has the VERBAL "watch," "guard," or "keep" (BDB 665 I, #4, KB 718, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE). It can denote

  1. a city besieged ‒ Isa. 1:8
  2. YHWH is Israel's keeper ‒ Isa. 27:3
  3. YHWH keeps Israel ‒ Isa. 42:6
  4. YHWH declares hidden things ‒ Isa. 48:6
  5. YHWH preserves Israel ‒ Isa. 49:6
  6. YHWH will keep Israel ‒ Isa. 49:8

The best parallel seems to be #4. If so, then REB is the best understanding of the VERBAL.

We really do not have any idea what this has reference to but it seems to involve the cultic arts in some way.

  1. necromancy
  2. ancestor worship

▣ "Who eat swine's flesh,

  And the broth of unclean meat is in their pots" Usually these two acts are connected by commentators although this is uncertain. They are a violation of the food laws of Leviticus 11 (cf. Isa. 11:7). Pigs were common sacrifices of the surrounding nations (i.e. Ugaritic Texts).

The MT has "fragment," פרק, BDB 830, but BDB suggests (Qere) מרק, BDB 600 II, "a rich broth," along with DSS, LXX, and Aramaic Targum.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOD LAWS

entries.title: Isaiah 65:5 "Who say, 'Keep to yourself, do not come near me,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:5 "Who say, 'Keep to yourself, do not come near me,

  For I am holier than you!'" The first two VERBS are commands.

  1. keep to yourself ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 897, KB 1132
  2. do not come near me ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 620, KB 670 used in a JUSSIVE sense

Notice that these commands are from the idolaters (cf. Isa. 65:2-4,7,11-12), possibly their "priests." They were concerned about

  1. a transfer of "holiness" (cf. Ezek. 44:19, i.e. somehow a reduction of their power or prestige)
  2. a transfer with possible negative effect to common pagan worshipers
▣
NASB, NKJV, NET  "I am holier than you"
NRSV  "I am too holy for you"
TEV  "we are too holy for you to touch"
NJB  "lest my sanctity come near you"
JPSOA  "I would render you consecrated"
REB  "my holiness will infect you"
Peshitta  "I am sanctified"
LXX  "I am clean"

The UBS Text Project, p. 166, gives a different vocalization, "I have sanctified you," (BDB 872, KB 1073, Qal PERFECT but notes the MT's, "I am sacred for you" has a "B" rating (some doubt).

▣ "These are smoke in My nostrils,

 A fire that burns all the day" This idiom shows God's irritation and anger at this type of attitude and idolatrous activity.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

entries.title: Isaiah 65:6 "Behold, it is written before Me,
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:6 "Behold, it is written before Me,

 I will not keep silent, but I will repay" The idea of something "written" is ancient imagery which refers to the memory of God (cf. The Book of Deeds and the Book of Life, Dan. 7:10; Rev. 20:12-15). The truth is that judgment will come one day. This is a word that all humans need to hear. Notice what YHWH will do.

  1. I will not keep silent
  2. I will repay
  3. I will repay into their bosom

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD

▣ "I will repay into their bosom" The imagery of "bosom" means "I will return to them their own sin" (cf. Job 34:11; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:19; Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12).

entries.title: Isaiah 65:7 "Both their own iniquities and the iniquities of their fathers together"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:7 "Both their own iniquities and the iniquities of their fathers together" This is a combination of corporate sin and individual, volitional sin. We are affected not only by the past corporately, and the present corporately, but also by individual choice in the present. We learn from the Ten Commandments in Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9, that we are affected by the sins of the parents to the third and fourth generation. We also learn from Ezekiel 18 the opposite truth that we are responsible only for our sins.

▣ "Because they have burned incense on the mountains

 And scorned Me on the hills" This, according to the prophet Hosea, is an aspect of the worship of the fertility god Ba'al (cf Hosea 4:13-14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

▣
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "their former work"
NRSV, REB  "full payment"
TEV  "their past deeds"
NJB, JPSOA  "in full"
LXX  "I will recompense their works
  into their bosom"

The NASB follows the MT text. The NRSV, NJB, and JPSOA suggest an emendation, ראשנה (BDB 911) meaning "former," to ראשׁובה (PREPOSITION plus KB 1165, #5) meaning "in full" (Lev. 6:5) or "first" (Jer. 16:18). This, then, denotes YHWH's full measure of judgment to these Judean idolators.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:8 "As the new wine is found in the cluster"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:8 "As the new wine is found in the cluster" This is imagery that even in a cluster of good grapes there are always some bad grapes. This is the beginning of a discussion that runs from Isa. 65:8 to Isa. 65:10 which states that a remnant of the covenant people will be faithful to YHWH. However, Isa. 65:11-13 shows the complete rejection and judgment of those of Judah who continue to reject YHWH by covenant disobedience and idolatry. This is the beginning of the painful but true emphasis that judgment will begin with the house of God (cf. 1 Pet. 4:17). There is a form of OT religion in which God takes no pleasure. God looks at the heart (cf. Isa. 29:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOL ABUSE

entries.title: Isaiah 65:10-11 "For My people who seek Me.
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:10-11 "For My people who seek Me.

 But you who forsake the Lord" This verse highlights the individual aspect of the covenant of Moses. YHWH had always dealt in a corporate aspect with the nation. The entire nation was blessed or the entire nation was cursed (i.e. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28-29). Now we are coming to the individualized focus of Ezek. 18:32; 30:10-19; and Jer. 31:29-30, where there is a distinction within the people of God as to those who believe and those who do not believe (cf. Deut. 29:24-28). Later in Isaiah 66 there will be a distinction between all mankind, of those who reject and those who receive YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord

entries.title: Isaiah 65:11 "you who forsake the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:11 "you who forsake the Lord" The VERB (Qal PARTICIPLE, BDB 736 I, KB 806) means "to abandon" or "to leave." It is regularly used of forsaking YHWH (cf. Deut. 28:20; 31:16; Jdg. 10:10; Jer. 1:16; Jonah 2:8). They abandoned YHWH for idols (cf. 2 Kgs. 9-22; 2 Chr. 36:13-21). He will forsake them (cf. Deut. 31:17; Isa. 41:17; 49:14; 54:7).

▣ "Who set a table for Fortune,

  And who fill cups with mixed wine for Destiny" The use of "table" and the implied "cups" are sacrificial imagery of the ANE theology of the necessity of feeding the gods. This imagery is never used in Israeli understanding of the physical needs of YHWH. Sacrifices were not viewed as food (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SOOTHING AROMA).
SPECIAL TOPIC: SACIFICES IN MESOPOTAMIA AND ISRAEL AND THEIR SIGNIFICANCE

The term "Fortune" (BDB 151 II, KB 176 II) and the Hebrew "Destiny" (BDB 584, KB 602) are names for Syrian gods (cf. Isa. 62:4), possibly relating to the worship of planetary deities (cf. Jer. 7:18; 44:17), which was the worship of "the queen of heaven." It is certain that these terms refer to idolatrous worship of some type!

65:12
NASB, REB, JPSOA  "I will destine you for the sword"
NKJV  "I will number you for the sword"
NRSV, NJB, Peshitta  "I will destine you to the sword"
TEV  "It will be your Fate"
LXX  "I will deliver you over to the dagger"

Notice the play on the VERB (Qal PERFECT with waw, BDB 584, KB 599), which is used as a title for a false god in Isa. 65:11, "Destiny" (meni, BDB 584).

▣ "Because I called, but you did not answer" This is a summary of Isa. 65:1-7. YHWH continually loved them and called them but they refused and rejected His call and His message (cf. Isa. 41:28; 50:2; 66:4; Hosea 11:2).

The last lines of Isa. 65:12 are repeated in Isa. 66:4.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:13 "the Lord God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:13 "the Lord God" This title is a combination of Adon and "YHWH."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (Adon and Kurios)

entries.title: Isaiah 65:13-16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 65:13-16 This is the continuing emphasis on the contrast between the two types of seed (i.e. descendants) of Abraham-believing and unbelieving. In the NT this turns to all humans (cf. Rom. 2:28-29; Eph. 2:11-3:13).

entries.title: Isaiah 65:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:14 Notice the contrast between

  1. the faithful ‒ shout with a glad heart
  2. the unfaithful ‒ cry out with a heavy, painful heart

There is a division among humans, even those who seem "religious" (cf. Matt. 7:13-14,15-23,24-27; Luke 13:22-30; 2 Tim. 3:5; 1 John 2:18-19; Jude)!

entries.title: Isaiah 65:15 "You will leave your name for a curse to My chosen ones"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:15 "You will leave your name for a curse to My chosen ones" This is another play on the word "name" (BDB 1027). Here it is the concept that the name of the unbelievers will become accursed, while the believers will have a new name. From the immediate context we do not know the new name by which they will be called. New names for God are given in Isa. 65:16.

  1. "the God of Amen"
  2. "the God of Truth"
  3. "the God of faithfulness" (cf. Rev. 3:14)

The believer's new name will possibly be related to that (cf. Isa. 56:5; 62:2; Rev. 2:17).

In Genesis YHWH's promise to Abraham carried a warning and a blessing related to the treatment of Abraham using "name" to represent him as a person (cf. Gen. 12:2; 18:18; 22:18).

65:16
NASB  "he who is blessed. . .will be blessed"
NKJV  "he who blesses himself. . .shall bless himself"
NRSV  "whoever invokes a blessing. . .shall bless"
TEV  "whoever. . .who asks for a blessing. . .will ask
  to be blessed"
REB  "anyone. . .invoking a blesing on himself"
NJB  "whoever blesses himself. . .will bless himself"
LXX  "which shall be blessed. . .they shall bless"
Peshitta  "he who blesses himself. . .shall bless himself"

The VERB "bless" (BDB 138, KB 159) is an important theological concept, especially in Gen. 12:3, but it is used in two senses (based on the Hebrew stem).

  1. Piel, "be blessed" ‒ Gen. 12:3; 18:18; 28:14
  2. Hithpael, "bless oneself" ‒ Gen. 22:18; 28:14

The issue: is the initiation by God or by the individual? The text in Genesis seems to be theologically synonymous. Together they document Divine and human activity.

▣  "Because the former troubles are forgotten,

And because they are hidden from My sight" In the Bible "when God forgets" it is imagery for total forgiveness. Notice the continuing imagery that sins are hidden from His sight. This is a repeated theme of the OT. When God forgives, God forgets (cf. Ps. 103:11-13; Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; and Micah 7:19)!

▣
NASB, NKJV, NJB, Peshitta  "the God of truth"
NRSV  "the God of faithfulness"
TEV  "the faithful God"
LXX. JPSOA  "the true God"
REB  "by God whose name is Amen"

The title for Deity, "God," אלה (Eloah, BDB 43), is often used in ancient biblical poems (cf. Deut. 32:15,17; Job 3:4; Ps. 18:32; 50:22; 114:7; 139:19; Prov. 30:5; Isa. 44:8; Hab. 3:3).

The second part of the title "truth" is literally "Amen" (cf. 2 Cor. 1:20; Rev. 3:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN

entries.title: Isaiah 65:17 "For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:17 "For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth" The context of Isa. 65:17-25 is extremely important because it is the key, not only of these last two chapters, but of God making all things new (cf. Isa. 42:9; 48:6; 66:22; 2 Pet. 3:13; Rev. 21-22). It is a discussion of the New Age or the Age of the Messiah (cf. Rom. 8:18-25). It also implies that the current order will be destroyed (cf. Isa. 51:6 and 2 Pet. 3:10). There is also a relation between Isa. 65:16 and 17 that the New Order will not contain sins because they will be forgiven, as is mentioned in the latter part of Isa. 65:16.

The terminology of "a new heaven and a new earth" is common in Jewish Apocalyptic Literature (cf. II Esdras 6:11-24; I Enoch 91:16). This becomes the imagery for Revelation 21-22! The earth will return to its pre-Genesis 3 glory and purpose. See full note at Isa. 62:2 and my new Partial Preterist commentary on the book of Revelation, online.

For a good discussion on the biblical material about earthly Jerusalem and heavenly Jerusalem, see Dale Moody, The Word of Truth, pp. 569-588.

SPECIAL TOPIC: OLD THINGS. . .NEW THINGS

▣ "earth" This is the word erets (BDB 75, KB 90), which can refer to a region, a field, a country, or the planet. Only context can determine which one. It is obvious in the phrase, "new heaven and new earth," that it denotes the whole planet.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH

SPECIAL TOPIC: WORLD (several terms)

entries.title: Isaiah 65:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:18 The first line of poetry has two parallel IMPERATIVES.

  1. be glad ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 965, KB 1314, cf. Isa. 61:10 (twice); 62:5; 64:5; 65:18,19; 66:10,14
  2. rejoice ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 162, KB 189, cf. Isa. 61:10; 65:18,19; 66:10

AB, p. 198, sees these as new titles for Jerusalem and the faithful returnees.

▣ "forever" This term (BDB 723 I) denotes perpetual fellowship with the Creator and His human vessels (cf. 1 Chr. 28:9; Micah 7:18). There is a Hebrew sound play between the PREPOSITION (BDB 723 III) and the NOUN "forever" (BDB 723 I), which denotes perpetuity.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:19 "And there will no longer be heard in her
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:19 "And there will no longer be heard in her

The voice of weeping and the sound of crying" This is the continual theme of Isaiah that the New Age will not have the pain of this former sin-cursed earth (cf. Isa. 25:8; 30:19; 35:10; 51:11). This seems to be alluded to in Rev. 7:17 and 21:4.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:20 "No longer will there be in it an infant who lives but
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:20 "No longer will there be in it an infant who lives but

  a few days,

 Or an old man who does not live out his days" This hyperbolic statement can have one of two origins.

  1. an allusion to the long lives of Genesis 1-5, thereby denoting a return to the Garden of Eden period
  2. an OT way of describing the "New Age," which we know from the NT involves not just protracted physical life (i.e. the OT view of an afterlife), but a new eternal life (zoa)

For a good discussion of Isaiah's discussion of extended lives and the NT discussion of eternal life, see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 307-309.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:22 This is imagery to describe the fact that the people will live in the land and enjoy its fruits. It is a direct allusion to the exile and the promise of a return to Palestine.

▣
NASB  "wear out"
NKJV, NRSV  "long enjoy"
TEV  "fully enjoy"
NJB  "use"
REB  "enjoy"
JPSOA  "outlive"
LXX  "make old"
Peshitta  "eat"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 115, KB 132, Piel IMPERFECT) which means "to wear out," but in the Piel stem it denotes "wear out by use" or "to the full." God's people will fully enjoy His blessing and protection (i.e. 2 Sam. 7:10; 1 Chr. 17:9).

▣ The Septuagint sees the word "tree" (BDB 781) as referring to the "tree of life" in the Garden of Eden, as do the Aramaic Targums.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARAMAIC TARGUMS

entries.title: Isaiah 65:24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 65:24 This is a beautiful promise of instantaneous answered prayer and is even more extensive than Matt. 6:8. Earlier, the Israelites wondered if YHWH heard their prayers and would forgive them and restore them to Palestine.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:25 "The wolf and the lamb will graze together"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
65:25 "The wolf and the lamb will graze together" Here again is the idyllic picture of God and mankind together in a garden setting with the animals (cf. Isa. 11:6-9; Genesis 1,2; Rev. 21:22). This goes along with my particular theology that we are not going to heaven, but heaven is coming back to a recreated and cleansed earth (i.e. Revelation 21-22, a restored Garden of Eden). It will be as it was!

▣ "and dust will be the serpent's food" This is a rather unusual idiom because dust was commonly understood as the food of serpents in that day. However, it may be a reference to

  1. Gen. 3:14, which shows that Satan's temptations will be completely finished as far as their effect on believing and renewed mankind
  2. Isa. 11:8, a strophe that also describes the new age

entries.title: Isaiah 66:1 "Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool.
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:1 "Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool.

 Where then is a house you could build for Me?

 And where is a place that I may rest?"

This is an obvious allusion to the dedicatory prayer of Solomon in 1 Kgs. 8:27 and is again alluded to in Acts 7:47-50.

What is difficult to know is to what historical period this relates. Some see it relating to the return from the exile and the rebuilding of the temple, which is possible from the larger context. However, others say that God does not live in manmade buildings and that this refers to

  1. the temple of the human body which God has made
  2. the family of God, the faith seed of Abraham (Jews and Gentiles of faith, cf. Rom. 2:28-29)
  3. the cosmic temple of Genesis 1 where Elohim may "rest" (cf. Gen. 2:2), see John H. Walton, The Lost World of Genesis One: An Ancient Cosmology

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

▣ "My footstool" (BDB 919) This imagery has three orientations.

  1. earth is YHWH's footstool (i.e. He is the Creator and King, cf. Isa. 66:1)
  2. the Ark of the Covenant is YHWH's footstool (the temple is where His presence resides, cf. 1 Chr. 28:2; Ps. 99:5; 132:7; Lam. 2:1)
    SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT
  3. YHWH's enemies and the enemies of His people will be His footstool (i.e. imagery of victory, cf. Ps. 110:1; Matt. 22:44; Mark 12:36; Luke 20:43; Acts 2:35; Heb. 1:13; 10:13

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Isaiah 66:2 "For My hand made all these things"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:2 "For My hand made all these things" We learn from the NT that God's agent in creation was no one other than the pre-Incarnate Jesus Christ (cf. John 1:3; 1 Cor. 8:6; Col. 1:16; Heb. 1:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣
NASB, JPSOA  "came into being"
NKJV  "exist"
NRSV, LXX  "are mine"
REB, Peshitta  "belong to me"

The MT has the "to be" VERB (BDB 224, KB 243, Qal PERFECT with waw). The UBS Text Project, p. 168, gives this a "B" rating (some doubt).

The ancient versions understood it as affirming YHWH's ownership because He was their creator.

▣  "But to this one I will look,

To him who is humble and contrite of spirit,

and who trembles at My word"

God looks first at the motives and character of the human heart. YHWH knows the thoughts and intents of the heart (cf. 1 Sam. 2:3; 16:7; 1 Kgs. 8:39; 1 Chr. 28:9; 2 Chr. 6:30; Ps. 7:9; 17:3; 26:2; 44:21; 139:1,23; Prov. 15:11; 16:2; 21:2; 24:12; Jer. 11:20; 17:9-10; 20:12; Luke 16:15; Acts 1:24; 15:8; Rom. 8:27). Jesus also knows the inner thoughts and motives of humans, see John 2:24-25; 6:61,64; 13:11!

This same description is used of David's contrition over the sin with Bathsheba (cf. Ps. 51:17); note Isa. 57:15; Ps. 34:18; Matt. 5:3-4; Luke 18:13-14.

This also has two descriptions of God's true people that are very beautiful and descriptive.

  1. a humble people (BDB 776)
  2. contrite people (BDB 646, cf. Isa. 57:15)
  3. those who tremble at His word (BDB 353, cf. Isa. 66:5)

▣ "of spirit" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE.

entries.title: Isaiah 66:3 "And their soul delights in their abominations"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:3 "And their soul delights in their abominations" This refers to various pagan worship rites (cf. Isa. 65:4,7,11; see SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC and SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY). They loved and chose (BDB 103, KB 119, used three times in Isa. 66:3-4) sin (cf. Isa. 1:4; 57:17; 65:2; 66:18; Ps. 81:11-12)!

For "soul" see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

For "abominations" see SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

66:4
NASB  "punishments"
NKJV  "delusions"
NRSV, JPSOA  "mock"
TEV  "disaster"
NJB  "making fools of them"
REB  "a willful course"
Peshitta  "humiliated"

The word (BDB 760, KB 1768) is found only here and Isa. 3:4.

  1. BDB suggests "wanton dealings"
  2. KB suggests
    1. acts of mischief (done by a child from the root, עולל (BDB 760) for Isa. 3:4
    2. ill treatment, here
  3. The NET Bible, p. 2286, #6, gets a meaning from עלל (BDB 760), "deal severely."

▣ "And will bring on them what they dread" Oh my! What a terrible curse from God (cf. Prov. 1:27; 10:24)!

▣ "Because I called, but no one answered" Here again is the repetition of the theme of no faith, no repentant response from YHWH's covenant people (cf. Isa. 41:28; 50:2; 65:12).

entries.title: Isaiah 66:3-4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 66:3-4 This shows that ritual alone is not satisfactory (cf. Isa. 29:13; Jeremiah 7), but combined with ritual must be a humble and repentant heart. That which we do over and over again tends to become common, but in the area of faith, our motive is the key (cf. Isa. 66:2).

entries.title: Isaiah 66:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:5 There is a distress and tension within the people of God (cf. Rom. 9:6-8). The persecution of the prophets by fellow Judeans is a good example of this (cf. Matt. 5:10-12; 10:22). Many horrible things have been done by "religious" people in God's name!

Notice how the true people of God should respond to persecution ‒ joy (BDB 970, cf. Isa. 51:11; 55:12; 61:7; note 66:10 which has several other words synonymous with joy. Jesus talks about God's joy often in John's Gospel (cf. John 3:29; 15:11; 16:24; 17:13).

  1. be glad ‒ BDB 162
  2. rejoice ‒ BDB 965 (twice)
  3. also Qal IMPERATIVE of "joy" (BDB 970)

There are three commands in Isa. 66:5.

  1. Hear the word of the Lord ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 1033, KB 1570
  2. Let the Lord be glorified ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 457, KB 455, used in a JUSSIVE sense (the LXX translates it as PASSIVE)
  3. That we may see your joy ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 906, KB 157, used in a COHORTATIVE sense

entries.title: Isaiah 66:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 66:6 There has been much discussion among commentators about how this verse relates to the context. Some say it is an unknown historical event, while others say it is related directly to Isa. 66:5, which shows the judgment of prideful, unbelieving Judeans (i.e. here called "enemies").

entries.title: Isaiah 66:7-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 66:7-13 This context refers to Zion bringing forth a nation in one day which includes Gentiles. Some see this as the return from exile, but in this event no Gentiles were included. Therefore, it must be eschatological (i.e. NT).

entries.title: Isaiah 66:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:10 As a result of what YHWH has done in restoring His people to their Promised Land (i.e. Gen. 12:1; 15:16), the commands are

  1. be joyful ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 970, KB 1333
  2. rejoice ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 162, KB 189
  3. be exceedingly glad ‒ the Qal IMPERATIVE and the NOUN, BDB 965, KB 965

entries.title: Isaiah 66:11-12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 66:11-12 Nursing imagery is used of YHWH's mercy. Please listen to my audio sermon, "The Femininity of God" (second green box on my homepage, www.freebiblecommentary.org, #111).

entries.title: Isaiah 66:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:12 The parental imagery of God's love for His people is so powerful in this verse. YHWH is described in feminine imagery (cf. Isa. 49:15; 66:9-13).

The fact that God would use "a nursing woman" to describe Himself says volumes.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN MINISTRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN MINISTERS

entries.title: Isaiah 66:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:13 The word "comforts" (BDB 636, KB 688) is used three times in this verse.

  1. Piel IMPERFECT (twice)
  2. same as #1
  3. Pual IMPERFECT

This reminds one of Isa. 40:1 (Piel IMPERATIVE, twice); also note Isa. 12:1; 53:3 (twice),12,19; 52:9; 61:2 (57:18, BDB 637). This is a major theme of Isaiah 40-66. YHWH has acted to forgive, forget, and restore those who trust Him and tremble at His word (Isa. 66:2,5)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COMFORT

entries.title: Isaiah 66:15-16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:15-16 Notice the different images used to describe YHWH's judgment.

  1. fire (BDB 77; see SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE)
  2. whirlwind (BDB 693 I, cf. Isa. 5:28; Jer. 4:13)
  3. His anger (BDB 60 I) with fury (BDB 404, cf. Isa. 42:25; 51:20; 63:3,6)
  4. His rebuke with flames of fire, cf. Isa. 29:6; 30:30
  5. judgment by fire
  6. His sword on all flesh, cf. Isa. 65:12

entries.title: Isaiah 66:16 "those slain by the Lord will be many"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:16 "those slain by the Lord will be many" This shows that judgment will begin with the household of God. We need to remember that there are many within the covenant community and, God help us, within the Church, who do not really know the Messiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

entries.title: Isaiah 66:17 "to the gardens"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:17 "to the gardens" This is a reference to a place of pagan worship (cf. Isa. 65:3).

▣ "Following one in the center" The word translated "center" (BDB 1063) is also used of the "tree of life" in Gen. 3:3. The Septuagint sees Isa. 65:22 as also referring to the tree of life. Here this may refer to the Asherah poles or carved stake of Canaanite fertility worship.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

▣ "Who eat. . ."

  1. swine's flesh, cf. Isa. 65:4
  2. detestable things (BDB 1054, cf. Lev. 11:10,11,12,13,20,23,41,42)
  3. mice (BDB 747, cf. Lev. 11:29)

I think the food laws of Leviticus 11 are not hygienic but cultic. They were meant to keep Israel from any social or religious contact with Canaanites.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOD LAWS (OT)

entries.title: Isaiah 66:18 "For I know their words and their thoughts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 66:18 "For I know their words and their thoughts" God knows the hearts of all humans. See full note at Isa. 1:2. YHWH knows the thoughts and intentions of the heart (cf. 1 Sam. 2:3; 16:7; 1 Kgs. 8:39; 1 Chr. 28:9; 2 Chr. 6:30; Ps. 7:9; 17:3; 26:2; 44:21; 139:1,23; Prov. 15:11; 16:2; 21:2; 24:12; Isa. 66:18; Jer. 11:20; 17:9-10; 20:12; Luke 16:15; Acts 1:24; 15:8; Rom. 8:27). Jesus also knows the inner thoughts and motives of humans, cf. John 2:24-25; 6:61,64; 13:11!

entries.title: Isaiah 66:18-21 "the time is coming to gather all nations and tongues"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:18-21 "the time is coming to gather all nations and tongues" The word "time" has been added by Eben Ezra in his translation of the Masoretic Text. There is some confusion as to the exact setting of this verse. The VERB "know" is also not in the Hebrew text.

This is a reference somehow to the gathering of the nations. They seem to come for hostile purposes against the people of God (i.e. "survivors"). But, in God's defeat of them (cf. Isa. 66:24b) some come to believe in Him. Then God sends them as a sign, Isa. 66:19 (cf. Isa. 11:10,12), to their own nations as evangelists. And, wonder of wonders - the heathen respond to the message and come back to God at Jerusalem to worship and He even makes some of them into priests and Levites (cf. Isa. 61:6; 66:21).

This section, Isa. 66:19-24, is absolutely shocking in its universal thrust. This has caused great consternation and uncertainty among the rabbis, but in context, it is obviously the fulfillment of the Abrahamic promise of Gen. 3:15; 12:1-3.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 66:19 "sign"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:19 "sign" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGN

▣ "Tarshish" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TARSHISH.

▣ "Put" The MT has Pul (BDB 806, Peshitta, JPSOA, REB, NET), which refers to a place in Babylon, but many modern translations (i.e. RSV, NEB) have "Put," which refers to Libya. The LXX has Phud, which also refers to Libya.

▣ "Lud" The location of this ethnic group is uncertain.

  1. Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11; Jer. 46:9 relate them to Egypt
  2. Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17 relate them to Shem, making them Semites
  3. Ezek. 27:10 relates them to North Africa (related to Libya)
  4. Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews 1:144, relates them to Asia Minor (Jewish Study Bible, p. 916); related to Libya

▣ "Meshech, Rosh, Tubal" First "Meshech" is from the LXX. The MT has "those who draw the bow." The UBS Text Project gives the LXX a "C" rating.

All of these names occur in Ezekiel 38 and refer to people groups in Asia Minor (i.e. Turkey).

▣ "Javan" This refers to Greece.

entries.title: Isaiah 66:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 66:20 This is one of several texts that speak of the Gentile nations bringing gifts and offerings (cf. Isa. 43:6; 49:22; 60:4; Micah 4:1-2) to Jerusalem/temple (cf. Isa. 2:2-3; 11:9; 56:7; 65:11,25; Ps. 22:27; 86:9; Jer. 3:17). This verse refers to part of the offering of the nations will be the Israelite and Judean returnees!.

entries.title: Isaiah 66:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:22 For "the new heavens and the new earth," see full note at Isa. 65:17.

The VERB "endure" (BDB 763, KB 840) is used twice.

  1. the new heavens and earth will endure ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (see full note at Isa. 62:2; also note Rev. 21-22)
  2. the seed of the faithful will endure ‒ Qal PERFECT with waw

This word, though used often in this section of Isaiah (cf. Isa. 44:11; 46:7; 47:12,13; 48:13; 50:8; 59:14; 61:5), is translated "endure" only in Isa. 66:22. It usually means "to stand."

entries.title: Isaiah 66:23 "All mankind will come to bow down before Me," says the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:23 "All mankind will come to bow down before Me," says the Lord" The VERB (BDB 1005, KB 295) is a rare Hishtapael (found only here). This is the obvious implication of monotheism. For a full list of the universal emphasis in Isaiah see 45:22.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Isaiah 66:24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
66:24 This is the description of the fate of the unfaithful of both covenant people and Gentiles. I do not think one can build a theology of end-time punishment based on this verse. This is the possible source of Jesus' use of the word Gehenna, which is a contraction of the phrase, "the valley of the sons of Hinnon," which was the place Judeans worshiped Molech and was made into a garbage dump of Jerusalem. Jesus used this term to describe eternal separation from God. Notice the elements of the worm that does not die and the fire that is not quenched. This is the imagery chosen by Jesus Himself to describe the fate of those who refuse to believe in Him (cf. Matt. 25:46).

I personally am becoming more and more convinced of the theological opinion related to eternal punishment called "limited immortality." Please see the following references.

  1. my SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT
  2. the YouTube video by Edward fudge, "The Fire That Consumes"
  3. the YouTube video by Steve Gregg, "Hell, Three Christian Views"

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. What is the central theme of Isaiah 65-66?
  2. List the pagan worship rites of Isa. 65.
  3. To whom Isa. 65:1 and 2 refer and why?
  4. What is so unique about Isaiah 65 which is particularly seen in Isa. 66:10 and 11?
  5. Why does God create a new heaven and a new earth?
  6. What is the significance of Isa. 66:19-23?
